ययौ तत्र स पैशाचः शूरायुतसमन्वितः ॥2॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Kutukoddīna, of demonic nature, occupied the kingdom of Dehalī. / There was a city, Valīgaḍha, exceedingly delightful, guarded by the Yādavas; / thither went that demonic one, accompanied by ten thousand warriors.

3.4.s:
vīrasenasya vai pautraṃ bhūpasenaṃ nṛpottamam ..
sa jitvā kutukoddīno dehalīgrāmasaṃsthitaḥ .. 3 ..
3.4.d:
वीरसेनस्य वै पौत्रं भूपसेनं नृपोत्तमम् ॥
स जित्वा कुतुकोद्दीनो देहलीग्रामसंस्थितः ॥ 3 ॥
3.4.m: Having conquered Bhūpasena, the best of kings, the grandson of Vīrasena, / Kutukoddīna established himself in the town of Dehalī.

3.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare bhūpā nānādeśyāḥ samāgatāḥ ..
jitvā sa kutukoddīnaḥ svadeśāttairnirākṛtaḥ .. 4 ..
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे भूपा नानादेश्याः समागताः ॥
जित्वा स कुतुकोद्दीनः स्वदेशात्तैर्निराकृतः ॥ 4 ॥
3.4.m: Meanwhile, kings from various lands assembled; / having defeated Kutukoddīna, he was expelled by them from his own country.

3.4.s:
sahoddīnastu tacchrutvā punarāgatya dehalīm ..
jitvā bhūpāndaityavaro mūrtikhaṃḍamathākarot .. 5 ..
3.4.d:
सहोद्दीनस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा पुनरागत्य देहलीम् ॥
जित्वा भूपान्दैत्यवरो मूर्तिखंडमथाकरोत् ॥ 5 ॥
3.4.m: Sahoddīna, having heard of that, came again to Dehalī; / having conquered the kings, that foremost of daityas then broke the [sacred] images.

3.4.s:
tatpaścādbahudhā mlecchā ihāgatya samantataḥ ..
paṃcaṣaṭsaptavarṣāṇi kṛtvā rājyaṃ layaṃ gatāḥ .. 6 ..
3.4.d:
तत्पश्चाद्बहुधा म्लेच्छा इहागत्य समन्ततः ॥
पंचषट्सप्तवर्षाणि कृत्वा राज्यं लयं गताः ॥ 6 ॥
3.4.m: After that, numerous mlecchas arrived here from every side; / having ruled for five, six, or seven years, they met their demise.

3.4.s:
adyaprabhṛti deśe'smiñchatavarṣāntare hi te ..
bhūtvā cālpāyuṣo mandā devatīrthavināśakāḥ .. 7 ..
3.4.d:
अद्यप्रभृति देशेऽस्मिञ्छतवर्षान्तरे हि ते ॥
भूत्वा चाल्पायुषो मन्दा देवतीर्थविनाशकाः ॥ 7 ॥
3.4.m: Beginning today, within a hundred years in this land, / having become short-lived, dull-witted destroyers of gods and sacred places,

3.4.s:
mlecchabhūpā muniśreṣṭhāstasmādyūyaṃ mayā saha ..
gaṃtumarhatha vai śīghraṃ viśālāṃ nagarīṃ śubhām .. 8 ..
3.4.d:
म्लेच्छभूपा मुनिश्रेष्ठास्तस्माद्यूयं मया सह ॥
गंतुमर्हथ वै शीघ्रं विशालां नगरीं शुभाम् ॥ 8 ॥
3.4.m: the mleccha kings [will perish], O best of sages! Therefore, you ought / to go quickly with me to the auspicious city of Viśālā.

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ duḥkhātsaṃtyajya naimiṣam ..
yayuḥ sarve viśālāyāṃ himādrau girisattame .. 9 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं दुःखात्संत्यज्य नैमिषम् ॥
ययुः सर्वे विशालायां हिमाद्रौ गिरिसत्तमे ॥ 9 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard this speech, abandoning Naimiṣa out of grief, / they all went to Viśālā in the snowy mountain, the best of mountains.

3.4.s:
tatra sarve samādhisthā dhyātvā sarvamayaṃ harim ..
śatavarṣāntare sarve dhyānādbrahmagṛhaṃ yayuḥ ..3.4.6.1 0..
3.4.d:
तत्र सर्वे समाधिस्था ध्यात्वा सर्वमयं हरिम् ॥
शतवर्षान्तरे सर्वे ध्यानाद्ब्रह्मगृहं ययुः ॥3.4.6.1 0॥
3.4.m: There, all remaining in deep absorption, meditating upon Hari who consists of all, / after a hundred years they all went from their meditation to the abode of Brahman.

3.4.s:
vyāsa uvāca ..
ityevaṃ sakalaṃ bhāvyaṃ yogābhyāsavaśāddrutam ..
varṇitaṃ ca mayā tubhyaṃ kimanyacchrotumicchasi . .. 11 ..
3.4.d:
व्यास उवाच ॥
इत्येवं सकलं भाव्यं योगाभ्यासवशाद्द्रुतम् ॥
वर्णितं च मया तुभ्यं किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥। 11 ॥
3.4.m: Vyāsa said: / Thus everything that is to happen has been swiftly described / to you by me through the power of yogic practice. What else do you wish to hear?

3.4.s:
.. manuruvāca .. ..
bhagavanvedatattvajña sarvalokaśivaṃkaraḥ ..
ahaṃ māyābhavo jāto bhavānvedabhavo bhuvi .. 12 ..
3.4.d:
॥ मनुरुवाच ॥ ॥
भगवन्वेदतत्त्वज्ञ सर्वलोकशिवंकरः ॥
अहं मायाभवो जातो भवान्वेदभवो भुवि ॥ 12 ॥
3.4.m: Manu said: / O Blessed One, knower of the truth of the Veda, creator of auspiciousness for all the worlds! / I was born from Māyā; you were born from the Veda on the earth.

3.4.s:
avidyayā ca sakalaṃ mama jñānaṃ samāhṛtam ..
ato'haṃ vividhā yonīrgṛhītvā lokamāgataḥ ..13..
3.4.d:
अविद्यया च सकलं मम ज्ञानं समाहृतम् ॥
अतोऽहं विविधा योनीर्गृहीत्वा लोकमागतः ॥13॥
3.4.m: And through nescience all my knowledge was taken away; / therefore, assuming various wombs, I have come to this world.

3.4.s:
paraṃ brahmaiva kṛpayā dṛṣṭvā māṃ maṃdabhāginam ..
vyāsarūpaṃ svayaṃ kṛtvā samuddhartumupāgataḥ .. 14 ..
3.4.d:
परं ब्रह्मैव कृपया दृष्ट्वा मां मंदभागिनम् ॥
व्यासरूपं स्वयं कृत्वा समुद्धर्तुमुपागतः ॥ 14 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing me unfortunate, the supreme Brahman itself, out of compassion, / having assumed the form of Vyāsa, has arrived to uplift [me].

3.4.s:
namastasmai munīṃdrāya vedavyāsāya sākṣiṇe ..
avidyāmohabhāvebhyo rakṣaṇāya namonamaḥ .. 15 ..
3.4.d:
नमस्तस्मै मुनींद्राय वेदव्यासाय साक्षिणे ॥
अविद्यामोहभावेभ्यो रक्षणाय नमोनमः ॥ 15 ॥
3.4.m: Obeisance to that lord of sages, Veda-Vyāsa, the witness; / repeated obeisance to him for protection from the states of nescience and delusion!

3.4.s:
punaranyacca me brūhi sūtādyaiḥ kiṃ kṛtaṃ mune ..
tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā svāminvaktumarhasi sāṃpratam .. 16 ..
3.4.d:
पुनरन्यच्च मे ब्रूहि सूताद्यैः किं कृतं मुने ॥
तत्सर्वं कृपया स्वामिन्वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम् ॥ 16 ॥
3.4.m: Tell me yet another thing, O sage: what was done by Sūta and the others? / You ought kindly to tell all of that now, O master.

3.4.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
brahmāṃḍe ye sthitā lokāste sarvesminkalevare ..
ahaṃkāro hi jīvātmā sarvaḥ syātkoṭihīnakaḥ .. 17 ..
3.4.d:
॥ व्यास उवाच ॥ ॥
ब्रह्मांडे ये स्थिता लोकास्ते सर्वेस्मिन्कलेवरे ॥
अहंकारो हि जीवात्मा सर्वः स्यात्कोटिहीनकः ॥ 17 ॥
3.4.m: Vyāsa said: / Whatever worlds are situated in the cosmic egg are all within this body. / The individual soul is indeed the ego, [though] it is entirely devoid of multiplicity.

3.4.s:
purāṇo'ṇoraṇīyāṃśca ṣoḍaśātmā sanātanaḥ ..
indriyāṇi manaścaiva pañca cendriyagocarāḥ .. 18 ..
3.4.d:
पुराणोऽणोरणीयांश्च षोडशात्मा सनातनः ॥
इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव पञ्च चेन्द्रियगोचराः ॥ 18 ॥
3.4.m: It is ancient, subtler than the subtle, sixteenfold, and eternal: / the senses, the mind, and the five objects of the senses.

3.4.s:
jñeyo jīvaḥ śarīre'sminsa īśaguṇabaṃdhitaḥ ..
īśo hyaṣṭādaśātmā vai śaṃkaro jīvaśaṃkaraḥ .. 19 ..
3.4.d:
ज्ञेयो जीवः शरीरेऽस्मिन्स ईशगुणबंधितः ॥
ईशो ह्यष्टादशात्मा वै शंकरो जीवशंकरः ॥ 19 ॥
3.4.m: The soul in this body is to be known as bound by the qualities of the Lord. / The Lord is eighteenfold, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the soul.

3.4.s:
buddhirmanaśca viṣayā iṃdriyāṇi tathaiva ca ..
ahaṃkārasya ceśo vai mahādevaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 3.4.6.20 ..
3.4.d:
बुद्धिर्मनश्च विषया इंद्रियाणि तथैव च ॥
अहंकारस्य चेशो वै महादेवः सनातनः ॥ 3.4.6.20 ॥
3.4.m: Intellect, mind, sensory objects, and likewise the senses; / and the Lord of ego is eternal Mahādeva.

3.4.s:
jīvo nārāyaṇassākṣācchaṃkareṇa vimohitaḥ ..
sa baddhastriguṇaiḥ pāśairekaśca bahudhābhavat .. .. 21 ..
3.4.d:
जीवो नारायणस्साक्षाच्छंकरेण विमोहितः ॥
स बद्धस्त्रिगुणैः पाशैरेकश्च बहुधाभवत् ॥ ॥ 21 ॥
3.4.m: The embodied soul is directly Nārāyaṇa, deluded by Śaṅkara; / bound by the three strands as if by snares, though one, it became manifold.

3.4.s:
kālātmā bhagavānīśo mahākalpasvarūpakaḥ ..
śivakalpo brahmakalpo viṣṇukalpastṛtīyakaḥ ..
īśanetrāṇi tānyeva bandhakalpaścaturthakaḥ .. 22 ..
3.4.d:
कालात्मा भगवानीशो महाकल्पस्वरूपकः ॥
शिवकल्पो ब्रह्मकल्पो विष्णुकल्पस्तृतीयकः ॥
ईशनेत्राणि तान्येव बन्धकल्पश्चतुर्थकः ॥ 22 ॥
3.4.m: The Lord, the supreme master, is the embodiment of time, consisting of the great kalpas: / the Śivakalpa, the Brahmakalpa, and the Viṣṇukalpa as the third; / those very ones are the eyes of the Lord, and the Bandhakalpa is the fourth.

3.4.s:
vāyukalpo vahnikalpo brahmāṃḍo liṃgakalpakaḥ ..
īśavaktrāṇi pañcaiva tattvajñaiḥ kathitāni vai .. 23 ..
3.4.d:
वायुकल्पो वह्निकल्पो ब्रह्मांडो लिंगकल्पकः ॥
ईशवक्त्राणि पञ्चैव तत्त्वज्ञैः कथितानि वै ॥ 23 ॥
3.4.m: The Vāyukalpa, the Vahnikalpa, the Brahmāṇḍa, and the Liṅgakalpa— / these five are indeed spoken of by the knowers of reality as the faces of the Lord.

3.4.s:
bhaviṣyakalpaśca tathā tathā garuḍaka lpakaḥ ..
kalpo bhāgavataścaiva mārkaṇḍeyaśca kalpakaḥ ..24..
3.4.d:
भविष्यकल्पश्च तथा तथा गरुडक ल्पकः ॥
कल्पो भागवतश्चैव मार्कण्डेयश्च कल्पकः ॥24॥
3.4.m: And likewise the Bhaviṣyakalpa, as well as the Garuḍakalpa, / the Bhāgavatakalpa, and the Mārkaṇḍeyakalpa,

3.4.s:
vāmanaśca nṛsiṃhaśca varāho matsyakūrmakau ..
jñānātmano maheśasya jñeyā daśa bhujā budhaiḥ .. 25 ..
3.4.d:
वामनश्च नृसिंहश्च वराहो मत्स्यकूर्मकौ ॥
ज्ञानात्मनो महेशस्य ज्ञेया दश भुजा बुधैः ॥ 25 ॥
3.4.m: and Vāmana, Nṛsiṃha, Varāha, Matsya, and Kūrma: / these should be known by the wise as the ten arms of Maheśa, whose essence is knowledge.

3.4.s:
aṣṭādaśadineṣveva brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ ..
kalpāścāṣṭādaśāssarve budhairjñeyā vilomataḥ .. 26 ..
3.4.d:
अष्टादशदिनेष्वेव ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः ॥
कल्पाश्चाष्टादशास्सर्वे बुधैर्ज्ञेया विलोमतः ॥ 26 ॥
3.4.m: Over the eighteen days of Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest, / all eighteen kalpas should be known by the wise in reverse order.

3.4.s:
kūrmakalpaśca tatrādyo matsyakalpo dvitīyakaḥ ..
tṛtīyaḥ śvetavārāhaḥ kalpo jñeyaḥ purātanaiḥ .. 27 ..
3.4.d:
कूर्मकल्पश्च तत्राद्यो मत्स्यकल्पो द्वितीयकः ॥
तृतीयः श्वेतवाराहः कल्पो ज्ञेयः पुरातनैः ॥ 27 ॥
3.4.m: Among them, the Kūrmakalpa is the first, the Matsyakalpa is the second, / and the third should be known by the ancients as the Śvetavārāha kalpa.

3.4.s:
dvidhā ca bhagavānbrahmā sūkṣmaḥ sthūlo'guṇo guṇī ..
saguṇaḥ sa virāṇnāmnā viṣṇu nābhisamudbhavaḥ .. 28 ..
3.4.d:
द्विधा च भगवान्ब्रह्मा सूक्ष्मः स्थूलोऽगुणो गुणी ॥
सगुणः स विराण्नाम्ना विष्णु नाभिसमुद्भवः ॥ 28 ॥
3.4.m: And the Lord Brahmā is twofold: subtle and gross, without qualities and endowed with qualities. / The one endowed with qualities is called Virāj, born from the navel of Viṣṇu.

3.4.s:
nirguṇovyayarūpaścāvyaktajanmā svabhūḥ svayam ..
brahmaṇaḥ saguṇasyaiva śatāyuḥ kālanirmitam .. 29 ..
3.4.d:
निर्गुणोव्ययरूपश्चाव्यक्तजन्मा स्वभूः स्वयम् ॥
ब्रह्मणः सगुणस्यैव शतायुः कालनिर्मितम् ॥ 29 ॥
3.4.m: The one without qualities is imperishable in nature, born from the unmanifest, self-existent himself. / The lifespan of Brahmā endowed with qualities is ordained by time as one hundred years.

3.4.s:
ūnaviṃśasahasrāṇi lakṣaiko mānuṣābdakaiḥ ..
ebhirvarṣairdinaṃ jñeyaṃ virājo brahmaṇaḥ svayam .. 3.4.6.30 ..
3.4.d:
ऊनविंशसहस्राणि लक्षैको मानुषाब्दकैः ॥
एभिर्वर्षैर्दिनं ज्ञेयं विराजो ब्रह्मणः स्वयम् ॥ 3.4.6.30 ॥
3.4.m: One hundred and nineteen thousand human years— / by these years, a single day of Virāj-Brahmā himself is to be known.

3.4.s:
nirguṇo'vyaktajanmā ca kālātsarveśvaraḥ paraḥ ..
avyaktaṃ prakṛtirjñeyā dvādaśāṃgāni vai tataḥ .. 31 ..
3.4.d:
निर्गुणोऽव्यक्तजन्मा च कालात्सर्वेश्वरः परः ॥
अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिर्ज्ञेया द्वादशांगानि वै ततः ॥ 31 ॥
3.4.m: He who is without qualities, born of the unmanifest, is the supreme ruler of all, beyond time. / The unmanifest is to be known as Prakṛti; from it, indeed, come the twelve limbs.

3.4.s:
indriyāṇi mano buddhiravyaktasya smṛtāni vai ..
avyaktācca paraṃ brahma sūkṣmajyotistadavyayam .. 32 ..
3.4.d:
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिरव्यक्तस्य स्मृतानि वै ॥
अव्यक्ताच्च परं ब्रह्म सूक्ष्मज्योतिस्तदव्ययम् ॥ 32 ॥
3.4.m: The sense organs, the mind, and the intellect are traditionally taught as belonging to the unmanifest. / Beyond the unmanifest is the supreme Brahman, that subtle, imperishable light.

3.4.s:
yadā vyakte svayaṃ prāpto'vyaktajanmā hi saṃsmṛtaḥ ..
śatavarṣasamādhistho yastiṣṭhecca niraṃtaram .. 33 ..
3.4.d:
यदा व्यक्ते स्वयं प्राप्तोऽव्यक्तजन्मा हि संस्मृतः ॥
शतवर्षसमाधिस्थो यस्तिष्ठेच्च निरंतरम् ॥ 33 ॥
3.4.m: When he who is known as born of the unmanifest arrives in the manifest himself, / whoever remains continuously absorbed in samādhi for a hundred years,

3.4.s:
sūkṣmo manonilo bhūtvā gacchedvai brahmaṇaḥ padam ..
satya lokamiti jñeyaṃ yogagamyaṃ sanātanam ..34..
3.4.d:
सूक्ष्मो मनोनिलो भूत्वा गच्छेद्वै ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥
सत्य लोकमिति ज्ञेयं योगगम्यं सनातनम् ॥34॥
3.4.m: becoming subtle as the wind of the mind, will go to the abode of Brahmā, / known as Satyaloka, accessible through yoga, eternal.

3.4.s:
tatra sthāne tu munayo gatāḥ sarve samādhinā ..
tatroṣitvā ca lakṣābdaṃ bhūrlokātkṣaṇamātrakam ..35..
3.4.d:
तत्र स्थाने तु मुनयो गताः सर्वे समाधिना ॥
तत्रोषित्वा च लक्षाब्दं भूर्लोकात्क्षणमात्रकम् ॥35॥
3.4.m: All the sages, having gone to that realm through samādhi, / and having dwelt there for a hundred thousand years—which was but a moment from the perspective of the earthly realm—

3.4.s:
saccidānaṃdaghanakaṃ tataḥ prāptāḥ kalevare ..
netrāṇi ca samunmīlya saṃprāpte dvitayāhnike .. 36 ..
3.4.d:
सच्चिदानंदघनकं ततः प्राप्ताः कलेवरे ॥
नेत्राणि च समुन्मील्य संप्राप्ते द्वितयाह्निके ॥ 36 ॥
3.4.m: then returned into their physical bodies, dense with being, consciousness, and bliss; / and opening their eyes when the second day arrived,

3.4.s:
dadṛśurmanujānsarvānpaśutulyānhi sūkṣmakān..
ṣaṣṭyabdāyuryutānghorānsārddhakiṣkudvayonnatān ..37..
3.4.d:
ददृशुर्मनुजान्सर्वान्पशुतुल्यान्हि सूक्ष्मकान्॥
षष्ट्यब्दायुर्युतान्घोरान्सार्द्धकिष्कुद्वयोन्नतान् ॥37॥
3.4.m: they saw all men to be like beasts, diminished in size, / with a lifespan of sixty years, terrible, two and a half cubits tall.

3.4.s:
kvacitkvacitsthitā varṇā varṇasaṃkarasannibhāḥ ..
sarve mlecchāśca pāṣaṃḍā bahurūpamato sthitāḥ ..38..
3.4.d:
क्वचित्क्वचित्स्थिता वर्णा वर्णसंकरसन्निभाः ॥
सर्वे म्लेच्छाश्च पाषंडा बहुरूपमतो स्थिताः ॥38॥
3.4.m: The classes remained here and there resembling a confusion of castes; / all were barbarians and heretics, established in various sectarian views.

3.4.s:
tīrthāni sakalā vedāstyaktvā bhūmaṃḍalaṃ tadā ..
gopyo bhūtvā ca hariṇā sārddhaṃ cakrurmahotsavam 39 ..
3.4.d:
तीर्थानि सकला वेदास्त्यक्त्वा भूमंडलं तदा ॥
गोप्यो भूत्वा च हरिणा सार्द्धं चक्रुर्महोत्सवम् 39 ॥
3.4.m: All the sacred fords and the Vedas then abandoned the earth, / and, having become cowherdesses, celebrated a great festival together with Hari.

3.4.s:
pāṣaṃḍā bahujātīyā nānāmārgapradarśakāḥ ..
kalinā nirmitānvarṇānvaṃcayitvā sthitā bhuvi .. 3.4.6.40 ..
3.4.d:
पाषंडा बहुजातीया नानामार्गप्रदर्शकाः ॥
कलिना निर्मितान्वर्णान्वंचयित्वा स्थिता भुवि ॥ 3.4.6.40 ॥
3.4.m: The heretics, belonging to many sects and showing various paths, / remained on earth having deceived the castes created by the Kali age.

3.4.s:
iti dṛṣṭvā tu munayo romaharṣaṇamaṃtike ..
gatvā tatra bhaviṣyaṃti tataḥ prāṃjalayo hi te .. 41 ..
3.4.d:
इति दृष्ट्वा तु मुनयो रोमहर्षणमंतिके ॥
गत्वा तत्र भविष्यंति ततः प्रांजलयो हि ते ॥ 41 ॥
3.4.m: Having seen this, the sages went near Romaharṣaṇa; / there, with folded hands, they will stand before him.

3.4.s:
taiśca tatra stutaḥ sūto yoganidrāṃ sanātanīm ..
kathayiṣyati saṃtyajya kalpākhyānaṃ munīnprati ..
tacchṛṇuṣva nṛpaśreṣṭha yathā sūtena varṇitam .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
तैश्च तत्र स्तुतः सूतो योगनिद्रां सनातनीम् ॥
कथयिष्यति संत्यज्य कल्पाख्यानं मुनीन्प्रति ॥
तच्छृणुष्व नृपश्रेष्ठ यथा सूतेन वर्णितम् ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m: Praised there by them, the Sūta, abandoning his eternal yogic slumber, / will narrate the account of the kalpas to the sages. / Hear that, O best of kings, just as it was described by the Sūta.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
kalpākhyānaṃ pravakṣyāmi yaddṛṣṭaṃ yoganidrayā ..
tacchṛṇudhvaṃ muniśreṣṭhā lakṣābdāṃte yathābhavat ..43..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
कल्पाख्यानं प्रवक्ष्यामि यद्दृष्टं योगनिद्रया ॥
तच्छृणुध्वं मुनिश्रेष्ठा लक्षाब्दांते यथाभवत् ॥43॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / I shall declare the account of the kalpas that was seen through yogic slumber. / Listen to that, O best of sages, as it happened at the end of a hundred thousand years.

3.4.s:
mukulānvayasaṃbhūto mlecchabhūpaḥ piśācakaḥ ..
nāmnā timiraliṃgaśca madhyadeśamupāyayau .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
मुकुलान्वयसंभूतो म्लेच्छभूपः पिशाचकः ॥
नाम्ना तिमिरलिंगश्च मध्यदेशमुपाययौ ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m: Born in the lineage of Mukula, a barbarian king, a demon / named Timiraliṅga, arrived in the Middle Country.

3.4.s:
āryānmlecchāṃstadā bhūpāñjitvā kālasvarūpakaḥ ..
dehalīnagarīmadhye mahāvadhamakārayat .. 45 ..
3.4.d:
आर्यान्म्लेच्छांस्तदा भूपाञ्जित्वा कालस्वरूपकः ॥
देहलीनगरीमध्ये महावधमकारयत् ॥ 45 ॥
3.4.m: Having conquered both the Āryan and barbarian kings, that embodiment of death / caused a great slaughter within the city of Dehalī.

3.4.s:
āhūya sakalānviprānāryadeśanivāsinaḥ ..
uvāca vacanaṃ dhīmānyūyaṃ mūrtiprapūjakāḥ .. 46 ..
3.4.d:
आहूय सकलान्विप्रानार्यदेशनिवासिनः ॥
उवाच वचनं धीमान्यूयं मूर्तिप्रपूजकाः ॥ 46 ॥
3.4.m: Summoning all the brahmins dwelling in the Āryan country, / the shrewd man spoke these words: 'You are idol-worshippers.

3.4.s:
nirmitā yena vā mūrtistasya putrīsamā smṛtā ..
tasyāḥ kiṃ pūjanaṃ śuddhaṃ śālagrāmaśilāmayam ..
viṣṇudevaśca yuṣmābhiḥ proktaḥ sa tu na vai hariḥ .. 47 ..
3.4.d:
निर्मिता येन वा मूर्तिस्तस्य पुत्रीसमा स्मृता ॥
तस्याः किं पूजनं शुद्धं शालग्रामशिलामयम् ॥
विष्णुदेवश्च युष्माभिः प्रोक्तः स तु न वै हरिः ॥ 47 ॥
3.4.m: By whomever an idol is fashioned, it is considered like his daughter. / What pure worship can there be of that, or of what is made of śālagrāma stone? / And that god Viṣṇu spoken of by you is certainly not Hari.

3.4.s:
ato vaḥ sakalā vedāḥ śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca ..
vṛthā kṛtāni munibhirlokavañcanahetave ..
ityuktvā tānbalādgṛhya jvaladagnau samākṣipat ..48..
3.4.d:
अतो वः सकला वेदाः शास्त्राणि विविधानि च ॥
वृथा कृतानि मुनिभिर्लोकवञ्चनहेतवे ॥
इत्युक्त्वा तान्बलाद्गृह्य ज्वलदग्नौ समाक्षिपत् ॥48॥
3.4.m: Therefore all your Vedas and various sacred texts / were composed in vain by sages for the purpose of deceiving the world.' / Having spoken thus, he seized them by force and cast them into a blazing fire.

3.4.s:
śālagrāmaśilāḥ sarvā balātteṣāṃ supūjyakāḥ ..
gṛhītvā coṣṭrapṛṣṭheṣu samāropya gṛhaṃ yayau ..49..
3.4.d:
शालग्रामशिलाः सर्वा बलात्तेषां सुपूज्यकाः ॥
गृहीत्वा चोष्ट्रपृष्ठेषु समारोप्य गृहं ययौ ॥49॥
3.4.m: Forcibly taking all their highly venerated śālagrāma stones / and loading them onto the backs of camels, he went home.

3.4.s:
taittiraṃ deśamāgamya durgaṃ tatra cakāra saḥ ..
śālagrāmaśilānāṃ ca svāsanārohaṇaṃ kṛtam .. 3.4.6.50 ..
3.4.d:
तैत्तिरं देशमागम्य दुर्गं तत्र चकार सः ॥
शालग्रामशिलानां च स्वासनारोहणं कृतम् ॥ 3.4.6.50 ॥
3.4.m: Having reached the Taittira country, he built a fortress there, / and used the śālagrāma stones as steps to mount his throne.

3.4.s:
tadā tu sakalā devā duḥkhitā vāsavaṃ prabhum ..
samūcurbahudhālapya devadevaṃ śacīpatim ..51..
3.4.d:
तदा तु सकला देवा दुःखिता वासवं प्रभुम् ॥
समूचुर्बहुधालप्य देवदेवं शचीपतिम् ॥51॥
3.4.m: Then all the gods, distressed, spoke in various ways, / crying out to Lord Vāsava, the god of gods, husband of Śacī:

3.4.s:
vayaṃ tu bhagavansarve śālagrāmaśilāsthitāḥ ..
tyaktvā mūrtīśca sakalāḥ kṛṣṇāṃśena prabodhitāḥ ..
śālagrāmaśilāmadhye vasāmo muditā vayam ..52 ..
3.4.d:
वयं तु भगवन्सर्वे शालग्रामशिलास्थिताः ॥
त्यक्त्वा मूर्तीश्च सकलाः कृष्णांशेन प्रबोधिताः ॥
शालग्रामशिलामध्ये वसामो मुदिता वयम् ॥52 ॥
3.4.m: 'Lord, all of us dwell in the śālagrāma stones; / having abandoned all idols, awakened by an aṃśa of Kṛṣṇa, / we reside happily within the śālagrāma stones.

3.4.s:
śilāssarvāśca no deva śāladeśasamudbhavāḥ ..
tāśca vai mleccharājena svapadārohaṇīkṛtāḥ ..53..
3.4.d:
शिलास्सर्वाश्च नो देव शालदेशसमुद्भवाः ॥
ताश्च वै म्लेच्छराजेन स्वपदारोहणीकृताः ॥53॥
3.4.m: All our stones, O god, originated in the Śāla country; / and those very stones have been made into footstools by the barbarian king.'

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ devānāṃ bhagavānsvarāṭ..
jñātvā balikṛtaṃ sarvaṃ devapūjānirākṛtam .. 54 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं देवानां भगवान्स्वराट्॥
ज्ञात्वा बलिकृतं सर्वं देवपूजानिराकृतम् ॥ 54 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing these words of the gods, the blessed sovereign ruler, / knowing that everything had been done by Bali and that the worship of the gods was obstructed,

3.4.s:
cukopa bhagavānindro daityānpratyabhravāhanaḥ ..
gṛhītvā vajramatulaṃ svāyudhaṃ daityanāśanam ..
taittire preṣayāmāsa deśe mlecchanivāsake .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
चुकोप भगवानिन्द्रो दैत्यान्प्रत्यभ्रवाहनः ॥
गृहीत्वा वज्रमतुलं स्वायुधं दैत्यनाशनम् ॥
तैत्तिरे प्रेषयामास देशे म्लेच्छनिवासके ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m: Lord Indra, who rides the clouds, grew furious at the demons; / grasping his incomparable thunderbolt, his own weapon that destroys demons, / he hurled it into the Taittira country, the dwelling place of the barbarian.

3.4.s:
tasya śabdena sakalā deśāśca bahubhinnakāḥ ..
sa mleccho maraṇaṃ prāptastadā sarvasabhājanaiḥ ..56..
3.4.d:
तस्य शब्देन सकला देशाश्च बहुभिन्नकाः ॥
स म्लेच्छो मरणं प्राप्तस्तदा सर्वसभाजनैः ॥56॥
3.4.m: By its sound all the regions were greatly shattered; / that barbarian met his death, together with all his courtiers.

3.4.s:
śālagrāmaśilāḥ sarvā gṛhītvā vibudhāstadā ..
gaṃḍakyāṃ ca samākṣipya svargalokamupāyayuḥ ..57..
3.4.d:
शालग्रामशिलाः सर्वा गृहीत्वा विबुधास्तदा ॥
गंडक्यां च समाक्षिप्य स्वर्गलोकमुपाययुः ॥57॥
3.4.m: Then, gathering all the śālagrāma stones, the gods / cast them into the Gaṇḍakī river and returned to the heavenly world.

3.4.s:
mahendrastu suraiḥ sārddhaṃ devapūjyamuvāca ha ..
mahītale kalau prāpte bhagavandānavottamāḥ ..58..
3.4.d:
महेन्द्रस्तु सुरैः सार्द्धं देवपूज्यमुवाच ह ॥
महीतले कलौ प्राप्ते भगवन्दानवोत्तमाः ॥58॥
3.4.m: Then Mahendra, together with the gods, spoke to the teacher of the gods: / 'Lord, when the Kali age arrived on earth, the foremost among the Dānavas,

3.4.s:
vedadharmaṃ samullaṃghya mama nāśanatatparāḥ ..
ato māṃ rakṣa bhagavandevaiḥ sārddhaṃ kalau yuge ..59..
3.4.d:
वेदधर्मं समुल्लंघ्य मम नाशनतत्पराः ॥
अतो मां रक्ष भगवन्देवैः सार्द्धं कलौ युगे ॥59॥
3.4.m: transgressing Vedic duty, became intent upon my destruction. / Therefore, O Lord, protect me along with the gods in the Kali age.'

3.4.s:
..jīva uvāca .. ..
mahendra tava yā patnī śacī nāmnā mahottamā ..
dadau tasyai varaṃ viṣṇurbhavitāsmi sutaḥ kalau ..3.4.6.60..
3.4.d:
॥जीव उवाच ॥ ॥
महेन्द्र तव या पत्नी शची नाम्ना महोत्तमा ॥
ददौ तस्यै वरं विष्णुर्भवितास्मि सुतः कलौ ॥3.4.6.60॥
3.4.m: Jīva said: / 'O Mahendra, to that most excellent wife of yours named Śacī, / Viṣṇu gave a boon: "I shall become your son in the Kali age."

3.4.s:
tvadājñayā ca sā devī purīṃ śāṃtimayīṃ śubhām..
gauḍadeśe ca gaṃgāyāḥ kūle lokanivāsinīm ..61..
3.4.d:
त्वदाज्ञया च सा देवी पुरीं शांतिमयीं शुभाम्॥
गौडदेशे च गंगायाः कूले लोकनिवासिनीम् ॥61॥
3.4.m: And by your command, that goddess [shall go to] the auspicious city full of peace, / in the Gauḍa country on the bank of the Gaṅgā, where people dwell.'

3.4.s:
pratyāgatya dvijo bhūtvā kāryasiddhiṃ kariṣyati ..
bhavānvai brāhmaṇo bhūtvā devakāryaṃ prasādhaya .. .. 62 ..
3.4.d:
प्रत्यागत्य द्विजो भूत्वा कार्यसिद्धिं करिष्यति ॥
भवान्वै ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा देवकार्यं प्रसाधय ॥ ॥ 62 ॥
3.4.m: Returning and becoming a twice-born, he will accomplish the objective. / You yourself indeed, becoming a brāhmaṇa, accomplish the task of the gods.

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ rudrairekādaśaiḥ saha ..
aṣṭabhirvasubhiḥ sārdhamaśvibhyāṃ sa ca vāsavaḥ .. 63 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं रुद्रैरेकादशैः सह ॥
अष्टभिर्वसुभिः सार्धमश्विभ्यां स च वासवः ॥ 63 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard this word of the preceptor, along with the eleven Rudras, / together with the eight Vasus and the two Aśvins, that Vāsava,

3.4.s:
tīrtharājamupāgamya prayāgaṃ ca ravipriyam..
māghe tu makare sūrye sūryadevamatoṣayat.. 64 ..
3.4.d:
तीर्थराजमुपागम्य प्रयागं च रविप्रियम्॥
माघे तु मकरे सूर्ये सूर्यदेवमतोषयत्॥ 64 ॥
3.4.m: having approached Prayāga, the king of sacred fords, dear to the Sun, / in Māgha when the sun was in Capricorn, propitiated the Sun God.

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatistadāgatya sūryamāhātmyamuttamam..
indrādīnkathayāmāsa dvādaśādhyāyamāpaṭhan..65..
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिस्तदागत्य सूर्यमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम्॥
इन्द्रादीन्कथयामास द्वादशाध्यायमापठन्॥65॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati, having arrived then, recited twelve chapters, / relating the supreme majesty of the Sun to Indra and the others.

3.4.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
bṛhaspatistu bhagavānmunirdevānsamāsthitān ..
kiṃ provāca ca māhātmyaṃ maṃḍalasthasya vai raveḥ ..1..
3.4.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥ ॥
बृहस्पतिस्तु भगवान्मुनिर्देवान्समास्थितान् ॥
किं प्रोवाच च माहात्म्यं मंडलस्थस्य वै रवेः ॥1॥
3.4.m: The sages said: / What majesty of the Sun abiding in his disc did the venerable sage Bṛhaspati indeed proclaim / to the assembled gods?

3.4.s:
tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā brahmanbrūhi nastatsamutsukān ..
iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ sūto vacanamabravīt ..2..
3.4.d:
तत्सर्वं कृपया ब्रह्मन्ब्रूहि नस्तत्समुत्सुकान् ॥
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां सूतो वचनमब्रवीत् ॥2॥
3.4.m: O brāhmaṇa, graciously tell all that to us who are eager for it. / Having heard their speech, Sūta spoke [these] words:

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatiṃ samāsīnaṃ jīvarūpaṃ guṇālayam ..
prayāgastho mahendraśca suraiḥ sārddhamuvāca ha..3..
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिं समासीनं जीवरूपं गुणालयम् ॥
प्रयागस्थो महेन्द्रश्च सुरैः सार्द्धमुवाच ह॥3॥
3.4.m: To Bṛhaspati, who was seated, the embodiment of Jīva, an abode of virtues, / great Indra, residing at Prayāga, spoke along with the gods:

3.4.s:
kathayasva mahābhāga sūryamāhātmyamuttamam..
yacchrutena raviḥ sākṣātprasannodya bhavetprabhuḥ..4..
3.4.d:
कथयस्व महाभाग सूर्यमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम्॥
यच्छ्रुतेन रविः साक्षात्प्रसन्नोद्य भवेत्प्रभुः॥4॥
3.4.m: Relate, O highly fortunate one, the supreme majesty of the Sun, / by the hearing of which the lord Sun may become directly pleased today.

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca..
dhātṛśarmā dvijaḥ kaścidapatyārthe prajāpatim..
tapasā toṣayāmāsa barhiṣmatipure sthitaḥ..5..
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच॥
धातृशर्मा द्विजः कश्चिदपत्यार्थे प्रजापतिम्॥
तपसा तोषयामास बर्हिष्मतिपुरे स्थितः॥5॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / A certain twice-born named Dhātṛśarman, residing in the city of Barhiṣmatī, / propitiated Prajāpati through ascetic penance for the sake of offspring.

3.4.s:
paṃcamābde tu bhagavānsaṃtuṣṭaśca prajāpatiḥ..
sutaṃ kanyāṃ punaḥ putraṃ trīṇyapatyāni saṃdadau ..6..
3.4.d:
पंचमाब्दे तु भगवान्संतुष्टश्च प्रजापतिः॥
सुतं कन्यां पुनः पुत्रं त्रीण्यपत्यानि संददौ ॥6॥
3.4.m: In the fifth year, the venerable Prajāpati, being well pleased, / bestowed three offspring: a son, a daughter, and again a son.

3.4.s:
varṣāṃtare janayitvā tryapatya sa dvijottamaḥ ..
dhātṛśarmā paraṃ harṣamāptavānputralālanaiḥ .. 7 ..
3.4.d:
वर्षांतरे जनयित्वा त्र्यपत्य स द्विजोत्तमः ॥
धातृशर्मा परं हर्षमाप्तवान्पुत्रलालनैः ॥ 7 ॥
3.4.m: Having fathered three offspring at yearly intervals, that best of twice-born, / Dhātṛśarman, attained supreme joy through fondling his children.

3.4.s:
vivāhāśca kathaṃ teṣāṃ bhavitavyā mahottamāḥ ..
iti cintānvito vipro gaṃdharveśaṃ ca tumburum .. 8 ..
3.4.d:
विवाहाश्च कथं तेषां भवितव्या महोत्तमाः ॥
इति चिन्तान्वितो विप्रो गंधर्वेशं च तुम्बुरुम् ॥ 8 ॥
3.4.m: “How shall their highly auspicious marriages take place?” / Filled with anxiety thus, the brāhmaṇa [propitiated] Tumburu, lord of the gandharvas,

3.4.s:
havanaistoṣayāmāsa varṣamātravidhānataḥ ..
tumburuśca tadāgatya taṃ cakāra manoratham .. 9 ..
3.4.d:
हवनैस्तोषयामास वर्षमात्रविधानतः ॥
तुम्बुरुश्च तदागत्य तं चकार मनोरथम् ॥ 9 ॥
3.4.m: pleasing [him] with fire oblations according to rule for the space of a year. / And Tumburu, arriving then, fulfilled that desire.

3.4.s:
prasannastu tadā vipro vadhūrjāmātaraṃ mudā ..
dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ vihāraṃ ca punaściṃtāṃ cakāra ha .. 3.4.7.10 ..
3.4.d:
प्रसन्नस्तु तदा विप्रो वधूर्जामातरं मुदा ॥
दृष्ट्वा तेषां विहारं च पुनश्चिंतां चकार ह ॥ 3.4.7.10 ॥
3.4.m: Pleased, the brāhmaṇa then, having seen with joy his daughters-in-law and sons-in-law / and their merriment, again fell into anxiety:

3.4.s:
bhūṣaṇāni ca vāsāṃsi dhanāni vividhāni ca ..
teṣāṃ kathaṃ bhaviṣyaṃti nirdhanānāṃ mamāśuca .. 11 ..
3.4.d:
भूषणानि च वासांसि धनानि विविधानि च ॥
तेषां कथं भविष्यंति निर्धनानां ममाशुच ॥ 11 ॥
3.4.m: “How will there be ornaments, clothes, and various kinds of wealth / for them, who are destitute, and [what of] my sorrow?”

3.4.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣamayo bhūtvā caṃdanādyairdhanādhipam ..
vidhivatpūjayāmāsa varṣamātraṃ tu tatparaḥ .. 12 ..
3.4.d:
षष्टिवर्षमयो भूत्वा चंदनाद्यैर्धनाधिपम् ॥
विधिवत्पूजयामास वर्षमात्रं तु तत्परः ॥ 12 ॥
3.4.m: Having reached sixty years of age, devoted to that, he worshipped the lord of wealth according to rule / with sandalwood and other [offerings] for just a year.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavāndadau tasmai dhanaṃ bahu ..
vidyāṃ yakṣamayīṃ ramyāṃ paṃcasvarṇapradāṃ mudā .. 13 ..
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्ददौ तस्मै धनं बहु ॥
विद्यां यक्षमयीं रम्यां पंचस्वर्णप्रदां मुदा ॥ 13 ॥
3.4.m: Then, being pleased, the lord joyfully gave him much wealth / and a charming knowledge pertaining to the yakṣas, which bestows five gold [coins].

3.4.s:
sahasrajāpī saṃpūjya havanaṃ taddaśāṃśakam ..
tarpaṇaṃ mārjanaṃ caiva kṛtvā vāṃchāmavāptavān ..14..
3.4.d:
सहस्रजापी संपूज्य हवनं तद्दशांशकम् ॥
तर्पणं मार्जनं चैव कृत्वा वांछामवाप्तवान् ॥14॥
3.4.m: Reciting [the mantra] a thousand times, having worshipped, having offered one-tenth of that as fire oblations, / and having performed libation and sprinkling, he obtained his desire.

3.4.s:
ityevaṃ vartamānasya gataḥ kālo mahānsvayam ..
mṛtyorāgamanaṃ tasya jātaṃ rogasamanvitam .. 15 ..
3.4.d:
इत्येवं वर्तमानस्य गतः कालो महान्स्वयम् ॥
मृत्योरागमनं तस्य जातं रोगसमन्वितम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.4.m: As he was living in this manner, a great length of time passed of itself. / The approach of death came upon him, accompanied by illness.

3.4.s:
pīḍitastu rujā vipraḥ śaṃkaraṃ lokaśaṃkaram ..
stutibhiḥ śrutirūpābhistuṣṭāva balavarjitaḥ ..
māsamātreṇa bhagavāndadau jñānaṃ svayaṃ haraḥ .. 16 ..
3.4.d:
पीडितस्तु रुजा विप्रः शंकरं लोकशंकरम् ॥
स्तुतिभिः श्रुतिरूपाभिस्तुष्टाव बलवर्जितः ॥
मासमात्रेण भगवान्ददौ ज्ञानं स्वयं हरः ॥ 16 ॥
3.4.m: Tormented by disease, bereft of strength, the brāhmaṇa praised Śaṅkara, / the benefactor of the world, with hymns in the form of Vedic verses; / in just a month, the venerable Hara himself gave [him] knowledge.

3.4.s:
dhātṛśarmā tu tatprāpya bhāskaraṃ mohanāśanam ..
sūryavāravrataistatra toṣayāmāsa namradhīḥ .. 17 ..
3.4.d:
धातृशर्मा तु तत्प्राप्य भास्करं मोहनाशनम् ॥
सूर्यवारव्रतैस्तत्र तोषयामास नम्रधीः ॥ 17 ॥
3.4.m: Having obtained that, Dhātṛśarman, with humble mind, / propitiated the Sun, the destroyer of delusion, with Sunday observances there.

3.4.s:
paṃcābde bhagavānsūryo bhaktibhāvena vatsalaḥ ..
caitryāṃ tamāha vacanaṃ varaṃ brūhi punaḥ punaḥ .. 18 ..
3.4.d:
पंचाब्दे भगवान्सूर्यो भक्तिभावेन वत्सलः ॥
चैत्र्यां तमाह वचनं वरं ब्रूहि पुनः पुनः ॥ 18 ॥
3.4.m: In the fifth year, the venerable Sun, affectionate because of his devotional disposition, / said to him on the full moon day of Caitra: “Ask a boon,” again and again.

3.4.s:
dhātṛśarmā tu tacchrutvā bhāskaraṃ mohanāśanam ..
praśrayāvanato bhūtvā tuṣṭāva parayā girā.. 19 ..
3.4.d:
धातृशर्मा तु तच्छ्रुत्वा भास्करं मोहनाशनम् ॥
प्रश्रयावनतो भूत्वा तुष्टाव परया गिरा॥ 19 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard that, Dhātṛśarman, bowing down with modesty / before the Sun, the destroyer of delusion, praised [him] with exalted speech.

3.4.s:
.. dhātṛśarmovāca .. ..
pravṛttiśca nivṛttiśca manasosya tanau priyā ..
rātrirūpā pravṛttiśca nivṛttirdinarūpiṇī..
bhavatastejasā jāte lokabaṃdhanahetave..3.4.7.20..
3.4.d:
॥ धातृशर्मोवाच ॥ ॥
प्रवृत्तिश्च निवृत्तिश्च मनसोस्य तनौ प्रिया ॥
रात्रिरूपा प्रवृत्तिश्च निवृत्तिर्दिनरूपिणी॥
भवतस्तेजसा जाते लोकबंधनहेतवे॥3.4.7.20॥
3.4.m: Dhātṛśarman said: / Both active worldly life and cessation from action are dear to this mind in the body; / active worldly life has the form of night, and cessation from action has the form of day; / they have arisen from your splendor for the purpose of binding the world.

3.4.s:
avyakte tu sthitaṃ tejo bhavato divyasūkṣmakam..
tridhābhūtaṃ tu viśvāya tasmai tejātmane namaḥ .. 21 ..
3.4.d:
अव्यक्ते तु स्थितं तेजो भवतो दिव्यसूक्ष्मकम्॥
त्रिधाभूतं तु विश्वाय तस्मै तेजात्मने नमः ॥ 21 ॥
3.4.m: Your divine and subtle splendor resides in the unmanifest, / yet it has become threefold for the sake of the universe; salutation to that embodiment of splendor.

3.4.s:
rājasī yā smṛtā buddhistatpatirbhagavānvidhiḥ..
bhavatastejasā jātastasmai te vidhaye namaḥ..22..
3.4.d:
राजसी या स्मृता बुद्धिस्तत्पतिर्भगवान्विधिः॥
भवतस्तेजसा जातस्तस्मै ते विधये नमः॥22॥
3.4.m: That intellect which is termed passionate has the venerable Vidhi as its lord; / he was born from your splendor; salutation to you who are that Vidhi.

3.4.s:
sāttvikī yā tanau buddhistatpatirbhagavānhariḥ..
bhavatā nirmitassattvāttasmai te haraye namaḥ .. 23 ..
3.4.d:
सात्त्विकी या तनौ बुद्धिस्तत्पतिर्भगवान्हरिः॥
भवता निर्मितस्सत्त्वात्तस्मै ते हरये नमः ॥ 23 ॥
3.4.m: That intellect which is pure in the body has the venerable Hari as its lord; / he was fashioned by you out of goodness; salutation to you who are that Hari.

3.4.s:
tāmasī mohanā buddhistatpatiśca svayaṃ śivaḥ ..
tamobhūtena bhavatā jātastasmai namonamaḥ ..
dehi me bhagavanmokṣaṃ saṃjñākāṃta namonamaḥ .. 24 ..
3.4.d:
तामसी मोहना बुद्धिस्तत्पतिश्च स्वयं शिवः ॥
तमोभूतेन भवता जातस्तस्मै नमोनमः ॥
देहि मे भगवन्मोक्षं संज्ञाकांत नमोनमः ॥ 24 ॥
3.4.m: The intellect that is dark and delusive has Śiva himself as its lord; / he was born from you who have become darkness; salutations, salutations to him. / Bestow liberation upon me, O Lord! O beloved of Saṃjñā, salutations, salutations!

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
ityevaṃ saṃstutastena bhagavāndhātṛśarmaṇā ..
mahendravacanaṃ prāha taṃ dvijaṃ jñānakovidam .. 25 ..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
इत्येवं संस्तुतस्तेन भगवान्धातृशर्मणा ॥
महेन्द्रवचनं प्राह तं द्विजं ज्ञानकोविदम् ॥ 25 ॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Praised in this manner by Dhātṛśarman, / the venerable one spoke words, O great Indra, to that twice-born who was skilled in knowledge:

3.4.s:
mokṣaścaturvidho vipra sālokyaṃ tapasodbhavam ..
sāmīpyaṃ bhaktito jātaṃ sārūpyaṃ dhyānasaṃbhavam .. .. 26 ..
3.4.d:
मोक्षश्चतुर्विधो विप्र सालोक्यं तपसोद्भवम् ॥
सामीप्यं भक्तितो जातं सारूप्यं ध्यानसंभवम् ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
3.4.m: “Liberation is of four kinds, O brāhmaṇa: dwelling in the same realm arises from ascetic penance; / proximity is born from devotion; having the same form arises from meditation;

3.4.s:
sāyujyaṃ jñānato jñeyaṃ teṣāṃ svāmī paraḥ pumān ..
saguṇo viguṇo jñeya ānando mokṣiṇāṃ kramāt .. 27 ..
3.4.d:
सायुज्यं ज्ञानतो ज्ञेयं तेषां स्वामी परः पुमान् ॥
सगुणो विगुणो ज्ञेय आनन्दो मोक्षिणां क्रमात् ॥ 27 ॥
3.4.m: absorption should be known to come from knowledge; the Supreme Person is the master of these. / Bliss for the liberated is to be known successively as qualified and unqualified.

3.4.s:
devānāṃ caiva deheṣu ye mokṣāḥ punarāgatāḥ ..
yadgatvā na nivartaṃte tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam .. 28 ..
3.4.d:
देवानां चैव देहेषु ये मोक्षाः पुनरागताः ॥
यद्गत्वा न निवर्तंते तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.4.m: Those liberations in the bodies of the gods are subject to return; / that highest abode of Viṣṇu is that from which, having gone, they do not return.

3.4.s:
yatprasannena viprendra sāyujyaṃ me bhavettava ..
manumātraśca yaḥ kālastāvatte mokṣa āsthitaḥ ..
ityuktvāṃtardadhe devastena mokṣīkṛto dvijaḥ .. 29 ..
3.4.d:
यत्प्रसन्नेन विप्रेन्द्र सायुज्यं मे भवेत्तव ॥
मनुमात्रश्च यः कालस्तावत्ते मोक्ष आस्थितः ॥
इत्युक्त्वांतर्दधे देवस्तेन मोक्षीकृतो द्विजः ॥ 29 ॥
3.4.m: Since I am pleased, O best of twice-born, your absorption into me shall occur; / and as long as the duration of a Manu lasts, so long is your liberation established.” / Having spoken thus, the god vanished, and the twice-born was liberated by him.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityuktavaṃtaṃ vāgīśaṃ caitramāse divākaraḥ ..
svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 3.4.7.30 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्तवंतं वागीशं चैत्रमासे दिवाकरः ॥
स्वरूपं दर्शयामास देवदेवः सनातनः ॥ 3.4.7.30 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / While the Lord of Speech was speaking thus in the month of Caitra, the Sun, / the eternal god of gods, showed his own form [saying]:

3.4.s:
śṛṇudhvaṃ sakalā devā yannimitāḥ samāgatāḥ ..
vaṃgīye svāṃśamutpādya devakāryaṃ karomyaham .. 31 ..
3.4.d:
शृणुध्वं सकला देवा यन्निमिताः समागताः ॥
वंगीये स्वांशमुत्पाद्य देवकार्यं करोम्यहम् ॥ 31 ॥
3.4.m: “Listen, all you gods, for whose sake you have gathered! / Having produced a portion of myself in Bengal, I shall accomplish the work of the gods.”

3.4.s:
ityuktvā svamukhāttejaḥ samutpādya divākaraḥ ..
svabhaktāyai sukanyāyai dvijapatnyai dadau hi tat .. 32 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स्वमुखात्तेजः समुत्पाद्य दिवाकरः ॥
स्वभक्तायै सुकन्यायै द्विजपत्न्यै ददौ हि तत् ॥ 32 ॥
3.4.m: Having spoken thus, the Sun, having brought forth splendor from his own mouth, / gave it indeed to his devotee, Sukanyā, the wife of a twice-born.

3.4.s:
dhātṛśarmā dvijo yo vai sūrye mokṣamupāgataḥ ..
sa vai tattejasā jātaḥ kāvyakārasya maṃdire .. 33 ..
3.4.d:
धातृशर्मा द्विजो यो वै सूर्ये मोक्षमुपागतः ॥
स वै तत्तेजसा जातः काव्यकारस्य मंदिरे ॥ 33 ॥
3.4.m: That twice-born Dhātṛśarman who had attained liberation in the Sun / was indeed born from that splendor in the house of a poet.

3.4.s:
īśvaro nāma vikhyātaḥ purīśadvānta ātmavān ..
jitvā viprānvedaparānmahatīṃ kīrtimāptavān..34..
3.4.d:
ईश्वरो नाम विख्यातः पुरीशद्वान्त आत्मवान् ॥
जित्वा विप्रान्वेदपरान्महतीं कीर्तिमाप्तवान्॥34॥
3.4.m: Renowned by the name Īśvara, self-controlled, dispeller of darkness in the city of the Lord, / having defeated brāhmaṇas devoted to the Vedas, he attained great renown.

3.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā jīvanabhāṣitam ..
punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ ramyāṃ devabhyo jīvanirmitām .. 35 ..
3.4.d:
इति ते कथितं विप्र यथा जीवनभाषितम् ॥
पुनः शृणु कथां रम्यां देवभ्यो जीवनिर्मिताम् ॥ 35 ॥
3.4.m: Thus has been related to you, O brāhmaṇa, what was spoken by Jīvana. / Hear again the charming narrative composed by Jīva for the gods.

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca.. ..
māyāvatyāṃ dvijaḥ kaścinmitraśarmeti viśrutaḥ ..
kāvyavidyāparo nityaṃ rasikaḥ kāminīpriyaḥ .. 36 ..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच॥ ॥
मायावत्यां द्विजः कश्चिन्मित्रशर्मेति विश्रुतः ॥
काव्यविद्यापरो नित्यं रसिकः कामिनीप्रियः ॥ 36 ॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / In Māyāvatī, there was a certain twice-born renowned as Mitraśarman, / always devoted to the art of poetry, a connoisseur, fond of passionate women.

3.4.s:
kuṃbharāśiṃ mayi prāpte gaṃgādvāre mahotsavaḥ ..
babhūva bahu lairbhūpeḥ kāritastīrthatatparaiḥ .. 37 ..
3.4.d:
कुंभराशिं मयि प्राप्ते गंगाद्वारे महोत्सवः ॥
बभूव बहु लैर्भूपेः कारितस्तीर्थतत्परैः ॥ 37 ॥
3.4.m: When I arrived in the sign of Kumbha, a great festival at Gaṅgādvāra / was celebrated by many kings devoted to sacred places.

3.4.s:
tatrotsave narā nāryyo bahubhūṣaṇabhūṣitāḥ ..
samāyayurdarśanārthe paramānandanirbharāḥ .. 38 ..
3.4.d:
तत्रोत्सवे नरा नार्य्यो बहुभूषणभूषिताः ॥
समाययुर्दर्शनार्थे परमानन्दनिर्भराः ॥ 38 ॥
3.4.m: At that festival, men and women adorned with many ornaments / came to see it, filled with supreme joy.

3.4.s:
mitraśarmā tu sa prāpya kāmasenasya vai sutām ..
kāvyakelikalāyuktāṃ dvādaśābdamayīṃ śubhām.. 39 ..
3.4.d:
मित्रशर्मा तु स प्राप्य कामसेनस्य वै सुताम् ॥
काव्यकेलिकलायुक्तां द्वादशाब्दमयीं शुभाम्॥ 39 ॥
3.4.m: Then Mitraśarman met the daughter of Kāmasena, / skilled in the arts of poetic play, twelve years of age and auspicious.

3.4.s:
dākṣiṇātyasya bhūpasya tanayāṃ madhurānanām ..
dṛṣṭvā tāṃ mṛgaśāvākṣīṃ tadvaśitvamupāgataḥ .. 3.4.7.40 ..
3.4.d:
दाक्षिणात्यस्य भूपस्य तनयां मधुराननाम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा तां मृगशावाक्षीं तद्वशित्वमुपागतः ॥ 3.4.7.40 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing that fawn-eyed daughter of the southern king, / endowed with a sweet face, he fell under her sway.

3.4.s:
sā tu taṃ citriṇī nāmnā mitraśarmāṇamuttamam ..
dṛṣṭvā tu mūrcchitā cāsīdvipramūrtirhadi sthitā .. 41 ..
3.4.d:
सा तु तं चित्रिणी नाम्ना मित्रशर्माणमुत्तमम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा तु मूर्च्छिता चासीद्विप्रमूर्तिर्हदि स्थिता ॥ 41 ॥
3.4.m: And that [maiden] named Citriṇī, having seen the excellent Mitraśarman, / swooned, and the form of the brahmin remained in her heart.

3.4.s:
svagehaṃ punarāgatya citriṇī bhāskaraṃ prabhum ..
pratyahaṃ pūjayāmāsa bahumānapurassarā .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
स्वगेहं पुनरागत्य चित्रिणी भास्करं प्रभुम् ॥
प्रत्यहं पूजयामास बहुमानपुरस्सरा ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m: Having returned to her home, Citriṇī worshipped the lord Bhāskara / every day, preceded by great reverence.

3.4.s:
mitraśarmā tu tatsthāne gaṃgākūle manohare ..
prātaḥ snātvā śucirbhūtvā vaiśākhe jalamadhyagaḥ .. 43 ..
3.4.d:
मित्रशर्मा तु तत्स्थाने गंगाकूले मनोहरे ॥
प्रातः स्नात्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा वैशाखे जलमध्यगः ॥ 43 ॥
3.4.m: Mitraśarman, however, in that place on the charming bank of the Gaṅgā, / having bathed in the morning and become pure, standing in the water in the month of Vaiśākha,

3.4.s:
stotramādityahṛdayamajapatsūryatatparaḥ ..
pratyahaṃ dvādaśāvartaistoṣayāmāsa bhāskaram .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
स्तोत्रमादित्यहृदयमजपत्सूर्यतत्परः ॥
प्रत्यहं द्वादशावर्तैस्तोषयामास भास्करम् ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m: devoted to the Sun, chanted the Ādityahṛdaya hymn; / with twelve recitations each day, he pleased Bhāskara.

3.4.s:
māsānte bhagavānsūryo dadau tasmai hi taṃ varam ..
sa tu labdhavaro vipraḥ svagehaṃ punarāgataḥ .. 45 ..
3.4.d:
मासान्ते भगवान्सूर्यो ददौ तस्मै हि तं वरम् ॥
स तु लब्धवरो विप्रः स्वगेहं पुनरागतः ॥ 45 ॥
3.4.m: At the end of the month, the blessed Sun granted him that boon; / having obtained the boon, that brahmin returned to his home.

3.4.s:
citriṇī tu varaṃ prāptā vāṃchitaṃ lokabhāskarāt ..
punastau pitarau svapne bhāskareṇa prabodhitau .. 46 ..
3.4.d:
चित्रिणी तु वरं प्राप्ता वांछितं लोकभास्करात् ॥
पुनस्तौ पितरौ स्वप्ने भास्करेण प्रबोधितौ ॥ 46 ॥
3.4.m: Citriṇī, too, obtained her desired boon from the Sun of the worlds; / then both parents were awakened in a dream by Bhāskara.

3.4.s:
mitraśarmāṇamāhūya varayāmāsatuḥ sutām ..
svānte nivāsayāmāsa kāmasenaśca daṃpatī..47..
3.4.d:
मित्रशर्माणमाहूय वरयामासतुः सुताम् ॥
स्वान्ते निवासयामास कामसेनश्च दंपती॥47॥
3.4.m: Having summoned Mitraśarman, they chose him for their daughter; / and Kāmasena made the couple dwell in his own abode.

3.4.s:
tau tu cakraṃ mudāviṣṭau pratyahaṃ sūryadevatam ..
tāmrapātre ca tadyaṃtraṃ lekhayitvā vidhānataḥ .. 48 ..
3.4.d:
तौ तु चक्रं मुदाविष्टौ प्रत्यहं सूर्यदेवतम् ॥
ताम्रपात्रे च तद्यंत्रं लेखयित्वा विधानतः ॥ 48 ॥
3.4.m: Filled with joy, the two of them daily worshipped the sun deity, / having caused his yantra to be inscribed on a copper vessel according to rule.

3.4.s: ījatū raktakusumairvrataṃ kṛtvā ravipriyam .. 49 ..
3.4.d: ईजतू रक्तकुसुमैर्व्रतं कृत्वा रविप्रियम् ॥ 49 ॥
3.4.m: Having undertaken the votive observance dear to the Sun, they worshipped him with red flowers.

3.4.s:
śatābdavapuṣau cobhau nirjarau śramavarjitau ..
ārogyau maraṇaṃ prāpya sāmīpyaṃ ca ravergatau .. 3.4.7.50 ..
3.4.d:
शताब्दवपुषौ चोभौ निर्जरौ श्रमवर्जितौ ॥
आरोग्यौ मरणं प्राप्य सामीप्यं च रवेर्गतौ ॥ 3.4.7.50 ॥
3.4.m: Both, having bodies lasting a hundred years, ageless, free from weariness, / and healthy, met death and went to the proximity of the Sun.

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā ravergāthāṃ vaiśākhyāṃ devarāṭ svayam ..
pratyakṣaṃ bhāskaraṃ devaṃ dadarśa sahitaṃ suraiḥ .. 51 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा रवेर्गाथां वैशाख्यां देवराट् स्वयम् ॥
प्रत्यक्षं भास्करं देवं ददर्श सहितं सुरैः ॥ 51 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard this story of the Sun on the full moon of Vaiśākha, the king of gods himself / directly beheld the divine Bhāskara along with the gods.

3.4.s:
bhaktinamrānsurāndṛṣṭvā bhagavāṃstimirāpahaḥ ..
uvāca vacanaṃ ramyaṃ devakāryaparaṃ śubham ..
mamāṃśāttanayo bhūmau bhaviṣyati surottama .. 52 ..
3.4.d:
भक्तिनम्रान्सुरान्दृष्ट्वा भगवांस्तिमिरापहः ॥
उवाच वचनं रम्यं देवकार्यपरं शुभम् ॥
ममांशात्तनयो भूमौ भविष्यति सुरोत्तम ॥ 52 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing the gods bowed in devotion, the blessed Dispeller of Darkness / spoke these charming, auspicious words dedicated to the gods' work: / “Best of gods, a son will be born on earth from a portion of me.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityuktvā svasya biṃbasya tejorāśiṃ samantataḥ ..
samutpādya kṛtaḥ kāśyāṃ rāmānaṃdastatobhavat .. 53 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्त्वा स्वस्य बिंबस्य तेजोराशिं समन्ततः ॥
समुत्पाद्य कृतः काश्यां रामानंदस्ततोभवत् ॥ 53 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, producing a mass of brilliance from all around his orb / and placing it in Kāśī, Rāmānanda was born from it.

3.4.s:
devalasya ca viprasya kānyakubjasya vai sutaḥ ..
bālyātprabhṛti sa jñānī rāmanāmaparāyaṇaḥ ..
pitrā mātrā parityakto rāghavaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ .. 54 ..
3.4.d:
देवलस्य च विप्रस्य कान्यकुब्जस्य वै सुतः ॥
बाल्यात्प्रभृति स ज्ञानी रामनामपरायणः ॥
पित्रा मात्रा परित्यक्तो राघवं शरणं गतः ॥ 54 ॥
3.4.m: He was the son of a Kanyakubja brahmin named Devala; / a knower of truth from his childhood, devoted to the name of Rāma. / Abandoned by his father and mother, he took refuge in Rāghava.

3.4.s:
tadā tu bhagavānsākṣāccaturdaśakalo hariḥ ..
sītāpatistaddhṛdaye nivāsaṃ kṛtavānmudā .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तु भगवान्साक्षाच्चतुर्दशकलो हरिः ॥
सीतापतिस्तद्धृदये निवासं कृतवान्मुदा ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m: Then indeed the blessed Hari in person, endowed with fourteen digits, / the husband of Sītā, joyfully took up residence in his heart.

3.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ vipra mitradevāṃśato yathā ..
rāmānaṃdastu balavānharibhakteśca saṃbhavaḥ .. 56 ..
3.4.d:
इति ते कथितं विप्र मित्रदेवांशतो यथा ॥
रामानंदस्तु बलवान्हरिभक्तेश्च संभवः ॥ 56 ॥
3.4.m: Thus it has been told to you, O brahmin, how from a portion of the god Mitra / the mighty Rāmānanda was born, and the origin of devotion to Hari.

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
śṛṇu śakra kathāṃ ramyāṃ jyeṣṭhamāsasya vai raveḥ..
aryamā nāma vai vipraḥ purā satyayuge hyabhūt ..
vedavedāṃgatattvajño dharmaśāstraparāyaṇaḥ .. 57 ..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
शृणु शक्र कथां रम्यां ज्येष्ठमासस्य वै रवेः॥
अर्यमा नाम वै विप्रः पुरा सत्ययुगे ह्यभूत् ॥
वेदवेदांगतत्त्वज्ञो धर्मशास्त्रपरायणः ॥ 57 ॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Hear, O Śakra, the charming tale of the Sun in the month of Jyeṣṭha: / Formerly in the Satyayuga there lived a brahmin named Aryaman, / who knew the essence of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas and was devoted to the Dharmaśāstras.

3.4.s:
tasya patnī pitṛmatī śrāddhayajñasya bhūpateḥ ..
tanayā ca mahāsādhvī sapta putrānakalmaṣān ..
aryamṇo janayāmāsa dharmaśāstraparāyaṇan.. 58 ..
3.4.d:
तस्य पत्नी पितृमती श्राद्धयज्ञस्य भूपतेः ॥
तनया च महासाध्वी सप्त पुत्रानकल्मषान् ॥
अर्यम्णो जनयामास धर्मशास्त्रपरायणन्॥ 58 ॥
3.4.m: His wife, Pitṛmatī, the daughter of King Śrāddhayajña, / a very virtuous woman, bore to Aryaman / seven sinless sons devoted to the Dharmaśāstras.

3.4.s:
ekadā sa dvijo dhīmānvicāryya bahudhā hṛdi..
dhanārthī bhāskaraṃ devaṃ tuṣṭāva bahupūjanaiḥ .. 59 ..
3.4.d:
एकदा स द्विजो धीमान्विचार्य्य बहुधा हृदि॥
धनार्थी भास्करं देवं तुष्टाव बहुपूजनैः ॥ 59 ॥
3.4.m: Once, that wise brahmin, having reflected deeply in his heart, / desiring wealth, praised the divine Bhāskara with many acts of worship:

3.4.s:
prabhāte śvetakusumaiścandanādibhirarcanaiḥ ..
madhyāhne raktakusumaiḥ pītapuṣpaiḥ pitṛprasau .. 3.4.7.60 ..
3.4.d:
प्रभाते श्वेतकुसुमैश्चन्दनादिभिरर्चनैः ॥
मध्याह्ने रक्तकुसुमैः पीतपुष्पैः पितृप्रसौ ॥ 3.4.7.60 ॥
3.4.m: at dawn with white flowers and acts of worship like sandalwood paste, / at midday with red flowers, and with yellow flowers in the evening.

3.4.s:
māsamātraṃ tu vidhinā pūjayāmāsa bhāskaram ..
jyeṣṭhe vai bhagavānsūryo dadau tasmai maṇiṃ śubham .. 61 ..
3.4.d:
मासमात्रं तु विधिना पूजयामास भास्करम् ॥
ज्येष्ठे वै भगवान्सूर्यो ददौ तस्मै मणिं शुभम् ॥ 61 ॥
3.4.m: He worshipped Bhāskara according to rule for a whole month; / in Jyeṣṭha, the blessed Sun gave him an auspicious gem.

3.4.s:
tanmaṇeśca prabhāveṇa prasthamātraṃ ca kāṃcanam ..
pratyahaṃ janayāmāsa tena dharmaḥ samarjitaḥ .. 62 ..
3.4.d:
तन्मणेश्च प्रभावेण प्रस्थमात्रं च कांचनम् ॥
प्रत्यहं जनयामास तेन धर्मः समर्जितः ॥ 62 ॥
3.4.m: By the power of that gem, he produced a prastha measure of gold / each day; by means of that, religious merit was amassed.

3.4.s:
vāpīkūpataḍāgānhi tathā harmyāṇi bhūtale ..
kārayāmāsa dharmārthī sūryadevaprasādataḥ .. 63 ..
3.4.d:
वापीकूपतडागान्हि तथा हर्म्याणि भूतले ॥
कारयामास धर्मार्थी सूर्यदेवप्रसादतः ॥ 63 ॥
3.4.m: Desiring religious merit, he caused stepped wells, regular wells, and reservoirs to be made, / as well as mansions on the earth, by the grace of the sun deity.

3.4.s:
sahasrābda vapurbhūtvā nirjaro nirupadravaḥ ..
tyaktvā kalevaraṃ ramyaṃ sūryalokamupāyayau ..
uṣitvā tatra lakṣābdaṃ sūryarūpo babhūva ha .. 64 ..
3.4.d:
सहस्राब्द वपुर्भूत्वा निर्जरो निरुपद्रवः ॥
त्यक्त्वा कलेवरं रम्यं सूर्यलोकमुपाययौ ॥
उषित्वा तत्र लक्षाब्दं सूर्यरूपो बभूव ह ॥ 64 ॥
3.4.m: Having attained a body lasting a thousand years, ageless and free from misfortune, / he abandoned his handsome body and departed for the world of the Sun; / having dwelled there for a hundred thousand years, he assumed the form of the Sun.

3.4.s:
ityevaṃ bhāskarasyaiva māhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ mayā ..
tasmācchakra suraiḥ sārddhaṃ bhaja maṃḍalagaṃ ravim .. 65 ..
3.4.d:
इत्येवं भास्करस्यैव माहात्म्यं कथितं मया ॥
तस्माच्छक्र सुरैः सार्द्धं भज मंडलगं रविम् ॥ 65 ॥
3.4.m: In this way the greatness of Bhāskara has been told by me; / therefore, O Śakra, worship together with the gods the Sun who resides in his orb.

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu te devāḥ padyaiḥ sūryakathā mayaiḥ ..
toṣayāṃcakrire premṇā jyeṣṭhamāsi ravistvasau ..
pratyakṣamabhavattatra devānāha prasannadhīḥ .. 66 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु ते देवाः पद्यैः सूर्यकथा मयैः ॥
तोषयांचक्रिरे प्रेम्णा ज्येष्ठमासि रविस्त्वसौ ॥
प्रत्यक्षमभवत्तत्र देवानाह प्रसन्नधीः ॥ 66 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard this, those gods, with verses consisting of the stories of the Sun, / pleased him with love in the month of Jyeṣṭha; and that Sun / appeared visibly there and, with a pleased mind, spoke to the gods:

3.4.s: sudarśano dvāparānte kṛṣṇājñapto janiṣyati .. 67 ..
3.4.d: सुदर्शनो द्वापरान्ते कृष्णाज्ञप्तो जनिष्यति ॥ 67 ॥
3.4.m: “At the end of the Dvāparayuga, Sudarśana will be born by command of Kṛṣṇa.

3.4.s:
nimbāditya iti khyāto dharmaglāniṃ hariṣyati ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
śṛṇuṣva caritaṃ tasya nimbārkasya mahātmanaḥ .. 68 ..
3.4.d:
निम्बादित्य इति ख्यातो धर्मग्लानिं हरिष्यति ॥
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
शृणुष्व चरितं तस्य निम्बार्कस्य महात्मनः ॥ 68 ॥
3.4.m: Known as Nimbāditya, he will remove the decline of dharma.” / Sūta said: / Hear the deeds of that great-souled Nimbārka,

3.4.s:
yamāha bhagavānkṛṣṇaḥ kuru kāryaṃ mamājñayā ..
merośca dakṣiṇe pārśve narmadāyāstaṭe śubhe .. 69 ..
3.4.d:
यमाह भगवान्कृष्णः कुरु कार्यं ममाज्ञया ॥
मेरोश्च दक्षिणे पार्श्वे नर्मदायास्तटे शुभे ॥ 69 ॥
3.4.m: whom the blessed Kṛṣṇa told: “Perform my work by my command: / on the southern side of Meru, on the auspicious bank of the Narmadā,

3.4.s:
deśe tailaṃgake ramye devarṣivarasevite ..
tatrāvatīrya saddharmānnāradāddevadarśanāt .. 3.4.7.70 ..
3.4.d:
देशे तैलंगके रम्ये देवर्षिवरसेविते ॥
तत्रावतीर्य सद्धर्मान्नारदाद्देवदर्शनात् ॥ 3.4.7.70 ॥
3.4.m: in the charming country of Tailaṅga, frequented by the best divine sages— / descending there, having received the true teachings from Nārada who beholds the gods,

3.4.s:
labdhvā bhūmau vartayasva naṣṭaprāyānmamājñayā ..
māthure naimiṣāraṇye dvāravatyāṃ mamāśrame .. 71 ..
3.4.d:
लब्ध्वा भूमौ वर्तयस्व नष्टप्रायान्ममाज्ञया ॥
माथुरे नैमिषारण्ये द्वारवत्यां ममाश्रमे ॥ 71 ॥
3.4.m: propagate on earth by my command those [teachings] which are nearly lost; / in the region of Mathurā, in Naimiṣāraṇya, in Dvāravatī, in my hermitage,

3.4.s:
sudarśanāśramādau ca sthitiḥ kāryā tvayānagha ..
omityādeśamādāya bhagavāñśrīsudarśanaḥ .. 72 ..
3.4.d:
सुदर्शनाश्रमादौ च स्थितिः कार्या त्वयानघ ॥
ओमित्यादेशमादाय भगवाञ्श्रीसुदर्शनः ॥ 72 ॥
3.4.m: and in the hermitage of Sudarśana and elsewhere, a stay should be made by you, O sinless one.” / Accepting the command saying “Om,” the blessed Śrī Sudarśana,

3.4.s:
bhaktābhīṣṭapradaḥ sākṣādavatīrṇo mahītale ..
deśe tailaṃgake puṇye dvijavaryo mahāmanā .. 73 ..
3.4.d:
भक्ताभीष्टप्रदः साक्षादवतीर्णो महीतले ॥
देशे तैलंगके पुण्ये द्विजवर्यो महामना ॥ 73 ॥
3.4.m: who grants the desires of devotees, descended directly onto the surface of the earth. / In the holy country of Tailaṅga, a noble, high-minded brahmin

3.4.s:
sudarśanāśrame puṇye bhṛguvaṃśasamudbhavaḥ ..
nāmnā''ruṇa iti khyāto vedavedāṃgapāragaḥ .. 74 ..
3.4.d:
सुदर्शनाश्रमे पुण्ये भृगुवंशसमुद्भवः ॥
नाम्ना'ऽरुण इति ख्यातो वेदवेदांगपारगः ॥ 74 ॥
3.4.m: in the holy hermitage of Sudarśana, born in the lineage of Bhṛgu, / famous by the name of Aruṇa, who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

3.4.s:
ṛṣirūpadharaścāsījjayaṃtyā bhāryayā saha ..
samāhitaṃ tena tejo viṣṇucakrasamudbhavam .. 75 ..
3.4.d:
ऋषिरूपधरश्चासीज्जयंत्या भार्यया सह ॥
समाहितं तेन तेजो विष्णुचक्रसमुद्भवम् ॥ 75 ॥
3.4.m: assumed the form of a sage together with his wife Jayantī. / By him was concentrated the brilliance born of Viṣṇu’s discus;

3.4.s:
dadhāra manasā devī jayantī patidevatā ..
tejasā śuśubhe tena candreṇeva diśāmalā .. 76 ..
3.4.d:
दधार मनसा देवी जयन्ती पतिदेवता ॥
तेजसा शुशुभे तेन चन्द्रेणेव दिशामला ॥ 76 ॥
3.4.m: the lady Jayantī, devoted to her husband, held it in her mind; / through that brilliance she shone, like a spotless quarter of the sky with the moon.

3.4.s:
atha sarvaguṇopete kāle paramaśobhane ..
kārttikasya site pakṣe pūrṇimāyāṃ vṛṣe vidhau .. 77 ..
3.4.d:
अथ सर्वगुणोपेते काले परमशोभने ॥
कार्त्तिकस्य सिते पक्षे पूर्णिमायां वृषे विधौ ॥ 77 ॥
3.4.m: Then, at a most splendid time endowed with all virtues, / in the bright fortnight of Kārttika, on the full moon day, with the moon in Taurus,

3.4.s:
kṛttikābhe mahāramye uccasthe grahapaṃ cakre ..
sūryāvasānasamaye meṣalagne niśāmukhe .. 78 ..
3.4.d:
कृत्तिकाभे महारम्ये उच्चस्थे ग्रहपं चक्रे ॥
सूर्यावसानसमये मेषलग्ने निशामुखे ॥ 78 ॥
3.4.m: with Kṛttikā shining, greatly charming, with a group of five planets in exaltation, / at the time of the sun's setting, in the ascendant of Aries, at nightfall,

3.4.s:
jayantyāṃ jayarūpiṇyāṃ jajāna jagadīśvaraḥ ..
yena sarvamidaṃ viśvaṃ vedadharme niyojitam.. .. 79 ..
3.4.d:
जयन्त्यां जयरूपिण्यां जजान जगदीश्वरः ॥
येन सर्वमिदं विश्वं वेदधर्मे नियोजितम्॥ ॥ 79 ॥
3.4.m: During the Jayantī [tithi], the embodiment of victory, the Lord of the universe was born, / by whom this entire universe was directed toward Vedic duty.

3.4.s:
viriñcirekadā tasminnimbārkasyāśrame śubhe ..
samāgatyāha bho brahmanprāpto'haṃ kṣudhayānvitaḥ .. 3.4.7.80 ..
3.4.d:
विरिञ्चिरेकदा तस्मिन्निम्बार्कस्याश्रमे शुभे ॥
समागत्याह भो ब्रह्मन्प्राप्तोऽहं क्षुधयान्वितः ॥ 3.4.7.80 ॥
3.4.m: Once Viriñci came to that auspicious hermitage of Nimbārka, / and having arrived, he said, “O Brahmin, I have arrived afflicted with hunger.

3.4.s:
yāvatsūryaḥ sthito vyomni tāvanmāṃ bhojaya dvija ..
iti śrutvā tathetyuktvā dadau tasmai ca bhojanam .. 81 ..
3.4.d:
यावत्सूर्यः स्थितो व्योम्नि तावन्मां भोजय द्विज ॥
इति श्रुत्वा तथेत्युक्त्वा ददौ तस्मै च भोजनम् ॥ 81 ॥
3.4.m: As long as the sun remains in the sky, feed me, O twice-born!” / Hearing this and saying, “So be it,” he offered him food.

3.4.s:
tadā tu bhagavānsūryo hyastācalamupāgataḥ ..
muninā ṛṣiṇā tena nimba vṛkṣe tadā śubhe .. 82 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तु भगवान्सूर्यो ह्यस्ताचलमुपागतः ॥
मुनिना ऋषिणा तेन निम्ब वृक्षे तदा शुभे ॥ 82 ॥
3.4.m: Just then, the blessed Sun approached the setting mountain. / Then, by that ascetic sage upon an auspicious nimba tree,

3.4.s:
sthāpitaṃ tejasā svena tejastattvaṃ sudarśanam ..
tattejaḥ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā vedhāḥ smayānvitaḥ .. 83 ..
3.4.d:
स्थापितं तेजसा स्वेन तेजस्तत्त्वं सुदर्शनम् ॥
तत्तेजः सूर्यसंकाशं दृष्ट्वा वेधाः स्मयान्वितः ॥ 83 ॥
3.4.m: the principle of light, the Sudarśana, was established through his own splendour. / Beholding that splendour resembling the sun, Brahmā was filled with wonder.

3.4.s:
bhikṣuveṣadharaṃ bālaṃ muniṃ sūryamivāparam ..
nanāma daṃḍavadbhūmau tapasā tasya toṣitaḥ ..84..
3.4.d:
भिक्षुवेषधरं बालं मुनिं सूर्यमिवापरम् ॥
ननाम दंडवद्भूमौ तपसा तस्य तोषितः ॥84॥
3.4.m: Seeing that young sage in the guise of an ascetic, like a second sun, / he bowed flat like a stick upon the ground, pleased by his penance.

3.4.s:
uvāca vacanaṃ ramyaṃ sādhu sādhviti pūjayan..
nimbāditya iti khyāto vasudhāyāṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 85 ..
3.4.d:
उवाच वचनं रम्यं साधु साध्विति पूजयन्॥
निम्बादित्य इति ख्यातो वसुधायां भविष्यसि ॥ 85 ॥
3.4.m: Honouring him, he spoke a charming word: “Well done, well done! / You shall become renowned upon the earth as Nimbāditya.”

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
purā tretāyuge śakra śakraśarmā dvijo hyabhūt .
ayodhyāyāṃ mahābhāgo devapūjanatatparaḥ .. 1 ..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा त्रेतायुगे शक्र शक्रशर्मा द्विजो ह्यभूत् ।
अयोध्यायां महाभागो देवपूजनतत्परः ॥ 1 ॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Formerly, O Śakra, in the Tretāyuga there lived a Brahmin named Śakraśarman / in Ayodhyā, a most fortunate soul devoted to the worship of the gods.

3.4.s:
aśvinau ca tathā rudvānvasūnsūryānpṛthakpṛthak ..
yajurvedamayairmaṃtrairarcayitvā prasannadhīḥ ..
havyaiśca tarpayāmāsa devām̐stānpratyahaṃ dvijaḥ .. 2 ..
3.4.d:
अश्विनौ च तथा रुद्वान्वसून्सूर्यान्पृथक्पृथक् ॥
यजुर्वेदमयैर्मंत्रैरर्चयित्वा प्रसन्नधीः ॥
हव्यैश्च तर्पयामास देवाम्̐स्तान्प्रत्यहं द्विजः ॥ 2 ॥
3.4.m: With a serene mind, having worshipped individually the two Aśvins, the Rudras, / the Vasus, and the Ādityas with mantras composed of the Yajurveda, / that twice-born offered daily satisfaction to those gods with sacrificial offerings.

3.4.s:
tadbhāvatastrayastriṃśaddevāḥ kṣudragaṇairyutāḥ ..
dudurmanorathaṃ tasmai durlabhaṃ sulabhīkṛtam .. 3 .
3.4.d:
तद्भावतस्त्रयस्त्रिंशद्देवाः क्षुद्रगणैर्युताः ॥
दुदुर्मनोरथं तस्मै दुर्लभं सुलभीकृतम् ॥ 3 ।
3.4.m: Because of his devotion, the thirty-three gods accompanied by their minor retinues / granted him his desire, making that which is hard to attain easily accessible.

3.4.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi nirjaro nirupadravaḥ ..
paścātkalevaraṃ tyaktvā paścātsūryo babhūva saḥ .. 4 .
3.4.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि निर्जरो निरुपद्रवः ॥
पश्चात्कलेवरं त्यक्त्वा पश्चात्सूर्यो बभूव सः ॥ 4 ।
3.4.m: For ten thousand years, he lived free of old age and free of calamity. / Afterwards, leaving behind his physical body, he later became the sun.

3.4.s:
lakṣābdaṃ maṇḍale tasminnadhikāraḥ kṛtastataḥ ..
brahmalokaṃ yayau vipraḥ sarvadevaprasādataḥ.. 5..
3.4.d:
लक्षाब्दं मण्डले तस्मिन्नधिकारः कृतस्ततः ॥
ब्रह्मलोकं ययौ विप्रः सर्वदेवप्रसादतः॥ 5॥
3.4.m: After exercising authority in that solar orb for a hundred thousand years, / the Brahmin went to the world of Brahmā through the grace of all the gods.

3.4.s:
aṣṭavarṣasahasrāṇi divyāni padamuttamam ..
vilokya maṃḍale prāptaṃ taṃ sūryaṃ japapūjanaiḥ .. 6..
3.4.d:
अष्टवर्षसहस्राणि दिव्यानि पदमुत्तमम् ॥
विलोक्य मंडले प्राप्तं तं सूर्यं जपपूजनैः ॥ 6॥
3.4.m: Having beheld that supreme station for eight thousand celestial years, / the sun who had attained the orb through his recitations and worship,

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ mahendraḥ surasaṃyutaḥ ..
āṣāḍhe bhāskaraṃ devaṃ pūjayāmāsa namradhīḥ .. 7 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं महेन्द्रः सुरसंयुतः ॥
आषाढे भास्करं देवं पूजयामास नम्रधीः ॥ 7 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing this speech, Mahendra, accompanied by the gods, / worshipped the divine Sun in the month of Āṣāḍha with a humble mind.

3.4.s:
āṣāḍhapūrṇimāyāṃ ca sa devo jagatītale..
pratyakṣamagamattatra surānāha śṛṇuṣva tat ..8..
3.4.d:
आषाढपूर्णिमायां च स देवो जगतीतले॥
प्रत्यक्षमगमत्तत्र सुरानाह शृणुष्व तत् ॥8॥
3.4.m: And on the full moon day of Āṣāḍha, that god manifested visibly / upon the earth there and spoke to the gods; hear that:

3.4.s:
vṛndāvane mahāramye janayiṣye kalau bhaye ..
sa dvijaḥ sūryarūpaśca devakāryaṃ kariṣyati .. 9 ..
3.4.d:
वृन्दावने महारम्ये जनयिष्ये कलौ भये ॥
स द्विजः सूर्यरूपश्च देवकार्यं करिष्यति ॥ 9 ॥
3.4.m: “In the dreadful Kali age, I shall be born in the exceedingly lovely Vṛndāvana. / As that Brahmin endowed with the form of the sun, I shall perform the work of the gods.

3.4.s:
mādhavasya dvijasyaiva tanayaḥ sa bhaviṣyati ..
madhurnāma mahābhāgo vedamārgaparāyaṇaḥ ..3.4.8.10..
3.4.d:
माधवस्य द्विजस्यैव तनयः स भविष्यति ॥
मधुर्नाम महाभागो वेदमार्गपरायणः ॥3.4.8.10॥
3.4.m: He shall be born as the son of the Brahmin Mādhava, / the highly fortunate one named Madhu, devoted to the Vedic path.”

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityuktvā bhagavānsūryo devakāryārthamudyataḥ..
svāṃgāttu teja utpādya vṛṃdāvanamapre(pe?)ṣayat .. 11..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्सूर्यो देवकार्यार्थमुद्यतः॥
स्वांगात्तु तेज उत्पाद्य वृंदावनमप्रे(पे?)षयत् ॥ 11॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the blessed Sun, intent upon accomplishing the purpose of the gods, / produced a splendour from his own body and dispatched it to Vṛndāvana.

3.4.s:
vimukhānmadhurālāpairvaśīkṛtya samantataḥ ..
tebhyaśca vaiṣṇavīṃ śaktiṃ pradadau bhuktimuktidām .
madhvācārya iti khyātaḥ prasiddho'bhūnmahītale... 12..
3.4.d:
विमुखान्मधुरालापैर्वशीकृत्य समन्ततः ॥
तेभ्यश्च वैष्णवीं शक्तिं प्रददौ भुक्तिमुक्तिदाम् ।
मध्वाचार्य इति ख्यातः प्रसिद्धोऽभून्महीतले॥। 12॥
3.4.m: Winning over the averse from all sides with sweet discourses, / he bestowed upon them the Vaiṣṇava power that grants worldly enjoyment and liberation. / He became celebrated and renowned upon the earth as Madhvācārya.

3.4.s:
jīva uvāca .. ..
dvāpare ca dvijaśreṣṭho meghaśarmā babhūva ha ..
jñānavānmatimāndharmī vedamārgaparāyaṇaḥ.. 13..
3.4.d:
जीव उवाच ॥ ॥
द्वापरे च द्विजश्रेष्ठो मेघशर्मा बभूव ह ॥
ज्ञानवान्मतिमान्धर्मी वेदमार्गपरायणः॥ 13॥
3.4.m: Jīva said: / And in the Dvāparayuga, there was an excellent Brahmin named Meghaśarman, / knowledgeable, wise, righteous, and devoted to the Vedic path.

3.4.s:
kṛṣikṛtyaparo nityaṃ taddhanaiśca daśāṃśakaiḥ ..
pratyahaṃ sakalāndevānarcayāmāsa bhaktimān ..14..
3.4.d:
कृषिकृत्यपरो नित्यं तद्धनैश्च दशांशकैः ॥
प्रत्यहं सकलान्देवानर्चयामास भक्तिमान् ॥14॥
3.4.m: Ever devoted to agriculture, and with one tenth of his wealth derived from it, / the devout man daily worshipped all the gods.

3.4.s:
ekadā pañcavarṣābde śantanau ca mahīpatau ..
saṃprāpte tasya vai deśe hyanāvṛṣṭirbabhūva ha..15..
3.4.d:
एकदा पञ्चवर्षाब्दे शन्तनौ च महीपतौ ॥
संप्राप्ते तस्य वै देशे ह्यनावृष्टिर्बभूव ह॥15॥
3.4.m: Once, in the fifth year of the reign of King Śantanu, / when drought befell his country,

3.4.s:
krośamātraṃ hi tatkṣetraṃ parjanyenaiva secitam ..
dhānyānāṃ droṇamānaśca bhāvo'bhūdekamudrayā..16..
3.4.d:
क्रोशमात्रं हि तत्क्षेत्रं पर्जन्येनैव सेचितम् ॥
धान्यानां द्रोणमानश्च भावोऽभूदेकमुद्रया॥16॥
3.4.m: his field alone, measuring just one krosa, was watered by the rain-cloud. / The price of grains rose to one droṇa for a single coin.

3.4.s:
meghaśarmā tadā tatra dhanadhānyayuto'bhavat.
anye tu pīḍitā lokā rājānaṃ śaraṇa yayuḥ..17..
3.4.d:
मेघशर्मा तदा तत्र धनधान्ययुतोऽभवत्।
अन्ये तु पीडिता लोका राजानं शरण ययुः॥17॥
3.4.m: Meghaśarman was then endowed with wealth and grain, / while other people, afflicted, took refuge with the king.

3.4.s:
tadā tu duḥkhito rājā meghaśarmāṇamāhvayat ..
dvijaśreṣṭha namastubhyaṃ gururbhava mama priyaḥ .. 18 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तु दुःखितो राजा मेघशर्माणमाह्वयत् ॥
द्विजश्रेष्ठ नमस्तुभ्यं गुरुर्भव मम प्रियः ॥ 18 ॥
3.4.m: Then the king, sorrowful, summoned Meghaśarman: / “Homage to you, O best of Brahmins! Become my dear guru.

3.4.s: anāvṛṣṭiryathā na syāttathā vipra samādiśa ..19..
3.4.d: अनावृष्टिर्यथा न स्यात्तथा विप्र समादिश ॥19॥
3.4.m: Instruct me, O Brahmin, so that there may be no drought.”

3.4.s:
ityevaṃvādinaṃ bhūpaṃ meghaśarmā vaco'bravīt ..
śrāvaṇe māsi saṃprāpte viprānvedaparāyaṇān.. 3.4.8.20..
3.4.d:
इत्येवंवादिनं भूपं मेघशर्मा वचोऽब्रवीत् ॥
श्रावणे मासि संप्राप्ते विप्रान्वेदपरायणान्॥ 3.4.8.20॥
3.4.m: To the king who spoke thus, Meghaśarman replied: / “When the month of Śrāvaṇa arrives, summon twelve Brahmins devoted to the Veda,

3.4.s:
dvādaśaiva samāhūya lakṣamātraṃ raveḥ svayam..
jāpayitvā sumanasā pūrṇimāyāṃ tu tadvratī ..
sūryamantrāhutīrvahnau taddaśāṃśaṃ hi taddvijaiḥ .. 21 ..
3.4.d:
द्वादशैव समाहूय लक्षमात्रं रवेः स्वयम्॥
जापयित्वा सुमनसा पूर्णिमायां तु तद्व्रती ॥
सूर्यमन्त्राहुतीर्वह्नौ तद्दशांशं हि तद्द्विजैः ॥ 21 ॥
3.4.m: and having caused a hundred thousand [mantras] of the Sun to be recited with a devoted mind, / observing that vow on the full moon day, having oblations of the solar mantra poured into the sacred fire / to one-tenth of that number by those Brahmins,

3.4.s:
kārayitvā vidhānena kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhī bhava ..
iti śrutvā tathā kṛtvā bhojayāmāsa vedagān..22..
3.4.d:
कारयित्वा विधानेन कृतकृत्यः सुखी भव ॥
इति श्रुत्वा तथा कृत्वा भोजयामास वेदगान्॥22॥
3.4.m: in accordance with ritual injunctions, you will attain your desire and be happy.” / Hearing this, having acted accordingly, he fed the knowers of the Veda.

3.4.s:
prasannastu tadā sūryaḥ parjanyātmā samantataḥ..
bhūmimācchādya sa diśaṃ prabhurvṛṣṭimakārayat..23..
3.4.d:
प्रसन्नस्तु तदा सूर्यः पर्जन्यात्मा समन्ततः॥
भूमिमाच्छाद्य स दिशं प्रभुर्वृष्टिमकारयत्॥23॥
3.4.m: Pleased then, the Sun, the embodiment of the rain-cloud, / having covered the earth and the directions from all sides, the Lord caused rain to fall.

3.4.s:
śantanustu tadā rājā sūryavrataparāyaṇaḥ ..
tadvratena mahāpuṇyo babhūva nṛpasattamaḥ .. 24..
3.4.d:
शन्तनुस्तु तदा राजा सूर्यव्रतपरायणः ॥
तद्व्रतेन महापुण्यो बभूव नृपसत्तमः ॥ 24॥
3.4.m: King Śantanu was then devoted to the vow of the Sun; / by means of that vow, the best of kings became exceedingly meritorious.

3.4.s:
yaṃ yaṃ kareṇa spṛśati vṛddho bhavati vai yuvā ..
sūryadevaprabhāvena meghaśarmā tathā hyabhūt.. 25 ..
3.4.d:
यं यं करेण स्पृशति वृद्धो भवति वै युवा ॥
सूर्यदेवप्रभावेन मेघशर्मा तथा ह्यभूत्॥ 25 ॥
3.4.m: Whomever [the king] touched with his hand, an old man would become a youth; / and by the power of the Sun god, Meghaśarman likewise became thus.

3.4.s:
sa vai paṃcaśatāyuśca nirjaro nirupadravaḥ ..
tyaktvā prāṇānravirbhūtvā sūryalokamupāgamat..
lakṣābda bhuvamāsādya brahmalokaṃ gamiṣyati ..26..
3.4.d:
स वै पंचशतायुश्च निर्जरो निरुपद्रवः ॥
त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्रविर्भूत्वा सूर्यलोकमुपागमत्॥
लक्षाब्द भुवमासाद्य ब्रह्मलोकं गमिष्यति ॥26॥
3.4.m: Living for five hundred years, free from old age and calamities, / he abandoned his life-breaths and, becoming the sun, went to the world of the Sun. / Having reached the earth for a hundred thousand years, he will go to the world of Brahmā.

3.4.s:
ityevaṃvādinaṃ jīvaṃ parjanyo bhagavānraviḥ ..
svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa prayāgaṃ prati cāgataḥ .. 27 ..
3.4.d:
इत्येवंवादिनं जीवं पर्जन्यो भगवान्रविः ॥
स्वरूपं दर्शयामास प्रयागं प्रति चागतः ॥ 27 ॥
3.4.m: To Jīva speaking thus, the blessed Sun, the rain-cloud, / revealed his true form and came toward Prayāga.

3.4.s:
murā nāha prasannātmā mleccharājye kalau yuge ..
vṛndāvane samāgamya devakāryaṃ karomyaham .. 28 ..
3.4.d:
मुरा नाह प्रसन्नात्मा म्लेच्छराज्ये कलौ युगे ॥
वृन्दावने समागम्य देवकार्यं करोम्यहम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.4.m: Graciously, he said: “In the Kali age, during the reign of the mlecchas, / I shall arrive in Vṛndāvana and perform the work of the gods.”

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityuktvā bhagavānsūryo gatvā vṛndāvanaṃ śubham ..
śrīdharo nāma vikhyātaḥ putrobhūdvedaśarmaṇaḥ .. 29 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्सूर्यो गत्वा वृन्दावनं शुभम् ॥
श्रीधरो नाम विख्यातः पुत्रोभूद्वेदशर्मणः ॥ 29 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the blessed Sun went to auspicious Vṛndāvana, / and became the son of Vedaśarman, renowned by the name Śrīdhara.

3.4.s:
śrīmadbhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ samālokya viśāradaḥ ..
cakāra viduṣāmarthe pradīptaṃ śrīdharaḥ śubham ..
śrīmadbhāgavataṃ śāstraṃ purāṇopari tatkṛtam .. 3.4.8.30 ..
3.4.d:
श्रीमद्भागवतं शास्त्रं समालोक्य विशारदः ॥
चकार विदुषामर्थे प्रदीप्तं श्रीधरः शुभम् ॥
श्रीमद्भागवतं शास्त्रं पुराणोपरि तत्कृतम् ॥ 3.4.8.30 ॥
3.4.m: Having examined the scripture Śrīmad Bhāgavata, the learned Śrīdhara / composed an illuminating and auspicious [commentary] for the sake of the wise; / it was composed upon that Purāṇa, the scripture Śrīmad Bhāgavata.

3.4.s:
.. jīva uvāca .. ..
purā kalau yuge prāpte prāṃśuśarmā dvijo'bhavat..
vedaśāstraparo nityaṃ devatātithipūjakaḥ .. 31 ..
3.4.d:
॥ जीव उवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा कलौ युगे प्राप्ते प्रांशुशर्मा द्विजोऽभवत्॥
वेदशास्त्रपरो नित्यं देवतातिथिपूजकः ॥ 31 ॥
3.4.m: Jīva said: / Formerly, when the Kali age had arrived, there was a Brahmin named Prāṃśuśarman, / ever devoted to the Vedic scriptures, a worshipper of the deities and guests,

3.4.s:
satyavādī mahāsādhuḥ steyahiṃsāvivarjitaḥ ..
bhikṣāvṛttiparo nityaṃ putradāraprapoṣakaḥ .. 32 ..
3.4.d:
सत्यवादी महासाधुः स्तेयहिंसाविवर्जितः ॥
भिक्षावृत्तिपरो नित्यं पुत्रदारप्रपोषकः ॥ 32 ॥
3.4.m: truth-speaking, a great saint, free from theft and violence, / ever devoted to a livelihood of begging, providing for his sons and wife.

3.4.s:
ekadā pathi bhikṣārthaṃ gacchatastasya bhūpateḥ ..
māyākṛtyakaro dhūrtaḥ kalistatrākṣigocaraḥ .. 33 ..
3.4.d:
एकदा पथि भिक्षार्थं गच्छतस्तस्य भूपतेः ॥
मायाकृत्यकरो धूर्तः कलिस्तत्राक्षिगोचरः ॥ 33 ॥
3.4.m: Once, as he was walking along the path seeking alms, O king, / the rogue Kali, who works with deceit, appeared before his eyes.

3.4.s:
babhūva vāṭikāṃ kṛtvā kalirdānamanoharām ..
tamuvāca dvijo bhūtvā prāṃśuśarmanvacaḥ śṛṇu .. 34 ..
3.4.d:
बभूव वाटिकां कृत्वा कलिर्दानमनोहराम् ॥
तमुवाच द्विजो भूत्वा प्रांशुशर्मन्वचः शृणु ॥ 34 ॥
3.4.m: Creating a garden charming with gifts, Kali waited; / becoming a twice-born, he spoke to him: “Hear my words, Prāṃśuśarman!

3.4.s:
mameyaṃ vāṭikā ramyā tatra gaccha sukhī bhava ..
iti vipravacaḥ śrutvā vāṭikāṃ tāṃ samāgataḥ .. 35 ..
3.4.d:
ममेयं वाटिका रम्या तत्र गच्छ सुखी भव ॥
इति विप्रवचः श्रुत्वा वाटिकां तां समागतः ॥ 35 ॥
3.4.m: This delightful garden is mine; go there and be happy.” / Hearing the twice-born’s words, he entered that garden.

3.4.s:
kalistu vāṭikāmadhye gatvā ramyaphalāni ca ..
troṭayitvā dadau tasmai bhojanārthaṃ mahākhalaḥ .. 36 ..
3.4.d:
कलिस्तु वाटिकामध्ये गत्वा रम्यफलानि च ॥
त्रोटयित्वा ददौ तस्मै भोजनार्थं महाखलः ॥ 36 ॥
3.4.m: Going into the midst of the garden and plucking lovely fruits, / Kali, the great villain, gave them to him for food.

3.4.s:
prāṃjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā prāṃśuśarmāṇamabravīt ..
bhuṃkṣva vipra mayā sārddhaṃ kaliṃdasya phalaṃ śubham .. 37 ..
3.4.d:
प्रांजलिः प्रणतो भूत्वा प्रांशुशर्माणमब्रवीत् ॥
भुंक्ष्व विप्र मया सार्द्धं कलिंदस्य फलं शुभम् ॥ 37 ॥
3.4.m: Folding his hands and bowing low, he said to Prāṃśuśarman: / “Eat together with me, O twice-born, the auspicious fruit of the watermelon.”

3.4.s:
ityuktaḥ sa tu taṃ prāha vihasya madhura svaram ..
vṛkṣe bibhītake caiva kaliṃdasya phale tathā ..
kaliḥ prāptaḥ smṛtaḥ prājñaistasmādgṛhṇāmyahaṃ na hi .. 38 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तः स तु तं प्राह विहस्य मधुर स्वरम् ॥
वृक्षे बिभीतके चैव कलिंदस्य फले तथा ॥
कलिः प्राप्तः स्मृतः प्राज्ञैस्तस्माद्गृह्णाम्यहं न हि ॥ 38 ॥
3.4.m: Thus addressed, he laughed and said in a sweet voice: / “In the bibhītaka tree and in the fruit of the watermelon, / Kali is present, as declared by the wise; therefore I do not accept it.

3.4.s:
yadi dattaṃ phalaṃ bhaktyā tvayādya dvijasevinā ..
śālagrāmāya vai dattvā prasādaṃ tadbhajāmyaham ..
śālagrāmaḥ svayaṃ brahma saccidānandavigrahaḥ .. 39 ..
3.4.d:
यदि दत्तं फलं भक्त्या त्वयाद्य द्विजसेविना ॥
शालग्रामाय वै दत्त्वा प्रसादं तद्भजाम्यहम् ॥
शालग्रामः स्वयं ब्रह्म सच्चिदानन्दविग्रहः ॥ 39 ॥
3.4.m: If the fruit was given with devotion by you who serve the twice-born today, / having offered it to the Śālagrāma, I shall partake of it as prasāda. / The Śālagrāma is Brahman Himself, the embodiment of being, consciousness, and bliss.

3.4.s:
darśanāttasya cābhakṣyo bhakṣyo bhavati niścitaḥ ..
iti śrutvā kalistatra lajjito'bhūnnirāśakaḥ ..
dvijastu tatphalaṃ gṛhya bhūmigrāmamupāyayau ..3.4.8.40..
3.4.d:
दर्शनात्तस्य चाभक्ष्यो भक्ष्यो भवति निश्चितः ॥
इति श्रुत्वा कलिस्तत्र लज्जितोऽभून्निराशकः ॥
द्विजस्तु तत्फलं गृह्य भूमिग्राममुपाययौ ॥3.4.8.40॥
3.4.m: From seeing it, even the inedible becomes certainly edible.” / Hearing this, Kali became ashamed and despondent there; / but the twice-born took that fruit and approached Bhūmigrāma.

3.4.s:
nṛpatistatra cāgatya dvijamāha prasannadhīḥ ..
kiṃ gṛhītaṃ tvayā vipra darśayāśu priyaṃ kuru .. 41 ..
3.4.d:
नृपतिस्तत्र चागत्य द्विजमाह प्रसन्नधीः ॥
किं गृहीतं त्वया विप्र दर्शयाशु प्रियं कुरु ॥ 41 ॥
3.4.m: The king arrived there and spoke to the twice-born with a pleased mind: / “What have you received, O twice-born? Show it at once and do what is pleasing.”

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā prāṃśuśarmā tatphalaṃ vatsamuṃḍavat ..
gṛhītvā pradadau rājñe vismito dvijasattamaḥ .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा प्रांशुशर्मा तत्फलं वत्समुंडवत् ॥
गृहीत्वा प्रददौ राज्ञे विस्मितो द्विजसत्तमः ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing this, Prāṃśuśarman took that fruit, which resembled a calf’s severed head, / and gave it to the king, astonished, best of the twice-born.

3.4.s:
tadā tu sa kalirbhūpastaṃ vipraṃ tāḍya vetasaiḥ ..
kārāgāre lohamaye kṛtavānnyāyamitrakaḥ .. .. 43 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तु स कलिर्भूपस्तं विप्रं ताड्य वेतसैः ॥
कारागारे लोहमये कृतवान्न्यायमित्रकः ॥ ॥ 43 ॥
3.4.m: Then that Kali, as the king, having beaten that twice-born with cane-rods, / the friend of injustice put him into an iron prison.

3.4.s:
prātaḥkāle ravau prāpte prāṃśuśarmā suduḥkhitaḥ ..
tuṣṭāva bhāskaraṃ devaṃ stotrairṛgvedasaṃbhavaiḥ .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
प्रातःकाले रवौ प्राप्ते प्रांशुशर्मा सुदुःखितः ॥
तुष्टाव भास्करं देवं स्तोत्रैरृग्वेदसंभवैः ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m: In the morning, when the sun had risen, Prāṃśuśarman, deeply grieved, / praised the divine Bhāskara with hymns originating from the Ṛgveda.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavānraviḥ sākṣātsanātanaḥ ..
viprasya karṇayorvākyamuvāca nabhaseritam .. 45 ..
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्रविः साक्षात्सनातनः ॥
विप्रस्य कर्णयोर्वाक्यमुवाच नभसेरितम् ॥ 45 ॥
3.4.m: Then the blessed eternal Sun, directly present, was pleased, / and spoke words uttered from the sky into the twice-born’s ears:

3.4.s:
śṛṇu vipra mahābhāga kālarūpo hariḥ svayam ..
caturyugaṃ tena kṛtaṃ viśvapālādihetave .. 46 ..
3.4.d:
शृणु विप्र महाभाग कालरूपो हरिः स्वयम् ॥
चतुर्युगं तेन कृतं विश्वपालादिहेतवे ॥ 46 ॥
3.4.m: “Hear, O highly fortunate twice-born! Hari Himself is Time incarnate. / The four yugas were created by Him for the protection of the universe and other purposes.

3.4.s:
kalirviśvasamūhānāṃ mṛtyave racitastathā ..
ato ghore kalau prāpte viṣṇumāyāvinirmitam ..
kaliñjaraṃ ca nagaraṃ tatroṣya mudito bhava .. 47 ..
3.4.d:
कलिर्विश्वसमूहानां मृत्यवे रचितस्तथा ॥
अतो घोरे कलौ प्राप्ते विष्णुमायाविनिर्मितम् ॥
कलिञ्जरं च नगरं तत्रोष्य मुदितो भव ॥ 47 ॥
3.4.m: Kali was likewise fashioned for the destruction of the hosts of the universe. / Therefore, now that terrible Kali has arrived, reside in the city of Kaliñjara / fashioned by the Māyā of Viṣṇu, and be joyful there.”

3.4.s:
ityuktvā rakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā tasya viprasya bhāskaraḥ ..
kaliñjare ca nagare preṣayāmāsa taṃ dvijam .. .. 48 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा रक्षणं कृत्वा तस्य विप्रस्य भास्करः ॥
कलिञ्जरे च नगरे प्रेषयामास तं द्विजम् ॥ ॥ 48 ॥
3.4.m: Having spoken thus and protected that twice-born, Bhāskara / dispatched that twice-born to the city of Kaliñjara.

3.4.s:
sapādaśatavarṣaṃ ca dvijastatra vasanravim ..
ārādhya putrapatnīko ravilokamupāyayau .. 49 ..
3.4.d:
सपादशतवर्षं च द्विजस्तत्र वसन्रविम् ॥
आराध्य पुत्रपत्नीको रविलोकमुपाययौ ॥ 49 ॥
3.4.m: Dwelling there for a hundred and twenty-five years, / worshipping the Sun, the twice-born went with his sons and wife to the realm of the Sun.

3.4.s:
sa vai bhādrapade māsi sūryo bhūtvāyutābdakam..
paścādbrahmapuraṃ prāpya paramānandamāptavān ..
iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā jīvastamabravīt .. 3.4.8.50 ..
3.4.d:
स वै भाद्रपदे मासि सूर्यो भूत्वायुताब्दकम्॥
पश्चाद्ब्रह्मपुरं प्राप्य परमानन्दमाप्तवान् ॥
इति ते कथितं विप्र यथा जीवस्तमब्रवीत् ॥ 3.4.8.50 ॥
3.4.m: Having become the Sun for ten thousand years in the month of Bhādrapada, / he later reached the city of Brahmā and attained supreme bliss. / Thus has been related to you, O twice-born, as Jīva spoke to him.

3.4.s:
āgatya bhāskaro devaḥ pūrṇimāyāṃ tu bhādrake ..
aṣṭāviṃśe kalau prāpte svayaṃ jātaḥ kaliñjare .. 51 ..
3.4.d:
आगत्य भास्करो देवः पूर्णिमायां तु भाद्रके ॥
अष्टाविंशे कलौ प्राप्ते स्वयं जातः कलिञ्जरे ॥ 51 ॥
3.4.m: The divine Bhāskara, arriving on the full-moon day in Bhādra, / was Himself born in Kaliñjara when the twenty-eighth Kali arrived,

3.4.s:
śivadattasya tanayo viṣṇuśarmeti viśrutaḥ ..
vedaśāstrakalābhijño vaiṣṇavo deva pūjakaḥ .. 52 ..
3.4.d:
शिवदत्तस्य तनयो विष्णुशर्मेति विश्रुतः ॥
वेदशास्त्रकलाभिज्ञो वैष्णवो देव पूजकः ॥ 52 ॥
3.4.m: as the son of Śivadatta, renowned as Viṣṇuśarman, / knowledgeable in the Vedas, śāstras, and arts, a Vaiṣṇava worshipper of the gods.

3.4.s:
caturvarṇānnarānvipra samāhūya harergṛhe ..
vacanaṃ prāha dharmātmā viṣṇuḥ sarveśvaro hariḥ .. 53 ..
3.4.d:
चतुर्वर्णान्नरान्विप्र समाहूय हरेर्गृहे ॥
वचनं प्राह धर्मात्मा विष्णुः सर्वेश्वरो हरिः ॥ 53 ॥
3.4.m: Summoning men of the four varṇas to the house of Hari, O twice-born, / the righteous one spoke these words: “Viṣṇu, Hari, is the Lord of all.

3.4.s:
śṛṇu tatkāraṇaṃ śiṣya viśvakāraṇa kārakaḥ ..
bhagavānsaccidānandaścaturviśatitattvavān ..
devānsasarja lokārthe tasmātsarveśvaro'bhavat .. 54 ..
3.4.d:
शृणु तत्कारणं शिष्य विश्वकारण कारकः ॥
भगवान्सच्चिदानन्दश्चतुर्विशतितत्त्ववान् ॥
देवान्ससर्ज लोकार्थे तस्मात्सर्वेश्वरोऽभवत् ॥ 54 ॥
3.4.m: Hear the cause of that, O disciple: the Maker, the cause of the universe, / the Blessed One, being, consciousness, and bliss, possessing the twenty-four tattvas, / created the gods for the sake of the worlds; therefore He became the Lord of all.

3.4.s:
pūrvaṃ hi sakalāndevānpūjayitvā naraḥ śuciḥ ..
paścācca pūjayedviṣṇuṃ yathā bhṛtyā nṛpaṃ punaḥ .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
पूर्वं हि सकलान्देवान्पूजयित्वा नरः शुचिः ॥
पश्चाच्च पूजयेद्विष्णुं यथा भृत्या नृपं पुनः ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m: Having first worshipped all the gods, a pure man / should afterwards worship Viṣṇu, just as servants [honour ministers before] the king.”

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu te sarve praśasya bahudhā hi tam ..
viṣṇusvāmīti taṃ nāmnā kathāṃ cakruśca harṣitāḥ ..56..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु ते सर्वे प्रशस्य बहुधा हि तम् ॥
विष्णुस्वामीति तं नाम्ना कथां चक्रुश्च हर्षिताः ॥56॥
3.4.m: Hearing this, they all praised him in many ways, / and, delighted, referred to him by the name Viṣṇusvāmin.

3.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ vipra viṣṇusvāmī yathābhavat ..
punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ ramyāṃ bṛhaspatimukheritām ..57..
3.4.d:
इति ते कथितं विप्र विष्णुस्वामी यथाभवत् ॥
पुनः शृणु कथां रम्यां बृहस्पतिमुखेरिताम् ॥57॥
3.4.m: Thus it has been related to you, O twice-born, how he became Viṣṇusvāmin. / Listen again to the delightful narrative uttered from the mouth of Bṛhaspati.

3.4.s:
.. jīva uvāca .. ..
purā caitrarathe deśe bhagaśarmā dvijo'bhavat ..
svarveśyā maṃjughoṣāyāṃ munimedhāvinā bhuvi .. 58 ..
3.4.d:
॥ जीव उवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा चैत्ररथे देशे भगशर्मा द्विजोऽभवत् ॥
स्वर्वेश्या मंजुघोषायां मुनिमेधाविना भुवि ॥ 58 ॥
3.4.m: Jīva said: / Formerly, in the Caitraratha region, there was a twice-born named Bhagaśarman, / born on earth through the sage Medhāvin from the celestial courtesan Mañjughoṣā.

3.4.s:
pitṛmātṛparityaktaḥ sa bālaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ ..
sūryamārādhayāmāsa tapasā śatavārṣikam .. 99 ..
3.4.d:
पितृमातृपरित्यक्तः स बालः श्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
सूर्यमाराधयामास तपसा शतवार्षिकम् ॥ 99 ॥
3.4.m: Abandoned by his parents, that boy, endowed with faith, / propitiated the Sun with ascetic penance for a hundred years.

3.4.s:
sūryamaṇḍalamadhyasthā sāvitrī nāma devatā ..
sarvasūryasya jananī kanyā tanmaṇḍalasya vai .. 3.4.8.60..
3.4.d:
सूर्यमण्डलमध्यस्था सावित्री नाम देवता ॥
सर्वसूर्यस्य जननी कन्या तन्मण्डलस्य वै ॥ 3.4.8.60॥
3.4.m: The deity named Sāvitrī, abiding in the midst of the Sun's orb, / the mother of all the suns, the maiden of that orb,

3.4.s:
prasannā tapasā tasya prādurbhūtā sanātanī ..
āśvine māsi rājānaṃ dvijaṃ cakre ca maṇḍale .. 61 ..
3.4.d:
प्रसन्ना तपसा तस्य प्रादुर्भूता सनातनी ॥
आश्विने मासि राजानं द्विजं चक्रे च मण्डले ॥ 61 ॥
3.4.m: pleased by his penance, that eternal goddess manifested Herself / and made the twice-born a king in the orb in the month of Āśvina.

3.4.s:
lakṣavarṣasahasrāṇi māsi māsi tathāśvine ..
prakāśaṃ kṛtavānvipraḥ pūjito lokavāsibhiḥ .. 62 ..
3.4.d:
लक्षवर्षसहस्राणि मासि मासि तथाश्विने ॥
प्रकाशं कृतवान्विप्रः पूजितो लोकवासिभिः ॥ 62 ॥
3.4.m: For a hundred thousand years, month after month in Āśvina, / the twice-born shone forth, worshipped by the inhabitants of the worlds.

3.4.s:
tvaṃ sūryaṃ bhaja devendra sa te kāryaṃ kariṣyati ..
iti śrutvāśvine māsi sa ravirdevapūjanāt .. 63 ..
3.4.d:
त्वं सूर्यं भज देवेन्द्र स ते कार्यं करिष्यति ॥
इति श्रुत्वाश्विने मासि स रविर्देवपूजनात् ॥ 63 ॥
3.4.m: “Worship the Sun, O lord of the gods; he will accomplish your purpose.” / Hearing this, in the month of Āśvina, through the worship of the gods, that Sun

3.4.s:
pratyakṣamagamattatra vacaḥ prāha surānprati ..
kānyakubje śubhe deśe vāṇībhūṣaṇa ityaham ..
bhavāmi satyadevasya viprasya tanayaḥ śubhaḥ .. 64 ..
3.4.d:
प्रत्यक्षमगमत्तत्र वचः प्राह सुरान्प्रति ॥
कान्यकुब्जे शुभे देशे वाणीभूषण इत्यहम् ॥
भवामि सत्यदेवस्य विप्रस्य तनयः शुभः ॥ 64 ॥
