3.4.m: became visible there and spoke words to the gods: / “In the auspicious land of Kānyakubja, I shall become / the auspicious son of the twice-born Satyadeva, named Vāṇībhūṣaṇa.”

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityuktvā bhagavānsūryo jātaḥ kānyapure śubhe ..
jitvā pākhaṃḍino viprānmāṃsabhakṣaṇatatparān ..
chaṃdograṃthaṃ svanāmnā vai kṛtavāndaivatapriyaḥ .. 65 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्सूर्यो जातः कान्यपुरे शुभे ॥
जित्वा पाखंडिनो विप्रान्मांसभक्षणतत्परान् ॥
छंदोग्रंथं स्वनाम्ना वै कृतवान्दैवतप्रियः ॥ 65 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the blessed Sun was born in the auspicious city of Kānya. / Having defeated the heretical twice-born devoted to eating meat, / he, beloved of the gods, composed a work on meter under his own name.

3.4.s:
matsyamāṃsāśanā viprā mṛgameṣājakāśanāḥ ..
ekībhūya samāgamya cakruḥ śāstrārthamulbaṇam ..66..
3.4.d:
मत्स्यमांसाशना विप्रा मृगमेषाजकाशनाः ॥
एकीभूय समागम्य चक्रुः शास्त्रार्थमुल्बणम् ॥66॥
3.4.m: The twice-born who ate fish and meat, who ate deer, sheep, and goats, / gathered together as one and engaged in a fierce scriptural debate.

3.4.s:
kalinā'dharmamitreṇa rakṣitāste dvijātayaḥ ..
taṃ dvijaṃ ca parājitya matsyaketuṃ ca tadgṛhe .. 67 ..
3.4.d:
कलिनाऽधर्ममित्रेण रक्षितास्ते द्विजातयः ॥
तं द्विजं च पराजित्य मत्स्यकेतुं च तद्गृहे ॥ 67 ॥
3.4.m: Those twice-born were protected by Kali, the friend of unrighteousness; / and having defeated that twice-born, they forcefully set up

3.4.s:
balācca staṃbhanaṃ cakrustadā viṣṇupriyo dvijaḥ ..
vaiṣṇavīṃ śaktimāgamya svamukhānmīnakhāditān .. 68 ..
3.4.d:
बलाच्च स्तंभनं चक्रुस्तदा विष्णुप्रियो द्विजः ॥
वैष्णवीं शक्तिमागम्य स्वमुखान्मीनखादितान् ॥ 68 ॥
3.4.m: a fish-banner in his house by paralytic power. Then the twice-born, beloved of Viṣṇu, / resorting to the Vaiṣṇava power, from his own mouth

3.4.s:
saṃjīvya darśayāmāsa te dṛṣṭvā vismitāstadā ..
śiṣyabhūtāśca te tasya vaiṣṇavaṃ matamā gaman .. 69 ..
3.4.d:
संजीव्य दर्शयामास ते दृष्ट्वा विस्मितास्तदा ॥
शिष्यभूताश्च ते तस्य वैष्णवं मतमा गमन् ॥ 69 ॥
3.4.m: revived the fish that had been eaten and displayed them. Seeing them, they were astonished; / becoming his disciples, they adopted the Vaiṣṇava doctrine.

3.4.s:
.. jīva uvāca .. ..
kadācitsarayūtīre devayājī dvijo'bhavat ..
sarvadevaparo nityaṃ vedapāṭhaparāyaṇaḥ .. 3.4.8.70 ..
3.4.d:
॥ जीव उवाच ॥ ॥
कदाचित्सरयूतीरे देवयाजी द्विजोऽभवत् ॥
सर्वदेवपरो नित्यं वेदपाठपरायणः ॥ 3.4.8.70 ॥
3.4.m: Jīva said: / Once, on the bank of the Sarayū, there was a twice-born named Devayājin, / always devoted to all the gods, dedicated to the recitation of the Vedas.

3.4.s:
tatsutastu mṛtiṃ prāpto janmamātre hi dāruṇe ..
tadā tu sa dvijaḥ śrutvā sūryadevamatoṣayat .. 71 ..
3.4.d:
तत्सुतस्तु मृतिं प्राप्तो जन्ममात्रे हि दारुणे ॥
तदा तु स द्विजः श्रुत्वा सूर्यदेवमतोषयत् ॥ 71 ॥
3.4.m: His son met his death immediately upon his dreadful birth. / Then that twice-born, hearing this, propitiated the Sun god.

3.4.s:
jijīva tatprasādena vivasvānnāma cābhavat ..
ṣoḍaśābda vapurbhūtvā sarvavidyāviśāradaḥ .. 72 ..
3.4.d:
जिजीव तत्प्रसादेन विवस्वान्नाम चाभवत् ॥
षोडशाब्द वपुर्भूत्वा सर्वविद्याविशारदः ॥ 72 ॥
3.4.m: By his grace he lived, and his name became Vivasvat. / Having attained a sixteen-year-old body, skilled in all sciences,

3.4.s:
apatyavāndharmaparaḥ sūryavataparāyaṇaḥ ..
śivarātridine prāpte tatpatnī bhūṣaṇapriyā .. 73 ..
3.4.d:
अपत्यवान्धर्मपरः सूर्यवतपरायणः ॥
शिवरात्रिदिने प्राप्ते तत्पत्नी भूषणप्रिया ॥ 73 ॥
3.4.m: blessed with offspring, devoted to righteousness, intent on the Sun's vrata, / when the day of Śivarātri arrived, his wife, who loved ornaments,

3.4.s:
suśīlā nāma vikhyātā patisevārthamāgatā ..
sa vratī rudradevasya dṛṣṭvā tāṃ madhurānanām .. 74 ..
3.4.d:
सुशीला नाम विख्याता पतिसेवार्थमागता ॥
स व्रती रुद्रदेवस्य दृष्ट्वा तां मधुराननाम् ॥ 74 ॥
3.4.m: renowned by the name Suśīlā, she came to attend upon her husband. / Observing the vow of the god Rudra, he saw her of sweet countenance,

3.4.s:
balādgṛhītvā tu niśi bubhuje smaravihvalaḥ ..
maithunasyaiva doṣeṇa tasya kuṣṭho mahānabhūt .. 75 ..
3.4.d:
बलाद्गृहीत्वा तु निशि बुभुजे स्मरविह्वलः ॥
मैथुनस्यैव दोषेण तस्य कुष्ठो महानभूत् ॥ 75 ॥
3.4.m: and, seized by passion, took her by force at night and enjoyed her. / From the very sin of that intercourse, a severe leprosy afflicted him,

3.4.s:
liṃgedriyaṃ ca patitaṃ gudabhraṣṭo mahāṃgaruk ..
kena cidupadeśena ravivārasya vai vratam .. 76 ..
3.4.d:
लिंगेद्रियं च पतितं गुदभ्रष्टो महांगरुक् ॥
केन चिदुपदेशेन रविवारस्य वै व्रतम् ॥ 76 ॥
3.4.m: his organ of generation fell off, his rectum collapsed, and he suffered great bodily pain. / Then, through some advice, he undertook the observance of Sunday;

3.4.s:
sa cakre dvādaśaṃ premṇā nirāhāro yatendriyaḥ ..
tena vrataprabhāveṇa sarvapīḍā layaṃ gatāḥ .. 77 ..
3.4.d:
स चक्रे द्वादशं प्रेम्णा निराहारो यतेन्द्रियः ॥
तेन व्रतप्रभावेण सर्वपीडा लयं गताः ॥ 77 ॥
3.4.m: subduing his senses, he lovingly observed the twelfth [day] fasting. / By the power of that observance, all his afflictions dissolved.

3.4.s:
tadā śraddhā ravau prāptā pratyahaṃ sa dvijottamaḥ ..
āditya hṛdayaṃ japtvā kāmarūpo dvijo'bhavat .. 78 ..
3.4.d:
तदा श्रद्धा रवौ प्राप्ता प्रत्यहं स द्विजोत्तमः ॥
आदित्य हृदयं जप्त्वा कामरूपो द्विजोऽभवत् ॥ 78 ॥
3.4.m: He then gained faith in the sun; daily reciting the Ādityahṛdaya, / that best of twice-born became endowed with a form assumed at will.

3.4.s:
nārībhirbhartsitaḥ pūrvaṃ sotha kāminīyācitaḥ ..
brahmacaryavrataṃ kṛtvā brahmadhyānaparo'bhavat .. 79 ..
3.4.d:
नारीभिर्भर्त्सितः पूर्वं सोथ कामिनीयाचितः ॥
ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतं कृत्वा ब्रह्मध्यानपरोऽभवत् ॥ 79 ॥
3.4.m: Formerly reviled by women, he was now solicited by passionate maidens. / Undertaking the vow of celibacy, he devoted himself to meditation on brahman.

3.4.s:
śatāyurbrāhmaṇo bhūtvā jñānavānrogavarjitaḥ ..
tyaktvā prāṇānravirbhūtvā sūryamaṇḍalamadhyagāt .. 3.4.8.80 ..
3.4.d:
शतायुर्ब्राह्मणो भूत्वा ज्ञानवान्रोगवर्जितः ॥
त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्रविर्भूत्वा सूर्यमण्डलमध्यगात् ॥ 3.4.8.80 ॥
3.4.m: Living as a centenarian brāhmaṇa, endowed with knowledge and free from disease, / he relinquished his vital breaths, became the sun, and entered the midst of the solar orb.

3.4.s:
kārtike māsi lakṣābdaṃ prakāśaṃ kṛtavānnabhaḥ ..
taṃ ca sūryaṃ mahendrastvaṃ pūjayāśu suraiḥ saha .. 81 ..
3.4.d:
कार्तिके मासि लक्षाब्दं प्रकाशं कृतवान्नभः ॥
तं च सूर्यं महेन्द्रस्त्वं पूजयाशु सुरैः सह ॥ 81 ॥
3.4.m: For a hundred thousand years in the month of Kārtika, he illumined the sky. / You too, O Mahendra, together with the gods, quickly worship that sun.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā mahendrastu māsamātraṃ hi bhāskaram ..
pūjayitvā vidhānena pūrṇimāyāṃ dadarśa ha .. 82 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा महेन्द्रस्तु मासमात्रं हि भास्करम् ॥
पूजयित्वा विधानेन पूर्णिमायां ददर्श ह ॥ 82 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this, Mahendra worshipped the sun for just one month / according to rule, and beheld him on the full moon day.

3.4.s:
uvāca śakraṃ sa ravirdevakāryaṃ karomyaham ..
bhaṭṭairvidyāmayairdhūrtaiḥ sūtrapāṭhaśca khaṃḍitaḥ .. 83 ..
3.4.d:
उवाच शक्रं स रविर्देवकार्यं करोम्यहम् ॥
भट्टैर्विद्यामयैर्धूर्तैः सूत्रपाठश्च खंडितः ॥ 83 ॥
3.4.m: The sun said to Śakra: "I am carrying out the work of the gods. / The recitation of the sūtras has been corrupted by rascally scholars pretending to learning;

3.4.s:
dhātupāṭho nyapaṭhito bhraṃśārthaḥ svaravarṇakaḥ ..
jitvā tānbhaṭṭapāṣaṃḍānvedamuddhārayāmi bhoḥ .. 84 ..
3.4.d:
धातुपाठो न्यपठितो भ्रंशार्थः स्वरवर्णकः ॥
जित्वा तान्भट्टपाषंडान्वेदमुद्धारयामि भोः ॥ 84 ॥
3.4.m: the recitation of the roots has been misread, with their accents and letters distorted in meaning. / Conquering those heretic scholars, I shall redeem the Veda, O King!"

3.4.s:
ityuktvā sa gataḥ kāśyāṃ gehe vai vedaśarmaṇaḥ ..
dīkṣitānvayabhūtasya nāmnā kāryaguṇo'bhavat .. 85 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स गतः काश्यां गेहे वै वेदशर्मणः ॥
दीक्षितान्वयभूतस्य नाम्ना कार्यगुणोऽभवत् ॥ 85 ॥
3.4.m: Having spoken thus, he went to Kāśī, to the house of Vedaśarman, / born of the lineage of Dīkṣita, and became known by the name Kāryaguṇa.

3.4.s:
dvādaśābdavapurbhūtvā sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ ..
śivamārādhayāmāsa viśvanāthaṃ śivāpriyam .. 86 ..
3.4.d:
द्वादशाब्दवपुर्भूत्वा सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ॥
शिवमाराधयामास विश्वनाथं शिवाप्रियम् ॥ 86 ॥
3.4.m: At the age of twelve years, versed in all the treatises, / he worshipped Śiva, Viśvanātha, dear to Śivā.

3.4.s:
trivarṣānte ca bhagavāṃstasmai jñānaṃ mahaddadau ..
tasya jñānaprabhāveṇa vyaktamavyaktamuttamam .. 87 ..
3.4.d:
त्रिवर्षान्ते च भगवांस्तस्मै ज्ञानं महद्ददौ ॥
तस्य ज्ञानप्रभावेण व्यक्तमव्यक्तमुत्तमम् ॥ 87 ॥
3.4.m: At the end of three years, the Lord gave him supreme knowledge. / By the power of that knowledge, the highest manifested and unmanifested

3.4.s:
jñātaṃ kāryaguṇenaiva dīkṣitena tadā hṛdi ..
avyakte yadā buddhiḥ sā vidyā dvādaśāṃginī .. 88 ..
3.4.d:
ज्ञातं कार्यगुणेनैव दीक्षितेन तदा हृदि ॥
अव्यक्ते यदा बुद्धिः सा विद्या द्वादशांगिनी ॥ 88 ॥
3.4.m: was understood in his heart by Kāryaguṇa Dīkṣita himself. / When the intellect is fixed on the unmanifest, that is the twelve-limbed knowledge;

3.4.s:
vyakte'haṃkārabhūte ca buddhirjñeyā budhairajā ..
avidyā nāma vikhyātā ṣoḍaśāṃgasvarūpiṇī .. 89 ..
3.4.d:
व्यक्तेऽहंकारभूते च बुद्धिर्ज्ञेया बुधैरजा ॥
अविद्या नाम विख्याता षोडशांगस्वरूपिणी ॥ 89 ॥
3.4.m: and when the intellect is fixed on the manifest, which consists of the ego, the wise should know it as unborn [matter], / renowned by the name Avidyā, whose nature possesses sixteen limbs.

3.4.s:
avyaktaṃ tu paraṃ brahma vyaktaṃ śabdamayaṃ smṛtam ..
ahaṃkāro lokakaro hi vyakto'ṣṭadaśāṃgakaḥ ..3.4.8.90..
3.4.d:
अव्यक्तं तु परं ब्रह्म व्यक्तं शब्दमयं स्मृतम् ॥
अहंकारो लोककरो हि व्यक्तोऽष्टदशांगकः ॥3.4.8.90॥
3.4.m: The unmanifest is regarded as the supreme brahman, and the manifest is regarded as consisting of sound. / The ego is the creator of the world, manifested indeed with eighteen limbs.

3.4.s:
vṛṣarūpadharo mukhyo nandiyānaḥ smṛto budhaiḥ ..
śṛṅgāṇi tasya catvāri tripādo dviśirā vṛṣaḥ..91..
3.4.d:
वृषरूपधरो मुख्यो नन्दियानः स्मृतो बुधैः ॥
शृङ्गाणि तस्य चत्वारि त्रिपादो द्विशिरा वृषः॥91॥
3.4.m: Taking the form of a bull, he is the foremost, celebrated by the wise as the mount Nandin. / Four are his horns, three his feet, and two his heads, this bull;

3.4.s:
saptahastastridhā baddho nityaśuddho mukhe sthitaḥ..
suvantaśca tiṅantaśca kṛdaṃtaścāvyayastathā..92..
3.4.d:
सप्तहस्तस्त्रिधा बद्धो नित्यशुद्धो मुखे स्थितः॥
सुवन्तश्च तिङन्तश्च कृदंतश्चाव्ययस्तथा॥92॥
3.4.m: he has seven hands, is tied in three places, eternally pure, seated in the mouth: / nominal inflections, verbal inflections, primary suffixes, and likewise indeclinables.

3.4.s:
dvaudvau śṛṃgau ca śirasornaṃdiyānasya vai smṛtau ..
bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavaccaiva trayaḥ pādā hi tasya vai .. 93 ..
3.4.d:
द्वौद्वौ शृंगौ च शिरसोर्नंदियानस्य वै स्मृतौ ॥
भूतं भव्यं भवच्चैव त्रयः पादा हि तस्य वै ॥ 93 ॥
3.4.m: Two horns each on his two heads are recorded for the mount Nandin; / the past, the future, and the present are his three feet.

3.4.s:
rūḍhiśca yogarūḍhiśca śabdau tasya śirodvayam ..
kartā karma ca karaṇaṃ saṃpradānaṃ vibhāgataḥ .. 94 ..
3.4.d:
रूढिश्च योगरूढिश्च शब्दौ तस्य शिरोद्वयम् ॥
कर्ता कर्म च करणं संप्रदानं विभागतः ॥ 94 ॥
3.4.m: Conventional usage and etymological-conventional usage are the two words that are his two heads; / the agent, the object, the instrument, and the recipient in their division,

3.4.s:
saṃvaṃdhaścādhikāraśca bhujāstasya vṛṣasya vai ..
vākyaṃ svarānvitaṃ jñeyaṃ vibhattyaṃtaṃ padaṃ smṛtam .. 95 ..
3.4.d:
संवंधश्चाधिकारश्च भुजास्तस्य वृषस्य वै ॥
वाक्यं स्वरान्वितं ज्ञेयं विभत्त्यंतं पदं स्मृतम् ॥ 95 ॥
3.4.m: relation, and domain are the arms of that bull. / A sentence should be known as endowed with accents, and a word is remembered as ending with an inflectional suffix.

3.4.s:
tābhyāṃ baddhaśca sa vṛṣo nandiyānātha te namaḥ ..
tasyoparisthitaṃ nityamavyaktaṃ liṃgarūpi yat .. 96 ..
3.4.d:
ताभ्यां बद्धश्च स वृषो नन्दियानाथ ते नमः ॥
तस्योपरिस्थितं नित्यमव्यक्तं लिंगरूपि यत् ॥ 96 ॥
3.4.m: Bound by these two is that bull; homage to you, O mount Nandin! / Situated eternally above him is the unmanifest, which takes the form of the liṅga.

3.4.s:
jātaśca vṛṣaliṃgābhyāṃ so'haṃkāro hariḥ svayam..
nārāyaṇaḥ ṣoḍaśātmā bahumūrtiramūrtikaḥ .. 97 ..
3.4.d:
जातश्च वृषलिंगाभ्यां सोऽहंकारो हरिः स्वयम्॥
नारायणः षोडशात्मा बहुमूर्तिरमूर्तिकः ॥ 97 ॥
3.4.m: And born from the bull and the liṅga is that ego, Hari himself, / Nārāyaṇa possessing sixteen aspects, multiform and formless.

3.4.s:
iti jñānaṃ hṛdi prāpya tadā siddhāntakaumudīm ..
jitvā bhaṭṭāṃścakārāśu bhaṭṭojiḥ praśruto'bhavat ..98..
3.4.d:
इति ज्ञानं हृदि प्राप्य तदा सिद्धान्तकौमुदीम् ॥
जित्वा भट्टांश्चकाराशु भट्टोजिः प्रश्रुतोऽभवत् ॥98॥
3.4.m: Attaining such knowledge in his heart, he then quickly composed the Siddhāntakaumudī / after defeating the Bhaṭṭas, and became renowned as Bhaṭṭoji.

3.4.s:
.. jīva uvāca .. ..
purā kāṃcīpure ramye gaṇako brāhmaṇottamaḥ..
purodhāḥ satyadattasya rājño vedaparasya vai .. 99 ..
3.4.d:
॥ जीव उवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा कांचीपुरे रम्ये गणको ब्राह्मणोत्तमः॥
पुरोधाः सत्यदत्तस्य राज्ञो वेदपरस्य वै ॥ 99 ॥
3.4.m: Jīva said: / Formerly in lovely Kāñcīpura there was an astrologer, an excellent brāhmaṇa, / the royal priest of King Satyadatta, who was devoted to the Vedas.

3.4.s:
ekadā gaṇako dhīmānsatyadattamuvāca ha ..
muhūrto'bhijidākhyoyaṃ puṣyanakṣatrasaṃyutaḥ ..
hāṭaṃ kuru mahārāja sāṃprataṃ bahuvṛttidam .. 3.4.8.100 ..
3.4.d:
एकदा गणको धीमान्सत्यदत्तमुवाच ह ॥
मुहूर्तोऽभिजिदाख्योयं पुष्यनक्षत्रसंयुतः ॥
हाटं कुरु महाराज सांप्रतं बहुवृत्तिदम् ॥ 3.4.8.100 ॥
3.4.m: Once the wise astrologer said to Satyadatta: / "This moment is named Abhijit, combined with the constellation Puṣya. / Establish a marketplace now, O great king; it will yield abundant livelihood."

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tathā kṛtvā ḍiṃḍimadhvaninā pure ..
narānājñāpayāmāsa tacchṛṇuṣva surottama .. 101 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तथा कृत्वा डिंडिमध्वनिना पुरे ॥
नरानाज्ञापयामास तच्छृणुष्व सुरोत्तम ॥ 101 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing this, he acted accordingly and, by the beating of drums in the city, / gave an order to the people; listen to that, O best of gods:

3.4.s:
akrītaṃ yasya vai vastu hāṭe'sminvaiśyakovidaiḥ ..
mayā krītaṃ ca tajjñeyaṃ satyametadvaco mama .. 102 ..
3.4.d:
अक्रीतं यस्य वै वस्तु हाटेऽस्मिन्वैश्यकोविदैः ॥
मया क्रीतं च तज्ज्ञेयं सत्यमेतद्वचो मम ॥ 102 ॥
3.4.m: "Whatever item is left unbought in this marketplace by the skilled vaiśyas / shall be known as bought by me; this word of mine is true."

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā śūdrajanāścakrurnānāvidhaṃ vasu ..
vaiśyaissarvaṃ tadā krītaṃ mahānhāṭo hi so'bhavat .. 103 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा शूद्रजनाश्चक्रुर्नानाविधं वसु ॥
वैश्यैस्सर्वं तदा क्रीतं महान्हाटो हि सोऽभवत् ॥ 103 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing this, the śūdra people produced various kinds of goods; / the vaiśyas then bought everything, and it became a great market.

3.4.s:
ekadā lohakāraśca dāridraṃ loharūpiṇam ..
kṛtvā hāṭamupāgamya śatamudrāmayācata .. 104 ..
3.4.d:
एकदा लोहकारश्च दारिद्रं लोहरूपिणम् ॥
कृत्वा हाटमुपागम्य शतमुद्रामयाचत ॥ 104 ॥
3.4.m: One day, a blacksmith made [an image of] Poverty in the form of iron / and, coming to the market, asked for a hundred coins.

3.4.s:
akrītaṃ puruṣaṃ rājā jñātvā lohadaridrakam ..
krītaṃ taṃ śatamudrābhirgṛhītvā gehamāgamat ..
kośāgāre tadā rājñā sthāpitobhūddaridrakaḥ .. 105 ..
3.4.d:
अक्रीतं पुरुषं राजा ज्ञात्वा लोहदरिद्रकम् ॥
क्रीतं तं शतमुद्राभिर्गृहीत्वा गेहमागमत् ॥
कोशागारे तदा राज्ञा स्थापितोभूद्दरिद्रकः ॥ 105 ॥
3.4.m: Learning of that person, the iron Poverty, remaining unbought, the king / purchased it for a hundred coins, took it, and returned home. / The king then deposited Poverty in his treasury.

3.4.s:
niśīthe tama udbhūte karma dharmaśca mā tathā ..
bhūpagehātsamāgatya paśyatastasya nirgatāḥ .. 106 ..
3.4.d:
निशीथे तम उद्भूते कर्म धर्मश्च मा तथा ॥
भूपगेहात्समागत्य पश्यतस्तस्य निर्गताः ॥ 106 ॥
3.4.m: At midnight, when darkness arose, Action and Duty, and likewise Fortune, / came forth from the king's palace and departed before his eyes.

3.4.s:
tatpaścātsatyapuruṣo rājānamidamabravīt ..
daridro yatra bhūpāla tatra karmaparo na hi ..
karmaṇā rahito dharmo bhūtale na sthiro bhavet .. 107 ..
3.4.d:
तत्पश्चात्सत्यपुरुषो राजानमिदमब्रवीत् ॥
दरिद्रो यत्र भूपाल तत्र कर्मपरो न हि ॥
कर्मणा रहितो धर्मो भूतले न स्थिरो भवेत् ॥ 107 ॥
3.4.m: After that, the embodiment of Truth spoke thus to the king: / "Where Poverty is, O protector of the earth, there is no one devoted to action; / and duty devoid of action cannot stand firm upon the earth.

3.4.s:
dharmeṇa rahitā lakṣmīrna śobheta kadācana ..
ahaṃ lakṣmyā vihīnaśca na tiṣṭhāmi kadācana .. 108 ..
3.4.d:
धर्मेण रहिता लक्ष्मीर्न शोभेत कदाचन ॥
अहं लक्ष्म्या विहीनश्च न तिष्ठामि कदाचन ॥ 108 ॥
3.4.m: Lakṣmī bereft of duty never shines; / and I, separated from Lakṣmī, never remain."

3.4.s:
ityuktvā gantumicchaṃtaṃ gṛhītvā karayornṛpaḥ ..
namrībhūto vacaḥ prāha śṛṇu satyaṃ mama priyam .. 109 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा गन्तुमिच्छंतं गृहीत्वा करयोर्नृपः ॥
नम्रीभूतो वचः प्राह शृणु सत्यं मम प्रियम् ॥ 109 ॥
3.4.m: As he spoke thus and wished to depart, the king grasped him by the hands, / bowed low, and spoke these words: "Hear, O Truth, my beloved:

3.4.s:
na tyājyo hi mayā deva bhavānkiṅgantumarhati ..
iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ satyadevo gṛhegamat .. 3.4.8.110 ..
3.4.d:
न त्याज्यो हि मया देव भवान्किङ्गन्तुमर्हति ॥
इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं सत्यदेवो गृहेगमत् ॥ 3.4.8.110 ॥
3.4.m: You must not be abandoned by me, O lord! Why should you depart?" / Hearing these words, the god of Truth entered his house.

3.4.s:
tatpaścācca svayaṃ lakṣmīstadgehe gaṃtumudyatā ..
tāmāha bhūpatirdhīro devi tvaṃ caṃcalā sadā .. 111 ..
3.4.d:
तत्पश्चाच्च स्वयं लक्ष्मीस्तद्गेहे गंतुमुद्यता ॥
तामाह भूपतिर्धीरो देवि त्वं चंचला सदा ॥ 111 ॥
3.4.m: Thereafter, Lakṣmī herself prepared to depart from his house. / To her the steadfast king said: "O goddess, you are ever fickle;

3.4.s:
acalā bhava bho mātastarhi manmadiraṃ vraja ..
iti śrutvā varaṃ dattvā nṛpagehaṃ yayau tadā .. 112 ..
3.4.d:
अचला भव भो मातस्तर्हि मन्मदिरं व्रज ॥
इति श्रुत्वा वरं दत्त्वा नृपगेहं ययौ तदा ॥ 112 ॥
3.4.m: become firm, O mother! Then enter my dwelling." / Hearing this and granting the boon, she then entered the king's house.

3.4.s:
purodhasaṃ taṃ gaṇakaṃ samāhūya nṛpottamaḥ ..
lakṣasvarṇaṃ dadau tasmai kathitvā sarvakāraṇam .. 113 ..
3.4.d:
पुरोधसं तं गणकं समाहूय नृपोत्तमः ॥
लक्षस्वर्णं ददौ तस्मै कथित्वा सर्वकारणम् ॥ 113 ॥
3.4.m: Summoning that astrologer priest, the best of kings / gave him a hundred thousand gold pieces, having related the whole reason.

3.4.s:
putrajanmani kāle tu saṃprāptaṃ tena vai dhanam ..
vyayaṃ kṛtvā dhanaṃ sarvaṃ poṣayāmāsa bālakam .. 114 ..
3.4.d:
पुत्रजन्मनि काले तु संप्राप्तं तेन वै धनम् ॥
व्ययं कृत्वा धनं सर्वं पोषयामास बालकम् ॥ 114 ॥
3.4.m: At the time of the birth of a son, that wealth was received by him; / spending all that wealth, he nourished the boy.

3.4.s:
pūṣā nāma tato jātaṃ mārgaśīrṣe śubhe dine ..
sa tu sūryaṃ samārādhya jyotiḥśāstraparaḥ sutaḥ .. 115 ..
3.4.d:
पूषा नाम ततो जातं मार्गशीर्षे शुभे दिने ॥
स तु सूर्यं समाराध्य ज्योतिःशास्त्रपरः सुतः ॥ 115 ॥
3.4.m: Then, on an auspicious day in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, he was named Pūṣan. / Worshipping the sun, that son became devoted to the science of astronomy.

3.4.s:
sūrye tu mokṣamagamaddevadevaprasādataḥ ..
tasmāttvaṃ mārgamāse vai raviṃ devendra pūjaya ..116..
3.4.d:
सूर्ये तु मोक्षमगमद्देवदेवप्रसादतः ॥
तस्मात्त्वं मार्गमासे वै रविं देवेन्द्र पूजय ॥116॥
3.4.m: [He] attained liberation in the sun by the grace of the God of gods. / Therefore, O Devendra, worship the sun in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
devendrapūjanātsūryassamāgamya tadā svayam ..
pūṣā nāma vaco devānuvāca madhurasvaram ..117..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
देवेन्द्रपूजनात्सूर्यस्समागम्य तदा स्वयम् ॥
पूषा नाम वचो देवानुवाच मधुरस्वरम् ॥117॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Then, because of Devendra's worship, the sun, called Pūṣan, / having come there in person, spoke sweet words to the gods:

3.4.s:
ujjayinyāmahaṃ devā yāsye rudrapaśorgṛhe ..
nāmnā ca mihirācāryo jyotiśśāstrapravarttakaḥ .. 118 ..
3.4.d:
उज्जयिन्यामहं देवा यास्ये रुद्रपशोर्गृहे ॥
नाम्ना च मिहिराचार्यो ज्योतिश्शास्त्रप्रवर्त्तकः ॥ 118 ॥
3.4.m: "O gods, I shall go to Ujjayinī to the house of Rudrapaśu / by the name of Mihirācārya, promulgator of the science of astronomy."

3.4.s:
ityuktvā bhagavānpūṣā putro jāto dvijasya vai ..
mūlagaḍāntaviṣaye'bhijidyoge śubhaṃkare .. 119 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्पूषा पुत्रो जातो द्विजस्य वै ॥
मूलगडान्तविषयेऽभिजिद्योगे शुभंकरे ॥ 119 ॥
3.4.m: Having said this, the blessed Pūṣan was indeed born as the son of the twice-born / in the region of the Mūla-gaṇḍānta under the auspicious Abhijit conjunction.

3.4.s:
jātamātraṃ ca taṃ putraṃ pitā kāṣṭhakaṭāhake ..
dhṛtvā kṣiptvā nadīmadhye niśīthe samavāhayat .. 3.4.8.120 ..
3.4.d:
जातमात्रं च तं पुत्रं पिता काष्ठकटाहके ॥
धृत्वा क्षिप्त्वा नदीमध्ये निशीथे समवाहयत् ॥ 3.4.8.120 ॥
3.4.m: And as soon as his son was born, the father placed him in a wooden vessel, / threw it into the middle of a river, and let it float away at midnight.

3.4.s:
samudramagamatputro rākṣasībhiśca rakṣitaḥ ..
laṃkāmāgamya tatraiva jyotiḥśāstramadhīta vān.. 121 ..
3.4.d:
समुद्रमगमत्पुत्रो राक्षसीभिश्च रक्षितः ॥
लंकामागम्य तत्रैव ज्योतिःशास्त्रमधीत वान्॥ 121 ॥
3.4.m: The son went to the ocean, protected by rākṣasīs; / reaching Laṅkā, right there he studied the science of astronomy.

3.4.s:
jātakaṃ phalitaṃ caiva mūkapraśnaṃ tathāditaḥ ..
paṭhitvā rākṣaseṃdraṃ ca vibhīṣaṇamupāgatam .. 122 ..
3.4.d:
जातकं फलितं चैव मूकप्रश्नं तथादितः ॥
पठित्वा राक्षसेंद्रं च विभीषणमुपागतम् ॥ 122 ॥
3.4.m: Having studied horoscopy, predictive [astrology], and silent questioning from the beginning, / he approached Vibhīṣaṇa, the king of the rākṣasas [who had] come [there]:

3.4.s:
bhaktarāja namastubhyaṃ vibhīṣaṇa hari priya ..
āhṛto rākṣasībhiśca tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ .. 123 ..
3.4.d:
भक्तराज नमस्तुभ्यं विभीषण हरि प्रिय ॥
आहृतो राक्षसीभिश्च त्वामहं शरणं गतः ॥ 123 ॥
3.4.m: "King of devotees, homage to you, Vibhīṣaṇa, dear to Hari! / Brought by rākṣasīs, I have come to you for refuge."

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā ca sa nṛpo vaiṣṇavaṃ dvijamuttamam ..
matvā saṃpreṣayāmasa yatra tajjanmabhūmikā .. 124 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा च स नृपो वैष्णवं द्विजमुत्तमम् ॥
मत्वा संप्रेषयामस यत्र तज्जन्मभूमिका ॥ 124 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard this, the king, considering him a Vaiṣṇava, an excellent twice-born, / sent him to the land of his birth.

3.4.s:
mlecchairvināśitaṃ yattu vedāṃgaṃ jyotiṣāṃ gatiḥ ..
punaruddhāritaṃ tena tridhābhūtaṃ sanātanam .. 125 ..
3.4.d:
म्लेच्छैर्विनाशितं यत्तु वेदांगं ज्योतिषां गतिः ॥
पुनरुद्धारितं तेन त्रिधाभूतं सनातनम् ॥ 125 ॥
3.4.m: That which was the limb of the Veda, the course of the heavenly luminaries, destroyed by the mlecchas, / was restored again by him, threefold and eternal.

3.4.s:
sūta uvāca ..
ityuktvā bhagavāñjīvassūryamāhātmyamuttamam..
prayāge tu punardevānuvāca vacasāṃ patiḥ ..1..
3.4.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
इत्युक्त्वा भगवाञ्जीवस्सूर्यमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम्॥
प्रयागे तु पुनर्देवानुवाच वचसां पतिः ॥1॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having related this excellent greatness of the sun, / the blessed Jīva, the master of speech, spoke again to the gods at Prayāga:

3.4.s:
pratiṣṭhānapure ramye sūryo jāto harājñayā ..
purā tretāyugāṃte ca tacchṛṇuṣva surottama .. 2 ..
3.4.d:
प्रतिष्ठानपुरे रम्ये सूर्यो जातो हराज्ञया ॥
पुरा त्रेतायुगांते च तच्छृणुष्व सुरोत्तम ॥ 2 ॥
3.4.m: "In the delightful city of Pratiṣṭhāna, the sun was born by the command of Hara / formerly at the end of the Tretāyuga. Listen to that, O best of the gods!

3.4.s:
tretānte siṃhaladvīpe parīkṣitanṛpo'bhavat ..
vedadharmaparo nityaṃ devatātithipūjakaḥ ..3..
3.4.d:
त्रेतान्ते सिंहलद्वीपे परीक्षितनृपोऽभवत् ॥
वेदधर्मपरो नित्यं देवतातिथिपूजकः ॥3॥
3.4.m: At the end of the Tretā[yuga], on the island of Siṃhala, there was a king [named] Parīkṣit, / constantly devoted to Vedic duty, a worshipper of the gods and guests.

3.4.s:
kanyā bhānumatī tasya sūryavrataparāyaṇā ..
bhaktibhāvena savitā pratyahaṃ tadgṛhe svayam .. 4 ..
3.4.d:
कन्या भानुमती तस्य सूर्यव्रतपरायणा ॥
भक्तिभावेन सविता प्रत्यहं तद्गृहे स्वयम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.4.m: His daughter Bhānumatī was devoted to the observance of the sun. / Out of devotion, Savitṛ himself [came] every day to her house.

3.4.s:
tayā kṛtaṃ śubhaṃ bhakṣyaṃ madhyāhne bhuktavānprabhuḥ..
ravivāre kadācitsā nalinī sāgaraṃ prati ..5..
3.4.d:
तया कृतं शुभं भक्ष्यं मध्याह्ने भुक्तवान्प्रभुः॥
रविवारे कदाचित्सा नलिनी सागरं प्रति ॥5॥
3.4.m: At midday the Lord ate the auspicious food prepared by her. / Once on a Sunday, the maiden, [as lovely as] a lotus, went towards the ocean

3.4.s:
snānārthamāgatā kanyā tadā nārada āgataḥ..
dṛṣṭvā manoramāṃ bālāmekākīṃ jalamadhyagām..6..
3.4.d:
स्नानार्थमागता कन्या तदा नारद आगतः॥
दृष्ट्वा मनोरमां बालामेकाकीं जलमध्यगाम्॥6॥
3.4.m: to bathe. Then Nārada arrived. / Seeing the lovely girl alone, standing in the middle of the water,

3.4.s:
gṛhītvā vasanaṃ tasyā vacanaṃ prāha nirbhayaḥ..
pāṇiṃ gṛhāṇa me subhrūstvaddṛṣṭyā vaśamāgataḥ .. 7 ..
3.4.d:
गृहीत्वा वसनं तस्या वचनं प्राह निर्भयः॥
पाणिं गृहाण मे सुभ्रूस्त्वद्दृष्ट्या वशमागतः ॥ 7 ॥
3.4.m: taking her garment, he spoke fearlessly: / 'Take my hand, O fair-browed one! I have fallen under your power by your glance.'

3.4.s:
ityuktavaṃtaṃ tu muniṃ kumārī namrakandharā ..
uvāca śṛṇu devarṣe kanyāhaṃ tvaṃ sutapradaḥ .. 8..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तवंतं तु मुनिं कुमारी नम्रकन्धरा ॥
उवाच शृणु देवर्षे कन्याहं त्वं सुतप्रदः ॥ 8॥
3.4.m: To the sage who spoke thus, the maiden, her head bowed, / said: 'Listen, O celestial sage! I am a maiden, and you are a giver of sons.

3.4.s:
bhavāndevāṅganābhiśca prārthitaḥ svargamaṇḍale ..
kva ca vai menakā raṃbhā kvāhaṃ manujayonijā .. ..9..
3.4.d:
भवान्देवाङ्गनाभिश्च प्रार्थितः स्वर्गमण्डले ॥
क्व च वै मेनका रंभा क्वाहं मनुजयोनिजा ॥ ॥9॥
3.4.m: You are sought after by divine maidens in the realm of heaven. / Where indeed are Menakā and Rambhā, and where am I, born of human womb?

3.4.s:
navadvāreṣu dehesmindurgandhāḥ saṃsthitāḥ sadā ..
naiva devāṅganāṅge vai tasmāttubhyaṃ namonamaḥ..3.4.9.10
3.4.d:
नवद्वारेषु देहेस्मिन्दुर्गन्धाः संस्थिताः सदा ॥
नैव देवाङ्गनाङ्गे वै तस्मात्तुभ्यं नमोनमः॥3.4.9.10
3.4.m: In the nine apertures of this body foul odours are ever present; / they are not at all in the body of a divine maiden. Therefore, homage, homage to you!'

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasyā lajjito nāradastadā..
mahādevamupāgamya coktavānsarvakāraṇam .. 11 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्या लज्जितो नारदस्तदा॥
महादेवमुपागम्य चोक्तवान्सर्वकारणम् ॥ 11 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing her words, Nārada was then ashamed. / Approaching Mahādeva, he told him the entire cause.

3.4.s:
kuṣṭhībhūtaṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṃkaro lokaśaṃkaraḥ ..
tuṣṭāva bhāskaraṃ devaṃ tadā prādurabhūtprabhuḥ .. 12 ..
3.4.d:
कुष्ठीभूतं मुनिं दृष्ट्वा शंकरो लोकशंकरः ॥
तुष्टाव भास्करं देवं तदा प्रादुरभूत्प्रभुः ॥ 12 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing the sage stricken with leprosy, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world, / praised the god Bhāskara; then the Lord appeared.

3.4.s:
nāradasya śubhaṃ dehaṃ kṛtvā śivamuvāca ha ..
ājñāṃ dehi mahādeva tavāśāṃ pūrayāmyaham .. 13 ..
3.4.d:
नारदस्य शुभं देहं कृत्वा शिवमुवाच ह ॥
आज्ञां देहि महादेव तवाशां पूरयाम्यहम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.4.m: Making Nārada's body auspicious, [the Sun] said to Śiva: / 'Give the command, O Mahādeva, and I shall fulfill your wish.'

3.4.s:
ityuktaṃ taṃ śivaḥ prāha dvijo bhūtvā bhavānbhuvi ..
gṛhāṇa nṛpateḥ kanyāṃ raviṇā tu tathā kṛtam .. 14 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तं तं शिवः प्राह द्विजो भूत्वा भवान्भुवि ॥
गृहाण नृपतेः कन्यां रविणा तु तथा कृतम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.4.m: To him who spoke thus, Śiva said: 'Becoming a twice-born on earth, / take the king's daughter.' And it was done so by Ravi.

3.4.s:
savitā bhānumatyā ca sārddhaṃ kṛtvā taponvaham ..
sūryalokaṃ punaḥ prāptassa pauṣe ca prakāśa kṛt..
taṃ bhajāśu mahendra tvaṃ devakāryaṃ prasādhaya..15..
3.4.d:
सविता भानुमत्या च सार्द्धं कृत्वा तपोन्वहम् ॥
सूर्यलोकं पुनः प्राप्तस्स पौषे च प्रकाश कृत्॥
तं भजाशु महेन्द्र त्वं देवकार्यं प्रसाधय॥15॥
3.4.m: Savitṛ, performing asceticism daily together with Bhānumatī, / reached the world of the sun again, and he brings light in the month of Pauṣa. / Worship him swiftly, O Mahendra, and accomplish the task of the gods!"

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ mahendraśca suraissaha ..
savitāraṃ pauṣamāse tuṣṭāva śubha pūjanaiḥ .. 16 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं महेन्द्रश्च सुरैस्सह ॥
सवितारं पौषमासे तुष्टाव शुभ पूजनैः ॥ 16 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this word of the Guru, Mahendra together with the gods / praised Savitṛ in the month of Pauṣa with auspicious offerings of worship.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavāndevānāha śubhaṃ vacaḥ ..
ahaṃ kāśyāṃ bhavāmyadya nāmnā dhanvatariḥ svayam .. 17 ..
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्देवानाह शुभं वचः ॥
अहं काश्यां भवाम्यद्य नाम्ना धन्वतरिः स्वयम् ॥ 17 ॥
3.4.m: Then, pleased, the Blessed One spoke an auspicious word to the gods: / "Today I will become Dhanvantari myself in Kāśī.

3.4.s:
rogaiśca pīḍitām̐llokānkalinā nirmitairbhuvi ..
śamayiṣyāmi tatroṣya devakāryaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 18 ..
3.4.d:
रोगैश्च पीडिताम्̐ल्लोकान्कलिना निर्मितैर्भुवि ॥
शमयिष्यामि तत्रोष्य देवकार्यं भविष्यति ॥ 18 ॥
3.4.m: And dwelling there, I shall pacify the people tormented by diseases / created on earth by Kali; the task of the gods will be accomplished."

3.4.s:
ityuktvā bhagavānsūryaḥ kāśīnagaramāgataḥ ..
kalpadattasya viprasya putro bhūtvā mahītale .. 19 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्सूर्यः काशीनगरमागतः ॥
कल्पदत्तस्य विप्रस्य पुत्रो भूत्वा महीतले ॥ 19 ॥
3.4.m: Having said this, the blessed Sun came to the city of Kāśī, / becoming the son of the twice-born Kalpadatta on the surface of the earth.

3.4.s:
suśrutaṃ rājaputraṃ ca vipravṛddhasamanvitam ..
śiṣyaṃ kṛtvā prasannātmā kalpavedamacīkarat .. 3.4.9.20 ..
3.4.d:
सुश्रुतं राजपुत्रं च विप्रवृद्धसमन्वितम् ॥
शिष्यं कृत्वा प्रसन्नात्मा कल्पवेदमचीकरत् ॥ 3.4.9.20 ॥
3.4.m: Making the prince Suśruta, accompanied by an aged brāhmaṇa, / his pupil, the gracious-minded one caused the Kalpaveda to be composed.

3.4.s:
rogaiśca kṣayitaṃ dehaṃ kālpametatsmṛtaṃ budhaiḥ ..
tasya jñānaṃ ca taṃtre'smikalpavedohyataḥ smṛtaḥ .. 21 ..
3.4.d:
रोगैश्च क्षयितं देहं काल्पमेतत्स्मृतं बुधैः ॥
तस्य ज्ञानं च तंत्रेऽस्मिकल्पवेदोह्यतः स्मृतः ॥ 21 ॥
3.4.m: "A body wasted by diseases is known by the wise as kālpa; / and the knowledge of that [is] in this Tantra, hence it is considered the Kalpaveda."

3.4.s:
dhanvatarissa bhagavānprasiddhobhūtkalau yuge ..
yasya darśanamātreṇa rogā naśyaṃti tatkṣaṇāt .. 22 ..
3.4.d:
धन्वतरिस्स भगवान्प्रसिद्धोभूत्कलौ युगे ॥
यस्य दर्शनमात्रेण रोगा नश्यंति तत्क्षणात् ॥ 22 ॥
3.4.m: He, the blessed Dhanvantari, became renowned in the Kali age, / at the mere sight of whom diseases perish that very instant.

3.4.s:
suśrutaḥ kalpavedaṃ taṃ dhanvattarivinirmitam ..
paṭhitvā ca śatādhyāyaṃ sau'śrutaṃ taṃtramākarot ..23..
3.4.d:
सुश्रुतः कल्पवेदं तं धन्वत्तरिविनिर्मितम् ॥
पठित्वा च शताध्यायं सौऽश्रुतं तंत्रमाकरोत् ॥23॥
3.4.m: Suśruta, having studied that Kalpaveda composed by Dhanvantari, / composed the Tantra of Suśruta consisting of one hundred chapters.

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
purā paṃpāpure ramye helī nāmnā dvijo'bhavat ..
catuṣṣaṣṭikalābhijño ravipūjanatatparaḥ ..24..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
पुरा पंपापुरे रम्ये हेली नाम्ना द्विजोऽभवत् ॥
चतुष्षष्टिकलाभिज्ञो रविपूजनतत्परः ॥24॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Formerly, in the delightful city of Pampāpura, there was a twice-born named Helī, / skilled in the sixty-four arts, intent on the worship of Ravi.

3.4.s:
tyaktvā pratigrahaṃ vṛttiṃ kāruvṛttiṃ gṛhītavān ..
kṛtvā vastrakalaṃ lauhaṃ tathā citrakalaṃ punaḥ ..25..
3.4.d:
त्यक्त्वा प्रतिग्रहं वृत्तिं कारुवृत्तिं गृहीतवान् ॥
कृत्वा वस्त्रकलं लौहं तथा चित्रकलं पुनः ॥25॥
3.4.m: Abandoning the livelihood of accepting gifts, he took up the livelihood of an artisan, / producing textiles, ironwork, and also paintings,

3.4.s:
dhātumūrtikalaṃ caiva sarvakārukalaṃ tathā ..
pañcasahasramudrābhirākrīṇankāruko'bhavat ..26..
3.4.d:
धातुमूर्तिकलं चैव सर्वकारुकलं तथा ॥
पञ्चसहस्रमुद्राभिराक्रीणन्कारुकोऽभवत् ॥26॥
3.4.m: as well as metal sculptures, and all the crafts of an artisan; / selling them for five thousand coins, he became an artisan.

3.4.s:
kalaeko māsamātre kāle tenaiva nirmitaḥ ..
taddhanena raviṃ devaṃ yajñairmāghe hi so'rcayat..
viśvakarmā raviḥ sākṣānmāghamāse prakāśakaḥ ..27..
3.4.d:
कलएको मासमात्रे काले तेनैव निर्मितः ॥
तद्धनेन रविं देवं यज्ञैर्माघे हि सोऽर्चयत्॥
विश्वकर्मा रविः साक्षान्माघमासे प्रकाशकः ॥27॥
3.4.m: A single mechanical device was fashioned by him in the space of just one month; / with that wealth he indeed worshipped the god Ravi with sacrifices in Māgha. / The sun is Viśvakarman himself, radiating light in the month of Māgha.

3.4.s:
helino bahulairyajñaissantuṣṭaḥ pratyahaṃ prabhuḥ ..
paṃpāsarovare ramye nirmitaḥ staṃbha uttamaḥ ..28..
3.4.d:
हेलिनो बहुलैर्यज्ञैस्सन्तुष्टः प्रत्यहं प्रभुः ॥
पंपासरोवरे रम्ये निर्मितः स्तंभ उत्तमः ॥28॥
3.4.m: Pleased daily by Helī's abundant sacrifices, the Lord / fashioned an excellent pillar in the delightful lake Pampā.

3.4.s:
jyotīrūpo mahāramyastatra prāpto raviḥ svayam..
madhyāhne helinā dattaṃ bhojana daivatapriyam ..29..
3.4.d:
ज्योतीरूपो महारम्यस्तत्र प्राप्तो रविः स्वयम्॥
मध्याह्ने हेलिना दत्तं भोजन दैवतप्रियम् ॥29॥
3.4.m: Consisting of light, exceedingly delightful, Ravi himself arrived there; / at midday, Helī offered food dear to the deities.

3.4.s:
bhuktvā sa pratyahaṃ svāmī māsimāsi divākaraḥ ..
trailokyaṃ bhāvayāṃcakre sarvadevamayo hariḥ ..3.4.9.30..
3.4.d:
भुक्त्वा स प्रत्यहं स्वामी मासिमासि दिवाकरः ॥
त्रैलोक्यं भावयांचक्रे सर्वदेवमयो हरिः ॥3.4.9.30॥
3.4.m: Eating [it] every day, the Master, the Maker of Day, month by month, / Hari, who embodies all the gods, sustained the three worlds.

3.4.s:
sahasrāyurdvijo bhūtvā tyaktvā prāṇānraviḥ svayam ..
bhūtvā maṇḍalamadhyāsya māghamāsamatoṣayat ..
taṃ sūryaṃ bhaja devendra sa te kāryaṃ kariṣyati .. 31 ..
3.4.d:
सहस्रायुर्द्विजो भूत्वा त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्रविः स्वयम् ॥
भूत्वा मण्डलमध्यास्य माघमासमतोषयत् ॥
तं सूर्यं भज देवेन्द्र स ते कार्यं करिष्यति ॥ 31 ॥
3.4.m: Having lived a thousand years as a twice-born, the Sun himself relinquished his vital breaths, / and sitting in the midst of his orb, he pleased the month of Māgha. / Worship that Sun, O lord of the gods; he will accomplish your purpose.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ vāsavo daivataissaha..
sūryamārādhayāmāsa viśvakarmāṇamuttamam..32..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं वासवो दैवतैस्सह॥
सूर्यमाराधयामास विश्वकर्माणमुत्तमम्॥32॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this advice from the preceptor, Indra, together with the gods, / worshipped the Sun, the supreme Viśvakarman.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavāṃstvaṣṭā tuṣṭikarojanān..
surānāha vaco ramyaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ surasattamāḥ ..33..
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवांस्त्वष्टा तुष्टिकरोजनान्॥
सुरानाह वचो रम्यं शृणुध्वं सुरसत्तमाः ॥33॥
3.4.m: Then the blessed Tvaṣṭṛ, delighting people, was pleased / and spoke delightful words to the gods: “Listen, O best of the gods!

3.4.s:
bilgrāme vaṃgadeśe saṃbhavāmi niruktakṛt ..
jayadeva iti khyātaḥ kavīnāṃ hi śiromaṇiḥ .. 34 ..
3.4.d:
बिल्ग्रामे वंगदेशे संभवामि निरुक्तकृत् ॥
जयदेव इति ख्यातः कवीनां हि शिरोमणिः ॥ 34 ॥
3.4.m: In the village of Bilva in the country of Bengal, I will be born as an author of Nirukta, / renowned as Jayadeva, indeed the crest-jewel of poets.”

3.4.s:
ityuktvā bhagavānsūryo vaṃgadeśamupāyayau ..
gehe kaṃdukino jāto brāhmaṇasya mahītale .. 35 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्सूर्यो वंगदेशमुपाययौ ॥
गेहे कंदुकिनो जातो ब्राह्मणस्य महीतले ॥ 35 ॥
3.4.m: Having spoken thus, the blessed Sun arrived in the country of Bengal / and was born on earth in the house of a brāhmaṇa named Kandukin.

3.4.s:
sa paṃcābdavapurbhūtvā pitṛmātṛparāyaṇaḥ ..
dvādaśābdaṃ mahāsevā tatra tena tayoḥ kṛtā .. 36 ..
3.4.d:
स पंचाब्दवपुर्भूत्वा पितृमातृपरायणः ॥
द्वादशाब्दं महासेवा तत्र तेन तयोः कृता ॥ 36 ॥
3.4.m: Reaching five years of age, devoted to his mother and father, / he performed great service there for the two of them for twelve years.

3.4.s:
mṛtimaṃtau ca pitarau pretakṛtyena tarpitau ..
jayadevena tau nākaṃ gayāśrāddhe hi jagmatuḥ .. 37 ..
3.4.d:
मृतिमंतौ च पितरौ प्रेतकृत्येन तर्पितौ ॥
जयदेवेन तौ नाकं गयाश्राद्धे हि जग्मतुः ॥ 37 ॥
3.4.m: When both parents died, they were gratified with funeral rites; / by Jayadeva’s śrāddha at Gayā, they indeed went to heaven.

3.4.s:
jayadevastadā vipro bhūtvā vairāgyavānbhuvi ..
tatrasthāne mahāramye vane vāsamakārayat .. 38 ..
3.4.d:
जयदेवस्तदा विप्रो भूत्वा वैराग्यवान्भुवि ॥
तत्रस्थाने महारम्ये वने वासमकारयत् ॥ 38 ॥
3.4.m: Then the brāhmaṇa Jayadeva, having attained detachment in the world, / made his dwelling in a forest at a very charming place there.

3.4.s:
triviṃśābde tataḥ prāpte kenacinmadhurānanā ..
brāhmaṇena śubhā kanyā jagannāthāya cārpitā .. 39 ..
3.4.d:
त्रिविंशाब्दे ततः प्राप्ते केनचिन्मधुरानना ॥
ब्राह्मणेन शुभा कन्या जगन्नाथाय चार्पिता ॥ 39 ॥
3.4.m: Then, when he reached his twenty-third year, a beautiful maiden with a sweet face / was offered by a certain brāhmaṇa to Jagannātha.

3.4.s:
arcāvasāne bhagavānaniruddhassanātanaḥ ..
dārubrahmamayaḥ sākṣādāha taṃ svena vai vacaḥ .. 3.4.9.40 ..
3.4.d:
अर्चावसाने भगवाननिरुद्धस्सनातनः ॥
दारुब्रह्ममयः साक्षादाह तं स्वेन वै वचः ॥ 3.4.9.40 ॥
3.4.m: At the conclusion of the worship, the eternal Lord Aniruddha, / who consists directly of the wooden Brahman, addressed him with his own voice:

3.4.s:
śṛṇu tvaṃ bhoḥ satyavrata jayadevo vapurmama ..
padmāvatīṃ sutāṃ tasmai nivedaya mamājñayā .. 41 ..
3.4.d:
शृणु त्वं भोः सत्यव्रत जयदेवो वपुर्मम ॥
पद्मावतीं सुतां तस्मै निवेदय ममाज्ञया ॥ 41 ॥
3.4.m: “Listen, O Satyavrata, Jayadeva is my own form; / by my command, offer your daughter Padmāvatī to him.”

3.4.s:
ityuktassa dvijastūrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vairāgarūpiṇam ..
tatra sthāpya nijāṃ kanyāṃ svagehāya mudā yayau .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तस्स द्विजस्तूर्णं दृष्ट्वा वैरागरूपिणम् ॥
तत्र स्थाप्य निजां कन्यां स्वगेहाय मुदा ययौ ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m: Addressed thus, that twice-born, quickly seeing the ascetic embodiment, / placed his daughter there and went gladly to his own home.

3.4.s:
sā tu padmāvatī kanyā matvā taṃ suṃdaraṃ patim ..
tatsevāṃ sā mudā yuktā cakāra bahuvārṣikam .. 43 ..
3.4.d:
सा तु पद्मावती कन्या मत्वा तं सुंदरं पतिम् ॥
तत्सेवां सा मुदा युक्ता चकार बहुवार्षिकम् ॥ 43 ॥
3.4.m: The maiden Padmāvatī, regarding him as her handsome husband, / served him with joy for many years.

3.4.s:
niruktaṃ vaidikaṃ cāṃgaṃ kṛtavānsa samādhinā ..
varṇāgamo gaveṃdrādau siṃhe varṇaviparyayaḥ ..
ṣoḍaśādau vikāraśca varṇanāśaḥ pṛṣodare .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
निरुक्तं वैदिकं चांगं कृतवान्स समाधिना ॥
वर्णागमो गवेंद्रादौ सिंहे वर्णविपर्ययः ॥
षोडशादौ विकारश्च वर्णनाशः पृषोदरे ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m: Through profound contemplation he composed Nirukta, the Vedic ancillary: / phonetic augmentation as in *gavendra* and the like, phonetic inversion in *siṃha*, / phonetic modification in *ṣoḍaśa* and the like, and phonetic elision in *pṛṣodara*;

3.4.s:
varṇavikāranāśābhyāṃ dhātoratiśayena yaḥ ..
yogastaducyate prājñairmayūrabhramarādiṣu .. 49 ..
3.4.d:
वर्णविकारनाशाभ्यां धातोरतिशयेन यः ॥
योगस्तदुच्यते प्राज्ञैर्मयूरभ्रमरादिषु ॥ 49 ॥
3.4.m: the combination that arises from the modification and elision of phonemes / by the intensity of the verbal root is described by the wise in words such as *mayūra* and *bhramara*.

3.4.s:
evaṃ paṃcavidhānyeva niruktāni smṛtāni vai ..
śūdraiśca nāgavaṃśīyairbhraṃśitāni kalau yuge .. 46 ..
3.4.d:
एवं पंचविधान्येव निरुक्तानि स्मृतानि वै ॥
शूद्रैश्च नागवंशीयैर्भ्रंशितानि कलौ युगे ॥ 46 ॥
3.4.m: Thus the Niruktas are recalled to be of five types; / they were corrupted in the Kali age by the Śūdras and members of the serpent race.

3.4.s:
jitvā prākṛtabhāṣāyāḥ kartṝnmūḍhānkalipriyān ..
śuddhaṃ hi pāṇiniḥ śāstraṃ cakāra surahetave .. 47 ..
3.4.d:
जित्वा प्राकृतभाषायाः कर्तॄन्मूढान्कलिप्रियान् ॥
शुद्धं हि पाणिनिः शास्त्रं चकार सुरहेतवे ॥ 47 ॥
3.4.m: Conquering the foolish authors of the Prakrit language, who are fond of Kali, / Pāṇini composed the pure treatise for the sake of the gods.

3.4.s:
ekadā tu kalirdhūrto hṛdisthaścaurakarmaṇām ..
nṛpadattaṃ dvijasyaiva luṃṭhayitvā dhanaṃ bahu .. 48 ..
3.4.d:
एकदा तु कलिर्धूर्तो हृदिस्थश्चौरकर्मणाम् ॥
नृपदत्तं द्विजस्यैव लुंठयित्वा धनं बहु ॥ 48 ॥
3.4.m: Once, however, the rogue Kali, residing in the hearts of robbers, / robbed the abundant wealth given by the king to the twice-born.

3.4.s:
padmāvatīṃ satīṃ matvā tyaktvā tadvai gato gṛham ..
hastau pādau dvijasyaiva kaliścoraiḥ samācchinat .. 49 ..
3.4.d:
पद्मावतीं सतीं मत्वा त्यक्त्वा तद्वै गतो गृहम् ॥
हस्तौ पादौ द्विजस्यैव कलिश्चोरैः समाच्छिनत् ॥ 49 ॥
3.4.m: Regarding Padmāvatī as a virtuous wife, Kali spared her and went to his house; / and through the thieves, he severed the hands and feet of that very twice-born.

3.4.s:
tadā tu duḥkhitā devī gartamadhye sthitaṃ patim ..
niṣkāsya bahudhālapyāpīḍya hastena cāharat .. 3.4.9.50 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तु दुःखिता देवी गर्तमध्ये स्थितं पतिम् ॥
निष्कास्य बहुधालप्यापीड्य हस्तेन चाहरत् ॥ 3.4.9.50 ॥
3.4.m: Then the distressed lady, extracting her husband who lay inside a pit, / weeping bitterly and embracing him with her hand, carried him away.

3.4.s:
ekasmindivase rājā mṛgayārthamupāgataḥ..
ahastapādaṃ ca muniṃ jayadevaṃ dadarśa ha ..
sa pṛṣṭastena tatraiva kṛtaṃ kena tavedṛśam .. 51 ..
3.4.d:
एकस्मिन्दिवसे राजा मृगयार्थमुपागतः॥
अहस्तपादं च मुनिं जयदेवं ददर्श ह ॥
स पृष्टस्तेन तत्रैव कृतं केन तवेदृशम् ॥ 51 ॥
3.4.m: One day the king, arriving for a hunt, / saw the sage Jayadeva devoid of hands and feet. / He was asked by the king right there: “By whom was this done to you?”

3.4.s:
sa hovāca mahārāja hastapādavihīnakaḥ ..
karmaṇāhamiha prāpto na kenāpi kṛtaṃ khalu .. 52 ..
3.4.d:
स होवाच महाराज हस्तपादविहीनकः ॥
कर्मणाहमिह प्राप्तो न केनापि कृतं खलु ॥ 52 ॥
3.4.m: Deceitless, he said: “O great king, destitute of hands and feet, / I have reached this state through my own action; indeed, it was done by no one.”

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā dharmapālo nṛpatistaṃ dvijottamam ..
sapatnīkaṃ ca śibikāmāropya svagṛhaṃ yayau .. 53 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा धर्मपालो नृपतिस्तं द्विजोत्तमम् ॥
सपत्नीकं च शिबिकामारोप्य स्वगृहं ययौ ॥ 53 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing this, King Dharmapāla placed that best of twice-born / along with his wife into a palanquin and went to his own palace.

3.4.s:
tasya dīkṣāṃ nṛpaḥ prāpya dharmaśālāmakāraya t ..
kadācidvaiṣṇavā bhūtā te caurāḥ kalinirmitāḥ ..
dharmapālagṛhaṃ prāpya rājānamidamabruvan .. 54 ..
3.4.d:
तस्य दीक्षां नृपः प्राप्य धर्मशालामकारय त् ॥
कदाचिद्वैष्णवा भूता ते चौराः कलिनिर्मिताः ॥
धर्मपालगृहं प्राप्य राजानमिदमब्रुवन् ॥ 54 ॥
3.4.m: Receiving initiation from him, the king caused a rest-house to be built. / Sometime later, those thieves created by Kali became Vaiṣṇavas, / and arriving at Dharmapāla’s residence, they said this to the king:

3.4.s:
vayaṃ hi śāstranipuṇāstava gehamupāgatāḥ..
asmābhirnirmitaṃ bhojyaṃ svayaṃ viṣṇuḥ śilāmayaḥ ..
saṃbhuṃkte pratyahaṃ prītyā tatpaśya nṛpasattama .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
वयं हि शास्त्रनिपुणास्तव गेहमुपागताः॥
अस्माभिर्निर्मितं भोज्यं स्वयं विष्णुः शिलामयः ॥
संभुंक्ते प्रत्यहं प्रीत्या तत्पश्य नृपसत्तम ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m: “We are skilled in the scriptures and have come to your house. / Viṣṇu himself in stone form joyfully eats daily / the food prepared by us; look upon that, O best of kings.”

3.4.s:
ityuktvā kalibhaktāste viṣṇurūpaṃ caturbhujam ..
nṛpāya darśayāmāsurbhuktavaṃtaṃ svamāyayā .. 56 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा कलिभक्तास्ते विष्णुरूपं चतुर्भुजम् ॥
नृपाय दर्शयामासुर्भुक्तवंतं स्वमायया ॥ 56 ॥
3.4.m: Having spoken thus, those devotees of Kali, through their own delusion, / showed to the king Viṣṇu’s four-armed form eating.

3.4.s:
vismito dharmapālaśca jayadevamuvāca ha ..
guro madbhavane prāptā vaiṣṇavā viṣṇutatparāḥ..
adīdṛśanhariṃ sākṣāttasmāttvaṃ śīghramāvraja ..57..
3.4.d:
विस्मितो धर्मपालश्च जयदेवमुवाच ह ॥
गुरो मद्भवने प्राप्ता वैष्णवा विष्णुतत्पराः॥
अदीदृशन्हरिं साक्षात्तस्मात्त्वं शीघ्रमाव्रज ॥57॥
3.4.m: Amazed, Dharmapāla said to Jayadeva: / “O master, Vaiṣṇavas devoted to Viṣṇu have arrived at my palace / and have shown Hari visibly before my eyes; therefore, come quickly.”

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā dvijaḥ prāpto vismito'bhūttathā nṛpaḥ ..
tadā tu taṃ hi pākhaṃḍā bhūpamūcurvihasya te .. .. 58 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा द्विजः प्राप्तो विस्मितोऽभूत्तथा नृपः ॥
तदा तु तं हि पाखंडा भूपमूचुर्विहस्य ते ॥ ॥ 58 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing this, the twice-born arrived, and the king was also amazed. / Then those heretics, laughing, said to the king:

3.4.s:
asau vipraśca nṛpate gauḍadeśe nivāsinaḥ ..
sūdo bhakṣyakarastasmai kadāciddhanalobhataḥ .. 59 ..
3.4.d:
असौ विप्रश्च नृपते गौडदेशे निवासिनः ॥
सूदो भक्ष्यकरस्तस्मै कदाचिद्धनलोभतः ॥ 59 ॥
3.4.m: “This twice-born, O king, was a cook who prepared food for a resident / of the Gauḍa country; once, out of greed for wealth,

3.4.s:
garalaṃ miśritaṃ bhakṣye tena pākhaṃḍarūpiṇā ..
jñātvā rājā tu taṃ vipraṃ śūlamadhye hyaropayat .. 3.4.9.60 ..
3.4.d:
गरलं मिश्रितं भक्ष्ये तेन पाखंडरूपिणा ॥
ज्ञात्वा राजा तु तं विप्रं शूलमध्ये ह्यरोपयत् ॥ 3.4.9.60 ॥
3.4.m: poison was mixed into the food by that heretic. / But the king, discovering him, impaled that twice-born on a stake.

3.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare rājanvayaṃ tatra samāgatāḥ ..
āgaskṛtaṃ dvijaṃ matvā dattvā jñānānya nekaśaḥ ..
śūlāttaṃ hi samuttārya hastau pādau nṛpo'cchinat .. 61 ..
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे राजन्वयं तत्र समागताः ॥
आगस्कृतं द्विजं मत्वा दत्त्वा ज्ञानान्य नेकशः ॥
शूलात्तं हि समुत्तार्य हस्तौ पादौ नृपोऽच्छिनत् ॥ 61 ॥
3.4.m: In the meantime, O king, we arrived there; / considering that the twice-born had committed a crime, after giving various teachings / and lifting him from the stake, the king severed his hands and feet.

3.4.s:
asmākaṃ śiṣyabhūto hi rājāsmābhiḥ prabodhitaḥ ..
ityuktamātre vacane duḥkhitābhūcca dāritā .. 62 ..
3.4.d:
अस्माकं शिष्यभूतो हि राजास्माभिः प्रबोधितः ॥
इत्युक्तमात्रे वचने दुःखिताभूच्च दारिता ॥ 62 ॥
3.4.m: The king became our disciple and was enlightened by us.” / As soon as these words were spoken, [the earth] became grieved and split open,

3.4.s:
caurām̐stānsā hi pātāle cakāra surarakṣitān ..
jayadevastathā bhūtāndṛṣṭvā caurānruroda ha .. 63 ..
3.4.d:
चौराम्̐स्तान्सा हि पाताले चकार सुररक्षितान् ॥
जयदेवस्तथा भूतान्दृष्ट्वा चौरान्रुरोद ह ॥ 63 ॥
3.4.m: and she cast those thieves into the netherworld, guarded by the gods. / Seeing the thieves in that state, Jayadeva wept.

3.4.s:
kraṃdamāne dvije tasminhastāṃghrī prakṛtiṃ gatau ..
vismitaṃ nṛpatiṃ tatra sarvaṃ hetumavarṇayat .. 64 ..
3.4.d:
क्रंदमाने द्विजे तस्मिन्हस्तांघ्री प्रकृतिं गतौ ॥
विस्मितं नृपतिं तत्र सर्वं हेतुमवर्णयत् ॥ 64 ॥
3.4.m: While that twice-born was weeping, his hands and feet returned to their natural state; / and to the astonished king, he explained the whole cause there.

3.4.s:
śrutvā rājā prasannātmā jayadevamukhodbhavam ..
gītagoviṃdamevāśu paṭhitvā mokṣamāgamat .. 65 ..
3.4.d:
श्रुत्वा राजा प्रसन्नात्मा जयदेवमुखोद्भवम् ॥
गीतगोविंदमेवाशु पठित्वा मोक्षमागमत् ॥ 65 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard it, the king, delighted in mind, recited the Gītagovinda / that had arisen from the mouth of Jayadeva, and quickly attained liberation.

3.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ vipra jayadevo yathābhavat ..
kṛṣṇacaitanyacaritaṃ yathā jātaṃ śṛṇuśva tat .. 66 ..
3.4.d:
इति ते कथितं विप्र जयदेवो यथाभवत् ॥
कृष्णचैतन्यचरितं यथा जातं शृणुश्व तत् ॥ 66 ॥
3.4.m: Thus it has been related to you, O twice-born, how Jayadeva came to be. / Hear about the deeds of Kṛṣṇa Caitanya as they occurred.

3.4.s:
.. jīva uvāca .. ..
viṣṇuśarmā purā kaścidviprobhūdvedapāragaḥ ..
sarvadevamayaṃ viṣṇuṃ pūjayitvā prasannadhīḥ ..1..
3.4.d:
॥ जीव उवाच ॥ ॥
विष्णुशर्मा पुरा कश्चिद्विप्रोभूद्वेदपारगः ॥
सर्वदेवमयं विष्णुं पूजयित्वा प्रसन्नधीः ॥1॥
3.4.m: Jīva said: / Formerly, there was a certain twice-born named Viṣṇuśarman who had mastered the Vedas. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu, who comprises all deities, he was clear-minded.

3.4.s:
anyaissuraiśca saṃpūjyo babhūva haripūjanāt ..
bhikṣāvṛttiparo nityaṃ patnīmānputravarjitaḥ .. 2 ..
3.4.d:
अन्यैस्सुरैश्च संपूज्यो बभूव हरिपूजनात् ॥
भिक्षावृत्तिपरो नित्यं पत्नीमान्पुत्रवर्जितः ॥ 2 ॥
3.4.m: Through his worship of Hari, he became worthy of worship even by other gods. / Constantly devoted to living on alms, he had a wife but was childless.

3.4.s:
kadācittasya gehe vai vratī kaścitsamāgataḥ ..
dvijapatnīṃ tadaikākīṃ bhaktinamrāṃ daridriṇīm ..
dṛṣṭvovāca mahābhāgaḥ sa sparśāḍhyo dayāparaḥ .. 3 ..
3.4.d:
कदाचित्तस्य गेहे वै व्रती कश्चित्समागतः ॥
द्विजपत्नीं तदैकाकीं भक्तिनम्रां दरिद्रिणीम् ॥
दृष्ट्वोवाच महाभागः स स्पर्शाढ्यो दयापरः ॥ 3 ॥
3.4.m: Once, a certain ascetic came to his house. / Seeing the brāhmaṇa’s wife alone, bowed in devotion and destitute, / the noble one, compassionate and full of divine touch, said:

3.4.s:
anena sparśamaṇinā lohadhātuśca kāṃcanam ..
bhavettasmānmahāsādhvi tridināṃtaṃ gṛhāṇa tam .. 4 ..
3.4.d:
अनेन स्पर्शमणिना लोहधातुश्च कांचनम् ॥
भवेत्तस्मान्महासाध्वि त्रिदिनांतं गृहाण तम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.4.m: "By this philosopher's stone, base iron turns to gold. / Therefore, O great and virtuous woman, keep it for three days."

3.4.s:
snātvā tāvatsarayvāṃ cāyāsyāmi teṃtikaṃ mudā ..
ityuktvā sa yayau vipro brāhmaṇī bahu kāṃcanam ..
kṛtvā lakṣmīṃ samāpyāsīdviṣṇuśarmā tadāgamat .. 5 ..
3.4.d:
स्नात्वा तावत्सरय्वां चायास्यामि तेंतिकं मुदा ॥
इत्युक्त्वा स ययौ विप्रो ब्राह्मणी बहु कांचनम् ॥
कृत्वा लक्ष्मीं समाप्यासीद्विष्णुशर्मा तदागमत् ॥ 5 ॥
3.4.m: "I shall bathe in the Sarayū meanwhile and return to your presence with joy." / Having spoken thus, that brāhmaṇa departed. The brāhmaṇa woman, having made much gold, / attained wealth, and then Viṣṇuśarman arrived.

3.4.s:
bahusvarṇayutāṃ patnīṃ dṛṣṭvovāca haripriyaḥ ..
gaccha nāri madāghūrṇe yatra vai rasiko janaḥ .. .. 6 ..
3.4.d:
बहुस्वर्णयुतां पत्नीं दृष्ट्वोवाच हरिप्रियः ॥
गच्छ नारि मदाघूर्णे यत्र वै रसिको जनः ॥ ॥ 6 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing his wife possessing much gold, he who was dear to Hari said: / "Go, woman intoxicated with pride, where men of pleasure dwell!

3.4.s:
ahaṃ viṣṇuparo dīnaścaurabhītaḥ sadaiva hi ..
madhumattāṃ kathaṃ tvāṃ vai gṛhītuṃ bhuvi ca kṣamaḥ ..7..
3.4.d:
अहं विष्णुपरो दीनश्चौरभीतः सदैव हि ॥
मधुमत्तां कथं त्वां वै गृहीतुं भुवि च क्षमः ॥7॥
3.4.m: I am devoted to Viṣṇu, destitute, and always terrified of thieves. / How can I be capable of keeping you on earth when you are intoxicated with sweet wine?"

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ patibhītā pativratā ..
sasvarṇaṃ sparśakaṃ tasmai dattvā sevāparābhavat .. 8 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचो घोरं पतिभीता पतिव्रता ॥
सस्वर्णं स्पर्शकं तस्मै दत्त्वा सेवापराभवत् ॥ 8 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing these dreadful words, the devoted wife, fearing her husband, / gave him the philosopher's stone along with the gold and became dedicated to serving him.

3.4.s:
dvijo'pi ghargharāmadhye taddravyaṃ balato'kṣipat ..
tridinānte ca sa yatistatrāgatya mudānvitaḥ ..
uvāca brāhmaṇīṃ dīnāṃ svarṇaṃ kiṃ na kṛtaṃ tvayā .. 9 ..
3.4.d:
द्विजोऽपि घर्घरामध्ये तद्द्रव्यं बलतोऽक्षिपत् ॥
त्रिदिनान्ते च स यतिस्तत्रागत्य मुदान्वितः ॥
उवाच ब्राह्मणीं दीनां स्वर्णं किं न कृतं त्वया ॥ 9 ॥
3.4.m: The brāhmaṇa forcibly cast that wealth into the midst of the Ghargharā river. / At the end of the three days, that ascetic arrived there filled with joy / and said to the humble brāhmaṇa woman: "Why have you made no gold?"

3.4.s:
sāha bho matpatiśśuddho gṛhītvā sparśakaṃ ruṣā ..
gharghare ca nicikṣepa tatohaṃ vahnipākinī ..
nirloho vartate viprastataḥ prabhṛti he guro .. 3.4.10.10 ..
3.4.d:
साह भो मत्पतिश्शुद्धो गृहीत्वा स्पर्शकं रुषा ॥
घर्घरे च निचिक्षेप ततोहं वह्निपाकिनी ॥
निर्लोहो वर्तते विप्रस्ततः प्रभृति हे गुरो ॥ 3.4.10.10 ॥
3.4.m: She said: "O Guru, my pure husband took the touchstone in anger / and cast it into the Ghargharā. Since then, I cook with fire [alone], / and the brāhmaṇa remains without any iron!"

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ sa yatirvismayānvitaḥ ..
sthitvā dinānte taṃ vipramuvāca bahu bhartsayan .. 11 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं स यतिर्विस्मयान्वितः ॥
स्थित्वा दिनान्ते तं विप्रमुवाच बहु भर्त्सयन् ॥ 11 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing these words, the ascetic was filled with wonder. / Remaining until the end of the day, he spoke to that brāhmaṇa, rebuking him greatly:

3.4.s:
daridro bhikṣukaścāsti bhavāndaivena mohitaḥ ..
dehi me sparśakaṃ śīghraṃ no cetprāṇāṃstyajāmyaham.. 12 ..
3.4.d:
दरिद्रो भिक्षुकश्चास्ति भवान्दैवेन मोहितः ॥
देहि मे स्पर्शकं शीघ्रं नो चेत्प्राणांस्त्यजाम्यहम्॥ 12 ॥
3.4.m: "You are a destitute beggar, deluded by fate! / Give me my touchstone at once, or else I shall abandon my life!"

3.4.s:
ityuktavaṃtaṃ yatinaṃ viṣṇu śarmā tadābravīt ..
gaccha tvaṃ ghargharākūle tatra vai sparśakastava ..13..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तवंतं यतिनं विष्णु शर्मा तदाब्रवीत् ॥
गच्छ त्वं घर्घराकूले तत्र वै स्पर्शकस्तव ॥13॥
3.4.m: To the ascetic who spoke thus, Viṣṇuśarman then said: / "Go to the bank of the Ghargharā; there is your touchstone."

3.4.s:
ityuktvā yatinā sārddhaṃ gṛhītvā kaṃṭakānbahūn ..
yatine darśayāmāsa sparśakāniva kaṃṭakān .. 14 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा यतिना सार्द्धं गृहीत्वा कंटकान्बहून् ॥
यतिने दर्शयामास स्पर्शकानिव कंटकान् ॥ 14 ॥
3.4.m: Having said this, going along with the ascetic and taking many thorns, / he showed the thorns to the ascetic as if they were touchstones.

3.4.s:
tadā tu sa yatī vipraṃ natvā provāca namradhīḥ ..
mayā vai dvādaśābdāṃtaṃ samyagārādhitaḥ śivaḥ ..
tataḥ prāptaṃ śubhaṃ ratnaṃ tattu taddarśanena vai .. 15 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तु स यती विप्रं नत्वा प्रोवाच नम्रधीः ॥
मया वै द्वादशाब्दांतं सम्यगाराधितः शिवः ॥
ततः प्राप्तं शुभं रत्नं तत्तु तद्दर्शनेन वै ॥ 15 ॥
3.4.m: Then, bowing to the brāhmaṇa with a humble mind, that ascetic said: / "Indeed, for twelve years Śiva was duly worshipped by me; / thence was this auspicious jewel obtained, but simply by seeing you,

3.4.s:
sparśako bahudhā prāpto mayā lobhātmanā dvija ..
ityābhāṣya śubhaṃ jñānaṃ prāpto mokṣamavāptavān .. 16 ..
3.4.d:
स्पर्शको बहुधा प्राप्तो मया लोभात्मना द्विज ॥
इत्याभाष्य शुभं ज्ञानं प्राप्तो मोक्षमवाप्तवान् ॥ 16 ॥
3.4.m: touchstones were obtained in abundance by greedy-minded me, O brāhmaṇa!" / Having spoken thus, he attained auspicious knowledge and reached liberation.

3.4.s:
viṣṇuśarmā sahasrābdamuṣitvā jagatītale ..
sūryamārādhya vidhivadviṣṇormokṣamavāptavān..17..
3.4.d:
विष्णुशर्मा सहस्राब्दमुषित्वा जगतीतले ॥
सूर्यमाराध्य विधिवद्विष्णोर्मोक्षमवाप्तवान्॥17॥
3.4.m: Viṣṇuśarman, having dwelt on the surface of the earth for a thousand years / and having worshipped Sūrya according to rule, attained liberation in Viṣṇu.

3.4.s:
sa dvijo vaiṣṇavaṃ tejo dhṛtvā vai māsi phālgune..
trailokyamatapatsvāmī devakāryaparāyaṇaḥ .. 18 ..
3.4.d:
स द्विजो वैष्णवं तेजो धृत्वा वै मासि फाल्गुने॥
त्रैलोक्यमतपत्स्वामी देवकार्यपरायणः ॥ 18 ॥
3.4.m: Assuming the splendour of Viṣṇu in the month of Phālguna, / that brāhmaṇa, as master, warmed the three worlds, devoted to the work of the gods.

3.4.s:
sūta uvāca ..
ityuktvā bhagavāñjīvaḥ punaḥ prāha śacīpatim ..
phālgune māsi taṃ sūryaṃ samārādhya sukhī bhava .. .. 19 ..
3.4.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
इत्युक्त्वा भगवाञ्जीवः पुनः प्राह शचीपतिम् ॥
फाल्गुने मासि तं सूर्यं समाराध्य सुखी भव ॥ ॥ 19 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the venerable Jīva again spoke to the lord of Śacī: / "In the month of Phālguna, worship that Sūrya and be happy!"

3.4.s:
ityukto guruṇā devo dhyātvā sarvamayaṃ harim ..
pūjanairbahudhākārairdevadevamapūjayat .. 3.4.10.20 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तो गुरुणा देवो ध्यात्वा सर्वमयं हरिम् ॥
पूजनैर्बहुधाकारैर्देवदेवमपूजयत् ॥ 3.4.10.20 ॥
3.4.m: Addressed thus by his guru, the god [Indra], meditating on Hari who is made of everything, / worshipped the God of gods with offerings of many kinds.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavānsamabhūtsūryamaṇḍalāt ..
caturbhujo hi raktāṃgo yathā yakṣastathaiva saḥ ..
paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ śakradehamupāgamat .. 21 ..
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्समभूत्सूर्यमण्डलात् ॥
चतुर्भुजो हि रक्तांगो यथा यक्षस्तथैव सः ॥
पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां शक्रदेहमुपागमत् ॥ 21 ॥
3.4.m: Then the Blessed Lord, pleased, emerged from the solar orb— / four-armed, red-limbed, resembling a yakṣa; / before the eyes of all the gods, he entered the body of Indra.

3.4.s:
tattejasā tadā śakraḥ svāntarlīya svakaṃ vapuḥ .. .
ayonissa dvijo bhūtvā śacī devī tathaiva sā .. 22 ..
3.4.d:
तत्तेजसा तदा शक्रः स्वान्तर्लीय स्वकं वपुः ॥ ।
अयोनिस्स द्विजो भूत्वा शची देवी तथैव सा ॥ 22 ॥
3.4.m: By his splendour, Indra then dissolved his own form within himself; / unborn of a womb, he became that brāhmaṇa, and goddess Śacī likewise became [his wife].

3.4.s:
tadā tau mithunībhūtau vaiṣṇavāgniprapīḍitau ..
remāte varṣaparyantaṃ gaṃgākūle mahāvane.. ... 23 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तौ मिथुनीभूतौ वैष्णवाग्निप्रपीडितौ ॥
रेमाते वर्षपर्यन्तं गंगाकूले महावने॥ ॥। 23 ॥
3.4.m: Then the two, having become a couple, ignited by the fire of Viṣṇu, / sported for a year in the great forest on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

3.4.s:
adhādgarbhaṃ tadā devī śacī tu dvijarūpiṇī ..
bhādraśukle gurau vāre dvādaśyāṃ brāhmamaṇḍale .. 24 ..
3.4.d:
अधाद्गर्भं तदा देवी शची तु द्विजरूपिणी ॥
भाद्रशुक्ले गुरौ वारे द्वादश्यां ब्राह्ममण्डले ॥ 24 ॥
3.4.m: Then the goddess Śacī, in the form of a brāhmaṇa woman, bore a child in her womb / on the bright twelfth lunar day of Bhādra, on a Thursday, in the Brāhma-maṇḍala.

3.4.s:
prādurāsītsvayaṃ viṣṇurdhṛtvā sarva kalāṃ hariḥ ..
caturbhujaśca raktāṅgo ravikuṃbhasamaprabhaḥ .. 25 ..
3.4.d:
प्रादुरासीत्स्वयं विष्णुर्धृत्वा सर्व कलां हरिः ॥
चतुर्भुजश्च रक्ताङ्गो रविकुंभसमप्रभः ॥ 25 ॥
3.4.m: Viṣṇu Hari manifested himself, bearing every digit [of divinity]— / four-armed, red-limbed, with splendour like the pitcher of the sun.

3.4.s:
tadā rudrāśca vasavo viśvedevā marudgaṇāḥ ..
sādhyāśca bhāskarāḥ siddhāstuṣṭuvustaṃ sanātanam .. 26 ..
3.4.d:
तदा रुद्राश्च वसवो विश्वेदेवा मरुद्गणाः ॥
साध्याश्च भास्कराः सिद्धास्तुष्टुवुस्तं सनातनम् ॥ 26 ॥
3.4.m: Then the Rudras, the Vasus, the Viśvedevas, the hosts of Maruts, / the Sādhyas, the Ādityas, and the Siddhas praised that eternal Lord.

3.4.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
kuliśadhvajapadmagadāṃkuśābhaṃ caraṇaṃ tava nātha mahābharaṇam ..
ramaṇaṃ munibhirvidhiśaṃbhuyutaṃ praṇamāma vayaṃ bhavabhītiharam .. 27 ..
3.4.d:
॥ देवा ऊचुः ॥ ॥
कुलिशध्वजपद्मगदांकुशाभं चरणं तव नाथ महाभरणम् ॥
रमणं मुनिभिर्विधिशंभुयुतं प्रणमाम वयं भवभीतिहरम् ॥ 27 ॥
3.4.m: The gods said: / "O Lord, we bow to your foot, an exalted ornament shining like the thunderbolt, banner, lotus, mace, and elephant goad, / which is the delight of the sages together with Brahmā and Śambhu, and which removes the fear of worldly existence.

3.4.s:
daracakragadāmbujamānadharaḥ suraśatrukaṭhoraśarīraharaḥ ..
sacarācaralokabharaścapalaḥ khalanāśakarassurakārya karaḥ .. 28 ..
3.4.d:
दरचक्रगदाम्बुजमानधरः सुरशत्रुकठोरशरीरहरः ॥
सचराचरलोकभरश्चपलः खलनाशकरस्सुरकार्य करः ॥ 28 ॥
3.4.m: Holding the standard of the conch, discus, mace, and lotus, destroying the fierce bodies of the enemies of the gods, / supporting the moving and unmoving worlds, active, destroying the wicked, performing the work of the gods.

3.4.s:
namaste śacīnaṃdanānandakārinmahāpāpasantāpadurlāpahārin ..
surārīnnihatyāśu lokādhidhārinsvabhaktyāghajātāṅgakoṭi prahārin .. 29 ..
3.4.d:
नमस्ते शचीनंदनानन्दकारिन्महापापसन्तापदुर्लापहारिन् ॥
सुरारीन्निहत्याशु लोकाधिधारिन्स्वभक्त्याघजाताङ्गकोटि प्रहारिन् ॥ 29 ॥
3.4.m: Salutations to you, O son of Śacī, who cause delight, who remove great sins, torments, and evil talk, / who quickly slay the enemies of the gods, who uphold the worlds, who strike down millions of sins born of the body by devotion to you!

3.4.s:
tvayā haṃsarūpeṇa satyaṃ prapālyaṃ tvayā yajñarūpeṇa vedaḥ prarakṣya ..
sa vai yajñarūpo bhavām̐llokadhārī śacīnandanaḥ śakraśarmaprasaktaḥ .. 3.4.10.30 ..
3.4.d:
त्वया हंसरूपेण सत्यं प्रपाल्यं त्वया यज्ञरूपेण वेदः प्ररक्ष्य ॥
स वै यज्ञरूपो भवाम्̐ल्लोकधारी शचीनन्दनः शक्रशर्मप्रसक्तः ॥ 3.4.10.30 ॥
3.4.m: Truth was protected by you in the form of a swan; the Veda was preserved by you in the form of sacrifice. / You, the supporter of the world in the form of sacrifice, are the son of Śacī, devoted to the delight of Indra.

3.4.s:
anarpitacarocirātkaruṇayāvatīrṇaḥ kalau samarpayitumunnatojvalarasāṃ svabhaktiśriyam ..
hareḥ punarasundaradyutikadaṃbasandīpitaḥ sadā sphuratu no hṛdayakandare śacīnaṃdanaḥ .. 31..
3.4.d:
अनर्पितचरोचिरात्करुणयावतीर्णः कलौ समर्पयितुमुन्नतोज्वलरसां स्वभक्तिश्रियम् ॥
हरेः पुनरसुन्दरद्युतिकदंबसन्दीपितः सदा स्फुरतु नो हृदयकन्दरे शचीनंदनः ॥ 31॥
3.4.m: Descended out of compassion in the Kali age, though never before bestowed, to deliver the radiant wealth of his own devotion imbued with exalted, luminous aesthetic emotion— / may that son of Śacī, illuminated by the cluster of Hari's incomparably beautiful radiances, shine forever in the cavern of our hearts!

3.4.s:
visarjati narānbhavānkaruṇayā prapālya kṣitau nivedayitumudbhavaḥ parātparaṃ svakīyaṃ padam ..
kalau ditijasaṃbhavādhivyathābdhisuramagnagānsamuddhara mahāprabho kṛṣṇacaitanya śacīsuta .. 32 ..
3.4.d:
विसर्जति नरान्भवान्करुणया प्रपाल्य क्षितौ निवेदयितुमुद्भवः परात्परं स्वकीयं पदम् ॥
कलौ दितिजसंभवाधिव्यथाब्धिसुरमग्नगान्समुद्धर महाप्रभो कृष्णचैतन्य शचीसुत ॥ 32 ॥
3.4.m: You dispatch men [to this world], protecting them out of compassion on earth, appearing in order to present your own highest abode, beyond the supreme. / In the Kali age, deliver those submerged in the ocean of agony and distress born of the sons of Diti, O great Lord, Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, son of Śacī!

3.4.s:
mādhuryyairmadhubhissugaṃdhavadanaḥ svarṇāṃbujānāṃ vanaṃ kāruṇyā mṛtanirjharairupacitaḥ satpremahemācalaḥ ..
bhaktāṃbhodharadhāriṇī vijayinī niṣkaṃpasaptāvalī devo naḥ kuladevataṃ vijayate caitanyakṛṣṇo hariḥ .. 33 ..
3.4.d:
माधुर्य्यैर्मधुभिस्सुगंधवदनः स्वर्णांबुजानां वनं कारुण्या मृतनिर्झरैरुपचितः सत्प्रेमहेमाचलः ॥
भक्तांभोधरधारिणी विजयिनी निष्कंपसप्तावली देवो नः कुलदेवतं विजयते चैतन्यकृष्णो हरिः ॥ 33 ॥
3.4.m: With a fragrant mouth [sweet] with the sweetness of honey, a forest of golden lotuses, nourished by cascades of the nectar of compassion, a golden mountain of true love, / bearing the clouds of devotees, victorious, with an unshakeable row of seven [modes of devotion], our family deity, the divine Caitanya Kṛṣṇa Hari, triumphs!

3.4.s:
devārātijanairadharmajanitaissapīḍiteyaṃ mahī saṃkucyāśu kalau kalevaramidaṃ bījāya hā vartate ..
tvannāmnaiva surārayo vidalitāḥ pātālagāḥ pīḍitā mlecchā dharmaparāḥ sureśanamanāstasmai namo vyāpine .. 34 ..
3.4.d:
देवारातिजनैरधर्मजनितैस्सपीडितेयं मही संकुच्याशु कलौ कलेवरमिदं बीजाय हा वर्तते ॥
त्वन्नाम्नैव सुरारयो विदलिताः पातालगाः पीडिता म्लेच्छा धर्मपराः सुरेशनमनास्तस्मै नमो व्यापिने ॥ 34 ॥
3.4.m: Afflicted by the enemies of the gods born of unrighteousness, this earth, shrinking rapidly in the Kali age, remains as this body merely for the sake of seed, alas! / By your name alone, the enemies of the gods are shattered, cast into the netherworld, and tormented, while even barbarians become devoted to righteousness and bow to the Lord of the gods. Salutations to that all-pervading One!"

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityabhiṣṭūya puruṣaṃ yajñeśaṃ ca śacīpatim ..
bṛhaspatimupāgamya devā vacanamabruvan .. 35 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्यभिष्टूय पुरुषं यज्ञेशं च शचीपतिम् ॥
बृहस्पतिमुपागम्य देवा वचनमब्रुवन् ॥ 35 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having thus praised the Puruṣa, the Lord of sacrifice, and the husband of Śacī, / the gods approached Bṛhaspati and spoke these words:

3.4.s:
vayaṃ rudrā mahābhāga ime ca vasavo'śvinau ..
kena kenāṃśakenaiva janiṣyāmo mahītale ..
tatsarvaṃ kṛpayā deva vaktu marhati no bhavān .. 36 ..
3.4.d:
वयं रुद्रा महाभाग इमे च वसवोऽश्विनौ ॥
केन केनांशकेनैव जनिष्यामो महीतले ॥
तत्सर्वं कृपया देव वक्तु मर्हति नो भवान् ॥ 36 ॥
3.4.m: "O highly fortunate one, as what portions shall we, the Rudras, / these Vasus, and the two Aśvins, be born on the face of the earth? / You ought, out of compassion, O god, to tell us all that."

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
ahaṃ vaḥ kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ surasattamāḥ ..
purā pūrvabhave cāsīnmṛgavyādho dvijādhamaḥ ..
dhanurbāṇadharo nityaṃ mārge vipravihiṃsakaḥ ..37..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
अहं वः कथयिष्यामि शृणुध्वं सुरसत्तमाः ॥
पुरा पूर्वभवे चासीन्मृगव्याधो द्विजाधमः ॥
धनुर्बाणधरो नित्यं मार्गे विप्रविहिंसकः ॥37॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / "I shall tell you; listen, O best of the gods! / Long ago, in a previous birth, there was a deer-hunter, a vile brāhmaṇa, / always bearing bow and arrows, who harmed brāhmaṇas on the road.

3.4.s:
hatvā dvijānmahāmūḍhasteṣāṃ yajñopavītakam ..
gṛhītvā helayā duṣṭo mahākrośastu tatkṛtaḥ .. 38 ..
3.4.d:
हत्वा द्विजान्महामूढस्तेषां यज्ञोपवीतकम् ॥
गृहीत्वा हेलया दुष्टो महाक्रोशस्तु तत्कृतः ॥ 38 ॥
3.4.m:
Having slain brāhmaṇas, the great fool took their sacred threads
with ease; indeed, that wicked man made a great outcry [among them].

3.4.s:
brāhmaṇasya ca yaddravyaṃ sudhopamamanuttamam ..
madhuraṃ kṣatriyasyaiva vaiśyasyānnasamaṃ smṛtam .. 39 ..
3.4.d:
ब्राह्मणस्य च यद्द्रव्यं सुधोपममनुत्तमम् ॥
मधुरं क्षत्रियस्यैव वैश्यस्यान्नसमं स्मृतम् ॥ 39 ॥
3.4.m:
The property of a brāhmaṇa is like nectar, unsurpassed;
that of a kṣatriya is sweet, while that of a vaiśya is considered equal to ordinary food;

3.4.s:
śūdrasya vastu rudhiramiti jñātvā dvijā dhamaḥ ..
sa jaghāna trivarṇāṃśca brāhmaṇānbahulānkhalaḥ .. 3.4.10.40 ..
3.4.d:
शूद्रस्य वस्तु रुधिरमिति ज्ञात्वा द्विजा धमः ॥
स जघान त्रिवर्णांश्च ब्राह्मणान्बहुलान्खलः ॥ 3.4.10.40 ॥
3.4.m:
and the possession of a śūdra is blood—knowing this, the vile twice-born
slew members of the three varnas, and that villain killed many brāhmaṇas.

3.4.s:
dvijanāśātsurāssarve bhayabhītāssamaṃtataḥ ..
parameṣṭhinamāgamya kathāṃścakuśca kāraṇam.. .. 41 ..
3.4.d:
द्विजनाशात्सुरास्सर्वे भयभीतास्समंततः ॥
परमेष्ठिनमागम्य कथांश्चकुश्च कारणम्॥ ॥ 41 ॥
3.4.m:
From the destruction of the twice-born, all the gods were terrified on every side;
approaching Parameṣṭhin, they told him the tale and the cause.

3.4.s:
śrutvā ca duḥkhito brahmā saptarṣīnprāha lokagān ..
uddeśaṃ kuru tatraiva gatvā tasya dvijottama .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
श्रुत्वा च दुःखितो ब्रह्मा सप्तर्षीन्प्राह लोकगान् ॥
उद्देशं कुरु तत्रैव गत्वा तस्य द्विजोत्तम ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m:
Hearing this, Brahmā was grieved and spoke to the Seven Rṣis who roam the worlds:
“Go right there, O best of the twice-born, and show him guidance!”

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā marīcistu vaśiṣṭhādibhiranvitaḥ ..
tatra gatvā sthitāssarve mṛgavyādhasya vai vane .. 43
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा मरीचिस्तु वशिष्ठादिभिरन्वितः ॥
तत्र गत्वा स्थितास्सर्वे मृगव्याधस्य वै वने ॥ 43
3.4.m:
Hearing this, Marīci, accompanied by Vasiṣṭha and others,
went there, and they all halted in the forest of the hunter.

3.4.s:
mṛgavyādhastu tāndṛṣṭvā dhanurbāṇadharo balī ..
uvāca vacanaṃ ghoraṃ haniṣyehaṃ ca vodya vai .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
मृगव्याधस्तु तान्दृष्ट्वा धनुर्बाणधरो बली ॥
उवाच वचनं घोरं हनिष्येहं च वोद्य वै ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m:
Seeing them, the mighty hunter, bearing bow and arrow,
spoke terrifying words: “Today I shall surely slay you!”

3.4.s:
marīcādyā vihasyāhuḥ kimarthaṃ haṃtumudyataḥ ..
kulārthaṃ vātmano'rthaṃ vā śīghraṃ vada mahābala .. 45 ..
3.4.d:
मरीचाद्या विहस्याहुः किमर्थं हंतुमुद्यतः ॥
कुलार्थं वात्मनोऽर्थं वा शीघ्रं वद महाबल ॥ 45 ॥
3.4.m:
Marīci and the others laughed and said, “Why are you intent on killing?
Is it for the sake of your family or for yourself? Speak quickly, O mighty one!”

3.4.s:
ityuktastāndvijaḥ prāha kulārthaṃ cātmano hite ..
hanmi yuṣmāndhanairyuktānbrāhmaṇām̐śca viśeṣataḥ .. 46 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तस्तान्द्विजः प्राह कुलार्थं चात्मनो हिते ॥
हन्मि युष्मान्धनैर्युक्तान्ब्राह्मणाम्̐श्च विशेषतः ॥ 46 ॥
3.4.m:
Thus addressed, the twice-born said to them: “For the sake of my family and my own welfare,
I slay you who possess riches, and brāhmaṇas in particular.”

3.4.s:
śrutvā tamāhuste viprā gaccha śīghraṃ dhanurdhara ..
viprahatyākṛtaṃ pāpaṃ bhuñjīyātko vicāraya ..47..
3.4.d:
श्रुत्वा तमाहुस्ते विप्रा गच्छ शीघ्रं धनुर्धर ॥
विप्रहत्याकृतं पापं भुञ्जीयात्को विचारय ॥47॥
3.4.m:
Hearing him, those vipras said: “Go quickly, O archer!
Reflect on who will partake of the sin committed by slaying vipras.”

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu ghorātmā teṣāṃ dṛṣṭyā sunirmalaḥ ..
gatvā vaṃśajanānāha bhūri pāpaṃ mayārjitam ..48..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु घोरात्मा तेषां दृष्ट्या सुनिर्मलः ॥
गत्वा वंशजनानाह भूरि पापं मयार्जितम् ॥48॥
3.4.m:
Hearing this, he of terrible soul became completely pure through their gaze;
he went and said to his family members: “Abundant sin has been earned by me.

3.4.s:
tatpāpakaṃ bhavadbhiśca grahaṇīyaṃ dhanaṃ yathā ..
te tu śrutvā dvijaṃ prāhurna vayaṃ pāpabhoginaḥ .. 49 ..
3.4.d:
तत्पापकं भवद्भिश्च ग्रहणीयं धनं यथा ॥
ते तु श्रुत्वा द्विजं प्राहुर्न वयं पापभोगिनः ॥ 49 ॥
3.4.m:
That little sin must be taken by you, just as you take the wealth.”
Hearing him, they said to the twice-born: “We are not partakers of your sin.

3.4.s:
sākṣīyaṃ bhūmiracalā sākṣī sūryo'yamuttamaḥ ..
iti śrutvā mṛgavyādho munīnāha kṛtāṃjaliḥ .. 3.4.10.50 ..
3.4.d:
साक्षीयं भूमिरचला साक्षी सूर्योऽयमुत्तमः ॥
इति श्रुत्वा मृगव्याधो मुनीनाह कृतांजलिः ॥ 3.4.10.50 ॥
3.4.m:
This unmoving earth is witness, and this supreme sun is witness!”
Hearing this, the hunter, with folded hands, said to the sages:

3.4.s:
yathā pāpaṃ kṣayaṃ yāti tathā mājñātumarhatha ..
ityuktāstena te prāhuḥ śṛṇu tvaṃ maṃtramuttamam .. 51 ..
3.4.d:
यथा पापं क्षयं याति तथा माज्ञातुमर्हथ ॥
इत्युक्तास्तेन ते प्राहुः शृणु त्वं मंत्रमुत्तमम् ॥ 51 ॥
3.4.m:
“You ought to teach me so that my sin may be destroyed.”
Thus addressed by him, they said: “Hear the supreme mantra!

3.4.s:
rāma nāma hi tajjñeyaṃ sarvāghaughavināśanam ..
yāvattvatpārśvamāyāmastāvattvaṃ japa cottamam .. 52 ..
3.4.d:
राम नाम हि तज्ज्ञेयं सर्वाघौघविनाशनम् ॥
यावत्त्वत्पार्श्वमायामस्तावत्त्वं जप चोत्तमम् ॥ 52 ॥
3.4.m:
It is known as the name ‘Rāma’, which destroys the flood of all sins.
Until we come back to your side, do you recite this supreme [name].”

3.4.s:
ityuktvā te gatā viprāstīrthāttīrthāntaraṃ prati ..
marāmarāmaretyevaṃ sahasrābdaṃ jajāpa ha .. 53 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा ते गता विप्रास्तीर्थात्तीर्थान्तरं प्रति ॥
मरामरामरेत्येवं सहस्राब्दं जजाप ह ॥ 53 ॥
3.4.m:
Having spoken thus, those vipras departed from holy site to holy site;
and he muttered “Marā, Marā, Marā” for a thousand years.

3.4.s:
japaprabhāvādabhavadvanamutpalasaṃkulam ..
tatsthānamutpalāraṇyaṃ prasiddhamabhavadbhuvi.. 54 ..
3.4.d:
जपप्रभावादभवद्वनमुत्पलसंकुलम् ॥
तत्स्थानमुत्पलारण्यं प्रसिद्धमभवद्भुवि॥ 54 ॥
3.4.m:
By the power of his recitation, the forest became filled with lotuses;
that place became famous on earth as the Utpalāraṇya.

3.4.s:
tataḥ saptarṣayaḥ prāptā valmīkāttaṃ nirākṛtam ..
dṛṣṭvā śuddhaṃ tadā vipramūcuste vismayānvitāḥ .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
ततः सप्तर्षयः प्राप्ता वल्मीकात्तं निराकृतम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा शुद्धं तदा विप्रमूचुस्ते विस्मयान्विताः ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m:
Then the Seven Ṛṣis arrived, and seeing that pure vipra
emerged from an anthill, they spoke with wonder:

3.4.s:
valmīkānnissṛto yasmāttasmādvālmīkiruttamam ..
tava nāma bhavedvipra trikālajña mahāmate .. 56 ..
3.4.d:
वल्मीकान्निस्सृतो यस्मात्तस्माद्वाल्मीकिरुत्तमम् ॥
तव नाम भवेद्विप्र त्रिकालज्ञ महामते ॥ 56 ॥
3.4.m:
“Because you came forth from an anthill (valmīka), therefore ‘Vālmīki’
shall be your supreme name, O wise vipra who knows past, present, and future!”

3.4.s:
evamuktvā yayurlokaṃ sa tu rāmāyaṇaṃ muniḥ ..
kalpāṣṭādaśayuktaṃ hi śatakoṭipravistaram ..57..
3.4.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ययुर्लोकं स तु रामायणं मुनिः ॥
कल्पाष्टादशयुक्तं हि शतकोटिप्रविस्तरम् ॥57॥
3.4.m:
Having spoken thus, they went to their world; and that sage [composed] the Rāmāyaṇa,
consisting of eighteen kalpas and extending to a hundred crores [of verses].

3.4.s:
cakāra nirmalaṃ padyaiḥ sarvāghaughavināśanam ..
tatpaścātsa śivo bhūtvā tatra vāsamakārayat .. 58 ..
3.4.d:
चकार निर्मलं पद्यैः सर्वाघौघविनाशनम् ॥
तत्पश्चात्स शिवो भूत्वा तत्र वासमकारयत् ॥ 58 ॥
3.4.m:
He made it spotless in verse, destroying the flood of all sins.
After that, he became Śiva and made his dwelling there.

3.4.s:
adyāpi saṃsthitaḥ svāmī mṛgavyādhaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
śṛṇudhvaṃ ca surāḥ sarve taccaritraṃ harapriyam .. 59 ..
3.4.d:
अद्यापि संस्थितः स्वामी मृगव्याधः सनातनः ॥
शृणुध्वं च सुराः सर्वे तच्चरित्रं हरप्रियम् ॥ 59 ॥
3.4.m:
Even today, the eternal master, the hunter, remains there.
Hear, all you gods, his deed dear to Hara!

3.4.s:
vaivasvate'ntare prāpte cādye satyayuge śubhe ..
brahmāgatyotpalāraṇyaṃ tatra yajñaṃ cakāra ha .. 3.4.10.60 ..
3.4.d:
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे प्राप्ते चाद्ये सत्ययुगे शुभे ॥
ब्रह्मागत्योत्पलारण्यं तत्र यज्ञं चकार ह ॥ 3.4.10.60 ॥
3.4.m:
When the Vaivasvata interval arrived in the first auspicious Kṛtayuga,
Brahmā, having come to Utpalāraṇya, performed a sacrifice there.

3.4.s:
tadā sarasvatī devī nadī bhūtvā samāgatā ..
taddarśanātsvayaṃ brahmā mukhato brāhmaṇaṃ śubham.. 61 ..
3.4.d:
तदा सरस्वती देवी नदी भूत्वा समागता ॥
तद्दर्शनात्स्वयं ब्रह्मा मुखतो ब्राह्मणं शुभम्॥ 61 ॥
3.4.m:
Then goddess Sarasvatī, having become a river, arrived;
at the sight of her, the potent Brahmā himself [produced] from his mouth the auspicious brāhmaṇa,

3.4.s:
bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyaṃ caiva corubhyāṃ vaiśyamuttamam ..
padbhyāṃ śūdraṃ śubhācāraṃ janayāmāsa vīryavān .. 62 ..
3.4.d:
बाहुभ्यां क्षत्रियं चैव चोरुभ्यां वैश्यमुत्तमम् ॥
पद्भ्यां शूद्रं शुभाचारं जनयामास वीर्यवान् ॥ 62 ॥
3.4.m:
from his arms the kṣatriya, from his thighs the excellent vaiśya,
and from his feet he produced the śūdra of auspicious conduct.

3.4.s:
dvijarājastathā somaścaṃdramā nāmato dvijaḥ ..
loke sarvātapaḥ sūryaḥ kaśyaṃ vīryaṃ hi pāti yaḥ .. 63 ..
3.4.d:
द्विजराजस्तथा सोमश्चंद्रमा नामतो द्विजः ॥
लोके सर्वातपः सूर्यः कश्यं वीर्यं हि पाति यः ॥ 63 ॥
3.4.m:
Likewise, Soma, the king of the twice-born, and the moon is a twice-born by name;
the sun gives all heat in the world, and he who protects the kaśya-virility,

3.4.s:
kaśyapo hi dvitīyo'sau marīcistu tato'bhavat ..
ratnānāmākaro yo vai sa hi ratnākaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 64..
3.4.d:
कश्यपो हि द्वितीयोऽसौ मरीचिस्तु ततोऽभवत् ॥
रत्नानामाकरो यो वै स हि रत्नाकरः स्मृतः ॥ 64॥
3.4.m:
he was Kaśyapa, that second one; and Marīci arose from him;
he who is a mine of gems is known as Ratnākara;

3.4.s:
lokāndharati yo dravyaiḥ sa tu dharmo hi nāmataḥ ..
gaṃbhīraścāsti sadṛśaḥ kośo yasya saritpatiḥ .. 65 ..
3.4.d:
लोकान्धरति यो द्रव्यैः स तु धर्मो हि नामतः ॥
गंभीरश्चास्ति सदृशः कोशो यस्य सरित्पतिः ॥ 65 ॥
3.4.m:
he who upholds the worlds with riches is Dharma by name;
he is deep, like whom the lord of rivers is his treasury;

3.4.s:
lokāndakṣati yaḥ kṛtyaiḥ sa tu dakṣaḥ prajāpatiḥ ..
brahmaṇoṃgācca te jātāstasmādvai brāhmaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 66 ..
3.4.d:
लोकान्दक्षति यः कृत्यैः स तु दक्षः प्रजापतिः ॥
ब्रह्मणोंगाच्च ते जातास्तस्माद्वै ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः ॥ 66 ॥
3.4.m:
he who shows skill toward the worlds through duties is Dakṣa Prajāpati.
They were born from the body of Brahmā; therefore they are remembered as brāhmaṇas.

3.4.s:
varṇadharmeṇa te sarve varṇātmānaśca vai kramāt ..
dakṣasya manaso jātāḥ kanyāḥ paṃcaśataṃ tataḥ ..
viṣṇu māyāprabhāvena kalābhūtāḥ sthitā bhuvi ..67..
3.4.d:
वर्णधर्मेण ते सर्वे वर्णात्मानश्च वै क्रमात् ॥
दक्षस्य मनसो जाताः कन्याः पंचशतं ततः ॥
विष्णु मायाप्रभावेन कलाभूताः स्थिता भुवि ॥67॥

3.4.s:
tadā tu bhagavānbrahmā somāyāśvinimaṇḍalam ..
saptaviṃśadgaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dadau lokavivṛddhaye ..68..
3.4.d:
तदा तु भगवान्ब्रह्मा सोमायाश्विनिमण्डलम् ॥
सप्तविंशद्गणं श्रेष्ठं ददौ लोकविवृद्धये ॥68॥
3.4.m:
Then the lord Brahmā gave to Soma the group of twenty-seven best [daughters],
the circle of Aśvinī [and the others], for the increase of the world.

3.4.s:
kaśyapāyāditigaṇaṃ kṣatrarūpaṃ trayodaśam ..
dharmāya kīrtiprabhṛtīrdadau sa ca mahāmuniḥ .. 69 ..
3.4.d:
कश्यपायादितिगणं क्षत्ररूपं त्रयोदशम् ॥
धर्माय कीर्तिप्रभृतीर्ददौ स च महामुनिः ॥ 69 ॥
3.4.m:
To Kaśyapa he gave the thirteen, the group of Aditi, having the form of sovereignty;
and to Dharma that great sage gave Kīrti and the rest.

3.4.s:
nānāvidhāni sṛṣṭāni cāsanvaivasvate'ntare ..
teṣāṃ patistvayaṃ dakṣo'bhūdvidherājñayā bhuvi .. 3.4.10.70 ..
3.4.d:
नानाविधानि सृष्टानि चासन्वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे ॥
तेषां पतिस्त्वयं दक्षोऽभूद्विधेराज्ञया भुवि ॥ 3.4.10.70 ॥
3.4.m:
Various kinds of creatures were created in the Vaivasvata interval;
by the command of the Ordainer, this Dakṣa became their lord on earth.

3.4.s:
tatra vāsaṃ svayaṃ dakṣaḥ kṛtavānyajñatatparaḥ ..
sarve devagaṇā dakṣaṃ namaskṛtya caraṃti hi ..71..
3.4.d:
तत्र वासं स्वयं दक्षः कृतवान्यज्ञतत्परः ॥
सर्वे देवगणा दक्षं नमस्कृत्य चरंति हि ॥71॥
3.4.m:
Dakṣa himself took up dwelling there, intent on sacrifice.
All the hosts of gods go about bowing to Dakṣa;

3.4.s:
bhūtanātho mahādevo na nanāma kadācana ..
tadā kruddhaḥ svayaṃ dakṣaḥ śivabhāgaṃ na dattavān .. 72 ..
3.4.d:
भूतनाथो महादेवो न ननाम कदाचन ॥
तदा क्रुद्धः स्वयं दक्षः शिवभागं न दत्तवान् ॥ 72 ॥
3.4.m:
Mahādeva, the lord of beings, never bowed.
Then Dakṣa himself became angry and did not give Śiva his share.

3.4.s:
mṛgavyādhaḥ śivaḥ kruddho vīrabhadro babhūva ha ..
triśirāśca trinetraśca tripadastatra cāgataḥ .. 73 ..
3.4.d:
मृगव्याधः शिवः क्रुद्धो वीरभद्रो बभूव ह ॥
त्रिशिराश्च त्रिनेत्रश्च त्रिपदस्तत्र चागतः ॥ 73 ॥
3.4.m:
Angry Śiva became the hunter and Vīrabhadra;
three-headed, three-eyed, and three-footed, he arrived there.

3.4.s:
tenaiva pīḍitā devā munayaḥ pitaro'bhavan ..
tadā vai yajñapuruṣo bhayabhītaḥ samaṃtataḥ .. 74 ..
3.4.d:
तेनैव पीडिता देवा मुनयः पितरोऽभवन् ॥
तदा वै यज्ञपुरुषो भयभीतः समंततः ॥ 74 ॥
3.4.m:
The gods, sages, and ancestors were afflicted by him alone;
then the Sacrifice Person became terrified on every side.

3.4.s:
mṛgabhūto yayau tūrṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā vyādhaḥ śivobhavat ..
rudravyādhena sa mṛgo vibhinnāṅgo babhūva ha .. 75 ..
3.4.d:
मृगभूतो ययौ तूर्णं दृष्ट्वा व्याधः शिवोभवत् ॥
रुद्रव्याधेन स मृगो विभिन्नाङ्गो बभूव ह ॥ 75 ॥
3.4.m:
Having assumed the form of a deer, he fled swiftly; seeing him, Śiva became a hunter.
By the Rudra-hunter, that deer had his limbs torn apart.

3.4.s:
tadā tu bhagavānbrahmā tuṣṭāva madhurasvaraiḥ ..
saṃtuṣṭaśca mṛgavyādho yajñaṃ pūrṇamakārayat .. 76 ..
3.4.d:
तदा तु भगवान्ब्रह्मा तुष्टाव मधुरस्वरैः ॥
संतुष्टश्च मृगव्याधो यज्ञं पूर्णमकारयत् ॥ 76 ॥
3.4.m:
Then the lord Brahmā praised him with sweet voices;
and the hunter, being pleased, had the sacrifice completed.

3.4.s:
tulārāśisthite bhānau taṃ rudraṃ candramaṇḍale ..
sthāpayitvā svayaṃ brahmā saptaviṃśaddinātmake ..
prayayau saptalokaṃ vai sa rudraścaṃdrarūpavān .. 77 ..
3.4.d:
तुलाराशिस्थिते भानौ तं रुद्रं चन्द्रमण्डले ॥
स्थापयित्वा स्वयं ब्रह्मा सप्तविंशद्दिनात्मके ॥
प्रययौ सप्तलोकं वै स रुद्रश्चंद्ररूपवान् ॥ 77 ॥
3.4.m:
When the sun stood in the sign of Libra, Brahmā himself,
having placed that Rudra in the orb of the moon consisting of twenty-seven days,
went away to the seven worlds; and that Rudra had the form of the moon.

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vīrabhadro rudraḥ saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ ..
svāṃśaṃ dehātsamutpādya dvijagehamacodayat .. 78 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वीरभद्रो रुद्रः संहृष्टमानसः ॥
स्वांशं देहात्समुत्पाद्य द्विजगेहमचोदयत् ॥ 78 ॥
3.4.m:
Hearing this, Vīrabhadra-Rudra, with a delighted mind,
emitted a portion of himself from his body and sent it to the house of a twice-born.

3.4.s:
vipra bhairavadattasya gehaṃ gatvā sa vai śivaḥ ..
tatputro'bhūtkalau ghore śaṃkaro nāma viśrutaḥ ..79..
3.4.d:
विप्र भैरवदत्तस्य गेहं गत्वा स वै शिवः ॥
तत्पुत्रोऽभूत्कलौ घोरे शंकरो नाम विश्रुतः ॥79॥
3.4.m:
Having gone to the house of the vipra Bhairavadatta, that Śiva
became his son in the terrible Kali age, renowned by the name Śaṅkara.

3.4.s:
sa bālaśca guṇī vettā brahmacārī babhūva ha ..
kṛtvā śaṃkarabhāṣyaṃ ca śaivamārgamadarśayat .. 3.4.10.80 ..
3.4.d:
स बालश्च गुणी वेत्ता ब्रह्मचारी बभूव ह ॥
कृत्वा शंकरभाष्यं च शैवमार्गमदर्शयत् ॥ 3.4.10.80 ॥
3.4.m: That boy became virtuous, wise, and a celibate student. / Having composed the Śaṅkarabhāṣya, he revealed the Śaiva path.

3.4.s:
tripuṇḍraścākṣamālā ca maṃtraḥ paṃcākṣaraḥ śubhaḥ ..
śaivānāṃ maṃgalakaraḥ śaṃkarācāryanirmitaḥ .. 81 ..
ānandagirivanaśarmapurīśarmautpattivarṇanam
3.4.d:
त्रिपुण्ड्रश्चाक्षमाला च मंत्रः पंचाक्षरः शुभः ॥
शैवानां मंगलकरः शंकराचार्यनिर्मितः ॥ 81 ॥
आनन्दगिरिवनशर्मपुरीशर्मौत्पत्तिवर्णनम्
3.4.m:
The tripuṇḍra, the rosary of akṣa beads, and the auspicious five-syllable mantra, / bringing welfare to the Śaivas, were instituted by Śaṅkarācārya.
The description of the birth of Ānandagiri, Vanaśarman, and Purīśarman.

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
purā tu naimiṣāraṇye vipraścājagaro'bhavat.
vedāntaśāstranipuṇo jñānavāñchambhupūjakaḥ..1..
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
पुरा तु नैमिषारण्ये विप्रश्चाजगरोऽभवत्।
वेदान्तशास्त्रनिपुणो ज्ञानवाञ्छम्भुपूजकः॥1॥
