3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Formerly, in the Naimiṣa forest, there was a brāhmaṇa named Ajagara, / skilled in the Vedānta scriptures, full of knowledge, and a worshipper of Śambhu.

3.4.s:
dvādaśābdāntare rudrastuṣṭo'bhūtpārthivārcanāt .
tadāgatya dadau jñānaṃ jīvanmokṣatvamāgataḥ . . 2
3.4.d:
द्वादशाब्दान्तरे रुद्रस्तुष्टोऽभूत्पार्थिवार्चनात् ।
तदागत्य ददौ ज्ञानं जीवन्मोक्षत्वमागतः ॥ 2
3.4.m: After twelve years, Rudra was pleased with his worship of the earthen liṅga. / Coming then, he gave him knowledge, and he attained liberation while living.

3.4.s:
saṅkarṣaṇaṃ samārādhya tajjñānena dvijottamaḥ .
tuṣṭāva puṣkalābhiśca stutibhiḥ parameśvaram . . 3
3.4.d:
सङ्कर्षणं समाराध्य तज्ज्ञानेन द्विजोत्तमः ।
तुष्टाव पुष्कलाभिश्च स्तुतिभिः परमेश्वरम् ॥ 3
3.4.m: Having worshipped Saṅkarṣaṇa with that knowledge, that best of brāhmaṇas / praised the Supreme Lord with copious hymns of praise.

3.4.s:
ajagara uvāca
sadaivyaṃ pradhānaṃ paraṃ jyotirūpaṃ nirākāramavyaktamānandanityam .
tridhā tattu jātaṃ triliṅgaikyabhinnaṃ pumānsattvarūpo rajorūpanārī . .
tayoryattu śeṣaṃ tamorūpameva tataśśeṣanāmne namastenamaste . . 4
3.4.d:
अजगर उवाच
सदैव्यं प्रधानं परं ज्योतिरूपं निराकारमव्यक्तमानन्दनित्यम् ।
त्रिधा तत्तु जातं त्रिलिङ्गैक्यभिन्नं पुमान्सत्त्वरूपो रजोरूपनारी ॥
तयोर्यत्तु शेषं तमोरूपमेव ततश्शेषनाम्ने नमस्तेनमस्ते ॥ 4
3.4.m: Ajagara said: / Always divine, the unmanifest source, supreme, possessing the form of light, formless, unmanifest, eternal bliss, / that [reality] became threefold, divided into the union of the three genders: the male having the form of sattva, the female having the form of rajas, / and that which is their remainder, having the form of tamas; therefore, praise, praise unto you whose name is Śeṣa!

3.4.s:
rajaścādibhūto guṇasyaiva māyā tathā madhyabhūto narassattvarūpam .
tathaivāntabhūto napuṃskaṃ tamovatsadaivādya nāgeśa tubhyaṃ namaste . . 5
3.4.d:
रजश्चादिभूतो गुणस्यैव माया तथा मध्यभूतो नरस्सत्त्वरूपम् ।
तथैवान्तभूतो नपुंस्कं तमोवत्सदैवाद्य नागेश तुभ्यं नमस्ते ॥ 5
3.4.m: Rajas is the primary element of the quality, Māyā; and in the middle is man, the form of sattva; / likewise, at the end is the neuter, like tamas; eternal, primeval lord of serpents, praise unto you!

3.4.s:
narādhārarūpo bhavānkālakartā narākarṣaṇastvaṃ hi saṅkarṣaṇaśca .
ramante munīśāstvayi brahmadhāmni namastenamaste punaste namo'stu . .
narāṅgeṣu cādhārabhūtā śivā yā smṛtā yoganidrā hi śaktistvadīyā . . 6
3.4.d:
नराधाररूपो भवान्कालकर्ता नराकर्षणस्त्वं हि सङ्कर्षणश्च ।
रमन्ते मुनीशास्त्वयि ब्रह्मधाम्नि नमस्तेनमस्ते पुनस्ते नमोऽस्तु ॥
नराङ्गेषु चाधारभूता शिवा या स्मृता योगनिद्रा हि शक्तिस्त्वदीया ॥ 6
3.4.m: You are the foundation of humanity, the maker of time; you draw in men, and are indeed Saṅkarṣaṇa. / The lords of sages delight in you, the realm of Brahman; praise, praise unto you, and once again praise be unto you! / And that auspicious goddess who is the foundation in human limbs is remembered as Yoganidrā, your very own power.

3.4.s:
jīva uvāca
evaṃ hi saṃstuto devo dvijaṃ cājagaraṃ prabhuḥ .
sāyujyaṃ kṛtavānsvāṅge rudraḥ sarpo hi so'bhavat . . 7
3.4.d:
जीव उवाच
एवं हि संस्तुतो देवो द्विजं चाजगरं प्रभुः ।
सायुज्यं कृतवान्स्वाङ्गे रुद्रः सर्पो हि सोऽभवत् ॥ 7
3.4.m: Jīva said: / Thus praised, the lord and god Rudra united the brāhmaṇa Ajagara / into his own body, and he indeed became a serpent.

3.4.s:
phaṇāsahasrasahito gaurāṅgo gauravigrahaḥ .
kṣīrābdhau mandiraṃ yasya babhūva ca guṇākaram . . 8
3.4.d:
फणासहस्रसहितो गौराङ्गो गौरविग्रहः ।
क्षीराब्धौ मन्दिरं यस्य बभूव च गुणाकरम् ॥ 8
3.4.m: Endowed with a thousand hoods, white-limbed, of fair body, / his abode, a mine of virtues, was in the ocean of milk.

3.4.s:
taṃ sarpākhyaṃ mahārudraṃ pratyāgatyātmabhūḥ svayam .
karkarāśisthite sūrye candre bhagaṇamaṇḍale . . 9
3.4.d:
तं सर्पाख्यं महारुद्रं प्रत्यागत्यात्मभूः स्वयम् ।
कर्कराशिस्थिते सूर्ये चन्द्रे भगणमण्डले ॥ 9
3.4.m: Approaching that Mahārudra known as the serpent, the Self-born one himself, / when the sun was in the sign of Cancer and the moon in the lunar mansion,

3.4.s:
taṃ rudraṃ sthāpayāmāsa candramāḥ sa tu cābhavat .
iti śrutvā śeṣanāgo rudraḥ śrīgurubhāṣitam . . 3.4.11.10
3.4.d:
तं रुद्रं स्थापयामास चन्द्रमाः स तु चाभवत् ।
इति श्रुत्वा शेषनागो रुद्रः श्रीगुरुभाषितम् ॥ 3.4.11.10
3.4.m: established that Rudra, and he became Candramas. / Having heard these words spoken by the holy guru, the serpent Śeṣa, Rudra,

3.4.s:
vacanaṃ sa prasannātmā teja utpādya vai mukhāt .
vindhyādrau janayāmāsa devadattadvijālaye . . 11
3.4.d:
वचनं स प्रसन्नात्मा तेज उत्पाद्य वै मुखात् ।
विन्ध्याद्रौ जनयामास देवदत्तद्विजालये ॥ 11
3.4.m: with a delighted mind, brought forth light from his mouth / and caused it to be born on the Vindhya mountain in the home of the brāhmaṇa Devadatta.

3.4.s:
giriśarmā sa vai vipro vijitya viduṣāṃ gaṇān .
kāśīpurīṃ samāyātaḥ śiṣyobhūcchaṅkarasya vai . . 12
3.4.d:
गिरिशर्मा स वै विप्रो विजित्य विदुषां गणान् ।
काशीपुरीं समायातः शिष्योभूच्छङ्करस्य वै ॥ 12
3.4.m: That brāhmaṇa Giriśarman, having defeated hosts of scholars, / arrived at the city of Kāśī and became a disciple of Śaṅkara.

3.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā rudro babhūva ha .
punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ vipra yathā jīvena bhāṣitām . . 13
3.4.d:
इति ते कथितं विप्र यथा रुद्रो बभूव ह ।
पुनः शृणु कथां विप्र यथा जीवेन भाषिताम् ॥ 13
3.4.m: Thus has it been told to you, O brāhmaṇa, how he became Rudra. / Hear again the story, O brāhmaṇa, as told by Jīva.

3.4.s:
jīva uvāca
prayāge ca purā hyāsīdbrāhmaṇo harisevakaḥ .
dāridryārtto mandabhāgyo nairṛto nāma viśrutaḥ . . 14
3.4.d:
जीव उवाच
प्रयागे च पुरा ह्यासीद्ब्राह्मणो हरिसेवकः ।
दारिद्र्यार्त्तो मन्दभाग्यो नैरृतो नाम विश्रुतः ॥ 14
3.4.m: Jīva said: / Formerly, in Prayāga, there was a brāhmaṇa who was a servant of Hari, / afflicted by poverty, unfortunate, renowned by the name Nairṛta.

3.4.s:
mahākaṣṭena tasyaiva bhikṣā prāptā dināntake .
nairṛtaḥ putrapatnīko dāridryārto dinedine . . 15
3.4.d:
महाकष्टेन तस्यैव भिक्षा प्राप्ता दिनान्तके ।
नैरृतः पुत्रपत्नीको दारिद्र्यार्तो दिनेदिने ॥ 15
3.4.m: Only with great hardship did he obtain alms at the end of the day. / Accompanied by his wife and son, Nairṛta was afflicted by poverty day after day.

3.4.s:
ekadā nārado yogī samprāpto vaiṣṇavapriyaḥ .
pūjitastena vipreṇa viṣṇulokamupāyayau . . 16
3.4.d:
एकदा नारदो योगी सम्प्राप्तो वैष्णवप्रियः ।
पूजितस्तेन विप्रेण विष्णुलोकमुपाययौ ॥ 16
3.4.m: Once, the yogin Nārada arrived, beloved of the Vaiṣṇavas. / Worshipped by that brāhmaṇa, he departed for the world of Viṣṇu.

3.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ namaskṛtya punaḥpunaḥ .
vacanaṃ prāha namrātmā sadaiva bhagavatpriyaḥ . . 17
3.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा नारायणं देवं नमस्कृत्य पुनःपुनः ।
वचनं प्राह नम्रात्मा सदैव भगवत्प्रियः ॥ 17
3.4.m: Seeing the god Nārāyaṇa, bowing down again and again, / humble-minded, ever dear to the Lord, he spoke these words:

3.4.s:
bhagavanye surāḥ sarve sadā tvatpūjane ratāḥ .
teṣāṃ bhaktāśca ye bhūmau dhanadhānyasamanvitāḥ . . 18
3.4.d:
भगवन्ये सुराः सर्वे सदा त्वत्पूजने रताः ।
तेषां भक्ताश्च ये भूमौ धनधान्यसमन्विताः ॥ 18
3.4.m: "O Lord, all those gods who are ever devoted to worshipping you, / their devotees on earth are endowed with wealth and grain.

3.4.s:
tvadbhaktāśca mayā dṛṣṭā dāridyārtāḥ sadā bhuvi .
kimarthaṃ brūhi me svāmiñjanārdana namo'stu te . . 19
3.4.d:
त्वद्भक्ताश्च मया दृष्टा दारिद्यार्ताः सदा भुवि ।
किमर्थं ब्रूहि मे स्वामिञ्जनार्दन नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 19
3.4.m: Yet your devotees on earth are seen by me to be ever afflicted by poverty. / For what reason? Tell me, O Master Janārdana, praise be unto you!"

3.4.s:
ityukto nāradenaiva bhagavānbhaktavatsalaḥ .
tamāha vacanaṃ ramyaṃ tacchṛṇu tvaṃ surottama . . 3.4.11.20
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तो नारदेनैव भगवान्भक्तवत्सलः ।
तमाह वचनं रम्यं तच्छृणु त्वं सुरोत्तम ॥ 3.4.11.20
3.4.m: Thus addressed by Nārada, the Blessed Lord, affectionate to his devotees, / addressed pleasing words to him; hear that, O best of the gods.

3.4.s:
madbhakto bhagavānbrahmā dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇapriyān .
janām̐śca svavaśīkṛtya lokakāryaṃ karoti hi . . 21
3.4.d:
मद्भक्तो भगवान्ब्रह्मा दृष्ट्वा नारायणप्रियान् ।
जनाम्̐श्च स्ववशीकृत्य लोककार्यं करोति हि ॥ 21
3.4.m: "My devotee, the blessed Brahmā, seeing people beloved of Nārāyaṇa, / brings them under his sway and carries out the affairs of the worlds.

3.4.s:
dharmo'dharmastena kṛto dharmo vedamayaḥ smṛtaḥ .
sapta lokāśca dharmasya nirmitāstena dhīmatā . . 22
3.4.d:
धर्मोऽधर्मस्तेन कृतो धर्मो वेदमयः स्मृतः ।
सप्त लोकाश्च धर्मस्य निर्मितास्तेन धीमता ॥ 22
3.4.m: Dharma and adharma were made by him; dharma is remembered as consisting of the Veda. / Seven worlds of dharma were created by that wise one:

3.4.s:
bhūrbhuvaḥ svo mahaścaiva janaścaiva tapastathā .
satyaṃ tathaiva kramato nṛṇāṃ dviguṇadaṃ sukham . . 23
3.4.d:
भूर्भुवः स्वो महश्चैव जनश्चैव तपस्तथा ।
सत्यं तथैव क्रमतो नृणां द्विगुणदं सुखम् ॥ 23
3.4.m: Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, and likewise Tapaḥ, / and Satya; in this order, they grant doubled happiness to humans.

3.4.s:
adharmo vedarahito bhuvi śabdānyakartṛkaḥ .
ye śabdāśca mahāvāṇyā dūṣitāste hi lokagāḥ . . 24
3.4.d:
अधर्मो वेदरहितो भुवि शब्दान्यकर्तृकः ।
ये शब्दाश्च महावाण्या दूषितास्ते हि लोकगाः ॥ 24
3.4.m: Adharma is devoid of the Veda, made of other sounds on earth. / Those sounds which are corrupted by the Great Voice, they dwell in the worlds.

3.4.s:
vedetara pāpamayā daityavṛddhikarāḥ sadā .
adharmaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ saptalokāśca tasya vai . . 25
3.4.d:
वेदेतर पापमया दैत्यवृद्धिकराः सदा ।
अधर्मः स तु विज्ञेयः सप्तलोकाश्च तस्य वै ॥ 25
3.4.m: They are outside the Veda, full of sin, constantly increasing the daityas. / That is to be understood as adharma; and its seven worlds,

3.4.s:
bhūmigarteṣu vidhinā nirmitāḥ sukhadāyakāḥ .
atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva sutalaṃ ca talātalam . .
mahātalaṃ rasā caiva pātālaṃ cānyadharmajam . . 26
3.4.d:
भूमिगर्तेषु विधिना निर्मिताः सुखदायकाः ।
अतलं वितलं चैव सुतलं च तलातलम् ॥
महातलं रसा चैव पातालं चान्यधर्मजम् ॥ 26
3.4.m: created in the cavities of the earth by the Creator, bestow comfort: / Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Talātala, / Mahātala, Rasā[tala], and Pātāla, born of another dharma.

3.4.s:
anyadharmo hyadharmaśca devāstvanye hi te'surāḥ .
dharmapakṣāḥ surā jñeyā asurāścānyadharmajāḥ . . 27
3.4.d:
अन्यधर्मो ह्यधर्मश्च देवास्त्वन्ये हि तेऽसुराः ।
धर्मपक्षाः सुरा ज्ञेया असुराश्चान्यधर्मजाः ॥ 27
3.4.m: That other dharma is indeed adharma; and the other gods are those asuras. / The gods are known to be on the side of dharma, and the asuras are born of the other dharma.

3.4.s:
tayorvihīno yo dharmo devairdetyaiśca dūṣitaḥ .
vidharmaḥ sa nu vijñeyastatra lokā vyathākulāḥ . . 28
3.4.d:
तयोर्विहीनो यो धर्मो देवैर्देत्यैश्च दूषितः ।
विधर्मः स नु विज्ञेयस्तत्र लोका व्यथाकुलाः ॥ 28
3.4.m: The conduct devoid of both, condemned by both gods and daityas, / is known as vidharma; there the worlds are agitated by suffering:

3.4.s:
tāmisramandhatāmisraṃ kumbhīpākaśca rauravam .
mahārauravamevāpi tathāmūrtirayastathā . . 29
3.4.d:
तामिस्रमन्धतामिस्रं कुम्भीपाकश्च रौरवम् ।
महारौरवमेवापि तथामूर्तिरयस्तथा ॥ 29
3.4.m: Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Kumbhīpāka, Raurava, / Mahāraurava, and likewise Amūrtirayas,

3.4.s:
ikṣuyantraṃ śālmalaṃ ca hyasipatravanaṃ tathā .
jñeyamityeva racitaṃ vidhinā caikaviṃśatiḥ . . 3.4.11.30
3.4.d:
इक्षुयन्त्रं शाल्मलं च ह्यसिपत्रवनं तथा ।
ज्ञेयमित्येव रचितं विधिना चैकविंशतिः ॥ 3.4.11.30
3.4.m: Ikṣuyantra, Śālmala, and Asipatravana; / thus are twenty-one [hells] arranged and created by the Creator.

3.4.s:
brahmāṇḍo'yaṃ lokamayaḥ paraṃ tasmācca matpadam .
madbhaktā bhūtale ye vai te gacchanti paraṃ padam . . 31
3.4.d:
ब्रह्माण्डोऽयं लोकमयः परं तस्माच्च मत्पदम् ।
मद्भक्ता भूतले ये वै ते गच्छन्ति परं पदम् ॥ 31
3.4.m: This cosmic egg consists of worlds, but higher than that is my abode. / Those who are my devotees on the surface of the earth go to that supreme abode.

3.4.s:
devabhaktāśca ye lokāḥ sapta lokānvrajanti te .
ye tu vai tāmasā lokā daityapūjanatatparāḥ . .
te gacchanti bhahīlokānatalādimayām̐stathā . . 32
3.4.d:
देवभक्ताश्च ये लोकाः सप्त लोकान्व्रजन्ति ते ।
ये तु वै तामसा लोका दैत्यपूजनतत्पराः ॥
ते गच्छन्ति भहीलोकानतलादिमयाम्̐स्तथा ॥ 32
3.4.m: And those people who are devotees of the gods proceed to the seven [upper] worlds. / But those people who are tāmasic, intent on worshipping the daityas, / go to the lower worlds consisting of Atala and the rest.

3.4.s:
pātālādyojanaṃ lakṣamadholokaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .
vidharmatatparā lokāste gacchanti hyadhogatim . .
ato vai vidhinā bhraṣṭā madbhaktāśca daridragāḥ . . 33
3.4.d:
पातालाद्योजनं लक्षमधोलोकः प्रकीर्तितः ।
विधर्मतत्परा लोकास्ते गच्छन्ति ह्यधोगतिम् ॥
अतो वै विधिना भ्रष्टा मद्भक्ताश्च दरिद्रगाः ॥ 33
3.4.m: One hundred thousand yojanas below Pātāla is declared to be the nether world. / People devoted to vidharma go to that downward course. / Therefore, fallen from the ordainment, my devotees fall into poverty.

3.4.s:
ye madbhaktāḥ surānpūrvaṃ pūjayitvā bhajanti mām .
lakṣmīvantaśca te jñeyā bhuktimuktiparāyaṇāḥ . . 34
3.4.d:
ये मद्भक्ताः सुरान्पूर्वं पूजयित्वा भजन्ति माम् ।
लक्ष्मीवन्तश्च ते ज्ञेया भुक्तिमुक्तिपरायणाः ॥ 34
3.4.m: Those devotees of mine who worship me after first worshipping the gods, / they are to be known as wealthy, dedicated to worldly enjoyment and liberation.

3.4.s:
prayāge nairṛto viprastyaktvā devānmama priyān .
bhajatyananyabhāvena tasmātsa hi daridravān . . 35
3.4.d:
प्रयागे नैरृतो विप्रस्त्यक्त्वा देवान्मम प्रियान् ।
भजत्यनन्यभावेन तस्मात्स हि दरिद्रवान् ॥ 35
3.4.m: In Prayāga, the brāhmaṇa Nairṛta, having abandoned the gods dear to me, / worships me with single-minded devotion; therefore he is poor."

3.4.s:
devairdattaṃ hi yaddravyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ sarvadā janaiḥ .
mayā dattaṃ hi yadvastu brahmāṇḍe nāsti nārada . .
ato madājñayā vipra dehi tasmai varaṃ śubham . . 36
3.4.d:
देवैर्दत्तं हि यद्द्रव्यं भोक्तव्यं सर्वदा जनैः ।
मया दत्तं हि यद्वस्तु ब्रह्माण्डे नास्ति नारद ॥
अतो मदाज्ञया विप्र देहि तस्मै वरं शुभम् ॥ 36
3.4.m: For whatever wealth is given by the gods must always be enjoyed by men; / but whatever thing is given by me, O Nārada, does not exist in the cosmic egg. / Therefore, at my command, O Brahmin, grant him an auspicious boon.

3.4.s:
ityukto nārado yogī hariṇā viśvakāriṇā .
dvijapatnī sthitā gehe tatra prāpya vaco'bravīt . . 37
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तो नारदो योगी हरिणा विश्वकारिणा ।
द्विजपत्नी स्थिता गेहे तत्र प्राप्य वचोऽब्रवीत् ॥ 37
3.4.m: Thus addressed by Hari, the maker of the universe, the yogin Nārada / reached the Brahmin's wife as she stayed in her house and spoke these words:

3.4.s:
varaṃ varaya he sādhvi tvayā yadvāñchitaṃ hṛdi .
sāha dehi varaṃ svāminbhūparājñī bhavāmyaham . . 38
3.4.d:
वरं वरय हे साध्वि त्वया यद्वाञ्छितं हृदि ।
साह देहि वरं स्वामिन्भूपराज्ञी भवाम्यहम् ॥ 38
3.4.m: "Choose a boon, O virtuous woman, whatever is desired in your heart." / She said, "Grant me a boon, my lord: let me become the queen of a king!"

3.4.s:
ityuktvā vacanaṃ tatra divyarūpā babhūva sā .
āgatastatra nṛpatirgṛhītvā gehamāyayau . . 39
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा वचनं तत्र दिव्यरूपा बभूव सा ।
आगतस्तत्र नृपतिर्गृहीत्वा गेहमाययौ ॥ 39
3.4.m: Having spoken those words, she then assumed a divine form. / A king arrived there, took her, and departed for his home.

3.4.s:
sāyaṅkāle tu samprāpte dvijastatra samāgataḥ .
nāradastaṃ vacaḥ prāha śṛṇu vipra haripriya . . 3.4.11.40
3.4.d:
सायङ्काले तु सम्प्राप्ते द्विजस्तत्र समागतः ।
नारदस्तं वचः प्राह शृणु विप्र हरिप्रिय ॥ 3.4.11.40
3.4.m: When evening arrived, the Brahmin returned there. / Nārada spoke these words to him: "Listen, O Brahmin, dear to Hari!

3.4.s:
varadānācca te patnī bhūparājñī hi vartate .
tvayā kiṃ vāñchitaṃ vastu mattaḥ prāpya sukhī bhava . . 41
3.4.d:
वरदानाच्च ते पत्नी भूपराज्ञी हि वर्तते ।
त्वया किं वाञ्छितं वस्तु मत्तः प्राप्य सुखी भव ॥ 41
3.4.m: By the granting of a boon, your wife is indeed a king's queen. / What object is desired by you? Receive it from me and be happy."

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā daivavaśo vacaḥ prāha ruṣānvitaḥ .
kroṣṭrī bhavecca matpatnī dehi vipra varaṃ mama . . 42
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा दैववशो वचः प्राह रुषान्वितः ।
क्रोष्ट्री भवेच्च मत्पत्नी देहि विप्र वरं मम ॥ 42
3.4.m: Hearing this, overwhelmed by fate, he spoke words full of anger: / "Let my wife become a female jackal! O Brahmin, grant me this boon!"

3.4.s:
ityuktvā vacanātkroṣṭrī sā babhūva dvijapriyā .
ekasminnantare prāstastatputro gurupūjakaḥ . . 43
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा वचनात्क्रोष्ट्री सा बभूव द्विजप्रिया ।
एकस्मिन्नन्तरे प्रास्तस्तत्पुत्रो गुरुपूजकः ॥ 43
3.4.m: As he spoke these words, that beloved [wife] of the Brahmin became a female jackal. / Meanwhile, his son arrived, a worshipper of elders.

3.4.s:
śrutvā tatkāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ nāradaṃ sa vaco'bravīt .
mama mātā yathā svāmiṃstathā śīghraṃ varādbhavet . . 44
3.4.d:
श्रुत्वा तत्कारणं सर्वं नारदं स वचोऽब्रवीत् ।
मम माता यथा स्वामिंस्तथा शीघ्रं वराद्भवेत् ॥ 44
3.4.m: Having heard the whole matter, he spoke these words to Nārada: / "O lord, through your boon let my mother swiftly become just as she was!"

3.4.s:
etattribhirvaraiḥ prāptaṃ daivamāyāvimohitaiḥ .
tadā tu nārado duḥkhī nairṛtaṃ prāha vai vacaḥ . . 45
3.4.d:
एतत्त्रिभिर्वरैः प्राप्तं दैवमायाविमोहितैः ।
तदा तु नारदो दुःखी नैरृतं प्राह वै वचः ॥ 45
3.4.m: Thus [nothing] was gained through these three boons by those deluded by the divine Māyā. / Then Nārada, grieved, spoke words indeed to Nairṛta:

3.4.s:
brahmāṇḍo'yaṃ devamayo bhavastasya maheśvaraḥ .
ato bhavaṃ bhajāśu tvaṃ sa te kāryaṃ kariṣyati . . 46
3.4.d:
ब्रह्माण्डोऽयं देवमयो भवस्तस्य महेश्वरः ।
अतो भवं भजाशु त्वं स ते कार्यं करिष्यति ॥ 46
3.4.m: "This cosmic egg is pervaded by the gods; Bhava is its great lord. / Therefore worship Bhava quickly; he will accomplish your purpose."

3.4.s:
ityuktavacano vipro bhavaṃ taṃ pārthivārcanaiḥ .
tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā varṣamātraṃ hi nairṛtaḥ . . 47
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तवचनो विप्रो भवं तं पार्थिवार्चनैः ।
तुष्टाव परया भक्त्या वर्षमात्रं हि नैरृतः ॥ 47
3.4.m: Having been thus addressed, the Brahmin Nairṛta praised Bhava / with supreme devotion through earthly worship for a whole year.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavānmaheśo bhaktavatsalaḥ .
kuberasadṛśaṃ divyaṃ dadau tasmai mahaddhanam . . 48
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्महेशो भक्तवत्सलः ।
कुबेरसदृशं दिव्यं ददौ तस्मै महद्धनम् ॥ 48
3.4.m: Then the blessed Maheśa, who loves his devotees, being pleased, / gave him great, divine wealth equal to that of Kubera.

3.4.s:
taddhanena sa vai vipro dharmakāryaṃ cakāra ha .
prasiddho'bhūnmahīpṛṣṭhe nāmnā puṇyajano dhanaiḥ . . 49
3.4.d:
तद्धनेन स वै विप्रो धर्मकार्यं चकार ह ।
प्रसिद्धोऽभून्महीपृष्ठे नाम्ना पुण्यजनो धनैः ॥ 49
3.4.m: With that wealth, the Brahmin performed righteous deeds. / Famous on the face of the earth, he was known as Puṇyajana for his riches.

3.4.s:
śivabhaktiprabhāveṇa prāpya dravyamakaṇṭakam .
sahasrābdavapurbhūtvā tyaktvā prāṇāndivaṃ yayau . . 3.4.11.50
3.4.d:
शिवभक्तिप्रभावेण प्राप्य द्रव्यमकण्टकम् ।
सहस्राब्दवपुर्भूत्वा त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्दिवं ययौ ॥ 3.4.11.50
3.4.m: Having obtained undisputed wealth through the power of devotion to Śiva, / and having lived in a body for a thousand years, he gave up his vital breaths and went to heaven.

3.4.s:
vṛṣarāśisthite sūrye rājā candrasya somavat .
nairṛto nāma vikhyāto rudraḥ sarvajanapriyaḥ . . 51
3.4.d:
वृषराशिस्थिते सूर्ये राजा चन्द्रस्य सोमवत् ।
नैरृतो नाम विख्यातो रुद्रः सर्वजनप्रियः ॥ 51
3.4.m: When the sun stood in the sign of Taurus, he became a king of the moon, like Soma, / renowned by the name Nairṛta, a Rudra dear to all people.

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā nairṛtastu bhṛguvarya gurūditam .
svāṃśādbhūtalamāgamya girinālagirau vane . . 52
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा नैरृतस्तु भृगुवर्य गुरूदितम् ।
स्वांशाद्भूतलमागम्य गिरिनालगिरौ वने ॥ 52
3.4.m: Having heard this what was told by the guru, O best of the Bhṛgus, Nairṛta / came from a portion of himself to the earthly plane, in the forest on Mount Girināla.

3.4.s:
yoginaḥ siddhasāṅkhyasya putro'bhūdvanavāsinaḥ .
vanaśarmeti vikhyāto vedaśāstraparāyaṇaḥ . . 53
3.4.d:
योगिनः सिद्धसाङ्ख्यस्य पुत्रोऽभूद्वनवासिनः ।
वनशर्मेति विख्यातो वेदशास्त्रपरायणः ॥ 53
3.4.m: He became the son of a forest-dwelling yogin who had perfected Sāṅkhya; / known as Vanaśarman, he was dedicated to the Vedas and Śāstras.

3.4.s:
dvādaśābdavapurbhūtvā jitvā vidvajjanānbahūn .
kāśīmāgamya tattvārthī śaṅkarācāryamuttamam . .
praṇamya tasya śiṣyo'bhūdvanaśarmā viśāradaḥ . . 54
3.4.d:
द्वादशाब्दवपुर्भूत्वा जित्वा विद्वज्जनान्बहून् ।
काशीमागम्य तत्त्वार्थी शङ्कराचार्यमुत्तमम् ॥
प्रणम्य तस्य शिष्योऽभूद्वनशर्मा विशारदः ॥ 54
3.4.m: Attaining a body of twelve years and conquering many learned men, / he went to Kāśī seeking the highest truth, bowed to the excellent Śaṅkarācārya, / and the wise Vanaśarman became his disciple.

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
vasuśarmā dvijaḥ kaścinmāhiṣmatyāṃ purābhavat .
śivavrataparo nityaṃ putrārthī pārthivārcaka. . . 55
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
वसुशर्मा द्विजः कश्चिन्माहिष्मत्यां पुराभवत् ।
शिवव्रतपरो नित्यं पुत्रार्थी पार्थिवार्चक॥ । 55
3.4.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
In ancient times there was a Brahmin named Vasuśarman in Māhiṣmatī, / constantly devoted to vows to Śiva, worshipping [him] with earthen emblems in desire of a son.

3.4.s:
caturviṃśativarṣāṇi pūjatastasya dhīmata .
vyatītāni surāstatra na prasanno'bhavacchivaḥ . . 56
3.4.d:
चतुर्विंशतिवर्षाणि पूजतस्तस्य धीमत ।
व्यतीतानि सुरास्तत्र न प्रसन्नोऽभवच्छिवः ॥ 56
3.4.m: As the wise man worshipped, twenty-four years / passed by, O gods, but Śiva was not pleased with him.

3.4.s:
tadā tu duḥkhito vipro vahniṃ prajvālya bhairavam .
juhāva svāṅgamāṃsāni mukhataścaraṇāntakam . . 57
3.4.d:
तदा तु दुःखितो विप्रो वह्निं प्रज्वाल्य भैरवम् ।
जुहाव स्वाङ्गमांसानि मुखतश्चरणान्तकम् ॥ 57
3.4.m: Then, distressed, the Brahmin kindled a terrible fire / and offered the flesh of his own limbs, from his face down to his feet.

3.4.s:
na prasannobhavadrudrastadā vipraḥ śucānvitaḥ .
gṛhītvā cottamaṃ meṣaṃ saṃskāraṃ kṛtavāñchuciḥ . .
tena meṣeṇa sahito jvaladagnau samāyayau . . 58
3.4.d:
न प्रसन्नोभवद्रुद्रस्तदा विप्रः शुचान्वितः ।
गृहीत्वा चोत्तमं मेषं संस्कारं कृतवाञ्छुचिः ॥
तेन मेषेण सहितो ज्वलदग्नौ समाययौ ॥ 58
3.4.m: When Rudra was still not pleased, the Brahmin, overwhelmed with sorrow, / took an excellent ram, purified it through ritual consecration, / and, pure himself, entered the blazing fire along with that ram.

3.4.s:
prasanno bhagavānrudrastatrāgatya gaṇairyutaḥ .
svarūpaṃ darśayāmāsa śuddhasphaṭikasundaram . .
varaṃ brūhi vacaḥ prāha vasuśarmāṇamuttamam . . 59
3.4.d:
प्रसन्नो भगवान्रुद्रस्तत्रागत्य गणैर्युतः ।
स्वरूपं दर्शयामास शुद्धस्फटिकसुन्दरम् ॥
वरं ब्रूहि वचः प्राह वसुशर्माणमुत्तमम् ॥ 59
3.4.m: Then the blessed Rudra, being pleased, came there accompanied by his gaṇas / and revealed his own form, beautiful like pure crystal. / He spoke words to the excellent Vasuśarman: "State a boon!"

3.4.s:
tacchrutvā sa prasannātmā natvā pārvativallabham .
praśrayāvanato bhūtvā vacanaṃ prāha śaṅkaram . . 3.4.11.60
3.4.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा स प्रसन्नात्मा नत्वा पार्वतिवल्लभम् ।
प्रश्रयावनतो भूत्वा वचनं प्राह शङ्करम् ॥ 3.4.11.60
3.4.m: Hearing that, his soul delighted, he bowed to the beloved of Pārvatī, / and bowing low in humility, spoke these words to Śaṅkara:

3.4.s:
dehi me tanayaṃ svāmiñcharaṇāgatavatsala .
ityuktaśśaṅkarastena vihasyovāca taṃ dvijam . . 61
3.4.d:
देहि मे तनयं स्वामिञ्छरणागतवत्सल ।
इत्युक्तश्शङ्करस्तेन विहस्योवाच तं द्विजम् ॥ 61
3.4.m: "Grant me a son, O lord who are affectionate to those who take refuge in you!" / Thus addressed by him, Śaṅkara laughed and said to the Brahmin:

3.4.s:
putradātā svayaṃ brahmā bhāgyakarttā parātparaḥ .
tubhyaṃ ca śatajanmāntaṃ tena putro na nirmitaḥ . .
tasmādahaṃ sutaṃ svāṃśāttava vipra dadāmi bhoḥ . . 62
3.4.d:
पुत्रदाता स्वयं ब्रह्मा भाग्यकर्त्ता परात्परः ।
तुभ्यं च शतजन्मान्तं तेन पुत्रो न निर्मितः ॥
तस्मादहं सुतं स्वांशात्तव विप्र ददामि भोः ॥ 62
3.4.m: "Brahmā himself is the giver of sons, the highest maker of destiny; / and by him no son has been fashioned for you for a hundred births to come. / Therefore, O Brahmin, I grant you a son from a portion of myself."

3.4.s:
ityuktvā svamukhāttejo nirākṛtya maheśvaraḥ .
tatpatnyāṃ janayāmāsa sakāśādvasuvarmaṇaḥ . . 63
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वा स्वमुखात्तेजो निराकृत्य महेश्वरः ।
तत्पत्न्यां जनयामास सकाशाद्वसुवर्मणः ॥ 63
3.4.m: Having said this, Maheśvara brought forth splendor from his own mouth / and engendered it in the wife of that Vasuvarman from his presence.

3.4.s:
daśamāsāntare jātaḥ suputro madhurānanaḥ .
ajasyeva padaścaiko dvitīyo naravattataḥ . .
ajaikapāda iti sa prasiddho'bhūnmahītale . . 64
3.4.d:
दशमासान्तरे जातः सुपुत्रो मधुराननः ।
अजस्येव पदश्चैको द्वितीयो नरवत्ततः ॥
अजैकपाद इति स प्रसिद्धोऽभून्महीतले ॥ 64
3.4.m: After ten months, a fine son with a sweet face was born; / one foot of his was like that of a goat, and the other was like a man's; / hence he became famous on the surface of the earth as Ajaikapād.

3.4.s:
catuśśatābdavapuṣi prāpte tasminsute priye .
samprāpto bhagavānmṛtyustadā rogagaṇairyutaḥ . . 65
3.4.d:
चतुश्शताब्दवपुषि प्राप्ते तस्मिन्सुते प्रिये ।
सम्प्राप्तो भगवान्मृत्युस्तदा रोगगणैर्युतः ॥ 65
3.4.m: When that beloved son had reached four hundred years of age, / the blessed Lord Death then arrived, accompanied by hosts of diseases.

3.4.s: tasya tairabhavadyuddhamajaikacaraṇasya vai . . 66
3.4.d: तस्य तैरभवद्युद्धमजैकचरणस्य वै ॥ 66
3.4.m: A battle indeed took place between them and that one-footed Ajaikapād.

3.4.s:
varṣamātreṇa tānsarvāñjitvā mallaraṇotkaṭaḥ .
mṛtyuñjayaḥ sa vai nāmnā prasiddho'bhūnmahītale . . 67
3.4.d:
वर्षमात्रेण तान्सर्वाञ्जित्वा मल्लरणोत्कटः ।
मृत्युञ्जयः स वै नाम्ना प्रसिद्धोऽभून्महीतले ॥ 67
3.4.m: Having conquered them all in just a year, mighty in wrestling combat, / he became famous indeed on the surface of the earth by the name Mṛtyuñjaya.

3.4.s:
duḥkhito bhagavānmṛtyustena vipreṇa nirjitaḥ .
parameṣṭhinamāgamya kathayāmāsa kāraṇam . . 68
3.4.d:
दुःखितो भगवान्मृत्युस्तेन विप्रेण निर्जितः ।
परमेष्ठिनमागम्य कथयामास कारणम् ॥ 68
3.4.m: The blessed Lord Death, distressed at being defeated by that Brahmin, / went to the Supreme Lord [Brahmā] and related the matter.

3.4.s:
tadā tu bhagavānbrahmā sarvadevagaṇairyutaḥ .
kumbhage dyumaṇau deve candramaṇḍalagaṃ nṛpam . .
taṃ dvijaṃ ca cakārāśu rudrarūpaṃ bhayāpaham . . 69
3.4.d:
तदा तु भगवान्ब्रह्मा सर्वदेवगणैर्युतः ।
कुम्भगे द्युमणौ देवे चन्द्रमण्डलगं नृपम् ॥
तं द्विजं च चकाराशु रुद्ररूपं भयापहम् ॥ 69
3.4.m: Then the blessed Brahmā, accompanied by all the hosts of gods, / while the sun-jewel was in Aquarius, quickly made that Brahmin, / who was in the lunar orb, into a king, a form of Rudra that dispels fear.

3.4.s:
sūta uvāca
iti śrutvā mahādevaḥ sa vipraśca tadājapād .
purīṃ māhiṣmatīṃ prāptaḥ kaliśuddhikaraḥ prabhuḥ . .
purīśarmeti vikhyāto yatidattasya vai sutaḥ . . 3.4.11.70
ṣoḍaśābdavapurbhūtvā jitvā veda parāyaṇān .
śaṅkarācāryamāgamya tasya śiṣyo babhūva ha . .
iti te kathitaṃ vipra yathā mṛtyuñjayobhavat . . 7
.. sūta uvāca ..
punaḥ śṛṇu kathāṃ ramyāṃ prayāge jīvabhāṣitām..
3.4.d:
सूत उवाच
इति श्रुत्वा महादेवः स विप्रश्च तदाजपाद् ।
पुरीं माहिष्मतीं प्राप्तः कलिशुद्धिकरः प्रभुः ॥
पुरीशर्मेति विख्यातो यतिदत्तस्य वै सुतः ॥ 3.4.11.70
षोडशाब्दवपुर्भूत्वा जित्वा वेद परायणान् ।
शङ्कराचार्यमागम्य तस्य शिष्यो बभूव ह ॥
इति ते कथितं विप्र यथा मृत्युञ्जयोभवत् ॥ 7
॥ सूत उवाच ॥
पुनः शृणु कथां रम्यां प्रयागे जीवभाषिताम्॥
3.4.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard this, that lord, Mahādeva, and the Brahmin born from Ajaikapād / who purifies the Kali age, came to the city of Māhiṣmatī / as the son of Yatidatta, renowned as Purīśarman.
Attaining a body of sixteen years and conquering those dedicated to the Vedas, / he approached Śaṅkarācārya and became his disciple. / Thus has it been related to you, O Brahmin, how he became Mṛtyuñjaya.
Sūta said:
Listen again to a delightful story told by Bṛhaspati at Prayāga.

3.4.s:
hirburnāma purā cāsīddānavo lokakaṃṭakaḥ..1..
nikuṃbhānvayasaṃbhūtaḥ śakratulyaparākramaḥ ..
3.4.d:
हिर्बुर्नाम पुरा चासीद्दानवो लोककंटकः॥1॥
निकुंभान्वयसंभूतः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः ॥
3.4.m:
Formerly there was a Dānava named Hirbu, a thorn to the worlds,
born in the lineage of Nikuṃbha, equal in valor to Śakra.

3.4.s:
sahasrābdaṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā tāpayāmāsa vai surān .. 2 ..
tadā lokapatirbrahmā lokarakṣārthamudyataḥ ..
3.4.d:
सहस्राब्दं तपः कृत्वा तापयामास वै सुरान् ॥ 2 ॥
तदा लोकपतिर्ब्रह्मा लोकरक्षार्थमुद्यतः ॥
3.4.m:
Having performed austerities for a thousand years, he tormented the gods.
Then Brahmā, the lord of the worlds, set out to protect the worlds.

3.4.s:
varaṃ brūhīti vacanamuvāca danujeśvaram .. 3 ..
namaskṛtya vidhātāraṃ vacanaṃ prāha namradhīḥ ..
3.4.d:
वरं ब्रूहीति वचनमुवाच दनुजेश्वरम् ॥ 3 ॥
नमस्कृत्य विधातारं वचनं प्राह नम्रधीः ॥
3.4.m:
He spoke these words to the lord of the Danus: "Choose a boon!"
Having bowed to the Creator, his mind humbled, he spoke these words:

3.4.s:
yadi deyo varaḥ svāmiṃstvayā viśvakṛtā vibho ..4..
maraṇaṃ na ca mebhūyāttvatkṛtaiśca carācaraiḥ ..
3.4.d:
यदि देयो वरः स्वामिंस्त्वया विश्वकृता विभो ॥4॥
मरणं न च मेभूयात्त्वत्कृतैश्च चराचरैः ॥
3.4.m:
"If a boon is to be granted by you, O lord, creator of the universe, O pervasive one,
may my death not come from moving and unmoving beings made by you."

3.4.s:
ityuktassa tathetyuktvā brahma lokamupāyayau .. 5 ..
dānavassa
tu raudrātmā jitvā svarganivāsinaḥ ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्तस्स तथेत्युक्त्वा ब्रह्म लोकमुपाययौ ॥ 5 ॥
दानवस्स
तु रौद्रात्मा जित्वा स्वर्गनिवासिनः ॥
3.4.m:
Having been spoken to thus, he said, "So be it," and went to the world of Brahmā.
Then that dānava of terrible nature, having conquered the dwellers of heaven,

3.4.s:
āhūya dānavāndaityānvivarebhyaḥ prasannadhīḥ .. 6 ..
svarge nivāsayāmāsa te devā bhūtalīkṛtāḥ ..
3.4.d:
आहूय दानवान्दैत्यान्विवरेभ्यः प्रसन्नधीः ॥ 6 ॥
स्वर्गे निवासयामास ते देवा भूतलीकृताः ॥
3.4.m:
called the dānavas and daityas from their subterranean cavities, pleased in mind,
and settled them in heaven; those gods were brought down to the earth.

3.4.s:
lakṣābdaṃ ca surāssarve bubhujuḥ paramāpadaḥ .. 7 ..
ekadā nārado dhīmāndṛṣṭvā devāṃstathāgatān ..
3.4.d:
लक्षाब्दं च सुरास्सर्वे बुभुजुः परमापदः ॥ 7 ॥
एकदा नारदो धीमान्दृष्ट्वा देवांस्तथागतान् ॥
3.4.m:
And for a hundred thousand years all the gods suffered extreme calamities.
Once, wise Nārada, having seen the gods reduced to that state,

3.4.s:
vacanaṃ prāha yogātmā bhajadhvaṃ lokaśaṃkaram .. 8 ..
sa devaśca mahādevo brahmāṇḍeśo vipattihā ..
3.4.d:
वचनं प्राह योगात्मा भजध्वं लोकशंकरम् ॥ 8 ॥
स देवश्च महादेवो ब्रह्माण्डेशो विपत्तिहा ॥
3.4.m:
that yogic-souled one spoke words [to them]: "Worship the benefactor of the world!
He is the god, Mahādeva, lord of the universe, destroyer of calamity."

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu vacanaṃ te devā vismayānvitāḥ .. 9 ..
pārthivaiḥ pūjayā māsurdevadevamumāpatim ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु वचनं ते देवा विस्मयान्विताः ॥ 9 ॥
पार्थिवैः पूजया मासुर्देवदेवमुमापतिम् ॥
3.4.m:
Hearing this speech, those gods were filled with wonder;
they worshipped the god of gods, the husband of Umā, with earthen [liṅgas].

3.4.s:
gataikādaśavarṣāśca teṣāṃ pūjanakāriṇām .. 10 ..
tadā prasanno bhagavānmaheśo lokaśaṃkaraḥ ..
3.4.d:
गतैकादशवर्षाश्च तेषां पूजनकारिणाम् ॥ 10 ॥
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्महेशो लोकशंकरः ॥
3.4.m:
Eleven years passed for them as they performed worship.
Then the blessed Maheśa, benefactor of the world, became pleased;

3.4.s:
jyotirliṃgamayo bhūtvā lokām̐strīnsamadāhayat .. 11 ..
ye tu vai devabhaktāśca śeṣāścāsanmahābhaye ..
3.4.d:
ज्योतिर्लिंगमयो भूत्वा लोकाम्̐स्त्रीन्समदाहयत् ॥ 11 ॥
ये तु वै देवभक्ताश्च शेषाश्चासन्महाभये ॥
3.4.m:
having assumed the form of a liṅga of light, he burned the three worlds.
Those who were devotees of the gods remained in that great peril,

3.4.s:
anye tu dānavaissārddhaṃ bhasmībhūtā babhūvire .. 12 ..
etasminnantare brahmā viṣṇunā saha harṣitaḥ ..
3.4.d:
अन्ये तु दानवैस्सार्द्धं भस्मीभूता बभूविरे ॥ 12 ॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्रह्मा विष्णुना सह हर्षितः ॥
3.4.m:
while others were turned to ashes along with the dānavas.
In the meantime, Brahmā, delighted along with Viṣṇu,

3.4.s:
tuṣṭāva sa mahārudraṃ stotraissāmasamudbhavaiḥ .. 13 ..
mithunasthe divānāthe śaśimaṇḍalabhūpatim ..
3.4.d:
तुष्टाव स महारुद्रं स्तोत्रैस्सामसमुद्भवैः ॥ 13 ॥
मिथुनस्थे दिवानाथे शशिमण्डलभूपतिम् ॥
3.4.m:
praised that Mahārudra with hymns born of the Sāmaveda.
When the sun was in Gemini, for the sake of the gods,

3.4.s:
hirbughnaṃ ca mahārudraṃ cakāra surahetave .. 14 ..
iti śrutvā sa hirbughno devakāryārthamudyataḥ ..
3.4.d:
हिर्बुघ्नं च महारुद्रं चकार सुरहेतवे ॥ 14 ॥
इति श्रुत्वा स हिर्बुघ्नो देवकार्यार्थमुद्यतः ॥
3.4.m:
he made Mahārudra, king of the moon's orb, as Ahirbudhnya.
Having heard this, that Ahirbudhnya was ready for the mission of the gods;

3.4.s:
himālaye girau ramye putro'bhūtsādyakarmaṇaḥ ..35 ..
patirūpaḥ kalābhijño bhāratīśa iti śrutaḥ ..
sa jitvā viduṣāṃ vṛṃdānkāśīnagaramāgataḥ ..
3.4.d:
हिमालये गिरौ रम्ये पुत्रोऽभूत्साद्यकर्मणः ॥35 ॥
पतिरूपः कलाभिज्ञो भारतीश इति श्रुतः ॥
स जित्वा विदुषां वृंदान्काशीनगरमागतः ॥

3.4.s:
śaṃkarācāryamāgamya śiṣyo'bhūttena nirjitaḥ .. 16 ..
.. bṛhaspati ruvāca .. ..
3.4.d:
शंकराचार्यमागम्य शिष्योऽभूत्तेन निर्जितः ॥ 16 ॥
॥ बृहस्पति रुवाच ॥ ॥
3.4.m:
having approached Śaṅkarācārya, he was defeated by him and became his pupil.
Bṛhaspati said:

3.4.s:
mayaputraḥ smṛto māyī tapo ghoraṃ cakāra ha .. 17 ..
padaikena sthitaḥ sūrye sahasrābdaṃ prayatnataḥ ..
3.4.d:
मयपुत्रः स्मृतो मायी तपो घोरं चकार ह ॥ 17 ॥
पदैकेन स्थितः सूर्ये सहस्राब्दं प्रयत्नतः ॥
3.4.m:
The sorcerer known as the son of Maya performed severe asceticism.
Standing on one foot, facing the sun, he [remained] zealously for a thousand years;

3.4.s:
sa lokām̐stāpayāmāsa tapasā lokavāsinaḥ .. 18 ..
tadā prasanno bhagavānparameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ ..
3.4.d:
स लोकाम्̐स्तापयामास तपसा लोकवासिनः ॥ 18 ॥
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्परमेष्ठी पितामहः ॥
3.4.m:
he tormented the worlds and the inhabitants of the worlds by his asceticism.
Then the blessed grandfather Parameṣṭhin was pleased;

3.4.s:
trayo grāmāstatpriyārthe kramādvai tena nirmitāḥ .. 19 ..
sauvarṇaṃ svargasadṛśaṃ puraṃ ṣoḍaśayojanam ..
3.4.d:
त्रयो ग्रामास्तत्प्रियार्थे क्रमाद्वै तेन निर्मिताः ॥ 19 ॥
सौवर्णं स्वर्गसदृशं पुरं षोडशयोजनम् ॥
3.4.m:
for his gratification three settlements were built by him in succession:
a golden city, resembling heaven, measuring sixteen yojanas;

3.4.s:
tadadho yojanānte ca rājataṃ ca bhuvarmayam..20..
tadadho yojanānte ca bhūrlokamiva cāyasam ..
3.4.d:
तदधो योजनान्ते च राजतं च भुवर्मयम्॥20॥
तदधो योजनान्ते च भूर्लोकमिव चायसम् ॥
3.4.m:
beneath that, at the distance of a yojana, a silver one consisting of Bhuvarloka;
and beneath that, at the distance of a yojana, one of iron, like the earth.

3.4.s:
evaṃ puranivāsinyo daityānāṃ yoṣito mudā .. 21 ..
śatakoṭimitā daityā dharmātmāno nivāsinaḥ ..
3.4.d:
एवं पुरनिवासिन्यो दैत्यानां योषितो मुदा ॥ 21 ॥
शतकोटिमिता दैत्या धर्मात्मानो निवासिनः ॥
3.4.m:
Thus the women of the daityas dwelt with joy in the cities.
The daityas who dwelt there, numbering one billion, were righteous in nature;

3.4.s:
gṛhītvā yajñabhāgaṃ ca devatulyā babhūvire .. 22 ..
tadā nirbalino devāḥ kṣudhayā pīḍitāḥ prabhum ..
3.4.d:
गृहीत्वा यज्ञभागं च देवतुल्या बभूविरे ॥ 22 ॥
तदा निर्बलिनो देवाः क्षुधया पीडिताः प्रभुम् ॥
3.4.m:
receiving their share of the sacrifice, they became equal to the gods.
Then the gods, rendered powerless and afflicted with hunger,

3.4.s:
bhagavantaṃ mahāviṣṇuṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ parayā girā .. 23 ..
caturyugasamūhānāṃ varṣāṇāṃ bhagavanprabho ..
3.4.d:
भगवन्तं महाविष्णुं तुष्टुवुः परया गिरा ॥ 23 ॥
चतुर्युगसमूहानां वर्षाणां भगवन्प्रभो ॥
3.4.m:
praised the master, the blessed Mahāviṣṇu, with supreme speech:
"O blessed master, for [many] years comprising collections of four yugas,

3.4.s:
adhikāravihīnāśca vartaṃte svargamaṇḍale .. 24 ..
tāmasāṃtaramevāpi ṣoḍaśaiva caturyugam ..
3.4.d:
अधिकारविहीनाश्च वर्तंते स्वर्गमण्डले ॥ 24 ॥
तामसांतरमेवापि षोडशैव चतुर्युगम् ॥
3.4.m:
[we] remain in the heavenly realm stripped of authority.
Indeed, in the Tāmasa Manu's era, sixteen cycles of four yugas

3.4.s:
vyatītāni mahāviṣṇo māyināṃ duḥkhaṃ bhuṃjatām .. 25 ..
iti śrutvā vacasteṣāṃ bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ ..
3.4.d:
व्यतीतानि महाविष्णो मायिनां दुःखं भुंजताम् ॥ 25 ॥
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां भगवान्मधुसूदनः ॥
3.4.m:
have passed, O Mahāviṣṇu, while the sorcerers enjoy our distress!"
Having heard their words, the blessed Madhusūdana,

3.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā saṃskṛtavārtāyāṃ daityāndharmaparāyaṇān ..26..
vauddharūpastvayaṃ jātaḥ kalau prāpte bhayānake ..
3.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा संस्कृतवार्तायां दैत्यान्धर्मपरायणान् ॥26॥
वौद्धरूपस्त्वयं जातः कलौ प्राप्ते भयानके ॥
3.4.m:
seeing the daityas devoted to dharma according to traditional report,
this [Janārdana] was born in the form of the Buddha when the terrible Kali [age] arrived;

3.4.s:
ajinasya dvijasyaiva suto bhūtvā janārdanaḥ .. 27 ..
vedadharmaparānviprānmohayāmāsa vīryavān ..
3.4.d:
अजिनस्य द्विजस्यैव सुतो भूत्वा जनार्दनः ॥ 27 ॥
वेदधर्मपरान्विप्रान्मोहयामास वीर्यवान् ॥
3.4.m:
having become the son of the twice-born Ajina, Janārdana,
the mighty one, deluded the brahmins devoted to Vedic dharma.

3.4.s:
nirvedāḥ karmarahitāstrivarṇāstāmasāntare .. 28 ..
ṣoḍaśe ca kalau prāpte babhūburyajñavarjitāḥ ..
3.4.d:
निर्वेदाः कर्मरहितास्त्रिवर्णास्तामसान्तरे ॥ 28 ॥
षोडशे च कलौ प्राप्ते बभूबुर्यज्ञवर्जिताः ॥
3.4.m:
Without the Vedas and devoid of ritual acts, the three twice-born classes in the Tāmasa era,
when the sixteenth Kali [age] arrived, became devoid of sacrifice.

3.4.s:
tadā daityā ruṣāviṣṭāssarve tripuravāsinaḥ .. 29 ..
manujānpīḍayāmāsurniryajñānvedavarjitān ..
3.4.d:
तदा दैत्या रुषाविष्टास्सर्वे त्रिपुरवासिनः ॥ 29 ॥
मनुजान्पीडयामासुर्निर्यज्ञान्वेदवर्जितान् ॥
3.4.m:
Then the daityas, all the dwellers of Tripura, filled with wrath,
tormented the men who were devoid of sacrifice and without the Vedas;

3.4.s:
kṣayaṃ jagmurnarāssarve kalpāṃte daityabhakṣitāḥ .. 30 ..
punassatyayuge prāpte kailāse guhyakālaye ..
3.4.d:
क्षयं जग्मुर्नरास्सर्वे कल्पांते दैत्यभक्षिताः ॥ 30 ॥
पुनस्सत्ययुगे प्राप्ते कैलासे गुह्यकालये ॥
3.4.m:
all men went to destruction at the end of the kalpa, devoured by the daityas.
When the Satya Yuga arrived again, on Kailāsa, the abode of the guhyakas,

3.4.s:
devaiścārādhitaḥ śaṃbhussarvalokaśivaṃkaraḥ .. 31 ..
jyotirligaṃ vapuḥ kṛtvā tatra tasthau bhayaṃkaraḥ ..
3.4.d:
देवैश्चाराधितः शंभुस्सर्वलोकशिवंकरः ॥ 31 ॥
ज्योतिर्लिगं वपुः कृत्वा तत्र तस्थौ भयंकरः ॥
3.4.m:
Śambhu, who brings auspiciousness to all the world, was worshipped by the gods.
Having made his body a liṅga of light, the terrible one stood there.

3.4.s:
etasminnantare devāḥ prasannāstāmasāntare .. 32 ..
bhūmessāraṃ gṛhītvā te rathaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ ..
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवाः प्रसन्नास्तामसान्तरे ॥ 32 ॥
भूमेस्सारं गृहीत्वा ते रथं कृत्वा विधानतः ॥
3.4.m:
In the meantime, the gods, delighted in that Tāmasa era,
took the essence of the earth and constructed a chariot according to rule;

3.4.s:
caṃdrabhāskarayossārāccakre kṛtvā tathaiva ca ..33..
sumerośca tathā sārātketuṃ kṛtvā rathasya vai ..
3.4.d:
चंद्रभास्करयोस्साराच्चक्रे कृत्वा तथैव च ॥33॥
सुमेरोश्च तथा सारात्केतुं कृत्वा रथस्य वै ॥
3.4.m:
and likewise made the two wheels from the essence of the moon and the sun.
And making the banner of the chariot from the essence of Mount Sumeru,

3.4.s:
dadau śivāya mahate yānaṃ syandanarūpi tat .. 34 ..
tadā brahmā svayaṃ prāpya babhūva rathasārathiḥ ..
3.4.d:
ददौ शिवाय महते यानं स्यन्दनरूपि तत् ॥ 34 ॥
तदा ब्रह्मा स्वयं प्राप्य बभूव रथसारथिः ॥
3.4.m:
they gave that vehicle in the form of a chariot to great Śiva.
Then Brahmā himself, arriving there, became the charioteer.

3.4.s:
vedāśca vājinaścāsandevadevasya vai rathe .. 35 ..
lokālokagireḥ sāro dhanuścāsīnmahātmanaḥ ..
3.4.d:
वेदाश्च वाजिनश्चासन्देवदेवस्य वै रथे ॥ 35 ॥
लोकालोकगिरेः सारो धनुश्चासीन्महात्मनः ॥
3.4.m:
And the Vedas became the horses on the chariot of the God of gods.
The essence of Mount Lokāloka became the bow of the great-souled one,

3.4.s:
ghoraṃ cājagavaṃ nāma prasiddha mabhavaddhanuḥ .. 36 ..
sajyaṃ cakāra bhagavāṃstaddhanuḥ kaṭhinaṃ mahat ..
3.4.d:
घोरं चाजगवं नाम प्रसिद्ध मभवद्धनुः ॥ 36 ॥
सज्यं चकार भगवांस्तद्धनुः कठिनं महत् ॥
3.4.m:
and that fierce bow became famous by the name Ajagava.
The Lord strung that huge, stiff bow;

3.4.s:
bhagnībhūtamabhūccāpaṃ devadevasya vai ruṣā .. 37 ..
vismito bhagavānviṣṇussāraṃ svargasya vai tadā ..
3.4.d:
भग्नीभूतमभूच्चापं देवदेवस्य वै रुषा ॥ 37 ॥
विस्मितो भगवान्विष्णुस्सारं स्वर्गस्य वै तदा ॥
3.4.m:
and the bow of the God of gods shattered through his wrath.
Astonished, the blessed Lord Viṣṇu then, taking the essence of heaven,

3.4.s:
gṛhītvāśu dhanurdivyaṃ pinākaṃ sa cakāra ha .. 38 ..
sajyaṃ jātaṃ ca rudreṇa puṣṭibhūtaṃ mahaddhanuḥ ..
3.4.d:
गृहीत्वाशु धनुर्दिव्यं पिनाकं स चकार ह ॥ 38 ॥
सज्यं जातं च रुद्रेण पुष्टिभूतं महद्धनुः ॥
3.4.m:
swiftly fashioned the divine bow Pināka.
The great bow was strung and strengthened by Rudra.

3.4.s:
tadā brahmarṣayastuṣṭāstuṣṭuvu rmanasā haram .. 39 ..
pinākīti ca tannāmā prasiddhobhūnmaheśvaraḥ ..
3.4.d:
तदा ब्रह्मर्षयस्तुष्टास्तुष्टुवु र्मनसा हरम् ॥ 39 ॥
पिनाकीति च तन्नामा प्रसिद्धोभून्महेश्वरः ॥
3.4.m:
Then the brahmin seers, pleased, praised Hara in their minds.
And Maheśvara became renowned by the name Pinākin.

3.4.s:
guṇaścāpasya vai śeṣaḥ śakro vāṇastadābhavat .. 40 ..
śarapakṣau vahnivāyū śalyaṃ viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ ..
3.4.d:
गुणश्चापस्य वै शेषः शक्रो वाणस्तदाभवत् ॥ 40 ॥
शरपक्षौ वह्निवायू शल्यं विष्णुः सनातनः ॥
3.4.m:
Śeṣa became the bowstring, and Śakra was the arrow then.
Fire and Wind were the two feathers of the arrow, and eternal Viṣṇu was the shaft.

3.4.s:
tena bāṇena daityānāṃ koṭisaṃkhyā mṛtā ca khe .. 41 ..
tripuraṃ dāhayāmāsa māyinā pālitaṃ śivaḥ ..
3.4.d:
तेन बाणेन दैत्यानां कोटिसंख्या मृता च खे ॥ 41 ॥
त्रिपुरं दाहयामास मायिना पालितं शिवः ॥
3.4.m:
By that arrow, a crore of Daityas were slain in the sky.
Śiva burned Tripura, which had been protected by the illusionist [demon].

3.4.s:
bhasmībhūte pure ghore tadā lokapatirvidhiḥ .. 42 ..
pinākinaṃ mahārudraṃ mīnarāśisthite ravau ..
śaśino maṇḍalasyaiva rājānaṃ sa cakāra tam ..
3.4.d:
भस्मीभूते पुरे घोरे तदा लोकपतिर्विधिः ॥ 42 ॥
पिनाकिनं महारुद्रं मीनराशिस्थिते रवौ ॥
शशिनो मण्डलस्यैव राजानं स चकार तम् ॥
3.4.m:
When that terrible city had turned to ashes, then the creator Brahmā, the lord of the worlds,
when the sun was in the sign of Pisces, to Pinākin, Great Rudra,
made him the king of the disc of the moon.

3.4.s:
svādhikārām̐stadā devā avāpustāmasāntare .. 43 ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
3.4.d:
स्वाधिकाराम्̐स्तदा देवा अवापुस्तामसान्तरे ॥ 43 ॥
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
3.4.m:
Then the gods obtained their own offices during the interval of Tāmasa.
Sūta said:

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā pinākī ca svamukhātsvāṃśamuttamam .. 44 ..
samutpādya haradvāre hima sānau cakāra ha ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा पिनाकी च स्वमुखात्स्वांशमुत्तमम् ॥ 44 ॥
समुत्पाद्य हरद्वारे हिम सानौ चकार ह ॥
3.4.m:
Having heard this, Pinākin, producing an excellent portion of himself from his mouth,
placed it at Haridvāra on the snow-peak.

3.4.s:
macchando nāma tatraiva yogī śaṃbhuparāyaṇaḥ .. 45 ..
gorakhasya gururyo vai tanmukhe teja āviśat ..
3.4.d:
मच्छन्दो नाम तत्रैव योगी शंभुपरायणः ॥ 45 ॥
गोरखस्य गुरुर्यो वै तन्मुखे तेज आविशत् ॥
3.4.m:
Right there was a yogin devoted to Śaṃbhu named Macchanda.
The splendour entered the mouth of him who was the guru of Gorakha.

3.4.s:
raṃbhā nāmnaiva tatraiva svarveśyā kāmarūpiṇī .. 46 ..
macchandaṃ ca vaśīkṛtya bubhuje smaravihvalā ..
3.4.d:
रंभा नाम्नैव तत्रैव स्वर्वेश्या कामरूपिणी ॥ 46 ॥
मच्छन्दं च वशीकृत्य बुभुजे स्मरविह्वला ॥
3.4.m:
Right there, a celestial courtezan named Rambhā, capable of changing her form at will,
enchanted Macchanda and, agitated by love, enjoyed union with him.

3.4.s:
tayossakāśādvai jātassa putro rucirānanaḥ .. 47 ..
nāthaśarmeti vikhyāto vidvāñcchreṣṭhataro'bhavat ..
sa jitvā paṃḍitānbhūmau purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgataḥ ..
3.4.d:
तयोस्सकाशाद्वै जातस्स पुत्रो रुचिराननः ॥ 47 ॥
नाथशर्मेति विख्यातो विद्वाञ्च्छ्रेष्ठतरोऽभवत् ॥
स जित्वा पंडितान्भूमौ पुरीं काशीं समागतः ॥
3.4.m:
From the two of them was born a charming-faced son.
Renowned as Nāthaśarman, he became a foremost scholar.
Having conquered the pandits on earth, he arrived at the city of Kāśī.

3.4.s:
śaṃkarācāryavijitastasya śiṣyo babhūva ha .. 48 ..
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
3.4.d:
शंकराचार्यविजितस्तस्य शिष्यो बभूव ह ॥ 48 ॥
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
3.4.m:
Defeated by Śaṅkarācārya, he became his disciple.
Bṛhaspati said:

3.4.s:
cākṣuṣāṃtarasaṃprāpte dvādaśe dvāpare yuge .. 49 ..
kṣatriyaistālajaṃghīyairbrāhmaṇā bhṛguvaṃśajāḥ ..
3.4.d:
चाक्षुषांतरसंप्राप्ते द्वादशे द्वापरे युगे ॥ 49 ॥
क्षत्रियैस्तालजंघीयैर्ब्राह्मणा भृगुवंशजाः ॥
3.4.m:
When the twelfth Dvāpara age arrived in the Cākṣuṣa Manvantara,
the brāhmaṇas born of the lineage of Bhṛgu were destroyed in Kurukṣetra

3.4.s:
vināśitāḥ kurukṣetre gṛhītvā taddhanaṃ bahu .. 50 ..
babhujurbalavaṃtaste daityapakṣā mahādhamāḥ ..
3.4.d:
विनाशिताः कुरुक्षेत्रे गृहीत्वा तद्धनं बहु ॥ 50 ॥
बभुजुर्बलवंतस्ते दैत्यपक्षा महाधमाः ॥
3.4.m:
by the kṣatriyas descended from Tālajaṅgha, who seized their abundant wealth.
Those mighty ones, sided with the Daityas, most vile, enjoyed [that wealth].

3.4.s:
kasyacittu muneḥ patnī gurviṇī ca bhayānvitā .. 51 ..
himatuṃge samāgamya tadgarbhaṃ munisaṃbhavam ..
3.4.d:
कस्यचित्तु मुनेः पत्नी गुर्विणी च भयान्विता ॥ 51 ॥
हिमतुंगे समागम्य तद्गर्भं मुनिसंभवम् ॥
3.4.m:
The pregnant and terrified wife of a certain sage,
reaching the snow-capped peak, that womb born of a sage

3.4.s:
śatavarṣaṃ dadau devī tapasā jñānarūpiṇī .. 52 ..
māturūrū suto bhittvā tato jāto mahītale ..
3.4.d:
शतवर्षं ददौ देवी तपसा ज्ञानरूपिणी ॥ 52 ॥
मातुरूरू सुतो भित्त्वा ततो जातो महीतले ॥
3.4.m:
the lady, the embodiment of wisdom, carried for a hundred years by her ascetic power.
The son, bursting forth from his mother's thigh, was then born on the surface of the earth.

3.4.s:
tejasā tasya putrasya bhasmībhūtamabhūjjagat .. 53 ..
tadā tu sakalā devāḥ puraskṛtya prajāpatim ..
3.4.d:
तेजसा तस्य पुत्रस्य भस्मीभूतमभूज्जगत् ॥ 53 ॥
तदा तु सकला देवाः पुरस्कृत्य प्रजापतिम् ॥
3.4.m:
By the splendour of that son, the world turned to ashes.
Then all the gods, placing Prajāpati at their head,

3.4.s:
vajrasthitaśca vai tālāssamājagmu rbhayāturāḥ .. 54 ..
pitṛbhidaivatairbālassamājñāto himācale ..
3.4.d:
वज्रस्थितश्च वै तालास्समाजग्मु र्भयातुराः ॥ 54 ॥
पितृभिदैवतैर्बालस्समाज्ञातो हिमाचले ॥
3.4.m:
and the Tālas situated in the thunderbolt, gathered together, afflicted with fear.
Instructed on the Himālaya by his ancestors and the deities, the boy

3.4.s:
lokanāśakaraṃ tejo jalamadhye sa cākṣipat .. 55 ..
jaladevī ca vaḍavā bhūtvā tatteja uttamam ..
3.4.d:
लोकनाशकरं तेजो जलमध्ये स चाक्षिपत् ॥ 55 ॥
जलदेवी च वडवा भूत्वा तत्तेज उत्तमम् ॥
3.4.m:
cast into the water that splendour which caused the destruction of the world.
And the goddess of waters, becoming a mare, drank that supreme splendour,

3.4.s:
pītvā vavāma tatraiva pīḍitā raudratejasā .. 56 ..
tadāgatya svayaṃ brahmā trikuṭo yatra vai giriḥ ..
3.4.d:
पीत्वा ववाम तत्रैव पीडिता रौद्रतेजसा ॥ 56 ॥
तदागत्य स्वयं ब्रह्मा त्रिकुटो यत्र वै गिरिः ॥
3.4.m:
and vomited it right there, tormented by the fierce fire.
Then, having arrived in person where Mount Trikuṭa stands,

3.4.s:
tadadhaḥ sāgare ghore sthāpayāmāsa lokapaḥ .. 57 ..
meṣage dyumaṇau prāpte śaśimaṇḍalagaṃ prabhum ..
3.4.d:
तदधः सागरे घोरे स्थापयामास लोकपः ॥ 57 ॥
मेषगे द्युमणौ प्राप्ते शशिमण्डलगं प्रभुम् ॥
3.4.m:
Brahmā, the protector of the worlds, placed it beneath it in the terrible ocean.
When the sun had entered Aries, to the Lord situated in the disc of the moon,

3.4.s:
taṃ rudraṃ sa cakārāśu parameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ .. 58 ..
ūrujātātsmṛto vorvo dahano lokadāhataḥ ..
3.4.d:
तं रुद्रं स चकाराशु परमेष्ठी पितामहः ॥ 58 ॥
ऊरुजातात्स्मृतो वोर्वो दहनो लोकदाहतः ॥
3.4.m:
to that Rudra, Brahmā, the grandfather of all, swiftly made [him lord].
Because he was born from the thigh, Aurva is remembered; he is the fire because he burns the world;

3.4.s:
vaḍavāmukhato jāto vāḍavo nāma sa prabhuḥ .. 59 ..
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā tu dahano guruvākyaṃ manoharam ..
3.4.d:
वडवामुखतो जातो वाडवो नाम स प्रभुः ॥ 59 ॥
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा तु दहनो गुरुवाक्यं मनोहरम् ॥
3.4.m:
because he was born from the mouth of the mare, that Lord is named Vāḍava.
Sūta said:
Having heard the charming words of his guru, the Fire,

3.4.s:
svamukhātteja utpādya kurukṣetraṃ cakāra ha .. 60 ..
sārasvatasya viprasya gṛhe jātassa vai śivaḥ ..
3.4.d:
स्वमुखात्तेज उत्पाद्य कुरुक्षेत्रं चकार ह ॥ 60 ॥
सारस्वतस्य विप्रस्य गृहे जातस्स वै शिवः ॥
3.4.m:
producing splendour from his mouth, directed it to Kurukṣetra.
Born in the house of a Sārasvata brāhmaṇa, that Śiva

3.4.s:
kṣetraśarmeti vikhyāto vidvacchreṣṭho babhūva ha .. 61 ..
śaṃkarācāryamāgamya śiṣyo bhūtvā parājitaḥ ..
3.4.d:
क्षेत्रशर्मेति विख्यातो विद्वच्छ्रेष्ठो बभूव ह ॥ 61 ॥
शंकराचार्यमागम्य शिष्यो भूत्वा पराजितः ॥
3.4.m:
became renowned as Kṣetraśarman, a foremost scholar.
Approaching Śaṅkarācārya, he was defeated and became his disciple.

3.4.s:
brahmacaryavratī kāśyāṃ tasthau śaṃbhuparāyaṇaḥ .. 62
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca ..
ekārṇave purā jāte naṣṭe sthāvara jaṃgame ..
3.4.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यव्रती काश्यां तस्थौ शंभुपरायणः ॥ 62
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥
एकार्णवे पुरा जाते नष्टे स्थावर जंगमे ॥
3.4.m:
observing the vow of celibacy, dwelt in Kāśī, devoted to Śambhu.
Bṛhaspati said:
Long ago, when the single ocean had arisen and the stationary and moving [beings] had perished,

3.4.s:
śatābde brahmaṇaḥ prāpte'vyaktajanmani lokage .. 63 ..
avyaktaṃ prakṛtirmāyā pītvā sarvajalaṃ mudā ..
3.4.d:
शताब्दे ब्रह्मणः प्राप्तेऽव्यक्तजन्मनि लोकगे ॥ 63 ॥
अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिर्माया पीत्वा सर्वजलं मुदा ॥
3.4.m:
when a century of Brahmā had arrived, at the unmanifest birth belonging to the world,
the unmanifest, nature, Māyā, joyfully drinking up all the water,

3.4.s:
mahākālī svayaṃ mūrtiraṃdhakārasvarū piṇī .. 64 ..
ekā babhūva tatraiva prākṛte kalpadāruṇe ..
3.4.d:
महाकाली स्वयं मूर्तिरंधकारस्वरू पिणी ॥ 64 ॥
एका बभूव तत्रैव प्राकृते कल्पदारुणे ॥
3.4.m:
herself [became] Mahākālī, the embodiment whose very nature is darkness.
She alone remained there in that terrible elemental dissolution.

3.4.s:
caturyugānāṃ koṭīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ dāruṇe laye .. 65 ..
ṣaṣṭilakṣayutānāṃ ca kālastatra vyatī tavān..
3.4.d:
चतुर्युगानां कोटीनां त्रयाणां दारुणे लये ॥ 65 ॥
षष्टिलक्षयुतानां च कालस्तत्र व्यती तवान्॥
3.4.m:
During the terrible dissolution of three crores of caturyugas
and sixty lakhs [more], time passed there.

3.4.s:
tadā sā prakṛtirdevī nityaśuddhā sanātanī ..66..
svecchayā ca svarūpaṃ svaṃ mahāgauramanuttamam ..
3.4.d:
तदा सा प्रकृतिर्देवी नित्यशुद्धा सनातनी ॥66॥
स्वेच्छया च स्वरूपं स्वं महागौरमनुत्तमम् ॥
3.4.m:
Then that Goddess, nature, eternally pure and everlasting,
by her own will assumed her own unsurpassed form, dazzling white,

3.4.s:
paṃcavaktraṃ daśabhujaṃ trinetraṃ ca dadhau śivā.. .. 67 ..
bhālanetreṇa sā mātā sūkṣmatejo dadarśa ha ..
3.4.d:
पंचवक्त्रं दशभुजं त्रिनेत्रं च दधौ शिवा॥ ॥ 67 ॥
भालनेत्रेण सा माता सूक्ष्मतेजो ददर्श ह ॥
3.4.m:
five-faced, ten-armed, and three-eyed, [as] Śivā.
With the eye in her forehead, that Mother perceived a subtle light,

3.4.s:
śūnyabhūtaṃ paraṃ nityamavikāri niraṃjanam .. 68 ..
tadā dikṣu gataṃ brahma svabhujaiḥ prakṛtiḥ purā ..
3.4.d:
शून्यभूतं परं नित्यमविकारि निरंजनम् ॥ 68 ॥
तदा दिक्षु गतं ब्रह्म स्वभुजैः प्रकृतिः पुरा ॥
3.4.m:
become a void, supreme, eternal, immutable, and taintless.
Then, long ago, nature, wishing with her own arms

3.4.s:
grahītumicchatī tatra na samarthā babhūva vai .. 69 ..
vismitā prakṛtirmātā paṃcavaktraiḥ sanātanam ..
3.4.d:
ग्रहीतुमिच्छती तत्र न समर्था बभूव वै ॥ 69 ॥
विस्मिता प्रकृतिर्माता पंचवक्त्रैः सनातनम् ॥
3.4.m:
to seize that Brahman which had gone into the quarters, was not able to do so there.
Astonished, Mother Nature, with her five mouths, praised the eternal,

3.4.s:
tuṣṭāva parayā bhaktyā cirakālātparātparam .. .. 70 ..
dhātuśabdaiḥ prāṅmukhajaiḥ pratyayairyāmyavaktrajaiḥ ..
3.4.d:
तुष्टाव परया भक्त्या चिरकालात्परात्परम् ॥ ॥ 70 ॥
धातुशब्दैः प्राङ्मुखजैः प्रत्ययैर्याम्यवक्त्रजैः ॥
3.4.m:
the highest of the high, with supreme devotion after a long time:
with words consisting of verbal roots born of her east-facing mouth, with suffixes born of her southern mouth,

3.4.s:
suvibhaktimayaiḥ śabdairmukhapaścimajaiḥ sthirā .. 71 ..
tiṅvibhaktimayairnityā mukhottaramayai rmudā ..
3.4.d:
सुविभक्तिमयैः शब्दैर्मुखपश्चिमजैः स्थिरा ॥ 71 ॥
तिङ्विभक्तिमयैर्नित्या मुखोत्तरमयै र्मुदा ॥
3.4.m:
with words composed of nominal case-endings born of her western mouth, the steadfast one,
with those composed of verbal endings born of her northern mouth, the eternal one joyfully [praised],

3.4.s:
nabhovaktramayaiḥ śabdairvarṇamātrairniraṃjanam .. 72 ..
saccidānaṃdaghanakaṃ pūrṇabrahma sanātanam ..
3.4.d:
नभोवक्त्रमयैः शब्दैर्वर्णमात्रैर्निरंजनम् ॥ 72 ॥
सच्चिदानंदघनकं पूर्णब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥
3.4.m:
and with words consisting solely of phonemes born of her upward mouth, [she praised] the taintless,
mass of being, consciousness, and bliss, the full and eternal Brahman.

3.4.s:
tutoṣa tattu sarvajñaṃ pacavaktreṣu cāgamat .. 73 ..
puruṣatvamabhūdbrahma svayaṃbhūrnāma cābhavat..
3.4.d:
तुतोष तत्तु सर्वज्ञं पचवक्त्रेषु चागमत् ॥ 73 ॥
पुरुषत्वमभूद्ब्रह्म स्वयंभूर्नाम चाभवत्॥
3.4.m:
That omniscient [Brahman] was pleased and entered into her five mouths.
Brahman attained manhood and came to be named Svayambhū.

3.4.s:
avyaktātprakṛterjāto'vyaktajanmā hi sa smṛtaḥ .. 74 ..
tasya hetoḥ svayaṃ devī varadā lokarūpiṇī ..
3.4.d:
अव्यक्तात्प्रकृतेर्जातोऽव्यक्तजन्मा हि स स्मृतः ॥ 74 ॥
तस्य हेतोः स्वयं देवी वरदा लोकरूपिणी ॥
3.4.m:
Born from unmanifest nature, he is indeed remembered as of unmanifest birth.
For his sake, the Goddess herself, the granter of boons, whose form is the worlds,

3.4.s:
mahālakṣmīśca pūrvārddhājjātā ṣoḍaśalokinī .. 75 ..
aṣṭādaśabhujāstasyā lokarakṣaṇatatparāḥ ..
3.4.d:
महालक्ष्मीश्च पूर्वार्द्धाज्जाता षोडशलोकिनी ॥ 75 ॥
अष्टादशभुजास्तस्या लोकरक्षणतत्पराः ॥
3.4.m:
Mahālakṣmī, possessing sixteen worlds, was born from her front half.
Her eighteen arms were intent upon protecting the worlds.

3.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā tadadbhutaṃ rūpaṃ svayaṃbhūrvismayānvitaḥ .. .. 76 ..
praviśya bahudhā bhūtvā nāntaṃ tasyā jagāma ha ..
3.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा तदद्भुतं रूपं स्वयंभूर्विस्मयान्वितः ॥ ॥ 76 ॥
प्रविश्य बहुधा भूत्वा नान्तं तस्या जगाम ह ॥
3.4.m:
Beholding that wondrous form, Svayambhū was filled with astonishment.
Having entered and become manifold, he did not reach her end.

3.4.s:
bṛhatvādbahurūpatvādbrahmā nāmeti viśrutaḥ .. 77 ..
śramito bhagavānbrahmā satyalokamupa sthitaḥ ..
3.4.d:
बृहत्वाद्बहुरूपत्वाद्ब्रह्मा नामेति विश्रुतः ॥ 77 ॥
श्रमितो भगवान्ब्रह्मा सत्यलोकमुप स्थितः ॥
3.4.m:
Because of his immensity and his manifold forms, he is renowned by the name Brahmā.
Exhausted, the Lord Brahmā arrived at Satyaloka.

3.4.s:
mukhebhya udbhavairdevo vedaistuṣṭāva śaṃkaram .. 78 ..
ciraṃ kālaṃ tadaṃgādvai nadīnadasamudbhavaḥ ..
3.4.d:
मुखेभ्य उद्भवैर्देवो वेदैस्तुष्टाव शंकरम् ॥ 78 ॥
चिरं कालं तदंगाद्वै नदीनदसमुद्भवः ॥
3.4.m:
With the Vedas born from his mouths, the god praised Śaṅkara.
For a long time, indeed, the arising of rivers and streams [came] from his limbs.

3.4.s:
ekārṇavaṃ tadā jātaṃ śete tatra svayaṃ prabhuḥ .. .. 79 ..
sahasrayugaparyaṃtamuṣitvā'vyaktabhūḥ svayam ..
3.4.d:
एकार्णवं तदा जातं शेते तत्र स्वयं प्रभुः ॥ ॥ 79 ॥
सहस्रयुगपर्यंतमुषित्वाऽव्यक्तभूः स्वयम् ॥
3.4.m:
A single ocean then arose; the Lord himself slept upon it.
Having dwelt [there] for the duration of a thousand yugas, the one born from the unmanifest himself,

3.4.s:
satyalokamupāgamya punaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ cakāra ha .. 80 ..
anantāḥ sṛṣṭayaścāsangaṇarūpāḥ pṛthakpṛthak ..
3.4.d:
सत्यलोकमुपागम्य पुनः सृष्टिं चकार ह ॥ 80 ॥
अनन्ताः सृष्टयश्चासन्गणरूपाः पृथक्पृथक् ॥
3.4.m:
having gone to Satyaloka, performed creation again.
And the creations were endless, having distinct forms of host after host.

3.4.s:
tābhirvyaktamabhūtsarvaṃ mahālakṣmīmayaṃ jagat.. 81 ..
dṛṣṭvā bahutvaṃ sṛṣṭīnāṃ mahālakṣmīḥ sanātanī..
3.4.d:
ताभिर्व्यक्तमभूत्सर्वं महालक्ष्मीमयं जगत्॥ 81 ॥
दृष्ट्वा बहुत्वं सृष्टीनां महालक्ष्मीः सनातनी॥
3.4.m:
Through them, the entire universe, consisting of Mahālakṣmī, became manifest.
Seeing the multitude of creations, eternal Mahālakṣmī

3.4.s:
vismitābhūcca sarveśaṃ bhagavantamupāyayau .. .. 82 ..
natvovāca vaco ramyaṃ kṛṣṇamavyaktamaṃgalam ..
3.4.d:
विस्मिताभूच्च सर्वेशं भगवन्तमुपाययौ ॥ ॥ 82 ॥
नत्वोवाच वचो रम्यं कृष्णमव्यक्तमंगलम् ॥
3.4.m:
was astonished and approached the Lord, the master of all.
Bowing down, she spoke delightful words, dark and auspiciously unmanifest:

3.4.s:
bhagavannityaśuddhātmannarāścāsanmahattarāḥ .. 83 ..
kathaṃ teṣāṃ ca gaṇanā kartavyā ca mayā sadā ..
3.4.d:
भगवन्नित्यशुद्धात्मन्नराश्चासन्महत्तराः ॥ 83 ॥
कथं तेषां च गणना कर्तव्या च मया सदा ॥
3.4.m:
“O Lord, whose self is eternally pure! Men have become exceedingly great.
How, then, is their reckoning always to be carried out by me?”

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasyā dvidhābhūtaśca so'vyayaḥ .. 84 ..
pūrvārddhātsa tu raktāṅgaḥ parārddhādgaurarūpavān ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्या द्विधाभूतश्च सोऽव्ययः ॥ 84 ॥
पूर्वार्द्धात्स तु रक्ताङ्गः परार्द्धाद्गौररूपवान् ॥
3.4.m:
Hearing this speech of hers, that imperishable one divided in two:
from his front half he had red limbs, and from his other half he had a fair form.

3.4.s:
caturbhujassa raktāṃgo gauravarṇaścatu rbhujaḥ ..85..
sarvasṛṣṭigaṇānāṃ ca sa īśo bhagavānbhavaḥ ..
3.4.d:
चतुर्भुजस्स रक्तांगो गौरवर्णश्चतु र्भुजः ॥85॥
सर्वसृष्टिगणानां च स ईशो भगवान्भवः ॥
3.4.m:
The red-limbed one was four-armed, and the fair-complexioned one was four-armed.
And he, the Lord Bhava, is the master of all the hosts of creation.

3.4.s:
gaṇeśo nāma vikhyātaśceśvarassa tu viśrutaḥ ..86..
paraścaturbhujo yo vai yogidhyeyo niraṃ janaḥ ..
3.4.d:
गणेशो नाम विख्यातश्चेश्वरस्स तु विश्रुतः ॥86॥
परश्चतुर्भुजो यो वै योगिध्येयो निरं जनः ॥
3.4.m:
He is renowned by the name Gaṇeśa and celebrated as Īśvara.
The other four-armed one is indeed the taintless one to be meditated upon by yogins.

3.4.s:
ekadā vidhito jātaḥ śivaḥ pārvativallabhaḥ .. 87 ..
gaṇeśaṃ pūjayāmāsa sahasrābdaṃ prayatnataḥ ..
3.4.d:
एकदा विधितो जातः शिवः पार्वतिवल्लभः ॥ 87 ॥
गणेशं पूजयामास सहस्राब्दं प्रयत्नतः ॥
3.4.m:
Once, Śiva, the beloved of Pārvatī, born through fate,
zealously worshipped Gaṇeśa for a thousand years.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavāngaṇeśaḥ śarvapūjakaḥ .. .. 88 ..
varaṃ varaya taṃ prāha pārvatīsahitaṃ haram ..
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्गणेशः शर्वपूजकः ॥ ॥ 88 ॥
वरं वरय तं प्राह पार्वतीसहितं हरम् ॥
3.4.m:
Then the Lord Gaṇeśa, the worshipper of Śarva, was pleased.
“Choose a boon,” he said to that Hara accompanied by Pārvatī.

3.4.s:
prasannātmā bhavaḥ sākṣāttuṣṭāva ca vinamradhīḥ .. 89 ..
.. śiva uvāca .. ..
namo viṣṇusvarūpāya gaṇeśāya parātmane ..
3.4.d:
प्रसन्नात्मा भवः साक्षात्तुष्टाव च विनम्रधीः ॥ 89 ॥
॥ शिव उवाच ॥ ॥
नमो विष्णुस्वरूपाय गणेशाय परात्मने ॥
3.4.m:
With a pleased soul and humble mind, Bhava in person praised [him]:
Śiva said:
“Homage to Gaṇeśa, the supreme self, whose form is Viṣṇu,

3.4.s:
caturbhujāya raktāya yajñapūrṇakarāya ca .. 90 ..
vighnahaṃtre jagadbhartre sarvānandapradāyine ..
3.4.d:
चतुर्भुजाय रक्ताय यज्ञपूर्णकराय च ॥ 90 ॥
विघ्नहंत्रे जगद्भर्त्रे सर्वानन्दप्रदायिने ॥
3.4.m:
four-armed, red-bodied, and the completer of sacrifices,
the destroyer of obstacles, the maintainer of the universe, the bestower of all bliss!”

3.4.s:
siddhīnāṃ pataye tubhyaṃ nidhīnāṃ pataye namaḥ .. 91 ..
prasanno bhava deveśa putro bhava mama priyaḥ ..
3.4.d:
सिद्धीनां पतये तुभ्यं निधीनां पतये नमः ॥ 91 ॥
प्रसन्नो भव देवेश पुत्रो भव मम प्रियः ॥
3.4.m:
Homage to you, lord of attainments, lord of treasures.
Be pleased, O lord of gods; become my dear son.

3.4.s:
iti śrutvādipūjyastu gaṇeśo bhaktavatsalaḥ ..92..
pārvatyāḥ sarvadehāttu tejobhūtātsamu dbhavaḥ ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वादिपूज्यस्तु गणेशो भक्तवत्सलः ॥92॥
पार्वत्याः सर्वदेहात्तु तेजोभूतात्समु द्भवः ॥
3.4.m:
Hearing this, Gaṇeśa, the first to be worshipped, fond of his devotees,
was born from the entire body of Pārvatī, formed of her splendour.

3.4.s:
tadā kailāsaśikhare sarve devāssavāsavāḥ .. 93 ..
maṃgalārthamupājagmurdevadevasya mandire..
3.4.d:
तदा कैलासशिखरे सर्वे देवास्सवासवाः ॥ 93 ॥
मंगलार्थमुपाजग्मुर्देवदेवस्य मन्दिरे॥
3.4.m:
Then, upon the peak of Kailāsa, all the gods together with Indra
came to the temple of the god of gods for the sake of celebration.

3.4.s:
mahotsavaśca tatrāsītsarvalokasukhāvahaḥ .. 94 ..
etasminnaṃtare tatra sūryaputraḥ śaniḥ svayam ..
3.4.d:
महोत्सवश्च तत्रासीत्सर्वलोकसुखावहः ॥ 94 ॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र सूर्यपुत्रः शनिः स्वयम् ॥
3.4.m:
And there was a great festival there, bringing joy to all the worlds.
Meanwhile, Śani, the son of the Sun himself,

3.4.s:
krūradṛṣṭiḥ samāyātaḥ kālātmā devamaṇḍape .. 95 ..
tasya darśanamātreṇa sa bālo viśirā hyabhūt ..
3.4.d:
क्रूरदृष्टिः समायातः कालात्मा देवमण्डपे ॥ 95 ॥
तस्य दर्शनमात्रेण स बालो विशिरा ह्यभूत् ॥
3.4.m:
arrived in the gods' pavilion, of cruel gaze and the embodiment of Time.
At mere sight of him, that boy became headless indeed.

3.4.s:
hāhākāro mahām̐ścāsītkailāse guhyakālaye .. 96 ..
tacchiraścaṃdraloke vai tulāsaṃsthe divākare ..
3.4.d:
हाहाकारो महाम्̐श्चासीत्कैलासे गुह्यकालये ॥ 96 ॥
तच्छिरश्चंद्रलोके वै तुलासंस्थे दिवाकरे ॥
3.4.m:
And a great cry of grief arose on Kailāsa, the abode of the Guhyakas.
That head went indeed to the realm of the Moon; when the Sun is in Libra,

3.4.s:
saptaviṃśaddinānyeva prakāśayati bhūtale .. 97 ..
niṃdito daivataistatra śanirjanabhayaṃkaraḥ ..
3.4.d:
सप्तविंशद्दिनान्येव प्रकाशयति भूतले ॥ 97 ॥
निंदितो दैवतैस्तत्र शनिर्जनभयंकरः ॥
3.4.m:
it shines down upon the earth for twenty-seven days alone.
Śani, terrifying to people, was rebuked there by the deities.

3.4.s:
gajasya mastakaṃ chittvā dantaikaṃ rāgarūpi yat .. 98 ..
tacchiśoḥ kaṃdhare rakte'ropayatsūryasaṃbhavaḥ ..
3.4.d:
गजस्य मस्तकं छित्त्वा दन्तैकं रागरूपि यत् ॥ 98 ॥
तच्छिशोः कंधरे रक्तेऽरोपयत्सूर्यसंभवः ॥
3.4.m:
Cutting off an elephant's head, which possessed a single tusk, red in color,
the son of the Sun fixed it onto the bloody neck of that child.

3.4.s:
gaja yonyā stuto brahmā karkaṭasya tadā śiraḥ .. 99 ..
samāropya tu tadyoniḥ karkaṭo viśirīkṛtaḥ ..
3.4.d:
गज योन्या स्तुतो ब्रह्मा कर्कटस्य तदा शिरः ॥ 99 ॥
समारोप्य तु तद्योनिः कर्कटो विशिरीकृतः ॥
3.4.m:
Praised by the elephant's womb, Brahmā then fixed
the head of a crab upon it; thus the crab of that womb was rendered headless.

3.4.s:
evaṃ gajānano jāto gaṇeśaśceśvaraḥ svayam .. .. 100
.. sūta uvāca ..
iti śrutvā gaṇeśastu gurorvacanamuttamam ..
3.4.d:
एवं गजाननो जातो गणेशश्चेश्वरः स्वयम् ॥ ॥ 100
॥ सूत उवाच ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गणेशस्तु गुरोर्वचनमुत्तमम् ॥
3.4.m:
Thus the elephant-faced Gaṇeśa, the Lord himself, was born.
Sūta said:
Hearing these excellent words of his guru, Gaṇeśa,

3.4.s:
svamukhātskaṃdhamutpādya kāśyāṃ jātaḥ sa ceśvaraḥ .. 101 ..
daivajñasya dvijasyaiva putro bhūtvā śubhānanaḥ ..
3.4.d:
स्वमुखात्स्कंधमुत्पाद्य काश्यां जातः स चेश्वरः ॥ 101 ॥
दैवज्ञस्य द्विजस्यैव पुत्रो भूत्वा शुभाननः ॥
3.4.m:
emitting a shoulder from his own mouth, was born in Kāśī as the Lord.
Having become the handsome-faced son of an astrologer brahmin,

3.4.s:
ḍhuṃḍhirājastato nāmnā prasiddho'bhūnmahītale .. 102 ..
jātakābharaṇaṃ nāma jyotiḥśāstraṃ phalātmakam ..
3.4.d:
ढुंढिराजस्ततो नाम्ना प्रसिद्धोऽभून्महीतले ॥ 102 ॥
जातकाभरणं नाम ज्योतिःशास्त्रं फलात्मकम् ॥
3.4.m:
he then became famed by the name Ḍhuṇḍhirāja on the surface of the earth.
Having composed the astrological treatise of prognostications named Jātakābharaṇa,

3.4.s:
kṛtvā sa vedarakṣārthe śaṃkarācāryamāgamat .. 103 ..
śiṣyo bhūtvā prasannātmā gurusevāparo'bhavat ..
3.4.d:
कृत्वा स वेदरक्षार्थे शंकराचार्यमागमत् ॥ 103 ॥
शिष्यो भूत्वा प्रसन्नात्मा गुरुसेवापरोऽभवत् ॥
3.4.m:
he went to Śaṅkarācārya for the protection of the Veda.
Becoming his pupil, pure in heart, he devoted himself to serving the guru.

3.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ vipra ḍhuṃḍhirājo yathābhavat .. 104 ..
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe pratisargaparvaṇi caturyugakhaṇḍāparaparyāye
kaliyugīyetihāsasamuccaye bhāratīśagorakhanāthakṣetraśarmaḍhuṃḍhirājasamutpatti varṇano nāma
dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 12 .. cha ..
aghorapathabhairavahanumajjanmarudramāhātmyabālaśarmasamutpattivarṇanam
3.4.d:
इति ते कथितं विप्र ढुंढिराजो यथाभवत् ॥ 104 ॥
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे प्रतिसर्गपर्वणि चतुर्युगखण्डापरपर्याये
कलियुगीयेतिहाससमुच्चये भारतीशगोरखनाथक्षेत्रशर्मढुंढिराजसमुत्पत्ति वर्णनो नाम
द्वादशोऽध्यायः ॥ 12 ॥ छ ॥
अघोरपथभैरवहनुमज्जन्मरुद्रमाहात्म्यबालशर्मसमुत्पत्तिवर्णनम्
3.4.m:
Thus has it been told to you, O brahmin, how Ḍhuṇḍhirāja came to be.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Origins of Bhāratīśa, Gorakhanātha, Kṣetraśarman, and Ḍhuṇḍhirāja', in the Compendium of Kaliyuga Histories, in the Four-Age Section, in the Pratisarga Book of the glorious and great Bhaviṣya Purāṇa.
The description of the Aghora path, the birth of Bhairava and Hanūmat, the glory of Rudra, and the origin of Bālaśarman.

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
ṣoḍaśābde ca samprāpte brahmaṇo'vyaktajanmanaḥ .
sa uṣitvā ca kamale sthitaḥ sṛṣṭyarthamudyataḥ . . 1
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
षोडशाब्दे च सम्प्राप्ते ब्रह्मणोऽव्यक्तजन्मनः ।
स उषित्वा च कमले स्थितः सृष्ट्यर्थमुद्यतः ॥ 1
3.4.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
When the sixteenth year of Brahmā, whose birth is unmanifest, arrived,
he, having dwelt and stayed on the lotus, set about creating.

3.4.s:
etasminnantare vaktrātsamudbhūtā ca śāradā .
dvivyāṅgaṃ sundaraṃ tasyā dṛṣṭvā brahmā smarāturaḥ . . 2
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वक्त्रात्समुद्भूता च शारदा ।
द्विव्याङ्गं सुन्दरं तस्या दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मा स्मरातुरः ॥ 2
3.4.m:
Meanwhile, Śāradā arose from his mouth.
Seeing her splendid and divine limb, Brahmā was afflicted with desire.

3.4.s:
balād gṛhītvā tāṃ kanyāmuvāca smarapīḍitaḥ .
ratiṃ dehi madāghūrṇe rakṣa māṃ kāmavihvalam . . 3
3.4.d:
बलाद् गृहीत्वा तां कन्यामुवाच स्मरपीडितः ।
रतिं देहि मदाघूर्णे रक्ष मां कामविह्वलम् ॥ 3
3.4.m:
Seizing that maiden by force, tormented by desire, he said:
'Grant me intercourse, O woman reeling with intoxication! Protect me, distraught with passion!'

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tu sā mātā ruṣā prāha pitāmaham .
pañcavaktro'yamaśubho na yogyastava kandhare . . 4
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तु सा माता रुषा प्राह पितामहम् ।
पञ्चवक्त्रोऽयमशुभो न योग्यस्तव कन्धरे ॥ 4
3.4.m:
Hearing this, that mother spoke in anger to the grandfather [of the worlds]:
'This inauspicious fifth face is not fit for your neck.

3.4.s:
caturvaktro vedamayo yogyassarveśvare tvayi .
ityuktvāntardadhe mātā brahmā krodhānvito'bhavat . . 5
3.4.d:
चतुर्वक्त्रो वेदमयो योग्यस्सर्वेश्वरे त्वयि ।
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे माता ब्रह्मा क्रोधान्वितोऽभवत् ॥ 5
3.4.m:
The four-faced one consisting of the Vedas is fit for you, the Lord of All.'
Having spoken thus, the mother vanished, and Brahmā was filled with wrath.

3.4.s:
tasya kopāgninā toyaṃ śuṣkabhūtamabhūdbhuvi .
śāntibhūte ca tatkope rudro jāto bhayaṅkaraḥ . . 6
3.4.d:
तस्य कोपाग्निना तोयं शुष्कभूतमभूद्भुवि ।
शान्तिभूते च तत्कोपे रुद्रो जातो भयङ्करः ॥ 6
3.4.m:
By the fire of his anger, water became dried up on the earth.
And when that anger subsided, terrifying Rudra was born.

3.4.s:
bhairavo nāma vikhyātaḥ kālātmā saptavāhanaḥ .
svanakhaiśca nṛsiṃhābhaiḥ kṣiptvā tatpañcamaṃ śiraḥ . . 7
3.4.d:
भैरवो नाम विख्यातः कालात्मा सप्तवाहनः ।
स्वनखैश्च नृसिंहाभैः क्षिप्त्वा तत्पञ्चमं शिरः ॥ 7
3.4.m:
Known by the name Bhairava, the embodiment of Time, having seven vehicles,
having cast down that fifth head with his claws resembling Narasiṃha's,

3.4.s:
jagarja balavānrudraḥ śaṅkaro lokaśaṅkaraḥ .
bhayabhītastadā brahmā bhairavaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau . . 8
3.4.d:
जगर्ज बलवान्रुद्रः शङ्करो लोकशङ्करः ।
भयभीतस्तदा ब्रह्मा भैरवं शरणं ययौ ॥ 8
3.4.m:
mighty Rudra, Śaṅkara the maker of auspiciousness for the worlds, roared.
Then Brahmā, terrified with fear, sought refuge in Bhairava:

3.4.s:
nātha naḥ pāpabhūtānāṃ dhiyo yo'sau pracodayāt .
iti śrutvā sa bhagavānbhairavo lokaviśrutaḥ . . 9
3.4.d:
नाथ नः पापभूतानां धियो योऽसौ प्रचोदयात् ।
इति श्रुत्वा स भगवान्भैरवो लोकविश्रुतः ॥ 9
3.4.m:
'[May he be] our lord who impels the intellects of us who have become sinful!'
Hearing this, the blessed Bhairava, renowned in the world, [said]:

3.4.s:
brahmabhūtamahaṃ svāminvareṇyaṃ tvāmupāgataḥ .
savitustadvareṇyaṃ yadbhargo devasya dhīmahi . . 3.4.13.10
3.4.d:
ब्रह्मभूतमहं स्वामिन्वरेण्यं त्वामुपागतः ।
सवितुस्तद्वरेण्यं यद्भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि ॥ 3.4.13.10
3.4.m:
'O Master, I have approached you, who have become Brahman, the most excellent one:
May we meditate upon that most excellent splendour of the divine Savitṛ.'

3.4.s:
gāḍhamuccai rurodāśu khātpetuścāśrubindavaḥ .
tato vṛkṣāssamudbhūtā rudrākṣāṇāṃ pṛthakpṛthak . . 11
3.4.d:
गाढमुच्चै रुरोदाशु खात्पेतुश्चाश्रुबिन्दवः ।
ततो वृक्षास्समुद्भूता रुद्राक्षाणां पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 11
3.4.m:
He wept vehemently and loudly at once, and tears fell from the sky.
From them arose various trees of rudrākṣa beads.

3.4.s:
śivo brahmavadhādbhītastatkapālaṃ gṛhītavān .
kapālī nāma vikhyātaṃ bhairavasya tadā hyabhūt . . 12
3.4.d:
शिवो ब्रह्मवधाद्भीतस्तत्कपालं गृहीतवान् ।
कपाली नाम विख्यातं भैरवस्य तदा ह्यभूत् ॥ 12
3.4.m:
Frightened by the slaying of a brahmin, Śiva took up that skull.
Then indeed Bhairava became renowned by the name Kapālin.

3.4.s:
sarvalokeṣu pūtāni yāni cāyatanāni ca .
tāni tānyeva gatvāśu śuddho nābhūcchivaṅkaraḥ . . 13
3.4.d:
सर्वलोकेषु पूतानि यानि चायतनानि च ।
तानि तान्येव गत्वाशु शुद्धो नाभूच्छिवङ्करः ॥ 13
3.4.m:
Whatever holy sanctuaries there were across all the worlds,
having gone to each of those at once, the bringer of auspiciousness was still not purified.

3.4.s:
ekadā teṣu vṛkṣeṣu saṃsthito bhagavānharaḥ .
tadā brahmavadhe doṣaṃ tyaktvā dūramupāgataḥ . . 14
3.4.d:
एकदा तेषु वृक्षेषु संस्थितो भगवान्हरः ।
तदा ब्रह्मवधे दोषं त्यक्त्वा दूरमुपागतः ॥ 14
3.4.m:
Once, the blessed Hara stood among those trees;
then, casting off the guilt of slaying a brahmin, he came afar.

3.4.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti vai śambhurdhṛtvā rudrākṣamuttamam .
purīṃ kāśīṃ samāyātaḥ kapālastena mocitaḥ . . 15
3.4.d:
ततः प्रभृति वै शम्भुर्धृत्वा रुद्राक्षमुत्तमम् ।
पुरीं काशीं समायातः कपालस्तेन मोचितः ॥ 15
3.4.m:
From then on indeed, Śambhu, wearing the excellent rudrākṣa,
arrived at the city of Kāśī; by him the skull was released.

3.4.s:
kapālamocanaṃ nāma tīrthaṃ jātamaghāpaham .
etasminnantare brahmā sarvadevasamanvitaḥ . . 16
3.4.d:
कपालमोचनं नाम तीर्थं जातमघापहम् ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्रह्मा सर्वदेवसमन्वितः ॥ 16
3.4.m:
The holy place named Kapālamocana came into being, removing sins.
Meanwhile, Brahmā, accompanied by all the gods,

3.4.s:
samāgatya mahādevaṃ tuṣṭāva stutijaistavaiḥ .
makarasthe divānāthe śaśinaśceśvaraṃ śubham . .
kapālinaṃ mahārudraṃ cakāra bhagavānvidhiḥ . . 17
3.4.d:
समागत्य महादेवं तुष्टाव स्तुतिजैस्तवैः ।
मकरस्थे दिवानाथे शशिनश्चेश्वरं शुभम् ॥
कपालिनं महारुद्रं चकार भगवान्विधिः ॥ 17
3.4.m:
having arrived, praised Mahādeva with praises born of hymn.
When the lord of day was in Capricorn, the blessed Ordainer made the auspicious Kapālin, the great Rudra, the lord of the Moon.

3.4.s:
sūta uvāca
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ kapālī bhairavaḥ śivaḥ .
svamukhātsvāṃśamutpādya kāśyāṃ jāto hyayonijaḥ . . 18
3.4.d:
सूत उवाच
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं कपाली भैरवः शिवः ।
स्वमुखात्स्वांशमुत्पाद्य काश्यां जातो ह्ययोनिजः ॥ 18
3.4.m:
Sūta said:
Hearing the guru's word, Kapālin, Bhairava, Śiva,
having produced a portion of himself from his own mouth, was born not from a womb in Kāśī.

3.4.s:
kapālamocanātkuṇḍātsamāgamya mahītale .
yatirūpo vedanidhirbhairavo nāma viśrutaḥ . .
aghoraṃ kaṭhinaṃ mārgaṃ svaśiṣyānsamacodaya . . 19
3.4.d:
कपालमोचनात्कुण्डात्समागम्य महीतले ।
यतिरूपो वेदनिधिर्भैरवो नाम विश्रुतः ॥
अघोरं कठिनं मार्गं स्वशिष्यान्समचोदय ॥ 19
3.4.m:
Coming forth onto the surface of the earth from the Kapālamocana pool,
the treasury of the Vedas in the form of an ascetic, famed by the name Bhairava,
he urged his disciples onto the harsh Aghora path.

3.4.s:
śaṅkarācāryamāgamya śiṣyobhūtvā sa bhairavaḥ .
ḍāmaraṃ nāma vai tantraṃ mantrabhūtaṃ cakāra ha . .
kīlitā ye tu vai mantrāstena cotkīlitīkṛtāḥ . . 3.4.13.20
3.4.d:
शङ्कराचार्यमागम्य शिष्योभूत्वा स भैरवः ।
डामरं नाम वै तन्त्रं मन्त्रभूतं चकार ह ॥
कीलिता ये तु वै मन्त्रास्तेन चोत्कीलितीकृताः ॥ 3.4.13.20

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
mandodarī mayasutā tripurādhipateḥ svasā .
tripure tu tadā naṣṭe mahāviṣṇuṃ sanātanam . .
bhaktyā tuṣṭāva sā devī pratyahaṃ guptabhāvinī . . 21
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
मन्दोदरी मयसुता त्रिपुराधिपतेः स्वसा ।
त्रिपुरे तु तदा नष्टे महाविष्णुं सनातनम् ॥
भक्त्या तुष्टाव सा देवी प्रत्यहं गुप्तभाविनी ॥ 21
3.4.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
Mandodarī was the daughter of Maya and sister of the lord of Tripura.
When Tripura was destroyed, that goddess, full of secret devotion,

3.4.s:
bhaktibhāvāttato yogaṃ harau prāpya mahottamam .
vindhyādrikandhare ghore tatraivāntaradhīyata . . 22
3.4.d:
भक्तिभावात्ततो योगं हरौ प्राप्य महोत्तमम् ।
विन्ध्याद्रिकन्धरे घोरे तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥ 22
3.4.m:
praised eternal Mahāviṣṇu with devotion every day.
Then, having attained supreme yoga in Hari through devotional feeling,
she vanished right there in a terrifying cave of the Vindhya mountain.

3.4.s:
caturyugaṃ ca dviśataṃ tasyā jātaṃ samādhitaḥ .
vaivasvate'ntare prāpte dvādaśe caiva kṛdyuge . . 23
3.4.d:
चतुर्युगं च द्विशतं तस्या जातं समाधितः ।
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे प्राप्ते द्वादशे चैव कृद्युगे ॥ 23
3.4.m:
Two hundred and four ages passed for her in meditative absorption.
When the Vaivasvata interval arrived, and in the twelfth Kṛta age,

3.4.s:
pulastyo brahmaṇaḥ putro viśravā roṣato'bhavat .
śatābdaṃ ca tapastaptvā viśravā nāma yo muniḥ . . 24
3.4.d:
पुलस्त्यो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो विश्रवा रोषतोऽभवत् ।
शताब्दं च तपस्तप्त्वा विश्रवा नाम यो मुनिः ॥ 24
3.4.m:
Pulastya was the son of Brahmā, and from anger Viśravas was born.
The sage named Viśravas, having performed ascetic penance for a hundred years,

3.4.s:
sumālino'tha daityasya sutāṃ vai kaikasīṃ mudā .
samudvāhya vidhānena pulastyassa ca viśravāḥ . . 25
3.4.d:
सुमालिनोऽथ दैत्यस्य सुतां वै कैकसीं मुदा ।
समुद्वाह्य विधानेन पुलस्त्यस्स च विश्रवाः ॥ 25
3.4.m:
then joyfully married Kaikasī, the daughter of the demon Sumālin, according to ritual rule;
he was Pulastya's [son] Viśravas.

3.4.s:
kadalīvipine ramye gandhamādanaparvate .
sa reme ca tayā sārddhaṃ viśravā bhagavānṛṣiḥ . . 26
3.4.d:
कदलीविपिने रम्ये गन्धमादनपर्वते ।
स रेमे च तया सार्द्धं विश्रवा भगवानृषिः ॥ 26
3.4.m:
In a delightful plantain forest on Mount Gandhamādana,
he, the venerable sage Viśravas, sported with her.

3.4.s:
rāvaṇaḥ kumbhakarṇaśca tayorjāto hi rākṣasau .
rāvaṇo mātṛbhaktaśca pitṛbhaktastato'nujaḥ . . 27
3.4.d:
रावणः कुम्भकर्णश्च तयोर्जातो हि राक्षसौ ।
रावणो मातृभक्तश्च पितृभक्तस्ततोऽनुजः ॥ 27
3.4.m: Rāvaṇa and Kumbhakarṇa were indeed the two rākṣasas born to them. / Rāvaṇa was devoted to his mother, and his younger brother was devoted to his father.

3.4.s:
sahasrābdaṃ tapo ghoraṃ cakratustau varārthinau .
tadā prasanno bhagavānparameṣṭhī pitāmahaḥ . . 28
3.4.d:
सहस्राब्दं तपो घोरं चक्रतुस्तौ वरार्थिनौ ।
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्परमेष्ठी पितामहः ॥ 28
3.4.m: Desiring a boon, the two performed severe asceticism for a thousand years. / Then the venerable grandfather Parameṣṭhin was pleased.

3.4.s:
dadau tābhyāṃ varaṃ ramyamajeyaṃ devadānavaiḥ .
tau tu labdhavarau kruddhau puṣpakaṃ yānamuttamam . .
gṛhītvā ca balādvīrau yuyudhāte parasparam . . 29
3.4.d:
ददौ ताभ्यां वरं रम्यमजेयं देवदानवैः ।
तौ तु लब्धवरौ क्रुद्धौ पुष्पकं यानमुत्तमम् ॥
गृहीत्वा च बलाद्वीरौ युयुधाते परस्परम् ॥ 29
3.4.m: He granted them a delightful boon [rendering them] invincible to gods and dānavas. / Having obtained the boon, enraged, those two heroes seized the supreme vehicle Puṣpaka by force / and fought with one another.

3.4.s:
tābhyāṃ vinirjitā devāstyaktvā svargaṃ sukhapradam .
pārthivaiḥ pūjayāmāsuḥ śivaṃ kailāsasaṃsthitāḥ . . 3.4.13.30
3.4.d:
ताभ्यां विनिर्जिता देवास्त्यक्त्वा स्वर्गं सुखप्रदम् ।
पार्थिवैः पूजयामासुः शिवं कैलाससंस्थिताः ॥ 3.4.13.30
3.4.m: Utterly vanquished by the two, the gods abandoned the bliss-bestowing heaven / and, residing on Mount Kailāsa, worshipped Śiva with earthly [lingas].

3.4.s:
ekādaśābdamārādhya te devā girijāpatim .
śaṅkarācca varaṃ prāptā nirbhayāśca tadābhavan . . 31
3.4.d:
एकादशाब्दमाराध्य ते देवा गिरिजापतिम् ।
शङ्कराच्च वरं प्राप्ता निर्भयाश्च तदाभवन् ॥ 31
3.4.m: Having propitiated the lord of the Mountain's Daughter for eleven years, / those gods received a boon from Śaṅkara and then became fearless.

3.4.s:
śivo'pi ca svapūrvārddhājjāto vai mānasottare .
girau yatra sthitā devī gautamasya tanūdbhavā . .
añjanā nāma vikhyātā kīśakesaribhoginī . . 32
3.4.d:
शिवोऽपि च स्वपूर्वार्द्धाज्जातो वै मानसोत्तरे ।
गिरौ यत्र स्थिता देवी गौतमस्य तनूद्भवा ॥
अञ्जना नाम विख्याता कीशकेसरिभोगिनी ॥ 32
3.4.m: Moreover, from his own anterior half, Śiva was indeed born on Mount Mānasottara, / where the goddess born of Gautama's body dwelt, / renowned by the name Añjanā, who enjoyed the monkey Kesarin.

3.4.s:
raudraṃ tejastadā ghoraṃ mukhe kesariṇo yayau .
smarāturaḥ kapīndrastu bubhuje tāṃ śubhānanām . . 33
3.4.d:
रौद्रं तेजस्तदा घोरं मुखे केसरिणो ययौ ।
स्मरातुरः कपीन्द्रस्तु बुभुजे तां शुभाननाम् ॥ 33
3.4.m: Then the fierce, terrible splendour of Rudra entered the mouth of Kesarin. / Afflicted by love, the lord of monkeys enjoyed that fair-faced woman.

3.4.s:
etasminnantare vāyuḥ kapīndrasya tanau gataḥ .
vāñchitāmañjanāṃ śubhrāṃ ramayāmāsa vai balāt . . 34
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुः कपीन्द्रस्य तनौ गतः ।
वाञ्छितामञ्जनां शुभ्रां रमयामास वै बलात् ॥ 34
3.4.m: Meanwhile, Vāyu entered the body of the lord of monkeys / and indeed forcibly took pleasure with the fair Añjanā whom he desired.

3.4.s:
dvādaśābdamato jātaṃ dampatyormaithunasthayoḥ .
tadanu bhrūṇamāsādya varṣamātraṃ hi sā dadhat . . 35
3.4.d:
द्वादशाब्दमतो जातं दम्पत्योर्मैथुनस्थयोः ।
तदनु भ्रूणमासाद्य वर्षमात्रं हि सा दधत् ॥ 35
3.4.m: From that, twelve years passed while the couple remained in intercourse. / After that, conceiving an embryo, she bore it for only a year.

3.4.s:
putro jātassa rāgātmā sa rudro vānarānanaḥ .
kurūpācca tato mātrā prakṣipto'bhūdgireradhaḥ . . 36
3.4.d:
पुत्रो जातस्स रागात्मा स रुद्रो वानराननः ।
कुरूपाच्च ततो मात्रा प्रक्षिप्तोऽभूद्गिरेरधः ॥ 36
3.4.m: A son was born, passionate by nature, who was Rudra with a monkey's face. / And because he was deformed, he was thrown down below the mountain by his mother.

3.4.s:
balādāgatya balavāndṛṣṭvā sūryamupasthitam .
vilikhya bhagavānrudro devastatra samāgataḥ . . 37
3.4.d:
बलादागत्य बलवान्दृष्ट्वा सूर्यमुपस्थितम् ।
विलिख्य भगवान्रुद्रो देवस्तत्र समागतः ॥ 37
3.4.m: Advancing with force, the mighty one, seeing the sun present [before him], / scratched [him], and the venerable god Rudra arrived there.

3.4.s:
vajrasantāḍito vāpi na tatyāja tadā ravim .
bhayabhītastadā prāṃśussūryaṃ trāhīti jalpitaḥ . . 38
3.4.d:
वज्रसन्ताडितो वापि न तत्याज तदा रविम् ।
भयभीतस्तदा प्रांशुस्सूर्यं त्राहीति जल्पितः ॥ 38
3.4.m: Even when struck by the thunderbolt, he did not release the sun then. / Terrified with fear, the tall one then cried out to the sun, 'Save [me]!'

3.4.s:
śrutvā tadārtavacanaṃ rāvaṇo lokarāvaṇaḥ .
pucche gṛhītvā taṃ kīśaṃ muṣṭiyuddhamacīkarat . . 39
3.4.d:
श्रुत्वा तदार्तवचनं रावणो लोकरावणः ।
पुच्छे गृहीत्वा तं कीशं मुष्टियुद्धमचीकरत् ॥ 39
3.4.m: Hearing that distressed cry, Rāvaṇa, who makes the worlds cry out, / seized that monkey by the tail and engaged [him] in fist-fighting.

3.4.s:
tadā tu kesarisuto raviṃ tyaktvā ruṣānvitaḥ .
varṣamātraṃ mahāghoraṃ mallayuddhaṃ cakāra ha . . 3.4.13.40
3.4.d:
तदा तु केसरिसुतो रविं त्यक्त्वा रुषान्वितः ।
वर्षमात्रं महाघोरं मल्लयुद्धं चकार ह ॥ 3.4.13.40
3.4.m: Then, releasing the sun, filled with rage, / the son of Kesarin indeed waged a most terrible wrestling combat for a full year.

3.4.s:
śramito rāvaṇastatra bhayabhītassamantataḥ .
palāyanaparo bhūtaḥ kīśarudreṇa tāḍitaḥ . . 41
3.4.d:
श्रमितो रावणस्तत्र भयभीतस्समन्ततः ।
पलायनपरो भूतः कीशरुद्रेण ताडितः ॥ 41
3.4.m: Exhausted there, terrified with fear on all sides, / Rāvaṇa was bent on fleeing, beaten by the monkey Rudra.

3.4.s:
etasminnantare prāpto viśravā bhagavānṛṣiḥ .
stotrairvedamayairdevaṃ tuṣṭāva parayā girā . .4 2
prasannastu tadā rudro rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam .
tyaktvā pampāsarastīre nivāsaṃ kṛtavānbalī . .
sthāṇubhūtaḥ sthitastatra sthāṇurnāma tato'bhavat . . 43
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे प्राप्तो विश्रवा भगवानृषिः ।
स्तोत्रैर्वेदमयैर्देवं तुष्टाव परया गिरा ॥4 2
प्रसन्नस्तु तदा रुद्रो रावणं लोकरावणम् ।
त्यक्त्वा पम्पासरस्तीरे निवासं कृतवान्बली ॥
स्थाणुभूतः स्थितस्तत्र स्थाणुर्नाम ततोऽभवत् ॥ 43
