3.4.m: Three years passed in this manner while he was performing worship; / then the goddess, the bestower of boons, all-auspicious, became pleased. / She said to that best of the twice-born: "Choose a boon!"

3.4.s:
iti vākyaṃ priyaṃ śrutvā dvija āpava namradhīḥ .
tuṣṭāva daṇḍavad bhūtvā bhadrakālīṃ sanātanīm . . 15
3.4.d:
इति वाक्यं प्रियं श्रुत्वा द्विज आपव नम्रधीः ।
तुष्टाव दण्डवद् भूत्वा भद्रकालीं सनातनीम् ॥ 15
3.4.m: Hearing this dear speech, the twice-born Āpava, humble in mind, / prostrated himself like a stick and praised eternal Bhadrakālī.

3.4.s:
āpava uvāca
viṣṇukalpe purā cāsīddānavo mahiṣāsuraḥ .
koṭikoṭisahasraistu rathairvājigajairyutaḥ . . 16
3.4.d:
आपव उवाच
विष्णुकल्पे पुरा चासीद्दानवो महिषासुरः ।
कोटिकोटिसहस्रैस्तु रथैर्वाजिगजैर्युतः ॥ 16
3.4.m:
Āpava said:
In ancient times, in the Viṣṇukalpa, there was the Dānava Mahiṣāsura, / accompanied by thousands of crores of chariots, horses, and elephants.

3.4.s:
trailokyaṃ svavaśe kṛtvā mahendrassa tadābhavat .
svārociṣāntaraḥ kālo gato rājyaṃ prakurvataḥ . . 17
3.4.d:
त्रैलोक्यं स्ववशे कृत्वा महेन्द्रस्स तदाभवत् ।
स्वारोचिषान्तरः कालो गतो राज्यं प्रकुर्वतः ॥ 17
3.4.m: Having brought the three worlds under his control, he then became the great Indra; / the period of the Svārociṣa manvantara passed while he ruled.

3.4.s:
tatassa bhagavānviṣṇussarvadevasamanvitaḥ .
samutpādya mukhāttejo jvālāmālī babhūva ha . . 18
3.4.d:
ततस्स भगवान्विष्णुस्सर्वदेवसमन्वितः ।
समुत्पाद्य मुखात्तेजो ज्वालामाली बभूव ह ॥ 18
3.4.m: Then the blessed Viṣṇu, accompanied by all the gods, / brought forth fiery energy from his mouth and became encircled with flames.

3.4.s:
jyotirliṅgāttadā devī bhavatī svecchayā bhuvi .
sambhūya mahiṣaṃ hantrī tasyai devyai namonamaḥ . . 19
3.4.d:
ज्योतिर्लिङ्गात्तदा देवी भवती स्वेच्छया भुवि ।
सम्भूय महिषं हन्त्री तस्यै देव्यै नमोनमः ॥ 19
3.4.m: Then you, O goddess, manifest by your own will on earth / from that liṅga of light, became the slayer of Mahiṣa; reverence, reverence to that goddess!

3.4.s:
rūdrakalpe purā cāsīdrudacchambhumukhāddivi .
rāvaṇaśca sahasrāsyo jāto brahmāṇḍarāvaṇaḥ . . 3.4.16.20
3.4.d:
रूद्रकल्पे पुरा चासीद्रुदच्छम्भुमुखाद्दिवि ।
रावणश्च सहस्रास्यो जातो ब्रह्माण्डरावणः ॥ 3.4.16.20
3.4.m: In ancient times, in the Rudrakalpa, from the mouth of weeping Śambhu in heaven, / the thousand-faced Rāvaṇa was born, the cosmic Rāvaṇa.

3.4.s:
rākṣaso balavānghoro lokālokagireradhaḥ .
nyavasaddevadaityānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ ca bhakṣakaḥ . .
ṣaṣṭhe manvantare tena brahmāṇḍaṃ rājyasātkṛtam . . 21
3.4.d:
राक्षसो बलवान्घोरो लोकालोकगिरेरधः ।
न्यवसद्देवदैत्यानां मनुष्याणां च भक्षकः ॥
षष्ठे मन्वन्तरे तेन ब्रह्माण्डं राज्यसात्कृतम् ॥ 21
3.4.m: A mighty, terrible rākṣasa, a devourer of gods, Daityas, / and humans, he dwelt below the Lokāloka mountain; / in the sixth manvantara, the universe was brought under his rule.

3.4.s:
tato vaivasvate prāpte tretāṣṭāviṃśake prabhuḥ .
sa jāto rāghavagṛhe rāmassaṅkarṣaṇaḥ svayam . . 22
3.4.d:
ततो वैवस्वते प्राप्ते त्रेताष्टाविंशके प्रभुः ।
स जातो राघवगृहे रामस्सङ्कर्षणः स्वयम् ॥ 22
3.4.m: Then, when the Vaivasvata manvantara arrived, in the twenty-eighth Tretā age, the Lord, / Rāma, who is Saṅkarṣaṇa himself, was born in the house of Raghu.

3.4.s:
ṣoḍaśābdavapurbhūtvā sa gato janakālaye .
dhanuścājagavaṃ ghoraṃ prabhagnaṃ tena dhīmatā . . 23
3.4.d:
षोडशाब्दवपुर्भूत्वा स गतो जनकालये ।
धनुश्चाजगवं घोरं प्रभग्नं तेन धीमता ॥ 23
3.4.m: Assuming the form of a sixteen-year-old, he went to Janaka's abode, / and that terrible bow of Śiva was broken by that wise one.

3.4.s:
tadā brahmādayo devā jñātvā rāmaṃ sanātanam .
sahasravadanasyaiva varṇayāmāsa kāraṇam . . 24
3.4.d:
तदा ब्रह्मादयो देवा ज्ञात्वा रामं सनातनम् ।
सहस्रवदनस्यैव वर्णयामास कारणम् ॥ 24
3.4.m: Then Brahmā and the other gods, knowing him to be the eternal Rāma, / described the cause of that thousand-faced one.

3.4.s:
tacchutvā haṃsayānaṃ ca samāruhya sa sītayā .
lokālokagirau prāpya ghorayuddhamacīkarat . . 25
3.4.d:
तच्छुत्वा हंसयानं च समारुह्य स सीतया ।
लोकालोकगिरौ प्राप्य घोरयुद्धमचीकरत् ॥ 25
3.4.m: Hearing that, he mounted the swan-chariot with Sītā, / reached the Lokāloka mountain, and waged a terrible battle.

3.4.s:
haṃsayānapatākāyāṃ saṃsthito hanumānkapiḥ .
vedāśca vājinastatra netā brahmā sanātanaḥ . . 26
3.4.d:
हंसयानपताकायां संस्थितो हनुमान्कपिः ।
वेदाश्च वाजिनस्तत्र नेता ब्रह्मा सनातनः ॥ 26
3.4.m: The monkey Hanumān stood on the flag of the swan-chariot; / the Vedas were the horses there, and eternal Brahmā was the charioteer.

3.4.s:
divyavarṣamabhūdghoraḥ saṅgrāmastena rakṣasā .
rāvaṇassa tadā kruddho dvisahasraiśca bāhubhiḥ . . 27
3.4.d:
दिव्यवर्षमभूद्घोरः सङ्ग्रामस्तेन रक्षसा ।
रावणस्स तदा क्रुद्धो द्विसहस्रैश्च बाहुभिः ॥ 27
3.4.m: A terrible battle took place with that rakṣas for a divine year. / Then Rāvaṇa, enraged with his two thousand arms,

3.4.s:
aparau mūrchayitvā tau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau .
jagarja balavānghorassa ca brahmāṇḍarāvaṇaḥ . . 28
3.4.d:
अपरौ मूर्छयित्वा तौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ ।
जगर्ज बलवान्घोरस्स च ब्रह्माण्डरावणः ॥ 28
3.4.m: struck those two other brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, unconscious; / and that mighty, terrible cosmic Rāvaṇa roared.

3.4.s:
brāhmaṇā saṃstutā mātā bhavatī brahmarūpiṇī .
sītā śāntimayī nityā tayā brahmāṇḍarāvaṇaḥ . .
vināśito namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ . . 29
3.4.d:
ब्राह्मणा संस्तुता माता भवती ब्रह्मरूपिणी ।
सीता शान्तिमयी नित्या तया ब्रह्माण्डरावणः ॥
विनाशितो नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ॥ 29
3.4.m: Praised by Brahmā, you, O Mother, whose form is Brahman, / the eternal Sītā full of peace, by you cosmic Rāvaṇa / was destroyed; reverence to her, reverence to her, reverence, reverence!

3.4.s:
brahmakalpe purā cāsīttālajaṃghānvayodbhavaḥ .
muro nāma mahādaityo brahmaṇo baladarpitaḥ . . 3.4.16.30
3.4.d:
ब्रह्मकल्पे पुरा चासीत्तालजंघान्वयोद्भवः ।
मुरो नाम महादैत्यो ब्रह्मणो बलदर्पितः ॥ 3.4.16.30
3.4.m: In ancient times, in the Brahmakalpa, born in the lineage of Tālajaṅgha, / there was a great Daitya named Mura, proud of his strength from Brahmā.

3.4.s:
brahmāṇḍeśaṃ mahārudraṃ mahendrādisamanvitam .
sa babhūva parājityādhikārī raudra āsane . . 31
3.4.d:
ब्रह्माण्डेशं महारुद्रं महेन्द्रादिसमन्वितम् ।
स बभूव पराजित्याधिकारी रौद्र आसने ॥ 31
3.4.m: Having defeated the lord of the universe, the great Rudra, along with great Indra and others, / he became the ruler upon the fierce throne.

3.4.s:
devaissārddhaṃ mahādevo mādhavaṃ kṣīraśāyinam .
gatvā nivedayāmāsa sa viṣṇuḥ krodhasaṃyutaḥ . . 32
3.4.d:
देवैस्सार्द्धं महादेवो माधवं क्षीरशायिनम् ।
गत्वा निवेदयामास स विष्णुः क्रोधसंयुतः ॥ 32
3.4.m: Together with the gods, Mahādeva approached Mādhava / who sleeps upon the milk ocean, and reported [this]; and that Viṣṇu was filled with wrath.

3.4.s:
jagāma garuḍārūḍho yatra daityo muraḥ sthitaḥ .
tena sārddhamabhūdyuddhaṃ tasya devasya dāruṇam . 33
3.4.d:
जगाम गरुडारूढो यत्र दैत्यो मुरः स्थितः ।
तेन सार्द्धमभूद्युद्धं तस्य देवस्य दारुणम् । 33
3.4.m: Mounted on Garuḍa, he went where the daitya Mura stood. / A dreadful battle took place between that god and him.

3.4.s:
sahasrābdamato jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā brahmā bhayānvitaḥ .
parāṃ tu prakṛtiṃ nityāṃ tuṣṭāva ślakṣṇayā girā . . 34
3.4.d:
सहस्राब्दमतो जातं दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मा भयान्वितः ।
परां तु प्रकृतिं नित्यां तुष्टाव श्लक्ष्णया गिरा ॥ 34
3.4.m: Seeing that a thousand years had passed [in this way], Brahmā was filled with fear. / With gentle speech he praised the supreme, eternal Prakṛti.

3.4.s:
prasannā sā tadā devī kumārī saptahāyinī .
caturbhujāstrasahitā bhūtvā daityamuvāca ha . . 35
3.4.d:
प्रसन्ना सा तदा देवी कुमारी सप्तहायिनी ।
चतुर्भुजास्त्रसहिता भूत्वा दैत्यमुवाच ह ॥ 35
3.4.m: Pleased, that goddess then became a maiden seven years old; / equipped with four arms and weapons, she addressed the daitya:

3.4.s:
parājito'yaṃ bhagavāndaityarājena vai tvayā .
vijayā nāma me ramyā kaiścinnāhaṃ parājitā . . 36
3.4.d:
पराजितोऽयं भगवान्दैत्यराजेन वै त्वया ।
विजया नाम मे रम्या कैश्चिन्नाहं पराजिता ॥ 36
3.4.m: ‘This Lord has indeed been defeated by you, the king of the daityas. / Delightful, my name is Vijayā; by none have I been defeated.

3.4.s:
unmīlinī viñculī ca trispṛśā pakṣavarddhinī .
jayā jayantī vijayā varṣevarṣe kramādaham . . 37
3.4.d:
उन्मीलिनी विञ्चुली च त्रिस्पृशा पक्षवर्द्धिनी ।
जया जयन्ती विजया वर्षेवर्षे क्रमादहम् ॥ 37
3.4.m: Year after year, in succession, I am / Unmīlinī, Viñculī, Trispṛśā, Pakṣavarddhinī, Jayā, Jayantī, and Vijayā.

3.4.s:
ekādaśaśubhācārā viṣṇavastanayā mama .
ekādaśīti vikhyātā vedamadhye sadā hyaham . . 38
3.4.d:
एकादशशुभाचारा विष्णवस्तनया मम ।
एकादशीति विख्याता वेदमध्ये सदा ह्यहम् ॥ 38
3.4.m: Conducting eleven auspicious observances, the Viṣṇus are my sons. / I am indeed always celebrated within the Veda as Ekādaśī.

3.4.s:
ato māṃ balavāñjitvā vijayāṃ viṣṇumātaram .
pāṇiṃ grahāṇa me ramyaṃ sarvapūjyo bhavānbhavet . . 39
3.4.d:
अतो मां बलवाञ्जित्वा विजयां विष्णुमातरम् ।
पाणिं ग्रहाण मे रम्यं सर्वपूज्यो भवान्भवेत् ॥ 39
3.4.m: Therefore, mighty one, having conquered me, Vijayā, the mother of Viṣṇu, / take my lovely hand; you shall become worshipped by all.’

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā muro daityastasyā rūpeṇa mohitaḥ .
yuyudhe sa tayā sārddhaṃ kṣaṇārddhena layaṅgataḥ . . 3.4.16.40
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा मुरो दैत्यस्तस्या रूपेण मोहितः ।
युयुधे स तया सार्द्धं क्षणार्द्धेन लयङ्गतः ॥ 3.4.16.40
3.4.m: Hearing this, the daitya Mura, infatuated by her beauty, / fought with her, and in half a moment met his destruction.

3.4.s:
taṃ muraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvānujastannarakāsuraḥ .
daityamāyāṃ mahāghorāṃ cakāra suranāśinīm . . 41
3.4.d:
तं मुरं निहतं दृष्ट्वानुजस्तन्नरकासुरः ।
दैत्यमायां महाघोरां चकार सुरनाशिनीम् ॥ 41
3.4.m: Seeing Mura slain, his younger brother, the asura Naraka, / conjured a terrifying daitya-illusion that destroyed the gods.

3.4.s:
ekādaśī svayaṃ māyā huṅkāreṇaiva taṃ tadā .
narakeṇa samaṃ hatvā jagarja jagadambikā . . 42
3.4.d:
एकादशी स्वयं माया हुङ्कारेणैव तं तदा ।
नरकेण समं हत्वा जगर्ज जगदम्बिका ॥ 42
3.4.m: Ekādaśī, herself Māyā, the mother of the universe, / then slew him together with Naraka with a mere roar, and bellowed.

3.4.s:
tayostejo mahāghoramannamadhyeṣu cāgamat .
duṣṭabhūtamamūdannaṃ nṛṇāṃ rogabhayapradam . . 43
3.4.d:
तयोस्तेजो महाघोरमन्नमध्येषु चागमत् ।
दुष्टभूतममूदन्नं नृणां रोगभयप्रदम् ॥ 43
3.4.m: The terrifying splendor of the two [demons] entered into the midst of food; / that food became corrupt and brought the fear of disease upon men.

3.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā caikādaśī nāmnā raviśukrāvuvāca ha .
kurutāṃ śuddhamevāntarbhavantau lokaviśrutau . . 44
3.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा चैकादशी नाम्ना रविशुक्रावुवाच ह ।
कुरुतां शुद्धमेवान्तर्भवन्तौ लोकविश्रुतौ ॥ 44
3.4.m: Seeing [this], she whose name is Ekādaśī said to the Sun and Venus: / ‘May the two of you, celebrated in the worlds, purify its interior.’

3.4.s:
tadājñayā tathā kṛtvā deva pūjyau babhūvatuḥ .
evaṃ mātastvayā sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ tasyai namo namaḥ . . 45
3.4.d:
तदाज्ञया तथा कृत्वा देव पूज्यौ बभूवतुः ।
एवं मातस्त्वया सर्वं कृतं तस्यै नमो नमः ॥ 45
3.4.m: Having done so by her command, they became worthy of worship by the gods. / ‘Thus everything was done by you, O Mother; reverence, reverence to her!’

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā bhadrakālī stotraṃ divyaṃ kathāmayam .
āpavaṃ prāha sā devī brāhmaṇaṃ vedakovidam . . 46
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा भद्रकाली स्तोत्रं दिव्यं कथामयम् ।
आपवं प्राह सा देवी ब्राह्मणं वेदकोविदम् ॥ 46
3.4.m: Hearing this divine hymn comprised of stories, / the goddess Bhadrakālī spoke to Āpava, the brāhmaṇa learned in the Vedas:

3.4.s:
pralaye ca tadā prāpte naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame .
ekārṇave purā tvaṃ vai matprasādātsukhī bhava . . 47
3.4.d:
प्रलये च तदा प्राप्ते नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे ।
एकार्णवे पुरा त्वं वै मत्प्रसादात्सुखी भव ॥ 47
3.4.m: ‘When the dissolution arrives and the moving and unmoving have perished / in the primeval single ocean, you shall indeed be happy through my grace.

3.4.s:
stotreṇānena suprītā varadāhaṃ sadā narān 1 .
ityuktyāntarhitā devī sa vipro varuṇo'bhavat . . 48
3.4.d:
स्तोत्रेणानेन सुप्रीता वरदाहं सदा नरान् 1 ।
इत्युक्त्यान्तर्हिता देवी स विप्रो वरुणोऽभवत् ॥ 48
3.4.m: Well-pleased by this hymn, I ever bestow boons upon men.’ / Having spoken thus, the goddess vanished; that twice-born man became Varuṇa.

3.4.s:
sūta uvāca
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ bhagavāndvitiyo2 vasuḥ .
varuṇaḥ svamukhāttejo janayāmāsa bhūtale . . 49
3.4.d:
सूत उवाच
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं भगवान्द्वितियो2 वसुः ।
वरुणः स्वमुखात्तेजो जनयामास भूतले ॥ 49
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this speech of his guru, the lord, the second Vasu, / Varuṇa, brought forth splendor from his mouth upon the surface of the earth.

3.4.s:
dehalyāṃ sa tu vai jāto dharmabhaktasya vai gṛhe .
vidhavā tasya yā kanyā garbhaṃ dhatte hareḥ svayam . . 3.4.16.50
3.4.d:
देहल्यां स तु वै जातो धर्मभक्तस्य वै गृहे ।
विधवा तस्य या कन्या गर्भं धत्ते हरेः स्वयम् ॥ 3.4.16.50
3.4.m: He was indeed born in Delhi in the house of Dharmabhakta. / His daughter, who was a widow, herself bore the child of Hari.

3.4.s:
iti jñātvā dharmabhakto mumude sutajanmani .
nāmadeva iti khyātaḥ sāṅkhyayogaparāyaṇaḥ . . 51
3.4.d:
इति ज्ञात्वा धर्मभक्तो मुमुदे सुतजन्मनि ।
नामदेव इति ख्यातः साङ्ख्ययोगपरायणः ॥ 51
3.4.m: Knowing this, Dharmabhakta rejoiced at the birth of the son. / Known as Nāmadeva, he was devoted to Sāṅkhya and Yoga.

3.4.s:
ābrahmastambaparyantaṃ sarvaṃ viṣṇumayaṃ jagat .
jñātvā dṛṣṭvā gataḥ kāśyāṃ rāmānandaṃ haripriyam . . 52
3.4.d:
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तं सर्वं विष्णुमयं जगत् ।
ज्ञात्वा दृष्ट्वा गतः काश्यां रामानन्दं हरिप्रियम् ॥ 52
3.4.m: Knowing and seeing the entire world from Brahmā down to a clump of grass as filled with Viṣṇu, / he went to Kāśī, to Rāmānanda, who was dear to Hari.

3.4.s:
natvā tacchiṣyatāṃ prāpya tatra vāsamakārayat .
sikandaro mlecchapatirdehalīrājyamāsthitaḥ . . 53
3.4.d:
नत्वा तच्छिष्यतां प्राप्य तत्र वासमकारयत् ।
सिकन्दरो म्लेच्छपतिर्देहलीराज्यमास्थितः ॥ 53
3.4.m: Having bowed and attained the status of his disciple, he took up residence there. / Sikandar, the ruler of the barbarians, was established in the realm of Delhi.

3.4.s:
nāmadevaṃ samāhūya samparīkṣya tadā sukhī .
ardhakoṭimitaṃ dravyaṃ dadau tasmai kalipriyaḥ . . 54
3.4.d:
नामदेवं समाहूय सम्परीक्ष्य तदा सुखी ।
अर्धकोटिमितं द्रव्यं ददौ तस्मै कलिप्रियः ॥ 54
3.4.m: Having summoned Nāmadeva and tested him, pleased at that time, / that lover of Kali gave him wealth to the amount of five million.

3.4.s:
nāmadevastu taddravyairgaṅgārohaṇamuttamam .
kārayāmāsa vai kāśyāṃ śubhraṃ sarvaṃ śilāmayam . . 55
3.4.d:
नामदेवस्तु तद्द्रव्यैर्गङ्गारोहणमुत्तमम् ।
कारयामास वै काश्यां शुभ्रं सर्वं शिलामयम् ॥ 55
3.4.m: With that wealth, Nāmadeva caused to be made in Kāśī / an excellent landing-ghat to the Gaṅgā, white and made entirely of stone.

3.4.s:
daśaviprānpañca nṛpānpañca vaiśyāñchataṃ gavām .
punarujjīvayāmāsa śavabhūtānsa yogavān . . 56
3.4.d:
दशविप्रान्पञ्च नृपान्पञ्च वैश्याञ्छतं गवाम् ।
पुनरुज्जीवयामास शवभूतान्स योगवान् ॥ 56
3.4.m: Possessed of yoga, he revived ten brāhmaṇas, / five kings, five vaiśyas, and a hundred cows who had become corpses.

3.4.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
viśvānaraḥ purā cāsīdbrāhmaṇo vedakovidaḥ .
anapatyo vidhātāraṃ tuṣṭāva bahupūjanaiḥ . . 57
3.4.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
विश्वानरः पुरा चासीद्ब्राह्मणो वेदकोविदः ।
अनपत्यो विधातारं तुष्टाव बहुपूजनैः ॥ 57
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Formerly there was a brāhmaṇa learned in the Vedas named Viśvānara. / Childless, he praised the Creator with numerous acts of worship.

3.4.s:
varṣamātreṇa bhagavānparameṣṭhī prajāpatiḥ .
samāgatya vacaḥ prāha varaṃ brūhi dvijottama . . 58
3.4.d:
वर्षमात्रेण भगवान्परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः ।
समागत्य वचः प्राह वरं ब्रूहि द्विजोत्तम ॥ 58
3.4.m: After merely a year, the lord Prajāpati, the Highest, / approached and spoke these words: ‘Choose a boon, O best of the twice-born.’

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā sa hovāca bhagavam̐ste namo namaḥ .
prakṛteśca paraḥ putro bhūyānmama varāttava . . 59
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा स होवाच भगवम्̐स्ते नमो नमः ।
प्रकृतेश्च परः पुत्रो भूयान्मम वरात्तव ॥ 59
3.4.m: Hearing this, he said: ‘Lord, reverence, reverence to you! / By your boon, may I have a son who is beyond Prakṛti.’

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā tadā brahmā vismitaḥ prāha taṃ dvijam .
ekā vai prakṛtirmāyā triliṅgajananī svayam . . 3.4.16.60
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा तदा ब्रह्मा विस्मितः प्राह तं द्विजम् ।
एका वै प्रकृतिर्माया त्रिलिङ्गजननी स्वयम् ॥ 3.4.16.60
3.4.m: Hearing this, Brahmā, astonished, said to that twice-born man: / ‘Prakṛti is the single Māyā, herself the mother of the three genders.

3.4.s:
tayā dṛśyaṃ jagatsarvaṃ samutpāditamātmanā .
prakṛteśca paro yo vai paramātmā sa cāvyayaḥ . . 61
3.4.d:
तया दृश्यं जगत्सर्वं समुत्पादितमात्मना ।
प्रकृतेश्च परो यो वै परमात्मा स चाव्ययः ॥ 61
3.4.m: By her, this whole visible world was brought forth of herself; / and he who is beyond Prakṛti is the supreme, imperishable Self.

3.4.s:
abuddhirbodhanirato hyaśrutiśca śṛṇoti vai .
adehaḥ sa spṛśatyetadacakṣuḥ paśyati svayam . . 62
3.4.d:
अबुद्धिर्बोधनिरतो ह्यश्रुतिश्च शृणोति वै ।
अदेहः स स्पृशत्येतदचक्षुः पश्यति स्वयम् ॥ 62
3.4.m: Deceitless, he is intent on understanding; having no ears, he indeed hears; / bodiless, he touches this; lacking eyes, he sees of himself.

3.4.s:
ajihvonnaṃ sa gṛhṇāti sa jighrati na sā vinā .
amukho vedavaktā ca karmakāraḥ karaṃ vinā . . 63
3.4.d:
अजिह्वोन्नं स गृह्णाति स जिघ्रति न सा विना ।
अमुखो वेदवक्ता च कर्मकारः करं विना ॥ 63
3.4.m: Without a tongue, he takes food; he smells without a nose; / mouthless, he speaks the Vedas; and without hands, he performs deeds.

3.4.s:
apado gacchati hyetadaliṅgo nāribhogavān .
aguhyo hi karotyetāṃ satattvāṃ guhyabhūtinīm . . 64
3.4.d:
अपदो गच्छति ह्येतदलिङ्गो नारिभोगवान् ।
अगुह्यो हि करोत्येतां सतत्त्वां गुह्यभूतिनीम् ॥ 64
3.4.m: Footless, he goes about this [earth]; genderless, he enjoys woman; / without private parts, he makes this [Prakṛti] possessed of true reality and secret power.

3.4.s:
śabdabrahma sparśamayaṃ rūpabrahma rasātmakam .
gandhabrahma paraṃ jñeya tasmai tadbrahmaṇe namaḥ . . 65
3.4.d:
शब्दब्रह्म स्पर्शमयं रूपब्रह्म रसात्मकम् ।
गन्धब्रह्म परं ज्ञेय तस्मै तद्ब्रह्मणे नमः ॥ 65
3.4.m: Brahman as sound consists of touch; Brahman as form is of the nature of taste; / Brahman as fragrance is known as supreme—reverence to that Brahman!

3.4.s:
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ caiva viddhyanādi ubhāvapi .
vikārāṃśca guṇāṃścaiva viddhi prakṛtisambhavān . . 66
3.4.d:
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव विद्ध्यनादि उभावपि ।
विकारांश्च गुणांश्चैव विद्धि प्रकृतिसम्भवान् ॥ 66
3.4.m: Know both Prakṛti and Puruṣa to be without beginning; / and know the transformations and the qualities to be born of Prakṛti.

3.4.s:
ekārthau tau ca śabdaikau rūpaikau nityavigrahau .
ādimadhyāntarahitau nityaśuddhau sanātanau . . 67
3.4.d:
एकार्थौ तौ च शब्दैकौ रूपैकौ नित्यविग्रहौ ।
आदिमध्यान्तरहितौ नित्यशुद्धौ सनातनौ ॥ 67
3.4.m: Those two have a single meaning, a single sound, a single form, and an eternal embodiment; / they are devoid of beginning, middle, and end, eternally pure and everlasting.

3.4.s:
puṃstrīnapuṃskajananī jñeyā sā prakṛtiḥ parā .
puruṣaśca kaviḥ sūkṣmaḥ kūṭastho jñānavānparaḥ .. 68 ..
3.4.d:
पुंस्त्रीनपुंस्कजननी ज्ञेया सा प्रकृतिः परा ।
पुरुषश्च कविः सूक्ष्मः कूटस्थो ज्ञानवान्परः ॥ 68 ॥
3.4.m: That supreme Prakṛti should be known as the mother of masculine, feminine, and neuter; / and the Puruṣa is the poet, subtle, changeless, possessed of knowledge, supreme.

3.4.s:
ajanmā janma cāpnoti mayā jātaḥ sa janmavān ..
kathaṃ sa puruṣo nityastava putro bhaviṣyati .. 69 ..
3.4.d:
अजन्मा जन्म चाप्नोति मया जातः स जन्मवान् ॥
कथं स पुरुषो नित्यस्तव पुत्रो भविष्यति ॥ 69 ॥
3.4.m: Though unborn, he attains birth; born through me, he possesses birth. / How shall that eternal Puruṣa become your son?

3.4.s:
ato viśvānara mune māyābhūto hariḥ svayam ..
tava putratvamāpnoti varānmama janārdanaḥ .. 3.4.16.70 ..
3.4.d:
अतो विश्वानर मुने मायाभूतो हरिः स्वयम् ॥
तव पुत्रत्वमाप्नोति वरान्मम जनार्दनः ॥ 3.4.16.70 ॥
3.4.m: Therefore, sage Viśvānara, Hari himself, transformed into Māyā, / Janārdana, will become your son by my boon.’

3.4.s:
ityuktvāntardadhe devaḥ pāvakastadvarādabhūt ..
aṣṭānāṃ ca vasūnāṃ ca pāvako hi patistvayam .. 71 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे देवः पावकस्तद्वरादभूत् ॥
अष्टानां च वसूनां च पावको हि पतिस्त्वयम् ॥ 71 ॥
3.4.m: Having spoken thus, the god vanished. By his boon, Pāvaka was born; / this Pāvaka is indeed the master of the eight Vasus.

3.4.s:
vaiśvānara iti khyāto'bhavatsvāhāpatiḥ prabhuḥ ..
sa tu pūrvabhave devaḥ purā kalpe'nalobhavat .. 72 ..
3.4.d:
वैश्वानर इति ख्यातोऽभवत्स्वाहापतिः प्रभुः ॥
स तु पूर्वभवे देवः पुरा कल्पेऽनलोभवत् ॥ 72 ॥
3.4.m: Celebrated as Vaiśvānara, he became the lord and husband of Svāhā. / That god had formerly been Anala in a previous birth in an earlier kalpa.

3.4.s:
naiṣadho brāhmaṇo dhīmānyathā rājā nalastathā ..
saṃkaṭāyāṃ gate bhūpe damayantī pativratā .. 73 ..
3.4.d:
नैषधो ब्राह्मणो धीमान्यथा राजा नलस्तथा ॥
संकटायां गते भूपे दमयन्ती पतिव्रता ॥ 73 ॥
3.4.m: There was a wise brāhmaṇa of the Niṣadhas, [looking] just like King Nala. / When the king had fallen into misfortune, the faithful wife Damayantī,

3.4.s:
svapiturgehamāsādyānveṣayāmāsa bhūpatim ..
tadā nalo dvijaṃ prāpto damayaṃtīpatiḥ prabhuḥ .. 74 ..
3.4.d:
स्वपितुर्गेहमासाद्यान्वेषयामास भूपतिम् ॥
तदा नलो द्विजं प्राप्तो दमयंतीपतिः प्रभुः ॥ 74 ॥
3.4.m: reaching her father’s house, searched for the king. / Then Nala, the lord and husband of Damayantī, came upon that twice-born man.

3.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ mohamāpannā damayaṃtī śubhānanā ..
etasminnaṃtare tatra vāguvācāśarīriṇī .. 75 ..
3.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं मोहमापन्ना दमयंती शुभानना ॥
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र वागुवाचाशरीरिणी ॥ 75 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing him, the fair-faced Damayantī fell into bewilderment. / Meanwhile, an incorporeal voice spoke there:

3.4.s:
nāyaṃ nalastava patirbrāhmaṇoyaṃ sumohitaḥ ..
analo nāma vikhyāto devavākyātsa cābhavat .. 76 ..
3.4.d:
नायं नलस्तव पतिर्ब्राह्मणोयं सुमोहितः ॥
अनलो नाम विख्यातो देववाक्यात्स चाभवत् ॥ 76 ॥
3.4.m: ‘This is not Nala, your husband; this is a deeply bewildered brāhmaṇa.’ / By the words of the god he became known as Anala.

3.4.s:
mahāsarasvatīṃ devīṃ tuṣṭāva sa tu mohitaḥ ..
tasya puṇyaprabhāvena viśvānarasuto'bhavat .. 77 ..
3.4.d:
महासरस्वतीं देवीं तुष्टाव स तु मोहितः ॥
तस्य पुण्यप्रभावेन विश्वानरसुतोऽभवत् ॥ 77 ॥
3.4.m: Bewildered, he praised the goddess Mahāsarasvatī; / through the power of his merit, he became the son of Viśvānara.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ pāvako bhagavānprabhuḥ ..
svamukhātsvāṃśamutpādya saṃjātastu tato vasuḥ .. 78 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं पावको भगवान्प्रभुः ॥
स्वमुखात्स्वांशमुत्पाद्य संजातस्तु ततो वसुः ॥ 78 ॥
3.4.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard the words of his guru, the lord, the holy Pāvaka,
produced a portion of himself from his own mouth, and from it Vasu was born.

3.4.s:
raṃkaṇo nāma vikhyāto lakṣmīdattasya vai sutaḥ ..
nagare kāṃcanapure vaiśyajātisamudbhavaḥ .. 79 ..
3.4.d:
रंकणो नाम विख्यातो लक्ष्मीदत्तस्य वै सुतः ॥
नगरे कांचनपुरे वैश्यजातिसमुद्भवः ॥ 79 ॥
3.4.m:
He became famous as Raṅkaṇa, the son of Lakṣmīdatta,
born into the Vaiśya caste in the city of Kāñcanapura.

3.4.s:
yaṃkaṇā nāma tatpatnī babhūva ca pativratā ..
sarvadravyavyayaṃ kṛtvā dharmakāryeṣu daṃpatī .. 3.4.16.80 ..
3.4.d:
यंकणा नाम तत्पत्नी बभूव च पतिव्रता ॥
सर्वद्रव्यव्ययं कृत्वा धर्मकार्येषु दंपती ॥ 3.4.16.80 ॥
3.4.m:
His wife was named Yaṅkaṇā, a devoted wife.
Having spent all their wealth on righteous deeds, the couple,

3.4.s:
kāṣṭhamānīya vikrīya bubhujāte parasparam ..
rāmānaṃdastasya gurū raṃkaṇasya mahātmanaḥ .. 81 ..
3.4.d:
काष्ठमानीय विक्रीय बुभुजाते परस्परम् ॥
रामानंदस्तस्य गुरू रंकणस्य महात्मनः ॥ 81 ॥
3.4.m:
brought firewood, sold it, and ate together.
Rāmānanda was the guru of that noble-minded Raṅkaṇa.

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
ditiputrau mahāghorau viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā ..
saṃhatau tu ditirjñātvā kaśyapaṃ samapūjayat.. 1 ..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
दितिपुत्रौ महाघोरौ विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना ॥
संहतौ तु दितिर्ज्ञात्वा कश्यपं समपूजयत्॥ 1 ॥
3.4.m:
Bṛhaspati said:
When Diti realized that her two exceedingly terrible sons had been slain
by the all-powerful Viṣṇu, she worshipped Kaśyapa.

3.4.s:
dvādaśābdāṃtare svāmī kaśyapo bhagavānṛṣiḥ ..
uvāca patnīṃ sa hi tāṃ varaṃ brūhi varānane ..
sā tu śrutvā namaskṛtya vacanaṃ prāha harṣitā .. 2 ..
3.4.d:
द्वादशाब्दांतरे स्वामी कश्यपो भगवानृषिः ॥
उवाच पत्नीं स हि तां वरं ब्रूहि वरानने ॥
सा तु श्रुत्वा नमस्कृत्य वचनं प्राह हर्षिता ॥ 2 ॥
3.4.m:
After twelve years, her lord, the blessed sage Kaśyapa,
said to his wife: "Choose a boon, O fair-faced woman!"
Having heard this and bowed down, she spoke joyfully:

3.4.s:
aditirmama yā devī sapatnī putrasaṃyutā ..
dvādaśatanayāstasyā mama dvau tanayau smṛtau .. 3 ..
3.4.d:
अदितिर्मम या देवी सपत्नी पुत्रसंयुता ॥
द्वादशतनयास्तस्या मम द्वौ तनयौ स्मृतौ ॥ 3 ॥
3.4.m:
"Aditi, my co-wife, is blessed with sons;
she has twelve sons, while I am remembered as having only two.

3.4.s:
tadavaryasute naiva viṣṇunā surapālinā ..
vināśitau sutau ghorau tato'haṃ bhṛśaduḥkhitā .. 4 ..
3.4.d:
तदवर्यसुते नैव विष्णुना सुरपालिना ॥
विनाशितौ सुतौ घोरौ ततोऽहं भृशदुःखिता ॥ 4 ॥
3.4.m:
By Viṣṇu, the protector of the gods, on behalf of her sons,
my two terrible sons were destroyed; therefore, I am exceedingly sorrowful.

3.4.s:
dehi me tanayaṃ svāmindvādaśādityanāśanam ..
iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ ditiṃ prāha suduḥkhitaḥ .. 5 ..
3.4.d:
देहि मे तनयं स्वामिन्द्वादशादित्यनाशनम् ॥
इति श्रुत्वा वचो घोरं दितिं प्राह सुदुःखितः ॥ 5 ॥
3.4.m:
Give me a son, my lord, who will destroy the twelve Ādityas!"
Having heard these dreadful words, he, deeply sorrowful, said to Diti:

3.4.s:
brahmaṇā nirmitau loke dharmādharmau parāparau ..
dharmapakṣāstu ye loke narāste brahmaṇaḥ priyāḥ .. 6 ..
3.4.d:
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितौ लोके धर्माधर्मौ परापरौ ॥
धर्मपक्षास्तु ये लोके नरास्ते ब्रह्मणः प्रियाः ॥ 6 ॥
3.4.m:
"By Brahmā, righteousness and unrighteousness, the higher and the lower, were created in the world.
Men who take the side of righteousness in this world are dear to Brahmā;

3.4.s:
adharmapakṣāstu narā vairiṇastasya dhīmataḥ ..
adharmapakṣau tanayau tasmānmṛtyumupāgatau .. 7 ..
3.4.d:
अधर्मपक्षास्तु नरा वैरिणस्तस्य धीमतः ॥
अधर्मपक्षौ तनयौ तस्मान्मृत्युमुपागतौ ॥ 7 ॥
3.4.m:
but men who take the side of unrighteousness are enemies of that wise one.
Your two sons took the side of unrighteousness; therefore, they met their death.

3.4.s:
ato dharmapriye śuddhaṃ kuru tasmānmahābalaḥ ..
bhaviṣyati suto dhīmām̐ścirajīvī tava priyaḥ.. 8 ..
3.4.d:
अतो धर्मप्रिये शुद्धं कुरु तस्मान्महाबलः ॥
भविष्यति सुतो धीमाम्̐श्चिरजीवी तव प्रियः॥ 8 ॥
3.4.m:
Therefore, O lover of righteousness, remain pure; from that, a mighty,
wise, and long-lived son will be born, who shall be dear to you."

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā ditirdevī kaśyapādgarbhamuttamam ..
saṃprāpya sā śubhācārā babhūva vratadhāriṇī .. 9 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा दितिर्देवी कश्यपाद्गर्भमुत्तमम् ॥
संप्राप्य सा शुभाचारा बभूव व्रतधारिणी ॥ 9 ॥
3.4.m:
Having heard this, the goddess Diti, receiving an excellent embryo from Kaśyapa,
observed proper conduct and maintained the vow.

3.4.s:
tasyā garbhagate putre mahendraśca bhayānvitaḥ ..
dāsabhūtaḥ sthito gehe sa diterājñayā guroḥ .. 3.4.17.10 ..
3.4.d:
तस्या गर्भगते पुत्रे महेन्द्रश्च भयान्वितः ॥
दासभूतः स्थितो गेहे स दितेराज्ञया गुरोः ॥ 3.4.17.10 ॥
3.4.m:
While the son was in her womb, Mahendra, seized with fear,
became a servant and stayed in Diti's house by order of his guru.

3.4.s:
saptamāsi sthite garbhe śakramāyāvimohitā ..
aśuciśca ditirdevī suṣvāpa nijamaṃdire .. 11 ..
3.4.d:
सप्तमासि स्थिते गर्भे शक्रमायाविमोहिता ॥
अशुचिश्च दितिर्देवी सुष्वाप निजमंदिरे ॥ 11 ॥
3.4.m:
In the seventh month of the pregnancy, deluded by the illusion of Śakra,
the goddess Diti became impure and fell asleep in her own chamber.

3.4.s:
aṃguṣṭhamātro bhagavānmahendro vajrasaṃyutaḥ ..
kukṣimadhye samāgamya cakre garbhaṃ sa saptadhā .. 12 ..
3.4.d:
अंगुष्ठमात्रो भगवान्महेन्द्रो वज्रसंयुतः ॥
कुक्षिमध्ये समागम्य चक्रे गर्भं स सप्तधा ॥ 12 ॥
3.4.m:
The blessed Mahendra, thumb-sized and bearing his vajra,
entered the middle of her belly and divided the embryo into seven parts.

3.4.s:
jīvabhūtānatibalāndṛṣṭvā sapta mahāripūn..
ekaikaḥ saptadhā tena mahendreṇa tadā kṛtaḥ .. 13 ..
3.4.d:
जीवभूतानतिबलान्दृष्ट्वा सप्त महारिपून्॥
एकैकः सप्तधा तेन महेन्द्रेण तदा कृतः ॥ 13 ॥
3.4.m:
Seeing the seven mighty adversaries alive and embodied,
each one was then divided into seven parts by Mahendra.

3.4.s:
namrībhūtaśca tāndṛṣṭvā mahendrastaiḥ samanvitaḥ ..
yoni dvāreṇa cāgamya praṇanāma tadā ditim .. 14 ..
3.4.d:
नम्रीभूतश्च तान्दृष्ट्वा महेन्द्रस्तैः समन्वितः ॥
योनि द्वारेण चागम्य प्रणनाम तदा दितिम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.4.m:
Seeing them humbled, Mahendra, accompanied by them,
came out through the passage of the womb and then bowed to Diti.

3.4.s:
prasannā sā ditirdevānmahendrāya ca tāndadau ..
marudgaṇāśca te sarve vikhyātāḥ śakrasevakāḥ ..15...
3.4.d:
प्रसन्ना सा दितिर्देवान्महेन्द्राय च तान्ददौ ॥
मरुद्गणाश्च ते सर्वे विख्याताः शक्रसेवकाः ॥15॥।
3.4.m:
Pleased, Diti gave those gods to Mahendra,
and they all became famous as the Marut hosts, the attendants of Śakra.

3.4.s:
sa tu pūrvabhave jāto brāhmaṇo lokaviśrutaḥ ..
ilo nāma sa vedajño yathelo nṛpatistadā .. 16 ..
3.4.d:
स तु पूर्वभवे जातो ब्राह्मणो लोकविश्रुतः ॥
इलो नाम स वेदज्ञो यथेलो नृपतिस्तदा ॥ 16 ॥
3.4.m:
In his previous birth, he was born as a brāhmaṇa renowned in the world,
named Ila, who knew the Vedas, just like King Ila at that time.

3.4.s:
ekadā balavānrājā manuputra ilaḥ svayam..
ekākī hayamāruhya merorvipinamāyayau .. 17 ..
3.4.d:
एकदा बलवान्राजा मनुपुत्र इलः स्वयम्॥
एकाकी हयमारुह्य मेरोर्विपिनमाययौ ॥ 17 ॥
3.4.m:
Once, the mighty King Ila himself, the son of Manu,
mounted a horse alone and came to the forest of Meru.

3.4.s:
meroradhaḥ sthitaḥ khaṇḍaḥ svarṇagarbho haripriyaḥ ..
nivāsaṃ kṛtavām̐statra kṛtvā rāṣṭraṃ mahottamam .. .. 18 ..
3.4.d:
मेरोरधः स्थितः खण्डः स्वर्णगर्भो हरिप्रियः ॥
निवासं कृतवाम्̐स्तत्र कृत्वा राष्ट्रं महोत्तमम् ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
3.4.m:
Below Meru is a continent containing gold, dear to Hari.
There he established his dwelling, having founded a great kingdom.

3.4.s:
ilenāvṛtamevāpi kṛtaṃ tatra sthale surāḥ ..
ilāvṛtamiti khyātaḥ khaṇḍo'bhūdvibudhapriyaḥ .. 19 ..
3.4.d:
इलेनावृतमेवापि कृतं तत्र स्थले सुराः ॥
इलावृतमिति ख्यातः खण्डोऽभूद्विबुधप्रियः ॥ 19 ॥
3.4.m:
Surrounded by Ila, that region was established, O gods;
it became famous as the continent of Ilāvṛta, dear to the gods.

3.4.s:
bhārate ye sthitā lokā ilāvṛtamupāgatāḥ ..
merurgirirvṛkṣamayo vidhātrā nirmito hi saḥ .. 3.4.17.20 ..
3.4.d:
भारते ये स्थिता लोका इलावृतमुपागताः ॥
मेरुर्गिरिर्वृक्षमयो विधात्रा निर्मितो हि सः ॥ 3.4.17.20 ॥
3.4.m:
The people living in Bhārata came to Ilāvṛta;
for Mount Meru, covered with trees, was indeed fashioned by the Creator.

3.4.s:
ārohaṇaṃ naraistasmitkṛtaṃ svarṇamayaṃ śubham ..
tamāruhya kramāllokaḥ svargalokamupāgataḥ ..21 ..
3.4.d:
आरोहणं नरैस्तस्मित्कृतं स्वर्णमयं शुभम् ॥
तमारुह्य क्रमाल्लोकः स्वर्गलोकमुपागतः ॥21 ॥
3.4.m:
An auspicious golden staircase was made upon it by men;
having ascended it step by step, the people reached the heavenly realm.

3.4.s:
tāndṛṣṭvā manujānprāptānsadehānsvargamaṇḍale ..
vismitāśca surāssarve maheśaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ .. 22 ..
3.4.d:
तान्दृष्ट्वा मनुजान्प्राप्तान्सदेहान्स्वर्गमण्डले ॥
विस्मिताश्च सुरास्सर्वे महेशं शरणं ययुः ॥ 22 ॥
3.4.m:
Seeing those mortals arriving in their physical bodies in the realm of heaven,
all the gods were astonished and sought refuge with Maheśa.

3.4.s:
jñātvā sa bhagavānrudro bhavānyā saha śaṃkaraḥ ..
ilāvṛtavane ramye sa reme ca tayā saha .. 23 ..
3.4.d:
ज्ञात्वा स भगवान्रुद्रो भवान्या सह शंकरः ॥
इलावृतवने रम्ये स रेमे च तया सह ॥ 23 ॥
3.4.m:
Knowing this, the blessed Lord Rudra Śaṅkara, along with Bhavānī,
enjoyed pleasure with her in the charming grove of Ilāvṛta.

3.4.s:
etasminnantare prāpto vaivasvatasuto mahān ..
ilonāma mahāprājño mṛgayārthī sadāśivam .. 24 ..
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे प्राप्तो वैवस्वतसुतो महान् ॥
इलोनाम महाप्राज्ञो मृगयार्थी सदाशिवम् ॥ 24 ॥
3.4.m:
At that moment, the great and exceedingly wise son of Vaivasvata,
named Ila, came to Sadāśiva desirous of hunting.

3.4.s:
nagnabhūtaṃ samālokya netre saṃmīlya saṃsthitaḥ ..
lajjitāṃ girijāṃ dṛṣṭvā śaśāpa bhaga vānharaḥ .. 25 ..
3.4.d:
नग्नभूतं समालोक्य नेत्रे संमील्य संस्थितः ॥
लज्जितां गिरिजां दृष्ट्वा शशाप भग वान्हरः ॥ 25 ॥
3.4.m:
Seeing him naked, he closed his eyes and remained standing;
seeing the Mountain's Daughter embarrassed, the blessed Lord Hara pronounced a curse:

3.4.s:
asminkhaṇḍe sadā nāryo bhaviṣyaṃti ca māṃ vinā ..
ityuktā vacanaṃ tasminnāryassarvā babhūvire .. 26 ..
3.4.d:
अस्मिन्खण्डे सदा नार्यो भविष्यंति च मां विना ॥
इत्युक्ता वचनं तस्मिन्नार्यस्सर्वा बभूविरे ॥ 26 ॥
3.4.m:
"In this continent, there shall always be women, except for me."
Having spoken these words, all [who entered] that place became women.

3.4.s:
ilā babhūva nṛpate kanyā janamanoharā ..
bahukālaṃ meruśṛṃge mahattapamacīkarat .. 27 ..
3.4.d:
इला बभूव नृपते कन्या जनमनोहरा ॥
बहुकालं मेरुशृंगे महत्तपमचीकरत् ॥ 27 ॥
3.4.m:
He became Ilā, O king, an enchanting maiden,
and for a long time performed great austerities upon the peak of Meru.

3.4.s:
ilāsamādhibhūtāyāḥ saptaviṃśaccaturyugam ..
jātaṃ tata ilā kanyā tretāmadhye tu candrajam ..
budhaṃ devaṃ patiṃ kṛtvā caṃdravaṃśamajījanat .. 28 ..
3.4.d:
इलासमाधिभूतायाः सप्तविंशच्चतुर्युगम् ॥
जातं तत इला कन्या त्रेतामध्ये तु चन्द्रजम् ॥
बुधं देवं पतिं कृत्वा चंद्रवंशमजीजनत् ॥ 28 ॥

3.4.s:
ayodhyādhipatiḥ śrīmānyadelāvṛtamāgataḥ ..
tasya rājñī madavatī nāmnā tuṣṭāva pārvatīm .. 29 ..
3.4.d:
अयोध्याधिपतिः श्रीमान्यदेलावृतमागतः ॥
तस्य राज्ञी मदवती नाम्ना तुष्टाव पार्वतीम् ॥ 29 ॥
3.4.m:
When the glorious ruler of Ayodhyā came to Ilāvṛta,
his queen, named Madavatī, praised Pārvatī.

3.4.s:
tadā prāpta ilo viprastasyā rūpeṇa mohitaḥ ..
pasparśa tāṃ madavatīṃ rājñīṃ kāmavimohitaḥ .. 3.4.17.30 ..
3.4.d:
तदा प्राप्त इलो विप्रस्तस्या रूपेण मोहितः ॥
पस्पर्श तां मदवतीं राज्ञीं कामविमोहितः ॥ 3.4.17.30 ॥
3.4.m:
Then the brāhmaṇa Ila arrived, infatuated with her beauty;
infatuated with desire, he touched that Queen Madavatī.

3.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare tatra vāguvā cāśarīriṇī ..
ilo nāyaṃ dvijaścāyaṃ tava rūpavimohitaḥ .. 31 ..
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र वागुवा चाशरीरिणी ॥
इलो नायं द्विजश्चायं तव रूपविमोहितः ॥ 31 ॥
3.4.m:
At that moment, a bodiless voice spoke there:
"This is not Ila; this is a twice-born, deluded by your beauty."

3.4.s:
anilo nāma tatraiva vikhyāto'bhūddvijasya vai ..
kāmāgnipīḍito viprassa tuṣṭāva ca pāvakam .. 32 ..
3.4.d:
अनिलो नाम तत्रैव विख्यातोऽभूद्द्विजस्य वै ॥
कामाग्निपीडितो विप्रस्स तुष्टाव च पावकम् ॥ 32 ॥
3.4.m:
He became famous right there as the twice-born named Anila;
afflicted by the fire of passion, that brāhmaṇa praised Pāvaka.

3.4.s:
chittvāchittvā śiro ramyaṃ tasmai jātaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ..
dattvā tuṣṭāva taṃ devaṃ prasanno'bhūddhanaṃjayaḥ .. 33 ..
3.4.d:
छित्त्वाछित्त्वा शिरो रम्यं तस्मै जातं पुनः पुनः ॥
दत्त्वा तुष्टाव तं देवं प्रसन्नोऽभूद्धनंजयः ॥ 33 ॥
3.4.m:
Severing his handsome head again and again, which grew anew,
he offered it and praised that god; Dhanañjaya became pleased with him,

3.4.s:
prāha tvamūnapaṃcā śadvibhedāñjanayiṣyasi ..
tathāhaṃ mitravānbhūtvā tatsaṃkhyastava kāmadaḥ .. 34 ..
3.4.d:
प्राह त्वमूनपंचा शद्विभेदाञ्जनयिष्यसि ॥
तथाहं मित्रवान्भूत्वा तत्संख्यस्तव कामदः ॥ 34 ॥
3.4.m:
and said: "You shall generate forty-nine divisions;
and I, having become your friend, having that same number, shall grant your desires.

3.4.s:
yathā kubero bhagavānṣaḍviṃśadvaruṇapriyaḥ ..
tathāhamūnapaṃcāśadvibhedastava vai sakhā ..35..
3.4.d:
यथा कुबेरो भगवान्षड्विंशद्वरुणप्रियः ॥
तथाहमूनपंचाशद्विभेदस्तव वै सखा ॥35॥
3.4.m:
Just as the blessed Kubera is twenty-six-fold, dear to Varuṇa,
so shall I be forty-nine-fold as your friend."

3.4.s:
ityukte vacane tasminditikukṣau dvijottamaḥ ..
vāyurnāma sa vai jātaḥ pāvakasya priyassakhā ..36..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्ते वचने तस्मिन्दितिकुक्षौ द्विजोत्तमः ॥
वायुर्नाम स वै जातः पावकस्य प्रियस्सखा ॥36॥
3.4.m:
When that word was spoken, that best of the twice-born in Diti's womb
was born as Vāyu, the dear friend of Pāvaka.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ ..
dhānyapālasya vai gehe mṛlagaṃḍāntajaḥ sutaḥ ..
pitṛmātṛparityaktaḥ kāśyāṃ viṃdhyavane tadā .. 37 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं वैश्यजात्यां समुद्भवः ॥
धान्यपालस्य वै गेहे मृलगंडान्तजः सुतः ॥
पितृमातृपरित्यक्तः काश्यां विंध्यवने तदा ॥ 37 ॥
3.4.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard the words of his guru, he was born into the Vaiśya caste
in the house of Dhānyapāla, as a son born under the Mṛlagaṇḍānta asterism,
abandoned by his father and mother in the Vindhya forest at Kāśī.

3.4.s: aliko nāma vai mlecchastatra sthāne samāgataḥ .. 38 ..
3.4.d: अलिको नाम वै म्लेच्छस्तत्र स्थाने समागतः ॥ 38 ॥
3.4.m: A mleccha named Alika arrived at that place.

3.4.s:
anapatyo vastrakārī sutaṃ prāpya gṛhaṃ yayau ..
kabīra iti vikhyātaḥ sa putro madhurānanaḥ .. .. 39 ..
3.4.d:
अनपत्यो वस्त्रकारी सुतं प्राप्य गृहं ययौ ॥
कबीर इति विख्यातः स पुत्रो मधुराननः ॥ ॥ 39 ॥
3.4.m: Being childless, the weaver took the son and went home. / That sweet-faced son became famous as Kabīra.

3.4.s:
sa saptābdavapurbhūtvā godugdhapānatatparaḥ ..
rāmānaṃdaṃ guruṃ matvā rāmadhyānaparo'bhavat ..3.4.17.40..
3.4.d:
स सप्ताब्दवपुर्भूत्वा गोदुग्धपानतत्परः ॥
रामानंदं गुरुं मत्वा रामध्यानपरोऽभवत् ॥3.4.17.40॥
3.4.m: When he reached seven years of age, devoted to drinking cow's milk, / he took Rāmānanda as his guru and became devoted to meditating on Rāma.

3.4.s:
svahastenaiva saṃskṛtya bhojanaṃ haraye'paryat ..
tatpriyārthaṃ harissākṣātsarvakāmaprado'bhavat .. 41 ..
3.4.d:
स्वहस्तेनैव संस्कृत्य भोजनं हरयेऽपर्यत् ॥
तत्प्रियार्थं हरिस्साक्षात्सर्वकामप्रदोऽभवत् ॥ 41 ॥
3.4.m: Preparing food with his own hand, he offered it to Hari; / and to please him, Hari directly became the granter of all desires.

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
uttānapādatanayo dhuvobhūtkṣatriyaḥ purā ..
pitṛmātṛparityaktaḥ sa bālaḥ paṃcahāyanaḥ .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
उत्तानपादतनयो धुवोभूत्क्षत्रियः पुरा ॥
पितृमातृपरित्यक्तः स बालः पंचहायनः ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Formerly, Dhruva, the son of Uttānapāda, was a kṣatriya. / Abandoned by his father and mother, he was a child of five years.

3.4.s:
govarddhanagirau prāpya nāradasyopadeśataḥ ..
sa cakre bhagavaddhyānaṃ māsānṣaṭ ca mahāvratī .. 43 ..
3.4.d:
गोवर्द्धनगिरौ प्राप्य नारदस्योपदेशतः ॥
स चक्रे भगवद्ध्यानं मासान्षट् च महाव्रती ॥ 43 ॥
3.4.m: Reaching Mount Govardhana, according to the instruction of Nārada, / he, observing a great vow, meditated upon the Lord for six months.

3.4.s:
tadā prasanno bhagavānviṣṇurnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ ..
khamaṃḍale padaṃ tasmai dadau prītyā nabhomayam .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
तदा प्रसन्नो भगवान्विष्णुर्नारायणः प्रभुः ॥
खमंडले पदं तस्मै ददौ प्रीत्या नभोमयम् ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m: Then the Lord, the master Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa, was pleased; / with affection, he gave him a celestial place in the vault of heaven.

3.4.s:
dṛṣṭvā tadvadanaṃ ramyaṃ māyāśaktyā diśo daśa ..
svāminaṃ ca dhruvaṃ matvā bhaktinamrā babhūvire .. 45 ..
3.4.d:
दृष्ट्वा तद्वदनं रम्यं मायाशक्त्या दिशो दश ॥
स्वामिनं च ध्रुवं मत्वा भक्तिनम्रा बभूविरे ॥ 45 ॥
3.4.m: Beholding his delightful face through the power of Māyā, the ten directions, / regarding Dhruva as their lord, bowed down in devotion.

3.4.s:
dhuvo'pi bhagavānsākṣātsarvapūjyo babhūva ha ..
dikpatiḥ sa tu vijñeyo bhagaṇānāṃ patiḥ svayam .. 46 ..
3.4.d:
धुवोऽपि भगवान्साक्षात्सर्वपूज्यो बभूव ह ॥
दिक्पतिः स तु विज्ञेयो भगणानां पतिः स्वयम् ॥ 46 ॥
3.4.m: Dhruva himself became the manifest Lord, worshipped by all; / he is indeed to be known as the guardian of the directions, himself the lord of the constellations,

3.4.s:
nabhaḥpatiḥ kālakaraḥ śiśumārapatissa vai ..
paṃcatattvā hi vai māyā prakṛtistatpatiḥ svayam .. 47 ..
3.4.d:
नभःपतिः कालकरः शिशुमारपतिस्स वै ॥
पंचतत्त्वा हि वै माया प्रकृतिस्तत्पतिः स्वयम् ॥ 47 ॥
3.4.m: the lord of the sky, the maker of time, and the lord of the Śiśumāra [constellation]. / Māyā is Prakṛti consisting of the five elements, and he himself is its lord.

3.4.s:
tasmāddharāyāṃ saṃbhūto bhaumo nāma mahāgrahaḥ ..
jaladevyāstato jātaḥ śukro nāma mahāgrahaḥ .. 48 ..
3.4.d:
तस्माद्धरायां संभूतो भौमो नाम महाग्रहः ॥
जलदेव्यास्ततो जातः शुक्रो नाम महाग्रहः ॥ 48 ॥
3.4.m: From him, the great planet named Bhauma (Mars) was born upon the earth; / then from the goddess of waters the great planet named Śukra (Venus) was born;

3.4.s:
vahnidevyā tato jātaścāhaṃ tatra mahāgrahaḥ ..
vāsudevyāṃ dhruvājjātaḥ keturnāma mahāgrahaḥ..49..
3.4.d:
वह्निदेव्या ततो जातश्चाहं तत्र महाग्रहः ॥
वासुदेव्यां ध्रुवाज्जातः केतुर्नाम महाग्रहः॥49॥
3.4.m: then from the goddess of fire I, a great planet, was born there; / and from Dhruva, in Vāsudevī, the great planet named Ketu was born.

3.4.s:
grahabhūtaḥ sthitastatra nabhodevyāṃ tadudbhavaḥ ..
rāhurnāma tathā ghoro mahāgraha upagrahaḥ .. 3.4.17.50 ..
3.4.d:
ग्रहभूतः स्थितस्तत्र नभोदेव्यां तदुद्भवः ॥
राहुर्नाम तथा घोरो महाग्रह उपग्रहः ॥ 3.4.17.50 ॥
3.4.m: Being a planet, he stood there; and from the goddess of the sky arose / the terrible great planet and secondary planet named Rāhu.

3.4.s:
pūrvasyāṃ diśi vai tasmājjātaścairāvato gajaḥ ..
āgneyyāṃ diśi vai tasmātpuṃḍarīko gajo'bhavat .. 51.
3.4.d:
पूर्वस्यां दिशि वै तस्माज्जातश्चैरावतो गजः ॥
आग्नेय्यां दिशि वै तस्मात्पुंडरीको गजोऽभवत् ॥ 51.
3.4.m: From him, in the eastern quarter, the elephant Airāvata was born; / and from him, in the south-eastern quarter, arose the elephant Puṇḍarīka.

3.4.s:
vāmanaḥ kumudaścaiva puṣpadaṃtaḥ kramādgajāḥ ..
sārvabhaumaḥ supratīko nabhodikṣu tu tatsutāḥ .52..
3.4.d:
वामनः कुमुदश्चैव पुष्पदंतः क्रमाद्गजाः ॥
सार्वभौमः सुप्रतीको नभोदिक्षु तु तत्सुताः .52॥
3.4.m: Vāmana, Kumuda, and Puṣpadanta in succession were the elephants, / and Sārvabhauma and Supratīka: these sons [of his were stationed] in the quarters of the sky.

3.4.s:
abhramuḥ kapilā caiva piṃgalākhyā imāḥ kramāt ..
tāmrakarṇī śubhradaṃtī cāṃganā cāṃjanāvatī ..53..
3.4.d:
अभ्रमुः कपिला चैव पिंगलाख्या इमाः क्रमात् ॥
ताम्रकर्णी शुभ्रदंती चांगना चांजनावती ॥53॥
3.4.m: Abhramu, Kapilā, and the one named Piṅgalā in succession, / Tāmrakarṇī, Śubhradantī, Aṅganā, and Añjanāvatī—

3.4.s:
bhūmidikṣu kariṇyaśca jātāstasmāttu tatpriyāḥ ...
bhaginī ca tathā mātā sutā caiva snuṣā tathā .. 54 ..
3.4.d:
भूमिदिक्षु करिण्यश्च जातास्तस्मात्तु तत्प्रियाः ॥।
भगिनी च तथा माता सुता चैव स्नुषा तथा ॥ 54 ॥
3.4.m: these female elephants in the quarters of the earth were born from him as their beloveds. / A sister, a mother, a daughter, and likewise a daughter-in-law:

3.4.s:
paśuyonyudbhavānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ tā yoṣitassadā ..
devayonyudbhavānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ patnī smṛtā svasā .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
पशुयोन्युद्भवानां च नृणां ता योषितस्सदा ॥
देवयोन्युद्भवानां च नृणां पत्नी स्मृता स्वसा ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m: these are always wives for men born of animal wombs; / for men born of divine wombs, a sister is remembered as a wife;

3.4.s:
manuvaṃśodbhavānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ cānyodbhavāḥ striyaḥ ..
iti dharmo vidhātrokto mayā proktaḥ surā hi vaḥ .. 56 ..
3.4.d:
मनुवंशोद्भवानां च नृणां चान्योद्भवाः स्त्रियः ॥
इति धर्मो विधात्रोक्तो मया प्रोक्तः सुरा हि वः ॥ 56 ॥
3.4.m: and for men born of the lineage of Manu, women born of other [families are wives]. / Thus was dharma spoken by the Creator, and spoken by me to you, O gods.

3.4.s:
dvidhā dhuvassa vijñeyo bhūmerūrddhvamadhastathā ..
sadguṇaḥ sa divārūpo rātrirūpastamoguṇaḥ .. 57 ..
3.4.d:
द्विधा धुवस्स विज्ञेयो भूमेरूर्द्ध्वमधस्तथा ॥
सद्गुणः स दिवारूपो रात्रिरूपस्तमोगुणः ॥ 57 ॥
3.4.m: Dhruva is to be known as two-fold: above the earth and below. / Having the quality of sattva, he has the form of day; having the quality of tamas, he has the form of night.

3.4.s:
adhodhruve sadā rātrirnārakāstatra vai sthitāḥ ..
ūrdhvadhruve divā nityaṃ tapomadhye niśā divā .. 58 ..
3.4.d:
अधोध्रुवे सदा रात्रिर्नारकास्तत्र वै स्थिताः ॥
ऊर्ध्वध्रुवे दिवा नित्यं तपोमध्ये निशा दिवा ॥ 58 ॥
3.4.m: In the lower Dhruva there is always night, and the dwellers of hell abide there; / in the upper Dhruva there is perpetual day, and within Tapas there is both night and day.

3.4.s:
maho janastapassatyaṃ teṣu nityaṃ dinaṃ smṛtam ..
rauravaścāṃdhakūpaśca tāmisraṃ ca tamomayam ..
teṣu nityaṃ smṛtā rātriḥ kalpamānaṃ ca kovidaiḥ .. 59 ..
3.4.d:
महो जनस्तपस्सत्यं तेषु नित्यं दिनं स्मृतम् ॥
रौरवश्चांधकूपश्च तामिस्रं च तमोमयम् ॥
तेषु नित्यं स्मृता रात्रिः कल्पमानं च कोविदैः ॥ 59 ॥
3.4.m: In Mahas, Janas, Tapas, and Satya, there is traditionally perpetual day; / in Raurava, Andhakūpa, and Tāmisra full of darkness, / there is traditionally perpetual night, as the measure of a kalpa is understood by the wise.

3.4.s:
sa tu pūrvabhave cāsīdbrāhmaṇo mādhavapriyaḥ ..
ṣaṣṭyabdaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu prātaḥsnānaṃ cakāra ha .. 3.4.17.60 ..
3.4.d:
स तु पूर्वभवे चासीद्ब्राह्मणो माधवप्रियः ॥
षष्ट्यब्दं सर्वतीर्थेषु प्रातःस्नानं चकार ह ॥ 3.4.17.60 ॥
3.4.m: In a previous life, he was a brāhmaṇa dear to Mādhava; / for sixty years he took his morning bath in all the sacred fords.

3.4.s:
tīrtha puṇyātsa vai vipro mādhavo mādhavapriyaḥ ..
sunītyāṃ garbhamāsādya dhruvo bhūtvā rarāja ha ..
ṣaṭtriṃśacca sahasrābdaṃ rājyaṃ kṛtvā dhruvo'bhavat .. 61 .. ..
3.4.d:
तीर्थ पुण्यात्स वै विप्रो माधवो माधवप्रियः ॥
सुनीत्यां गर्भमासाद्य ध्रुवो भूत्वा रराज ह ॥
षट्त्रिंशच्च सहस्राब्दं राज्यं कृत्वा ध्रुवोऽभवत् ॥ 61 ॥ ॥
3.4.m: By the merit of the sacred fords, that brāhmaṇa Mādhava, dear to Mādhava, / entered the womb of Sunīti, became Dhruva, and shone forth; / having ruled for thirty-six thousand years, he became [the pole-star] Dhruva.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ sa dhruvaḥ paṃcamo vasuḥ ..
gurjare deśa āgamya vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ ..
naraśrīrnāma vikhyāto guṇavaiśyasya vai sutaḥ .. 62 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं स ध्रुवः पंचमो वसुः ॥
गुर्जरे देश आगम्य वैश्यजात्यां समुद्भवः ॥
नरश्रीर्नाम विख्यातो गुणवैश्यस्य वै सुतः ॥ 62 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Hearing this speech of the guru, that Dhruva, the fifth Vasu, / came to the Gurjara country and was born in the vaiśya caste, / famous by the name Naraśrī, the son of a virtuous vaiśya.

3.4.s:
kusīdaguṇaguptaśca naraśrīḥ putravatsalaḥ ..
tyaktvā prāṇānyayau svargaṃ sa vaiśyatanayo dhruvaḥ .. 63 ..
3.4.d:
कुसीदगुणगुप्तश्च नरश्रीः पुत्रवत्सलः ॥
त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्ययौ स्वर्गं स वैश्यतनयो ध्रुवः ॥ 63 ॥
3.4.m: Prudent in the ways of lending and loving toward his son, / that Dhruva, the son of a vaiśya named Naraśrī, gave up his life-breaths and went to heaven.

3.4.s:
pratyahaṃ sa hareḥ krīḍāṃ vṛndāvanamahottame ..
śivaprasādātpratyakṣāṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣamavāptavān .. 64 ..
3.4.d:
प्रत्यहं स हरेः क्रीडां वृन्दावनमहोत्तमे ॥
शिवप्रसादात्प्रत्यक्षां दृष्ट्वा हर्षमवाप्तवान् ॥ 64 ॥
3.4.m: By the grace of Śiva, he directly beheld every day / the sport of Hari in most excellent Vṛndāvana, and attained joy.

3.4.s:
yasya putravivāhe ca bhagavānbhaktavatsalaḥ ..
yādavaissaha saṃprāptastasya vāṃchitadāyakaḥ .. 65 ..
3.4.d:
यस्य पुत्रविवाहे च भगवान्भक्तवत्सलः ॥
यादवैस्सह संप्राप्तस्तस्य वांछितदायकः ॥ 65 ॥
3.4.m: At the wedding of whose son, the Lord, compassionate to his devotees, / arrived along with the Yādavas, granting his desire.

3.4.s:
purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgamya naraśrībharktarāṭ svayam ..
rāmānandasya śiṣyo'bhūdviṣṇudharma viśāradaḥ .. 66 ..
3.4.d:
पुरीं काशीं समागम्य नरश्रीभर्क्तराट् स्वयम् ॥
रामानन्दस्य शिष्योऽभूद्विष्णुधर्म विशारदः ॥ 66 ॥
3.4.m: Having come to the city of Kāśī, Naraśrī, himself the king of devotees, / became a disciple of Rāmānanda, skilled in the dharma of Viṣṇu.

3.4.s:
.. bṛhaspatiruvāca .. ..
kadācidbhagavānatrirgaṃgākūle'nasūyayā ..
sārddhaṃ tapo mahatkurvanbrahmadhyānaparo'bhavat .. .. 67 ..
3.4.d:
॥ बृहस्पतिरुवाच ॥ ॥
कदाचिद्भगवानत्रिर्गंगाकूलेऽनसूयया ॥
सार्द्धं तपो महत्कुर्वन्ब्रह्मध्यानपरोऽभवत् ॥ ॥ 67 ॥
3.4.m: Bṛhaspati said: / Once the venerable Atri, on the bank of the Gaṅgā, / performing great austerity together with Anasūyā, became devoted to meditating on Brahman.

3.4.s:
tadā brahmā hariśśaṃbhuḥ svasvavāhanamāsthitāḥ ..
varaṃ brūhīti vacanaṃ tamāhuste sanātanāḥ .. 68 ..
3.4.d:
तदा ब्रह्मा हरिश्शंभुः स्वस्ववाहनमास्थिताः ॥
वरं ब्रूहीति वचनं तमाहुस्ते सनातनाः ॥ 68 ॥
3.4.m: Then Brahmā, Hari, and Śambhu, mounted on their respective vehicles, / these eternal ones, spoke to him the words: 'Choose a boon!'

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vaca steṣāṃ svayaṃbhūtanayo muniḥ ..
naiva kiñcidvacaḥ prāha saṃsthitaḥ paramātmani .. 69 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वच स्तेषां स्वयंभूतनयो मुनिः ॥
नैव किञ्चिद्वचः प्राह संस्थितः परमात्मनि ॥ 69 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing their words, the sage, the son of the Self-born, / being established in the Supreme Self, spoke not a word.

3.4.s:
tasya bhāvaṃ samālokya trayo devāḥ sanātanāḥ ..
anasūyāṃ tasya patnīṃ samāgamya vaco'bruvan ..3.4.17.70..
3.4.d:
तस्य भावं समालोक्य त्रयो देवाः सनातनाः ॥
अनसूयां तस्य पत्नीं समागम्य वचोऽब्रुवन् ॥3.4.17.70॥
3.4.m: Observing his state, the three eternal gods / approached his wife Anasūyā and spoke these words:

3.4.s:
liṃgahastaḥ svayaṃ rudro viṣṇustadrasavarddhanaḥ ..
brahmā kāmabrahmalopaḥ sthitastasyā vaśaṃ gataḥ ..
ratiṃ dehi madāghūrṇe no cetprāṇāṃstyajāmyaham .. 71 ..
3.4.d:
लिंगहस्तः स्वयं रुद्रो विष्णुस्तद्रसवर्द्धनः ॥
ब्रह्मा कामब्रह्मलोपः स्थितस्तस्या वशं गतः ॥
रतिं देहि मदाघूर्णे नो चेत्प्राणांस्त्यजाम्यहम् ॥ 71 ॥
3.4.m: Rudra himself with liṅga in hand, Viṣṇu intensifying that passion, / and Brahmā with the desire for Brahman abandoned, stood overcome by her: / 'Grant us sexual union, O woman reeling with passion! If not, I shall abandon my life-breaths.'

3.4.s:
pativratā'nasūyā ca śrutvā teṣāṃ vaco'śubham ..
naiva kiṃcidvacaḥ prāha kopa bhītā surānprati .. 72 ..
3.4.d:
पतिव्रताऽनसूया च श्रुत्वा तेषां वचोऽशुभम् ॥
नैव किंचिद्वचः प्राह कोप भीता सुरान्प्रति ॥ 72 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing their inauspicious words, the devoted wife Anasūyā, / fearful of her own wrath, spoke not a word to the gods.

3.4.s:
mohitāstatra te devā gṛhītvā tāṃ balāttadā ..
maithunāya samudyogaṃ cakrurmāyāvimohitāḥ .. 73 ..
3.4.d:
मोहितास्तत्र ते देवा गृहीत्वा तां बलात्तदा ॥
मैथुनाय समुद्योगं चक्रुर्मायाविमोहिताः ॥ 73 ॥
3.4.m: Bewildered there, those gods, seizing her by force then, / deluded by Māyā, made an effort to have intercourse.

3.4.s:
tadā kruddhā satī sā vai tāñchaśāpa munipriyā ..
mama putrā bhaviṣyaṃti yūyaṃ kāmavimohitāḥ .. 74 ..
3.4.d:
तदा क्रुद्धा सती सा वै ताञ्छशाप मुनिप्रिया ॥
मम पुत्रा भविष्यंति यूयं कामविमोहिताः ॥ 74 ॥
3.4.m: Then that chaste woman, the beloved of the sage, enraged, cursed them: / 'You who are deluded by lust shall become my sons!

3.4.s:
mahādevasya vai liṃgaṃ brahmaṇo'sya mahāśiraḥ ..
caraṇau vāsudevasya pūjanīyā naraissadā ..
bhaviṣyaṃti suraśreṣṭhā upahāso'yamuttamaḥ .. 75 ..
3.4.d:
महादेवस्य वै लिंगं ब्रह्मणोऽस्य महाशिरः ॥
चरणौ वासुदेवस्य पूजनीया नरैस्सदा ॥
भविष्यंति सुरश्रेष्ठा उपहासोऽयमुत्तमः ॥ 75 ॥
3.4.m: The liṅga of Mahādeva, this great head of Brahmā, / and the feet of Vāsudeva are always to be worshipped by men, / O best of gods; this will be an excellent mockery!'

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vaco ghoraṃ namaskṛtya munipriyām ..
tuṣṭuvurbhaktinamrāśca devapāṭhaiśca ṛṅmayaiḥ ..76..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचो घोरं नमस्कृत्य मुनिप्रियाम् ॥
तुष्टुवुर्भक्तिनम्राश्च देवपाठैश्च ऋङ्मयैः ॥76॥
3.4.m: Hearing these dreadful words, bowing down to the sage's beloved, / humble with devotion, they praised her with divine hymns composed of ṛcs.

3.4.s:
anasūyā tadā prāha bhavanto mama putrakāḥ ..
bhūtvā śāpaṃ madīyaṃ ca tyaktvā tṛptimavāpsyatha ..77..
3.4.d:
अनसूया तदा प्राह भवन्तो मम पुत्रकाः ॥
भूत्वा शापं मदीयं च त्यक्त्वा तृप्तिमवाप्स्यथ ॥77॥
3.4.m: Then Anasūyā said: 'Becoming my little sons / and being freed from my curse, you will attain contentment.'

3.4.s:
ityukte vacane brahmā caṃdramāśca tadā hyabhūt ..
dattātreyo hariḥ sākṣāddurvāsā bhagavānharaḥ ..
tatpāpaparihārārthaṃ yogavanto babhūvire .. 78 ..
3.4.d:
इत्युक्ते वचने ब्रह्मा चंद्रमाश्च तदा ह्यभूत् ॥
दत्तात्रेयो हरिः साक्षाद्दुर्वासा भगवान्हरः ॥
तत्पापपरिहारार्थं योगवन्तो बभूविरे ॥ 78 ॥
3.4.m: When these words were spoken, Brahmā then became the Moon, / Hari directly became Dattātreya, and the venerable Hara became Durvāsas; / in order to remove that sin, they became endowed with yoga.

3.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare devī prakṛtissarva dharmiṇī ..
vidhiṃ viṣṇuṃ haraṃ cānyaṃ cakre sā guṇarūpiṇī .. 79 ..
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवी प्रकृतिस्सर्व धर्मिणी ॥
विधिं विष्णुं हरं चान्यं चक्रे सा गुणरूपिणी ॥ 79 ॥
3.4.m: Meanwhile, the goddess Prakṛti, possessing all properties, / embodied in the guṇas, made another Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.

3.4.s:
manvaṃtaramato jātaṃ teṣāṃ yogaṃ prakurvatām ..
hṛṣitāśca trayo devāssamāgamya ca tānprati .. 3.4.17.80 ..
3.4.d:
मन्वंतरमतो जातं तेषां योगं प्रकुर्वताम् ॥
हृषिताश्च त्रयो देवास्समागम्य च तान्प्रति ॥ 3.4.17.80 ॥
3.4.m: Then, as they practiced yoga, a Manvantara elapsed. / And the three delighted gods approached them

3.4.s:
uvāca vacanaṃ ramyaṃ teṣāṃ maṃgalahetave ..
candramāśca bhavetsomo vasuḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ surapriyaḥ .. 81 ..
3.4.d:
उवाच वचनं रम्यं तेषां मंगलहेतवे ॥
चन्द्रमाश्च भवेत्सोमो वसुः षष्ठः सुरप्रियः ॥ 81 ॥
3.4.m: and spoke pleasant words for their welfare: / 'May the Moon become Soma, the sixth Vasu, dear to the gods;

3.4.s:
rudrāṃśaścaiva durvāsāḥ pratyūṣaḥ saptamo vasuḥ ..
dattātreyamayo yogī prabhāsaścāṣṭamo vasuḥ ..
teṣāṃ vākyaṃ samākarṇya vasavaste trayo'bhavan ..82..
3.4.d:
रुद्रांशश्चैव दुर्वासाः प्रत्यूषः सप्तमो वसुः ॥
दत्तात्रेयमयो योगी प्रभासश्चाष्टमो वसुः ॥
तेषां वाक्यं समाकर्ण्य वसवस्ते त्रयोऽभवन् ॥82॥
3.4.m: and may Durvāsas, a portion of Rudra, become Pratyūṣa, the seventh Vasu; / and may the yogin who is Dattātreya become Prabhāsa, the eighth Vasu.' / Hearing their words, those three became Vasus.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ vasavo harṣitāstrayaḥ ..
svāṃśena bhūtalaṃ jagmuḥ kaliśuddhāya dāruṇe ..
dākṣiṇātye rājagṛhe vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ .. 83 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं वसवो हर्षितास्त्रयः ॥
स्वांशेन भूतलं जग्मुः कलिशुद्धाय दारुणे ॥
दाक्षिणात्ये राजगृहे वैश्यजात्यां समुद्भवः ॥ 83 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having heard the words of the guru thus, the three delighted Vasus / went with their own portions to the earth to purify the terrible Kali age. / In the south, an incarnation occurred in a royal house, in the vaiśya class:

3.4.s:
pīpā nāma sutaḥ somaḥ sudevasya tadā hyabhūt ..
kṛtaṃ rājyapadaṃ tena yathā bhūpena tatpure .. 84..
3.4.d:
पीपा नाम सुतः सोमः सुदेवस्य तदा ह्यभूत् ॥
कृतं राज्यपदं तेन यथा भूपेन तत्पुरे ॥ 84॥
3.4.m: Soma became the son of Sudeva named Pīpā; / the rank of royalty was maintained by him as king in that city.

3.4.s:
rāmānandasya śiṣyo'bhūddvārakāṃ sa samāgataḥ ..
harermudrāṃ svarṇamayīṃ prāpya kṛṣṇātsa vai nṛpaḥ ..
vaiṣṇavebhyo dadau tatra pretatattvavināśinīm .. 85 ..
3.4.d:
रामानन्दस्य शिष्योऽभूद्द्वारकां स समागतः ॥
हरेर्मुद्रां स्वर्णमयीं प्राप्य कृष्णात्स वै नृपः ॥
वैष्णवेभ्यो ददौ तत्र प्रेततत्त्वविनाशिनीम् ॥ 85 ॥
3.4.m: He became a disciple of Rāmānanda and went to Dvārakā. / Having obtained the golden seal of Hari from Kṛṣṇa, that king / gave it there to the Vaiṣṇavas, destroying the nature of pretas.

3.4.s:
pratyūṣaścaiva pāṃcāle vaiśyajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ ..
mārgapālasya tanayo nānako nāma viśrutaḥ .. 86 ..
3.4.d:
प्रत्यूषश्चैव पांचाले वैश्यजात्यां समुद्भवः ॥
मार्गपालस्य तनयो नानको नाम विश्रुतः ॥ 86 ॥
3.4.m: And Pratyūṣa was born in Pāñcāla in the vaiśya class / as the son of Mārgapāla, renowned by the name Nānaka.

3.4.s:
rāmānandaṃ samāgamya śiṣyo bhūtvā sa nānakaḥ ..
sa vai mlecchānvaśīkṛtya sūkṣmamārgamadarśayat .. 87 ..
3.4.d:
रामानन्दं समागम्य शिष्यो भूत्वा स नानकः ॥
स वै म्लेच्छान्वशीकृत्य सूक्ष्ममार्गमदर्शयत् ॥ 87 ॥
3.4.m: Approaching Rāmānanda, that Nānaka became his disciple; / having subdued the mlecchas, he showed the subtle path.

3.4.s:
prabhāso vai śāṃtipure brahmajātyāṃ samudbhavaḥ ..
śukladattasya tanayo nityānaṃda iti smṛtaḥ ..
iti te vasumāhātmyaṃ mayā śaunaka varṇitam .. 88 ..
atri śabdopari ṭippaṇī
3.4.d:
प्रभासो वै शांतिपुरे ब्रह्मजात्यां समुद्भवः ॥
शुक्लदत्तस्य तनयो नित्यानंद इति स्मृतः ॥
इति ते वसुमाहात्म्यं मया शौनक वर्णितम् ॥ 88 ॥
अत्रि शब्दोपरि टिप्पणी
3.4.m:
Prabhāsa was born in Śāntipura in the brāhmaṇa class, / the son of Śukladatta, known as Nityānanda. / Thus the greatness of the Vasus has been described to you by me, O Śaunaka.
Note on the word Atri.

3.4.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ityuktvā tānsurāndevo bhagavānbṛhatāṃpatiḥ ..
aśvinau ca samālokya tayorgāthāmavarṇayat .. 1 ..
3.4.d:
॥ सूत उवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्त्वा तान्सुरान्देवो भगवान्बृहतांपतिः ॥
अश्विनौ च समालोक्य तयोर्गाथामवर्णयत् ॥ 1 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus to those gods, the lord, the master of speech, / looked at the two Aśvins and described their story:

3.4.s:
vaivasvate'ntare pūrvaṃ viśvakarmā vicitrakṛt ..
citraguptaśriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā citralekhāvinirmitām ..
sparddhābhūto mahāmāyāṃ tuṣṭāva bahupūjanaiḥ .. 2 ..
3.4.d:
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे पूर्वं विश्वकर्मा विचित्रकृत् ॥
चित्रगुप्तश्रियं दृष्ट्वा चित्रलेखाविनिर्मिताम् ॥
स्पर्द्धाभूतो महामायां तुष्टाव बहुपूजनैः ॥ 2 ॥
3.4.m: Formerly, in the Vaivasvata interval, Viśvakarman, the creator of wonders, / seeing the glory of Citragupta crafted by Citralekhā, / felt rivalry and praised Mahāmāyā with many worships.

3.4.s:
prasannā sā tadā devī citrāyāṃ tasya yoṣiti ..
svāṃśājjātā smṛtā saṃjñā sarvajñānakarī svayam .. 3 ..
3.4.d:
प्रसन्ना सा तदा देवी चित्रायां तस्य योषिति ॥
स्वांशाज्जाता स्मृता संज्ञा सर्वज्ञानकरी स्वयम् ॥ 3 ॥
3.4.m: Then that pleased goddess was born from her own portion in his wife Citrā; / she is known as Saṃjñā, who herself produces all knowledge.

3.4.s:
ṣoḍaśābde vayaḥ prāpte saṃjñāyāstatpitā sukhī ..
vivāhārthī surānsarvānāhvayanmerumūrddhani .. 4 ..
3.4.d:
षोडशाब्दे वयः प्राप्ते संज्ञायास्तत्पिता सुखी ॥
विवाहार्थी सुरान्सर्वानाह्वयन्मेरुमूर्द्धनि ॥ 4 ॥
3.4.m: When Saṃjñā reached sixteen years of age, her joyful father, / desiring her marriage, summoned all the gods to the peak of Mount Meru.

3.4.s:
yakṣādhīśāśca ṣaḍviṃśatkuberādyāssamāgatāḥ ..
yādasāṃ patayaḥ prāptā daśa tatraiva kāmukāḥ .. 5 ..
3.4.d:
यक्षाधीशाश्च षड्विंशत्कुबेराद्यास्समागताः ॥
यादसां पतयः प्राप्ता दश तत्रैव कामुकाः ॥ 5 ॥
3.4.m: Twenty-six lords of yakṣas, Kubera and others, arrived; / ten lustful lords of aquatic creatures arrived right there;

3.4.s:
pāvakā ūnapaṃcāśadvāyavaśca tathā smṛtāḥ ..
dhruvau dvau ca svayaṃ prāptau somāstatraiva ṣoḍaśa ..6..
3.4.d:
पावका ऊनपंचाशद्वायवश्च तथा स्मृताः ॥
ध्रुवौ द्वौ च स्वयं प्राप्तौ सोमास्तत्रैव षोडश ॥6॥
3.4.m: forty-nine fires, and likewise the winds, are recorded; / two Dhruvas arrived in person, and right there sixteen Somas;

3.4.s:
trayodaśa ca pratyūṣāḥ prāptā viśvaprarakṣakāḥ ..
ṣaṣṭyuttaraṃ ca triśataṃ prabhāsā dinarakṣakāḥ ..7 ..
3.4.d:
त्रयोदश च प्रत्यूषाः प्राप्ता विश्वप्ररक्षकाः ॥
षष्ट्युत्तरं च त्रिशतं प्रभासा दिनरक्षकाः ॥7 ॥
3.4.m: thirteen Pratyūṣas arrived, protectors of the universe; / three hundred and sixty Prabhāsas, protectors of the day;

3.4.s:
bhavādyāśca tadāḥ rudrāḥ śaśimaṇḍalarakṣakāḥ ..
ādityāśca sthitāssarve saṃjñāyāśca svayaṃvare .. 8 ..
3.4.d:
भवाद्याश्च तदाः रुद्राः शशिमण्डलरक्षकाः ॥
आदित्याश्च स्थितास्सर्वे संज्ञायाश्च स्वयंवरे ॥ 8 ॥
3.4.m: Bhava and the other Rudras, protectors of the lunar disc; / and all the Ādityas stood at the svayaṃvara of Saṃjñā.

3.4.s:
dānavā vipracittyādyāścaturāśītirāyayuḥ ..
prahlādādyāstadā daityā vāsukyādyāśca pannagāḥ .. 9 ..
3.4.d:
दानवा विप्रचित्त्याद्याश्चतुराशीतिराययुः ॥
प्रह्लादाद्यास्तदा दैत्या वासुक्याद्याश्च पन्नगाः ॥ 9 ॥
3.4.m: Eighty-four Dānavas, Vipracitti and others, arrived; / then Daityas such as Prahlāda, and snakes such as Vāsuki;

3.4.s:
śeṣādyāśca tadā nāgāstārkṣyādyā garuḍāḥ smṛtāḥ ..
sarve svayaṃvare prāptā mahākolāhalohyabhūt .. 3.4.18.10 ..
3.4.d:
शेषाद्याश्च तदा नागास्तार्क्ष्याद्या गरुडाः स्मृताः ॥
सर्वे स्वयंवरे प्राप्ता महाकोलाहलोह्यभूत् ॥ 3.4.18.10 ॥
3.4.m: the nāgas such as Śeṣa, and the Garuḍas such as Tārkṣya are mentioned; / all arrived at the svayaṃvara, and a great uproar arose.

3.4.s:
etasminnaṃtare devī devakanyāsamanvitā ..
saṃjñā devānprati tadā pratyakṣamabhavaddivi .. 11 ..
3.4.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे देवी देवकन्यासमन्विता ॥
संज्ञा देवान्प्रति तदा प्रत्यक्षमभवद्दिवि ॥ 11 ॥
3.4.m: At that moment, the goddess Saṃjñā, accompanied by divine maidens, / became visible before the gods in heaven.

3.4.s:
tāṃ samālokya balavānbaliḥ kāmavimohitaḥ ..
kare gṛhītvā prayayau paśyatāṃ sarvadhanvinām .. 12 ..
3.4.d:
तां समालोक्य बलवान्बलिः कामविमोहितः ॥
करे गृहीत्वा प्रययौ पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम् ॥ 12 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing her, the mighty Bali, infatuated with desire, / seized her by the hand and went away before the eyes of all the archers.

3.4.s:
tadā krodhāturā devā rurudhurdaityasattamam ..
śastrāstraistarpayitvā taṃ mahadyuddhamakārayan .. 13 ..
3.4.d:
तदा क्रोधातुरा देवा रुरुधुर्दैत्यसत्तमम् ॥
शस्त्रास्त्रैस्तर्पयित्वा तं महद्युद्धमकारयन् ॥ 13 ॥
3.4.m: Then the gods, overcome with anger, obstructed that best of Daityas; / gratifying him with weapons and missiles, they fought a great battle.

3.4.s:
dānavāśca tadā daityā nānāvāhanasaṃsthitāḥ ..
devaiḥ sārddhaṃ mahadyuddhaṃ tumulaṃ cakrire mudā .. 14 ..
3.4.d:
दानवाश्च तदा दैत्या नानावाहनसंस्थिताः ॥
देवैः सार्द्धं महद्युद्धं तुमुलं चक्रिरे मुदा ॥ 14 ॥
3.4.m: Then the Dānavas and Daityas, mounted on various vehicles, / gladly fought a great, tumultuous battle alongside the gods.

3.4.s:
dānavaiśca hatā devāḥ surairdaityā vināśitāḥ ..
śavabhūtairilāvarte'bhūdagamyā vasuṃdharā .. 15 ..
3.4.d:
दानवैश्च हता देवाः सुरैर्दैत्या विनाशिताः ॥
शवभूतैरिलावर्तेऽभूदगम्या वसुंधरा ॥ 15 ॥
3.4.m: Gods were killed by the Dānavas, and Daityas were destroyed by the gods; / filled with corpses in Ilāvarta, the earth became impassable.

3.4.s:
pakṣamātra mabhūdyuddhaṃ divyaṃ dānavadevayoḥ ..
pāṃcajanyastathā dhātā hayagrīvaśca mitrakaḥ .. 16 ..
3.4.d:
पक्षमात्र मभूद्युद्धं दिव्यं दानवदेवयोः ॥
पांचजन्यस्तथा धाता हयग्रीवश्च मित्रकः ॥ 16 ॥
3.4.m: The heavenly battle between the Dānavas and the gods lasted for a fortnight: / Pāñcajanya and Dhātṛ, Hayagrīva and Mitra,

3.4.s:
aghāsuro'ryamā caiva balaḥ śakrastathaiva ca ..
bakāsuraśca varuṇaḥ śakaṭaḥ prāṃśureva ca .. 17 ..
3.4.d:
अघासुरोऽर्यमा चैव बलः शक्रस्तथैव च ॥
बकासुरश्च वरुणः शकटः प्रांशुरेव च ॥ 17 ॥
3.4.m: Aghāsura and Aryaman, and likewise Bala and Śakra, / Bakāsura and Varuṇa, Śakaṭa and Prāṃśu,

3.4.s:
vatsāsuro bhagaścaiva vivasvāṃśca baliḥ svayam ..
pralaṃbaśca tathā pūṣā gardabhaḥ savitā yudhi ..18..
3.4.d:
वत्सासुरो भगश्चैव विवस्वांश्च बलिः स्वयम् ॥
प्रलंबश्च तथा पूषा गर्दभः सविता युधि ॥18॥
3.4.m: Vatsāsura and Bhaga, and Vivasvat and Bali himself, / Pralamba and Pūṣan, Gardabha and Savitṛ in battle,

3.4.s:
viśvakarmā mayaścaiva kālanemirhariḥ svayam ..
kāṃkṣamāṇau ca vijayaṃ yuyudhāte parasparam ..
parājitāśca te daityā yuddhaṃ tyaktvā pradudruvuḥ .. 19 ..
3.4.d:
विश्वकर्मा मयश्चैव कालनेमिर्हरिः स्वयम् ॥
कांक्षमाणौ च विजयं युयुधाते परस्परम् ॥
पराजिताश्च ते दैत्या युद्धं त्यक्त्वा प्रदुद्रुवुः ॥ 19 ॥
3.4.m: Viśvakarman and Maya, and Kālanemi and Hari himself— / desiring victory, they fought one another. / And defeated, those Daityas abandoned the battle and fled.

3.4.s:
vivasvām̐śca tadā saṃjñāṃ gṛhītvā rathasaṃsthitām ..
viśvakarmāṇamāgamya dadau tasmai prasannadhīḥ .. 3.4.18.20 ..
3.4.d:
विवस्वाम्̐श्च तदा संज्ञां गृहीत्वा रथसंस्थिताम् ॥
विश्वकर्माणमागम्य ददौ तस्मै प्रसन्नधीः ॥ 3.4.18.20 ॥
3.4.m: Then Vivasvat, having taken Saṃjñā standing in the chariot, / approached Viśvakarman and gave her to him with a pleased mind.

3.4.s:
vivasvaṃtaṃ suraśreṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃjñā vaco'bravīt ..
matpatiśca bhavāndevo bhavetkāryakarassadā .. 21 ..
3.4.d:
विवस्वंतं सुरश्रेष्ठं दृष्ट्वा संज्ञा वचोऽब्रवीत् ॥
मत्पतिश्च भवान्देवो भवेत्कार्यकरस्सदा ॥ 21 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing Vivasvat, the best of the gods, Saṃjñā spoke these words: / 'May you, O god, be my husband, always doing what is needed.

3.4.s:
tvayā jitāhaṃ bhagavanbalervipriyakāriṇaḥ ..
bhrātṛjāgrahaṇe doṣo na bhavetsa kadācana .. 22 ..
3.4.d:
त्वया जिताहं भगवन्बलेर्विप्रियकारिणः ॥
भ्रातृजाग्रहणे दोषो न भवेत्स कदाचन ॥ 22 ॥
3.4.m: I was won by you, O lord, from Bali who does unwelcome deeds; / in taking a brother’s daughter, there can never be any fault.

3.4.s:
vīrabhuktā sadā nārī strīratnaṃ munibhiḥ smṛtam ..
caturddhā prakṛtirdevī guṇabhinnā guṇaikikā ..
ekā sā prakṛtirmātā guṇasāmyātsanātanī .. 23 ..
3.4.d:
वीरभुक्ता सदा नारी स्त्रीरत्नं मुनिभिः स्मृतम् ॥
चतुर्द्धा प्रकृतिर्देवी गुणभिन्ना गुणैकिका ॥
एका सा प्रकृतिर्माता गुणसाम्यात्सनातनी ॥ 23 ॥
3.4.m: A woman enjoyed by a hero is always considered a gem among women by the sages. / The goddess Prakṛti is fourfold, differentiated by guṇas or united with each guṇa; / through the equilibrium of the guṇas, that eternal Prakṛti is one, the Mother.

3.4.s:
sattvabhūtā ca bhagi nī rajobhūtā ca gehinī ..
tamobhūtā ca sā kanyā tasyai devyai namonamaḥ .. 24 ..
3.4.d:
सत्त्वभूता च भगि नी रजोभूता च गेहिनी ॥
तमोभूता च सा कन्या तस्यै देव्यै नमोनमः ॥ 24 ॥
3.4.m: Embodying sattva, she is the sister; embodying rajas, she is the wife; / and embodying tamas, she is the maiden. Reverence, reverence to that goddess!

3.4.s:
bahavaḥ puruṣā ye vai nirguṇāścaikarūpiṇaḥ ..
caitanyā'jñānavaṃtaśca loke prakṛtisaṃbhavāḥ .. 25 ..
3.4.d:
बहवः पुरुषा ये वै निर्गुणाश्चैकरूपिणः ॥
चैतन्याऽज्ञानवंतश्च लोके प्रकृतिसंभवाः ॥ 25 ॥
3.4.m: The many puruṣas, who are without attributes and uniform, / conscious and ignorant, are born of Prakṛti in this world.

3.4.s:
aloke pāpajāssarve devabrahmasamudbhavāḥ ..
yā tu jñānamayī nārī vṛṇedyaṃ puruṣaṃ śubham ..
ko'pi putraḥ pitā bhrātā sa ca tasyāḥ patirbhavet .. 26 ..
3.4.d:
अलोके पापजास्सर्वे देवब्रह्मसमुद्भवाः ॥
या तु ज्ञानमयी नारी वृणेद्यं पुरुषं शुभम् ॥
कोऽपि पुत्रः पिता भ्राता स च तस्याः पतिर्भवेत् ॥ 26 ॥
3.4.m: In the unworldly, all born of sin arise from gods and Brahmā. / But whichever auspicious man a woman made of knowledge chooses, / be he a son, father, or brother, he becomes her husband.

3.4.s:
svakīyāṃ ca sutāṃ brahmā viṣṇudevaḥ svamātaram ..
bhaginīṃ bhagavāñchaṃbhurgṛhītvā śreṣṭhatāmagāt .. 27 ..
3.4.d:
स्वकीयां च सुतां ब्रह्मा विष्णुदेवः स्वमातरम् ॥
भगिनीं भगवाञ्छंभुर्गृहीत्वा श्रेष्ठतामगात् ॥ 27 ॥
3.4.m: Taking his own daughter, Brahmā, taking his mother, Lord Viṣṇu, / and taking his sister, Lord Śambhu attained preeminence.'

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vedamayaṃ vākyaṃ cāditisaṃbhavaḥ ..
vivasvānbhrātṛjāṃ saṃjñāṃ gṛhītvā śreṣṭhavānabhūt .. 28 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वेदमयं वाक्यं चादितिसंभवः ॥
विवस्वान्भ्रातृजां संज्ञां गृहीत्वा श्रेष्ठवानभूत् ॥ 28 ॥
3.4.m: Hearing this speech filled with the Veda, the son of Aditi, / Vivasvat, took his brother's daughter Saṃjñā and attained preeminence.

3.4.s:
sutāḥ kanyāstayorjātā manurvaivasvatastathā ..
yamaśca yamunā caiva divyatejobhiranvitāḥ .. 29 ..
3.4.d:
सुताः कन्यास्तयोर्जाता मनुर्वैवस्वतस्तथा ॥
यमश्च यमुना चैव दिव्यतेजोभिरन्विताः ॥ 29 ॥
3.4.m: Sons and a daughter were born to the two: Manu Vaivasvata, / and Yama, and Yamunā, endowed with divine splendour.

3.4.s:
tadā saṃjñā satī sākṣāttejobhūtaṃ patiṃ svakam ..
jñātvā chāyāṃ samutpādya tapase vanamā gatā .. 3.4.18.30 ..
3.4.d:
तदा संज्ञा सती साक्षात्तेजोभूतं पतिं स्वकम् ॥
ज्ञात्वा छायां समुत्पाद्य तपसे वनमा गता ॥ 3.4.18.30 ॥
3.4.m: Then the virtuous Saṃjñā, realising directly that her husband was made of fiery energy, / created Chāyā and went to the forest to perform austerities.

3.4.s:
sāvarṇiśca manustasyāṃ śaniśca tapatī tathā ..
chāyāyāṃ ca samudbhūtāḥ kūradṛṣṭyā vivasvataḥ .. 31 ..
3.4.d:
सावर्णिश्च मनुस्तस्यां शनिश्च तपती तथा ॥
छायायां च समुद्भूताः कूरदृष्ट्या विवस्वतः ॥ 31 ॥
3.4.m: And through Chāyā were born Manu Sāvarṇi, / and Śani, and Tapatī, under the harsh gaze of Vivasvat.

3.4.s:
putrabhedena tāṃ nārīṃ matvā māyāṃ ruṣānvitaḥ ..
cakāra bhasmabhūtāṃ tāṃ vivasvānbhagavānraviḥ .. 32 ..
3.4.d:
पुत्रभेदेन तां नारीं मत्वा मायां रुषान्वितः ॥
चकार भस्मभूतां तां विवस्वान्भगवान्रविः ॥ 32 ॥
3.4.m: Considering that woman an illusion because of the difference between the sons, filled with rage, / the blessed Sun, Vivasvat, reduced her to ashes.

3.4.s:
tadā śaniśca sāvarṇirvivasvataṃ ruṣānvitam ..
jñātvā ca krodhatāmrākṣau yuyudhāte parasparam .. 33 ..
3.4.d:
तदा शनिश्च सावर्णिर्विवस्वतं रुषान्वितम् ॥
ज्ञात्वा च क्रोधताम्राक्षौ युयुधाते परस्परम् ॥ 33 ॥
3.4.m: Then Śani and Sāvarṇi, seeing Vivasvat filled with rage, / with eyes red with fury, fought against each other.

3.4.s:
kiyato caiva kālena bhagnabhūtau vivasvatā ..
himācale girau prāpya tepatuḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ .. 34 ..
3.4.d:
कियतो चैव कालेन भग्नभूतौ विवस्वता ॥
हिमाचले गिरौ प्राप्य तेपतुः परमं तपः ॥ 34 ॥
3.4.m: And after some time, having been defeated by Vivasvat, / they reached the Himālaya mountain and performed supreme austerities.

3.4.s:
trivarṣānte ca sā devī mahākālī samāgatā..
arcitaṃ ca varaṃ tābhyāṃ dadau tadbhaktivatsalā ..35..
3.4.d:
त्रिवर्षान्ते च सा देवी महाकाली समागता॥
अर्चितं च वरं ताभ्यां ददौ तद्भक्तिवत्सला ॥35॥
3.4.m: At the end of three years, that goddess Mahākālī arrived; / affectionate toward her devotees, she granted the boon requested by the two.

3.4.s:
punastau ca samāgamya yuyudhāte vivasvatā..
vivasvānbhayabhītaśca tyaktvā yuddhaṃ parābhavat .. 36 ..
3.4.d:
पुनस्तौ च समागम्य युयुधाते विवस्वता॥
विवस्वान्भयभीतश्च त्यक्त्वा युद्धं पराभवत् ॥ 36 ॥
3.4.m: Returning again, the two fought with Vivasvat; / terrified, Vivasvat abandoned the fight and suffered defeat.

3.4.s:
tatra sthitā priyā saṃjñā vaḍavārūpadhariṇī ..
kurukhaṃḍe mahāramye tapaṃtī tapa ulbaṇam .. 37 ..
3.4.d:
तत्र स्थिता प्रिया संज्ञा वडवारूपधरिणी ॥
कुरुखंडे महारम्ये तपंती तप उल्बणम् ॥ 37 ॥
3.4.m: His beloved Saṃjñā was staying there, having assumed the form of a mare, / performing severe austerities in the delightful region of Kurukṣetra.

3.4.s:
gatvā dadarśa bhagavānsajñāṃ saṃbodhakāriṇīm ..
kāmāturo hayo bhūtvā tatra reme tayā saha .. 38 ..
3.4.d:
गत्वा ददर्श भगवान्सज्ञां संबोधकारिणीम् ॥
कामातुरो हयो भूत्वा तत्र रेमे तया सह ॥ 38 ॥
3.4.m: Going there, the Lord saw Saṃjñā, who brought enlightenment; / stricken with passion, he became a horse and sported with her there.

3.4.s:
paṃcavarṣāntare saṃjñā garbhaṃ tasmāddadhau svayam ..
tanayau ca samudbhūtau divya rūpaparākramau .. 39 ..
3.4.d:
पंचवर्षान्तरे संज्ञा गर्भं तस्माद्दधौ स्वयम् ॥
तनयौ च समुद्भूतौ दिव्य रूपपराक्रमौ ॥ 39 ॥
3.4.m: At the end of five years, Saṃjñā herself conceived from him; / and two sons were born, possessed of divine beauty and prowess.

3.4.s:
piturduḥkhaṃ samālokya jagmatū ravimaṇḍalam ..
jitvā baṃdhū durācārau krūradṛṣṭyā tadā svayam .. 3.4.18.40 ..
3.4.d:
पितुर्दुःखं समालोक्य जग्मतू रविमण्डलम् ॥
जित्वा बंधू दुराचारौ क्रूरदृष्ट्या तदा स्वयम् ॥ 3.4.18.40 ॥
3.4.m: Seeing their father's distress, they went to the orb of the Sun; / having defeated the two wicked brothers then by their fierce glance,

3.4.s:
baddhvā tau svapituḥ pārśvama saṃprāptau vaḍavāsutau ..
dṛṣṭvā vivasvānbhagavānvairiṇau samupāgatau .. 41 ..
3.4.d:
बद्ध्वा तौ स्वपितुः पार्श्वम संप्राप्तौ वडवासुतौ ॥
दृष्ट्वा विवस्वान्भगवान्वैरिणौ समुपागतौ ॥ 41 ॥
3.4.m: and binding the two, the sons of the mare brought them to their father's presence. / Seeing his two enemies arrived, the blessed Vivasvat

3.4.s:
saṃpīḍya tāḍayāmāsa lohadaṃḍairbhayānakaiḥ ..
paṃgubhūtau punastyaktvā chāyāputrau divākaraḥ .. 42 ..
3.4.d:
संपीड्य ताडयामास लोहदंडैर्भयानकैः ॥
पंगुभूतौ पुनस्त्यक्त्वा छायापुत्रौ दिवाकरः ॥ 42 ॥
3.4.m: tormented them and struck them with terrifying iron rods. / Having rendered the two sons of Chāyā lame, the Sun-god dismissed them.

3.4.s:
āśvineyau samālokya vacanaṃ prāha tau mudā ..
jīva īśo yathā mitre naranārāyaṇau yathā..
ekanāmnā yuvāṃ prītau nāsatyau ca bhaviṣyathaḥ .. 43 ..
3.4.d:
आश्विनेयौ समालोक्य वचनं प्राह तौ मुदा ॥
जीव ईशो यथा मित्रे नरनारायणौ यथा॥
एकनाम्ना युवां प्रीतौ नासत्यौ च भविष्यथः ॥ 43 ॥
3.4.m: Looking at the two sons of Aśvinī, he gladly spoke these words: / 'Just as the individual soul and God are friends, just as Nara and Nārāyaṇa are, / so you two, affectionate, shall be known by a single name as the Nāsatyas.

3.4.s:
somaśaktiriḍādevī jyeṣṭhapatnī bhaviṣyati ..
piṃgalā sūryaśaktiśca laghupatnī bhaviṣyati .. 44 ..
3.4.d:
सोमशक्तिरिडादेवी ज्येष्ठपत्नी भविष्यति ॥
पिंगला सूर्यशक्तिश्च लघुपत्नी भविष्यति ॥ 44 ॥
3.4.m: Goddess Iḍā, the lunar power, will be the elder wife; / and Piṅgalā, the solar power, will be the younger wife.

3.4.s:
iḍāpatissa vai nāma dvitīyaḥ piṃgalāpatiḥ ..
dvādaśassa nṛṇāṃ rāśeḥ krūradṛṣṭiḥ śanaiścaraḥ ..
tasya śāntikaro jyeṣṭho bhaviṣyati mahītale .. 45 ..
3.4.d:
इडापतिस्स वै नाम द्वितीयः पिंगलापतिः ॥
द्वादशस्स नृणां राशेः क्रूरदृष्टिः शनैश्चरः ॥
तस्य शान्तिकरो ज्येष्ठो भविष्यति महीतले ॥ 45 ॥
3.4.m: One shall indeed be named Iḍāpati, and the second Piṅgalāpati. / Saturn of cruel gaze is in the twelfth sign of men; / the elder one will be his pacifier on the earth.

3.4.s:
dvitīyaśca nṛṇāṃ rāśeḥ sāvarṇirbhramakārakaḥ ..
tasya śāntikaro bhūmau bhavitā piṃgalāpatiḥ .. 46..
3.4.d:
द्वितीयश्च नृणां राशेः सावर्णिर्भ्रमकारकः ॥
तस्य शान्तिकरो भूमौ भविता पिंगलापतिः ॥ 46॥
3.4.m: And Sāvarṇi, the cause of delusion, is in the second sign of men; / Piṅgalāpati will be his pacifier on earth.

3.4.s:
janmarāśisthitā devī tapatī tā pakāriṇī ..
iḍā ca piṃgalā tasyāḥ śāntikartryau bhaviṣyataḥ .. 47 ..
3.4.d:
जन्मराशिस्थिता देवी तपती ता पकारिणी ॥
इडा च पिंगला तस्याः शान्तिकर्त्र्यौ भविष्यतः ॥ 47 ॥
3.4.m: Goddess Tapatī, residing in the birth sign, causes burning; / Iḍā and Piṅgalā will both become her pacifiers.'

3.4.s:
iti śrutvā vacastasya suravaidyau babhūvatuḥ ..
sāvarṇiśca śanī rāhuḥ ketuḥ svargapratāpanaḥ ..
teṣāṃ tu parihārārthau dasrau cāśvinisaṃbhavau .. 48 ..
3.4.d:
इति श्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य सुरवैद्यौ बभूवतुः ॥
सावर्णिश्च शनी राहुः केतुः स्वर्गप्रतापनः ॥
तेषां तु परिहारार्थौ दस्रौ चाश्विनिसंभवौ ॥ 48 ॥
3.4.m: Having heard his words, the two became physicians to the gods. / To counter Sāvarṇi, Śani, Rāhu, and Ketu who torments heaven, / the Dasras were born of Aśvinī.

3.4.s:
sūta uvāca ..
iti śrutvā gurorvākyaṃ prasannau surasattamau ..
svāṃśānmahītale jātau śūdrayonyāṃ ravestutau .. 49 ..
3.4.d:
सूत उवाच ॥
इति श्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं प्रसन्नौ सुरसत्तमौ ॥
स्वांशान्महीतले जातौ शूद्रयोन्यां रवेस्तुतौ ॥ 49 ॥
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Hearing thus the words of their father, the two best of gods were pleased. / By their own portions, the two sons of the Sun were born on earth in the womb of Śūdras.

3.4.s:
cāṇḍālasya gṛhe jātaśchāgahaṃturiḍāpatiḥ ..
sadhano nāma vikhyātaḥ pitṛmātṛparāyaṇaḥ .. 3.4.18.50 ..
3.4.d:
चाण्डालस्य गृहे जातश्छागहंतुरिडापतिः ॥
सधनो नाम विख्यातः पितृमातृपरायणः ॥ 3.4.18.50 ॥
3.4.m: Iḍāpati was born in the house of an outcaste, a slaughterer of goats; / renowned by the name Sadhana, devoted to his parents,

3.4.s:
śāligrāmaśilātulyaṃ chāgamāṃsaṃ vicikriye ..
kabīraṃ samupāgamya śiṣyo bhūtvā rarāja vai.. 51 ..
3.4.d:
शालिग्रामशिलातुल्यं छागमांसं विचिक्रिये ॥
कबीरं समुपागम्य शिष्यो भूत्वा रराज वै॥ 51 ॥
3.4.m: he sold goat meat [weighed] equal to the Śāligrāma stone. / Approaching Kabīra, he became his disciple and shone forth.

3.4.s:
sa tu satyanidhiḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇastapa āsthitaḥ..
bhayabhītāṃ ca gāṃ tatra cāṇḍālāya hyadarśayat ..
rājagehe karastasmātsadhanasya layaṃ gataḥ .. 52 ..
3.4.d:
स तु सत्यनिधिः पूर्वं ब्रह्मणस्तप आस्थितः॥
भयभीतां च गां तत्र चाण्डालाय ह्यदर्शयत् ॥
राजगेहे करस्तस्मात्सधनस्य लयं गतः ॥ 52 ॥
3.4.m: He had formerly been Satyanidhi, engaged in the asceticism of Brahmā; / there he had pointed out a terrified cow to an outcaste, / and therefore in the royal palace Sadhana's hand was cut off.

3.4.s:
carmakāragṛhe jāto dvitīyaḥ piṃgalāpatiḥ ..
mānadā sasya tanayo raidāsa iti viśrutaḥ .. 53 ..
3.4.d:
चर्मकारगृहे जातो द्वितीयः पिंगलापतिः ॥
मानदा सस्य तनयो रैदास इति विश्रुतः ॥ 53 ॥
3.4.m: The second, Piṅgalāpati, was born in the house of a leather-worker; / the son of Mānadāsa, renowned as Raidāsa.

3.4.s:
purīṃ kāśīṃ samāgamya kabīraṃ rāmatatparam ..
jitvā matavivādena śaṃkarācāryamāgataḥ ..54 ..
3.4.d:
पुरीं काशीं समागम्य कबीरं रामतत्परम् ॥
जित्वा मतविवादेन शंकराचार्यमागतः ॥54 ॥
3.4.m: Going to the city of Kāśī, he defeated Kabīra, who was devoted to Rāma, / in a doctrinal dispute, and then went to Śaṅkarācārya.

3.4.s:
tayorvivādo sabhavadahorātraṃ matāntare ..
parājitassa raidāso natvā taṃ dvijasattamam ..
rāmānandamupāgamya tasya śiṣyatvamāgataḥ .. 55 ..
3.4.d:
तयोर्विवादो सभवदहोरात्रं मतान्तरे ॥
पराजितस्स रैदासो नत्वा तं द्विजसत्तमम् ॥
रामानन्दमुपागम्य तस्य शिष्यत्वमागतः ॥ 55 ॥
3.4.m: A debate on differing doctrines took place between the two day and night. / Defeated, Raidāsa bowed to that best of Brahmins; / he approached Rāmānanda and became his disciple.

3.4.s:
iti te kathitaṃ vipra surāṃśāśca yathābhavan ..
kaliśuddhikarī līlā teṣāṃ mārgapradarśinām .. 56 ..
viṣṇusvāmīmadhvācāryavarṇanam
3.4.d:
इति ते कथितं विप्र सुरांशाश्च यथाभवन् ॥
कलिशुद्धिकरी लीला तेषां मार्गप्रदर्शिनाम् ॥ 56 ॥
विष्णुस्वामीमध्वाचार्यवर्णनम्
3.4.m:
Thus has been told to you, O Brahmin, how the portions of the gods came to be; / their pastimes, purifying the Kali age, show the right path.
Description of Viṣṇusvāmin and Madhvācārya

3.4.s:
sūta uvāca
ityuktvā bhagavāñjīvo devamāhātmyamuttamam .
svamukhātsvāṃśamutpādya brahmayonau babhūva ha . . 1
3.4.d:
सूत उवाच
इत्युक्त्वा भगवाञ्जीवो देवमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ।
स्वमुखात्स्वांशमुत्पाद्य ब्रह्मयोनौ बभूव ह ॥ 1
3.4.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus of the supreme greatness of the gods, the blessed Jīva, / producing a portion of himself from his mouth, was born indeed from a Brahmin womb.

3.4.s:
iṣṭikā nagarī ramyā gurudattasya vai sutaḥ .
ropaṇo nāma vikhyāto brahmamārgapradarśakaḥ . . 2
3.4.d:
इष्टिका नगरी रम्या गुरुदत्तस्य वै सुतः ।
रोपणो नाम विख्यातो ब्रह्ममार्गप्रदर्शकः ॥ 2
3.4.m: In the delightful town of Iṣṭikā, the son of Gurudatta, / renowned by the name Ropaṇa, showed the path of Brahman.

3.4.s:
sūtragranthamayīṃ mālāṃ tilakaṃ jalanirmitam .
vāsudeveti tanmantre kalau kṛtvā janejane . . 3
3.4.d:
सूत्रग्रन्थमयीं मालां तिलकं जलनिर्मितम् ।
वासुदेवेति तन्मन्त्रे कलौ कृत्वा जनेजने ॥ 3
3.4.m: Giving a garland of knotted threads and a tilaka made with water, / and chanting the mantra 'Vāsudeva' to every person in the Kali age,

3.4.s:
kṛṣṇacaitanyamāgamya kambalaṃ ca tadājñayā .
gṛhītvā svapurīṃ prāpya kṛṣṇadhyānaparobhavat . . 4
3.4.d:
कृष्णचैतन्यमागम्य कम्बलं च तदाज्ञया ।
गृहीत्वा स्वपुरीं प्राप्य कृष्णध्यानपरोभवत् ॥ 4
3.4.m: he approached Kṛṣṇa Caitanya and, receiving a blanket by his order, / returned to his town and became devoted to meditation on Kṛṣṇa.

3.4.s:
ataḥ paraṃ śṛṇu mune caritraṃ ca harermudā .
yacchrutvā ca kalau ghore jano naiva bhayaṃ vrajet . . 5
3.4.d:
अतः परं शृणु मुने चरित्रं च हरेर्मुदा ।
यच्छ्रुत्वा च कलौ घोरे जनो नैव भयं व्रजेत् ॥ 5
3.4.m: Listen further with joy, O sage, to the acts of Hari, / hearing which in the terrible Kali age a man will never experience fear.

3.4.s:
pañcābde kṛṣṇacaitanye yajñāṃśe yajñakāriṇi .
vaṅgadeśabhavo vipra īśvaraḥ śāradāpriyaḥ . . 6
3.4.d:
पञ्चाब्दे कृष्णचैतन्ये यज्ञांशे यज्ञकारिणि ।
वङ्गदेशभवो विप्र ईश्वरः शारदाप्रियः ॥ 6
3.4.m: When Kṛṣṇa Caitanya, a portion of the sacrifice who performs sacrifices, was five years old, / a Brahmin born in the country of Bengal named Īśvara, beloved of Sarasvatī,

3.4.s:
prāptaḥ śāntipure grāme vāgdevīvaradarpitaḥ .
satāṃ digvijayaṃ kṛtvā sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ . . 7
3.4.d:
प्राप्तः शान्तिपुरे ग्रामे वाग्देवीवरदर्पितः ।
सतां दिग्विजयं कृत्वा सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ॥ 7
3.4.m: proud of the boon of the goddess of speech, arrived at the village of Śāntipura, / having conquered the wise everywhere, skilled in all scriptures.

3.4.s:
gaṅgākūle stavaṃ divyaṃ racitvā 1 so'paṭhaddvijaḥ .
etasminnantare tatra yajñāṃśassamupāgataḥ . .
uvāca vacanaṃ ramyamīśvaraṃ stutikāriṇam . . 8
3.4.d:
गङ्गाकूले स्तवं दिव्यं रचित्वा 1 सोऽपठद्द्विजः ।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र यज्ञांशस्समुपागतः ॥
उवाच वचनं रम्यमीश्वरं स्तुतिकारिणम् ॥ 8
3.4.m: Having composed a divine hymn on the bank of the Gaṅgā, that Brahmin recited it. / Meanwhile, the incarnation of the sacrifice came there / and spoke pleasant words to Īśvara who was reciting the praise:

3.4.s:
sukṛtaṃ pūrtamarṇaṃ ca śrutīnāṃ sārameva hi .
ityuktaṃ bhavatā stotre dūṣaṇaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ vada . . 9
3.4.d:
सुकृतं पूर्तमर्णं च श्रुतीनां सारमेव हि ।
इत्युक्तं भवता स्तोत्रे दूषणं भूषणं वद ॥ 9
3.4.m: '"Good deeds, civic works, the ocean, and the essence of the Vedic revelations"; / since this was said by you in the hymn, state the defect or the ornament [of it].'

3.4.s:
tathāha ceśvaro dhīmāndūṣaṇaṃ naiva dṛśyate .
ityuktyā prāha bhagavānbhūṣaṇaṃ naiva dṛśyate . . 3.4.19.10
3.4.d:
तथाह चेश्वरो धीमान्दूषणं नैव दृश्यते ।
इत्युक्त्या प्राह भगवान्भूषणं नैव दृश्यते ॥ 3.4.19.10
